We show that on an image classification task, the resulting CLS model is more resistant to forgetting in a domain-incremental continual learning setting than a baseline ResNet LTM, and generalizes more effectively in a few-shot setting than other continual learners. In the continual setting, overall accuracy is slightly worse than existing continual learning models, but with a different mix of performance characteristics. Results analysis suggests that the model is limited by the representations and representational plasticity of the LTM. In future work, we will seek to address this by replaying STM memories to the LTM.

data.title: Dual DeltaNet: Value-Side Memory Reorganization for Linear Attention
data.abstract: Linear attention and state space models (SSMs) offer efficient alternatives to softmax attention by maintaining a fixed-size recurrent state, but this design requires careful management to preserve useful historical associations and limit interference. The delta rule helps reduce interference through correction of the value associated with each key, but it does not explicitly account for how related value features are distributed across the state. We observe that a state $\boldsymbol{S}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_k\times d_v}$ can be viewed as a bank of $d_k$ addresses storing $d_v$-dimensional values. While a key-side read $\boldsymbol{S}^\top\boldsymbol{k}$ retrieves the value associated with $\boldsymbol{k}$, a value-side read $\boldsymbol{S}\boldsymbol{e}$ aggregates addresses whose stored value features match the selector $\boldsymbol{e}$. Based on this observation, we propose Dual DeltaNet (DDN), which extends Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) with a two-sided delta rule. The key-side delta rule reads with the current key to correct its associated value, while the complementary value-side delta rule reads with selected features of the current value to reorganize the addresses it occupies. We derive a chunkwise parallel training algorithm and a rank-2 recurrence that increases arithmetic intensity during inference. Compared with KDA, GDN-2, and Mamba-3, DDN achieves the strongest overall performance across language modeling, zero-shot downstream tasks, and retrieval, while incurring modest training and inference overhead relative to KDA. Code: https://github.com/ReichtumQian/DualDeltaNet

data.title: Structural Pattern Mining in Inka Khipus: A KFG Re-Analysis
data.abstract: This paper reports a methodological pivot from the Open Khipu Repository to the Khipu Field Guide (KFG) database, prompted by stalled progress on the OKR, and a full re-analysis of the resulting 650-khipu sample. Three findings recur across every analysis attempted. First, khipu size confounds nearly every derived structural count, explaining 42-70% of its variance; all subsequent models control for it. Second, the two-letter name prefix (AS, UR, HP, QU, JC, MM, KH) identifies the original cataloger, not a site or period, which turns documentation completeness into a second confound that must be modeled explicitly. Controlling for both, khipus cataloged by Hugo Pereyra's Proyecto Quipu (HP) show significantly fewer Ascher sum-relation types than Gary Urton's (UR) khipus (p = 0.044), while the Ascher-cataloged (AS) khipus are too collinear with their own near-total lack of side/direction documentation to assess (VIF = 5.0). Third, generic structural clustering (UMAP+HDBSCAN) does not separate the pooled 650-khipu sample from two independent null models (permutation and Gaussian), corroborating an independent conclusion already reached by the KFG itself; the same test restricted to a single cataloger (UR) proved not reproducible across runtime environments and is reported here as a methodological caveat rather than evidence of structure. A targeted replication of the KFG's own S/Z-knot spatial-block heuristic for calendar/astronomical khipus recovers 8 of 10 published candidates and proposes 34 additional ones under the same criterion.

data.title: Session-Bound Behavioral Watermarking for Autonomous LLM Agents
data.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly acting through Web interfaces and external tools. They produce trajectories. Those trajectories may pass through several intermediaries. They can store, modify, or dispute those trajectories. In Web-based agent deployments, trajectories may pass through APIs, marketplaces, and tool servers. As such, a copied or disputed log may not by itself reveal which agent owner produced it. Behavioral watermarking can embed ownership evidence in agent action choices. However, existing methods mainly address detection, removal, rewriting, or imitation. They do not directly test whether repeated observation of watermarked trajectories enables cross-session forgery by exploiting learned action preferences. We formulate this learned-forgery threat and propose AgentAnchor, a session-keyed behavioral watermark for owner attribution from trajectory logs. We derive each step key from a secret key, a fresh public session identifier, and semantic states of recent observations, while a guarded digest of the action-policy state diversifies linear coding rows. It embeds parity evidence through a KL-bounded exponential tilt, and a trusted verifier checks a disputed log without rerunning the agent, using wrong-key calibration and abstention.

data.title: Lifting mod $p$ Galois representations over local fields
data.abstract: Let $K$ be a local field with absolute Galois group $G_{K}$ and let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. We prove that every continuous representation $G_K\to \operatorname{GL}_{n}(k)$ lifts to a continuous representation $G_K\to\operatorname{GL}_{n}(W(k))$ where $W(k)$ is the ring of infinite Witt vectors over $k$.

data.title: Robust Active Learning for More Efficient and Reliable Paths to Optimal Design
data.abstract: Simulation-driven design optimization requires active learning strategies that efficiently combine models with different computational costs and levels of fidelity. We introduce Multifidelity Cost-Aware Screening (MF-CAS), which enables the joint selection of sampling location and fidelity using a surrogate that provides decomposed uncertainty intervals rather than a complete predictive probability distribution. MF-CAS exploits the contribution of each fidelity to the high-fidelity uncertainty together with its computational cost to determine whether a candidate should first be evaluated at low fidelity or directly progressed towards high fidelity. The method is assessed on the constrained 14-dimensional hydrodynamic optimization of the DTMB 5415 hull under a deliberately limited computational budget. MF-CAS achieves an approximately 9.0% resistance reduction, compared with 6.7% for the best baseline optimisation method, demonstrating that incorporating fidelity-resolved uncertainty directly into the joint location-fidelity decision can substantially improve multifidelity active learning efficiency.

data.title: Engineering Canalized Near-Field Radiative Heat Transfer between Fixed Nanoparticles with Twisted $α$-MoO$_3$ Trilayers
data.abstract: Canalized phonon polaritons in twisted van der Waals crystals offer a route to control nanoscale thermal energy flow. Building on the established twisted $α$-MoO$_3$ trilayer platform, we examine how internal twist angles modify near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) between a prescribed nanoparticle pair while both the nanoparticle axis and the bottom-layer crystallographic orientation remain fixed. Under this constraint and at equal total $α$-MoO$_3$ thickness, the optimized trilayer reaches 2.84 times the bilayer maximum radiative power, while its mean power over the sampled internal twist configurations is 1.51 times the bilayer value. The second internal twist coordinate also enlarges the set of configurations supporting strong transfer, with local angular tolerance when either internal angle is varied separately. Momentum-space Green-tensor diagnostics and real-space energy-density maps associate the enhancement with stronger receiver-directed scattering and improved channel alignment. Selected trilayer configurations retain enhanced coupling across the sampled family of nanoparticle resonances and at long distances. These results quantify the additional internal configurational freedom available for engineering radiative heat transfer under a fixed laboratory-frame geometry.

data.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlevé Equation
data.abstract: For the first Painlevé equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_π\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-π}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8π/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2π/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlevé transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.

data.title: Integrated data, metadata, and paradata management system for 3D Digital Cultural Heritage objects: Workflow automation, federated authentication, and publication
data.abstract: The complexity of high-quality 3D digitised cultural heritage objects creates challenges for existing data management systems as they need to develop metadata management and processing capabilities to provide semantic insight into the interconnectivity of data that constitutes cultural heritage objects. To address these challenges, we propose a global federated authentication and authorisation mechanism, a data and metadata management system, and an integrated engine for designing and executing automated workflows that facilitate the processing of both data and metadata. The solution is evaluated with three distinct 3D digitised cultural objects and presents the complete process from data upload to cultural heritage object publication

data.title: Estimating the number of nodes and paths in a DAG by following a random path
data.abstract: We investigate a simple method to compute an unbiased estimate of the number of nodes of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) by following a random directed path. This method is due to Leonard Pitt from 1987, and it generalizes a method of D. E. Knuth from the 1960s for estimating the size of a rooted tree. A slight variation makes it possible to estimate the number of source-sink paths. We extend the algorithm to use many "agents" that walk cooperatively through the graph. This extension unifies and generalizes several methods that have been proposed for approximately counting the nodes of a tree.

data.title: RoSAMDepth: Robust Self-supervised Depth Estimation Leveraging Segment Anything Model
data.abstract: Robust depth estimation aims to maintain high-quality depths across diverse conditions. However, most existing methods estimate depth without taking into account the object-level information. As a result, the predicted depth may easily deviate within objects and become blurred under adverse conditions. To overcome this weakness, we propose RoSAMDepth, a novel framework that can assist robust self-supervised depth estimation in leveraging rich and diverse object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model (SAM). We focus on incorporating object-level information across three key aspects: a segment-guided representation contrasting method that injects object-level awareness into the feature representation space; an adaptive regional outlier masking strategy combined with a regional Gaussian likelihood loss that enforces regional depth smoothness; and an object-level reliability estimation strategy that mitigates the influence of unreliable supervision. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions demonstrate that our method produces sharper, more accurate depth predictions, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/xagao/RoSAMDepth.

data.title: The smallest singular value of products of random combinatorial and deterministic matrices
data.abstract: Let $p\in(0,1/2]$ be fixed, and let $d,n$ be positive integers satisfying $d=pn$. Let $Q_n$ be an $n\times n$ random combinatorial matrix whose rows are independent and uniformly distributed over the vectors in $\{0,1\}^n$ having exactly $d$ ones. For an arbitrary deterministic invertible $n\times n$ matrix $M$, we establish two-sided bounds for the smallest singular value of $Q_nM$. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left( \varepsilon\le s_n(Q_nM)\cdot \|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le \varepsilon^{-2} \right) \ge 1-C\left( \varepsilon+d^{-1/2}+e^{-c\,\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})} \right)-2e^{-cn}, \] where positive constants $C, c$ depend only on $p$ and $\operatorname{sr}$ denotes the stable rank. Consequently, for any sequence of deterministic invertible matrices $M$ satisfying $\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})\to\infty$, $s_n(Q_nM)$ is typically of order $\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{-1}$. In particular, taking $M=\mathbf I_n$ recovers the known $n^{-1/2}$ scale for $s_n(Q_n)$.

data.title: GRAVITY-RESOLVE: A comprehensive image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations with GRAVITY
data.abstract: We aim to improve and extend the imaging capabilities of the GRAVITY beam combiner instrument of ESOs VLTI with respect to reconstruction software in the Galactic Center. We revise and develop the image reconstruction code GRAVITY-RESOLVE $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, which has been specifically developed to reconstruct stars in the Galactic Center with GRAVITY. The main objectives are to increase the limiting magnitude in GRAVITY images, reduce its computational runtime, and allow for a joint reconstruction of multiple, spatially separate datasets/pointings on sky. We apply $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ to recent GRAVITY data, featuring the implemented GRAVITY-faint mode as part of GRAVITY+, the upgrade of GRAVITY. We reconstruct visibility phases and amplitudes and present the first GRAVITY image reconstructed with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ from these quantities. We demonstrate NIR mosaicking with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ by jointly reconstructing nine separately acquired datasets of 2025 into a single image on a scale of $\simeq 3390\ \text{AU}\times 3390\ \text{AU}$, corresponding to $409.6\ \text{mas}\times 409.6\ \text{mas}$. With dedicated injection tests of point sources into GRAVITY data, we estimate the limiting magnitude to be $m_{\text{K}}\ \simeq\ 20.0$ within a radius of $25\ \text{mas}$ around the field center when reconstructing from closure phases and visibility amplitudes. We report on the discovery of two new faint stars in the Galactic Center: S303 and S304. Finally, we find a decrease in computational runtime by a factor of at least $\sim10$. With $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, we demonstrate GRAVITYs capabilities for NIR imaging. We show that $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ is a fast, precise, and deep image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations, enabling the discovery of even more faint stars.

data.title: Finite-State Time-Inhomogeneous Markov Chains Conditioned to Survive
data.abstract: We study conditioning on long survival for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains on finite state spaces. We assume that a sequence of substochastic transition kernels converges to an irreducible substochastic kernel and that the transition probabilities admit asymptotic expansions up to order $n^{-2}$. Under these assumptions, we construct a positive space-time harmonic function and prove that the limiting path distributions under conditioning on long survival are given by the corresponding Doob h-transform. We also investigate the long-time behavior of the resulting conditioned process. Finally, we apply our general theory to an elephant random walk, a generalized Pólya urn model, time-inhomogeneous Wright--Fisher and Moran models, and noncolliding random walks.

data.title: The Polynomially Self-repelling Motion
data.abstract: [Kosygina et al. 2023] showed that the rescaled polynomially self-repelling walk does not converge to any Brownian motion perturbed at extrema (BMPE). Motivated by this result, we introduce an explicit candidate for the scaling limit, the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM), and study its properties. The construction relies on a new family of continuous stochastic flows, called polynomially self-repelling flows, introduced in [Yu 2026]. A key ingredient in relating the limiting process of the rescaled walk to the PSRM is a joint Ray-Knight theorem for rescaled local time processes, extending the classical Ray-Knight theorems of [Tóth 1996].

data.title: Unique Positive Extremals and Sharp Stability Constants for Singular Moser-Trudinger Inequalities
data.abstract: We combine spectral perturbation with orthogonal transformations in $H_0^1(Ω)$ to study singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities under the energy constraint $\int_Ω|\nabla u|^2\,dx\le1$, where $Ω$ is a smooth bounded planar domain containing the origin. For the weight $|x|^{-2β}$, $0\leβ<1$, the positive maximizer is unique for small $α>0$, and the sharp global stability constant satisfies \[ C_α=\fracα{2} \left(\frac1{μ_1}-\frac1{μ_2}\right)+O(α^2), \qquad α\downarrow0, \] where $μ_1<μ_2$ are the first two weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues. We compute the second asymptotic coefficient by a weighted quartic maximization on the second eigenspace, even when the second eigenvalue is multiple. An exact reduction to the sphere orthogonal to the maximizer identifies the attaining functions and yields a limiting global-to-local ratio of $1/2$. On the disk, the energy derivative with respect to the central value characterizes radial constrained degeneracy and yields finitely many exceptional normalized parameters. Combined with known critical uniqueness and nondegeneracy, this gives uniform quadratic stability near criticality, while compactness and analytic reduction yield finite-power stability throughout the admissible range.

data.title: SpectralTF-MAE: A Pre-trained Spectral Foundation Model for Tokamak Fusion Plasma Diagnostics
data.abstract: Spectroscopic diagnostics provide rich information for characterizing plasma states in tokamak fusion experiments, while existing learning-based approaches are often designed for individual tasks and rely heavily on labeled data. In this work, we propose SpectralTF-MAE, a self-supervised spectral foundation model for tokamak plasma diagnostics. The model is pretrained on paired charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) and X-ray crystal spectroscopy (XCS) measurements through masked spectral reconstruction. To better capture diagnostically important spectral structures, we introduce a peak-aware masking strategy together with a peak-enhanced reconstruction objective, encouraging the model to focus on characteristic spectral regions. A shared Transformer encoder is employed to learn transferable representations across different diagnostic modalities. The pretrained model is further adapted to several downstream tasks, including plasma-parameter prediction, cross-diagnostic spectral generation, and spectral peak analysis. Experiments on EAST diagnostic data demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance across different tasks and consistently benefits from self-supervised spectral pretraining. These results indicate the potential of SpectralTF-MAE as a general and transferable representation learning framework for plasma spectroscopic diagnostics. The source code and pre-trained models will be released on https://github.com/Event-AHU/OpenFusion/tree/main/SpectralTF-MAE.

data.title: JYVA at BeTraC: Audio-Based Medical Note Generation with SOAP Section-Specific Queries
data.abstract: We present our submission to the Beyond Transcription Challenge (BeTraC) on medical note generation from doctor-patient audio conversations. We propose a section-aware approach based on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, in which a lightweight Q-Former learns SOAP section-specific queries to extract compact clinical representations from speech. In the lightweight track, our system ranks fourth and substantially outperforms the challenge baseline, achieving a Concept F1 of 0.5005 on the official test set. The organizers' analysis and our heuristic evaluation suggest improved robustness to hallucinations, and better stability under difficult audio conditions. These results show that explicitly modeling SOAP structure through section-specific queries is an effective way to improve the faithfulness and reliability of audio-based medical note generation.

data.title: Swimming versus Screening: How Activity Reshapes the Ionic Cloud of a Charged Particle
data.abstract: A major question in active matter is how interactions between particles are modified by activity. Here, we address this question for Coulomb interactions by considering a charged swimmer immersed in an electrolyte. A static charge is screened by an ionic cloud that decays over the Debye length $λ_D$. We show that the persistent motion of the swimmer can qualitatively modify the steady-state ionic charge-density profile. At low activity, the swimmer appears effectively quasistatic to the ions, and conventional Debye-Hückel screening is recovered. At higher activity, the ballistic-to-diffusive dynamics of the swimmer are reflected in distinct spatial regimes. A power-law decay is followed by a stretched-exponential decay at intermediate distances. At sufficiently large distances, exponential screening is restored, but with an increased screening length, $λ>λ_D$, revealing activity-induced underscreening. Thus, active motion modifies both the spatial form and the range of electrostatic screening. Our results motivate the study of active electrolytes composed of positively and negatively charged swimmers.

data.title: A $p$-Laplacian Problem with Slightly Subcritical Regularly Varying Nonlinearity
data.abstract: We study a quasilinear elliptic problem involving the $p$-laplacian operator and a slightly subcritical nonlinearity with a sign-changing weight. We assume that the slightly subcritical nonlinearity is a regularly varying function at zero and at infinity, which are not necessarily asymptotic to a power at infinity. We state sufficient conditions which guarantee a Palais-Smale condition. We also provide a bifurcation theorem for these nonlinearities, which allow us to state the existence of a bifurcated branch of positive solutions, containing a turning point, and multiplicity of solutions.

data.title: Rethinking LLM Jailbreak Evaluation: Continuous Risk Landscapes Beyond Binary Outcomes
data.abstract: A binary success indicator is a natural representation for discriminative tasks such as image classification under adversarial perturbations, where each input is mapped to a single prediction. However, generative tasks are fundamentally different: an LLM jailbreak prompt induces a distribution over open-ended trajectories, while a sampled response reveals only one path. Yet LLM jailbreak evaluation typically retains the binary response indicator underlying attack success rate, obscuring the surrounding structure of possible generations. We introduce a continuous, context-conditioned risk landscape over first-token branches, estimated by fixing candidate openings and repeatedly sampling their continuations. This continuous risk-landscape perspective reveals two complementary properties: current decoder exposure and safe rerouting capacity, which have been obscured by binary-indicator-based ASR. The resulting representation also provides a common basis for comparing clean prompts, attacked variants, and attack strength against a known adaptive defense. Across multiple target models and jailbreak attacks, we uncover risky branches beneath apparently safe outputs, identify qualitatively different ways attacks reshape the model's opening distribution, and show that attacks strongest before a defense do not necessarily remain the strongest after the adaptive defense reacts. These findings recast jailbreaks as deformations of the surrounding continuation-risk landscape, establishing a more informative foundation for understanding jailbreak behavior and developing safer language models.

data.title: Nonreciprocal Floquet tunneling dynamics of spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a non-Hermitian double-well potential
data.abstract: The stable tunneling dynamics in non-Hermitian quantum systems is one of the fundamental issues in the study of quantum transport. Nonreciprocal coupling, as another crucial manifestation of non-Hermiticity, exerts significant regulatory effects on the stability of quantum devices and on spin tunneling dynamics. Here we place spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a double-well potential with gain and loss, and investigate the effect of nonreciprocal coupling on the system dynamics. Through an analytical analysis of the Floquet states and the quasi-energy spectrum under periodic driving, we obtain the PT-symmetry phase diagram of the system. We further explore the synergistic regulation mechanism of several factors---including the strength of nonreciprocal coupling, the non-Hermitian strength arising from gain-loss, and the periodic driving---on stable spin-flip tunneling. The results show that precise manipulation of nonreciprocity and gain-loss can substantially enlarge the stable parameter region. In nonreciprocal systems with balanced gain and loss, the continuity or discreteness of the stable parameter region is determined by the parity of the driving-frequency ratio $Ω/ω$, and the spin-flip tunneling can be precisely controlled through the parameters $λ$ and $2\varepsilon/ω$. For the unbalanced gain-loss scenario, the equilibrium conditions for achieving stable spin-flip tunneling under different parities of $Ω/ω$ are further provided. These findings offer a new theoretical approach for realizing robust spin-flip tunneling, provide guiding significance for the study of quantum-state transport in non-Hermitian ultracold atomic systems, and also serve as a reference for the experimental design of novel spin-based quantum devices.

data.title: Two-Stage Clipping: Linear-Time Approximate and Exact Mixed-Norm Projections for Transformers
data.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) based on Transformer architectures have achieved remarkable performance across artificial intelligence tasks, but their computational cost remains a major bottleneck. Structured sparsification provides a promising approach to reducing this cost. In particular, $\ell_{1,\infty}$ projections can induce column-wise sparsity in model matrices, but existing proximal methods (Prox) typically require $\mathcal{O}(nm\log(nm))$ operations for matrices in $\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, limiting their computational and energy efficiency. In this paper, we introduce Two-Stage Clipping (TSC), an efficient structured sparsification operator inspired by bilevel optimization. Rather than solving a bilevel optimization problem in the strict sense, TSC decomposes the computation into two successive stages. First, group-level quantities are projected to allocate the global sparsity budget and identify active groups. Second, the resulting values are used as group-wise clipping thresholds for the matrix coefficients. For square attention matrices ($n \times n$), the complexity of our TSC method is $O(n^2)$, which is linear in the number of matrix coefficients. We establish a theoretical bound on the discrepancy between TSC and the exact proximal projection and show on synthetic data that the additional Euclidean approximation cost remains small in practice. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate substantial runtime improvements over proximal baselines and validate the theoretical norm identities underlying the proposed construction.

data.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
data.abstract: We develop a framework for pure and mixed graphon colourings and use it to study the limiting behaviour of graph partition parameters under cut convergence. Pure colourings correspond to measurable partitions, while mixed colourings assign a probability distribution on the colour set to each point. We develop the representation, equivalence and convergence theory, and show that every mixed graphon colouring has an equivalent pure representative, possibly on a different probability space. For each fixed finite colour set, we establish compactness and describe the topology of coloured graph limits using the cut norm on graphons and the weak-$*$ topology on colourings. The usual coloured cut distance characterises convergence for pure colourings, but not for general mixed colourings. As applications, we prove that the Cheeger constant and modularity converge to their mixed graphon counterparts along cut-convergent graph sequences whose orders tend to infinity, assuming uniformly linear minimum degree and positive limiting edge density, respectively. Both mixed functionals are invariant under graphon equivalence. We also establish their continuity in cut distance on the corresponding classes of graphons, with a stability bound for the Cheeger constant. For modularity, we further characterise coloured graphons attaining extremal modularity values and prove attainment of the mixed optimum for each fixed number of colours. We also exhibit a graphon whose modularity supremum is not attained by any finite colouring.

data.title: Data Scaling Laws in Stereo Matching: From In-domain Fitting to Cross-domain Generalization
data.abstract: In the era of large models, stereo matching is developing towards generalizable foundation models trained on million-scale synthetic images. However, how model performance scales up with synthetic data is still underexplored. In this work, we preliminarily investigate the in-domain and cross-domain data scaling laws in stereo matching. A realistic synthetic dataset, named XStereo, containing 200 thousand samples is first built to serve as a high-quality benchmark for data scaling research. In-domain training on five large-scale datasets demonstrate a two-regime scaling behavior with data, transitioning from the standard power law to saturation, where the critical transition point is approximately invariant under a fixed model. Cross-domain performance exhibits a substantially weaker and less predictable dependence on the source-domain data scale. The distribution and coverage diversity are more effective for diminishing domain gaps. More instructive suggestions are provided for high-efficiency data construction and training. The insightful findings are significant verification and extension of the existing scaling laws in both language and vision, paving the way to efficient and stronger stereo matching. The XStereo dataset is public at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Tong-Zhao/XStereo.

data.title: Atmospheric Parameter Determination of RR Lyrae Stars With Mephisto Multi-band Photometry
data.abstract: Phase-resolved atmospheric parameters of pulsating stars, including RR Lyrae stars and Cepheids, are essential for studying stellar structure and pulsation physics and for establishing accurate stellar benchmarks for Galactic structure and assembly history. We present a photometric framework that simultaneously infers Teff, log g, and [Fe/H] from Mephisto multi-epoch, multi-band (u, v, g, r, i, z) photometry. A supervised neural-network forward model is built by training on synthetic colors derived from theoretical stellar atmosphere models. It reproduces the synthetic colors to a precision of 0.01 per cent. The model is applied to observed multi-epoch colors to derive phase-dependent atmospheric parameters. We apply the method to six RRab and four RRc stars in three globular clusters observed with Mephisto. We find typical per-phase uncertainties of about 62 K in effective temperature (Teff), 0.10 dex in surface gravity (log g), and 0.16 dex in metallicity ([Fe/H]). Repeated measurements across the pulsation cycle reduce the typical formal uncertainty of the final [Fe/H] estimates to roughly 0.03 dex. A sensitivity analysis indicates that the five Mephisto colors provide distinct and complementary constraints on the three stellar atmospheric parameters: (u-v) provides robust constraints on log g, (v-g) is informative for estimating [Fe/H], and (u-v), (v-g), (g-r), (r-i), and (i-z) all provide information on Teff. The results demonstrate that Mephisto multi-epoch, multi-band photometry can deliver precise, cost-effective phase-resolved atmospheric parameters for RR Lyrae stars, offering an efficient way to construct large samples of stellar benchmarks for studies of stellar pulsation physics and Galactic structure and evolution.

data.title: STAR: Scalable TEE-based Anonymous Rate-limiter
data.abstract: Protecting Internet services from attacks such as TLS/HTTP floods requires rate limiting, yet identifying users to enforce these limits can compromise their privacy. Anonymous rate limiting promises to reconcile these goals, but existing schemes either struggle to scale or assume that services and authorities do not collude. We present STAR, which uses server-side trusted execution environments (TEEs) to overcome these limitations. By enabling lightweight cryptographic operations, TEEs make authentication efficient, but introduce a privacy challenge: malicious services can observe memory-access patterns to infer user secrets. We address this threat through countermeasures against secret-dependent memory accesses and assess our implementation using dynamic analysis. To extend these efficiency gains across servers, we also design a secure sharding mechanism that distributes client requests. We demonstrate that strong privacy guarantees can coexist with efficient authentication at scale; STAR processes authentication requests in tens of microseconds and handles approximately 13.9K requests per second per CPU core.

data.title: Matrix orthogonal polynomials related to diffference operators for $L$-orthogonal polynomials
data.abstract: The difference operator $J$ arising from the higher order occurrence for the $L$-orthogonal polynomials is studied using various families of matrix orthogonal polynomials. The matrix orthogonal polynomials determine the polar decomposition of $J$ and its adjoint $J^\ast$ considered as operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$. The special case of symmetric $J$ leads to the case where the matrix polynomials reduce to diagonal matrix polynomials. The example of the symmetric case with constant coefficients for $L=2$ is discussed in detail.

data.title: Pulse-Informed Physical Placement for Parallel Two-Qubit Gates in Qubit Arrays
data.abstract: A parallel two-qubit layer can often be realized with several nonoverlapping sets of physical couplers, but isolated calibrations do not reveal how each realization performs after optimizing its own simultaneous control pulse. We formulate physical placement and pulse synthesis as a coupled decision problem for parallel controlled-$Z$ gates in heterogeneous frequency tunable transmon arrays. The proposed processor-aware structural quantum multi-domain matrix (QMDM) links static processor, edge, incidence, and task information to a dynamic candidate response block. For each candidate placement $P$, QMDM instantiates the active Hamiltonian $H_P$; quantum optimal control (QOCT) generates a placement-specific pulse, direct coupled propagation returns the projected computational subspace overlap $F_{\rm proj}$ and computational survival; and these pulse-conditioned responses are fed back to QMDM to rank and progressively promote physical placements. This placement pulse response feedback defines pulse-informed physical placement. Here, to see the performance of the proposed method on 30 held-out synthetic $3\times3$ processors, the median final $F_{\rm proj}$ is $0.993826$ for pulse-informed placement and $0.984981$ for calibration-based placement. Also, when tested under different system conditions, the proposed pulse-informed approach uses $59.1\%$ fewer candidate QOCT optimizer iterations than the exhaustive finite-budget reference. The QMDM representation and outer search are formulated for arbitrary $L$ simultaneous two-qubit gates. Here, the present global candidate ranking validation is used for $L=2$.

data.title: Efficient Group-Penalty k-means for Text Clustering with Noisy LLM-Generated Constraints
data.abstract: k-means provides a simple and efficient foundation for text clustering, but embedding alone can miss task-specific semantic boundaries. Must-link (ML) and cannot-link (CL) constraints can correct such errors, yet conventional constrained clustering assumes that these relations are already supplied. LLMs can generate them without task-specific labels, but exhaustive querying is costly and their judgments can be incorrect. We present GPKmeans, an efficient Group-Penalty k-means method for text clustering with noisy LLM-generated constraints. GPKmeans uses LLM as an offline local pairwise annotator, querying selected anchor-candidate pairs for sparse ML links and constructing set-valued CL evidence without all-pairs queries. It converts connected components of the ML-link graph and the generated CL sets into groups with normalized, bounded soft penalties, limiting each group's influence independently of its size. Cached coordinate descent is proposed to efficiently solve the constraints clustering problem. We prove finite-step convergence and derive deterministic and probabilistic oracle-referenced bounds that relate objective distortion to the penalty coefficients and to the group-level error probabilities of the generated constraints. Across nine datasets, GPKmeans uses fewer LLM calls and yields more accurate constraints. It achieves the best average ACC, NMI, and ARI while running approximately 30 times faster than state-of-the-art constrained clustering methods.

data.title: The Non-Relativistic Limit of Five-Dimensional Boson Stars and Scale Invariance Violation
data.abstract: We investigate the non-relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in (4+1)-dimensional general relativity (GR). In this limit, the resulting Newtonian theory exhibits an exact scale invariance, leading to a critical boson star configuration with a fixed global U(1) charge and vanishing binding energy. We identify the origin of these properties in the restored scale symmetry and analyze how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry. By comparing the full (4+1)-dimensional Einstein-Klein-Gordon system with the Wick-Cutkosky model, we quantify the effects of these corrections on the energy-charge relation and the kinematic stability of the configurations. Our results demonstrate how weak violation of scale invariance lifts the degeneracy of the non-relativistic solutions and determines the behavior of boson stars away from the critical limit.

data.title: The nature of the Norma arm as a bar-driven star-forming shock front
data.abstract: The Milky Way is commonly depicted as having four major spiral arms, including the Norma-Outer arm, and a central stellar bar whose properties remain debated. Masers associated with young high-mass stars have been used to trace a segment of the "Norma arm" extending from one end of the Galaxy's central stellar bar. Recent work suggests that these masers may reside along a spiral arm or occupy the dominant x1 stellar orbits that give the bar its shape. We now use a new generation of N-body, hydrodynamic simulations to argue that these million-year old masers instead trace the Galactic bar's Quadrant I shock front or, equivalently, its dust lane. This implies that the bar dust-lane is star-forming, shedding new light on our understanding of star formation processes in the Milky Way. By associating the masers with the simulated shock front, we determine the bar's parameters to be: a ~ 4.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, b ~ 2.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, phi = 20 (+5/-2) deg, Omega_p <~ 40 km s^-1 kpc^-1, representing the bar's semi-major and semi-minor half-lengths, inclination angle and pattern speed, respectively. This raises questions about the Milky Way's spiral structure and suggests that the Galactic bar is long, slow and star-forming.

data.title: The Artificial Personality Model: Theory, Implementation, Measurement and Experimental Validation in Conversational Agents
data.abstract: Artificial personality shapes user experience (UX) in human-machine interaction, yet coherent theoretical frameworks and validated measurement instruments remain limited. This paper refines and empirically evaluates the Artificial Personality Model (APM), a hybrid framework integrating human-centred and machine-specific personality dimensions. Across three experiments (N = 395), the model was operationalised and evaluated using the Artificial Personality Questionnaire (APQ). Factor analyses revealed that some human personality dimensions (e.g., agreeableness, conscientiousness) are partially transferable, whereas others (e.g., extraversion) did not emerge as distinct dimensions. Additional machine-specific dimensions were identified. The APQ provided encouraging initial psychometric evidence, while the human-centred BFI-2 showed poor reliability and an uninterpretable factor structure in Experiment 3. Experimental manipulations demonstrated significant effects of artificial personality on user satisfaction, continuous use intention, and social presence. The findings contribute an empirically refined framework and a novel instrument for measuring perceived artificial personality, offering practical guidance for designing conversational agents.

data.title: Stability Study of Photo-inscribed Bragg Gratings in Sapphire Fibers at Very High Temperature
data.abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings inscribed by femtosecond laser in sapphire fibers were subjected to thermal cycling up to 1500$\degree$C. Adding a multimode silica fiber reduces modal interference, improves the quality of the Bragg spectrum and the measurement accuracy. The measurement uncertainty is about 1.9$\degree$C at 1500$\degree$C.

data.title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
data.abstract: When an LLM agent fails, repair methods choose which action to replace and what to put in its place. They often score candidate repairs with greedy replay, a stronger model, an environment oracle, or a judge that reads the failed log. We ask whether these evaluators pick repairs that help the agent that will actually execute them. Holding failed trajectories and candidate single-step repairs fixed, we label every candidate with independent rollouts of the deployed policy and measure how much deployment value each evaluator's choice loses. On failures not screened for repair value, pre-specified tests show that greedy replay loses 0.08-0.13 in expected net success gain in ALFWorld and 0.06-0.13 in net reward in WebShop, relative to selection with the deployed agent's own rollouts. At an equal rollout budget, selecting repairs for Qwen2.5-7B with Qwen2.5-14B rollouts loses 0.25 in ALFWorld and 0.07 in WebShop, twenty 14B rollouts per candidate are worth no more than two of the 7B agent's own, and fresh rollouts confirm that the two models prefer opposite repairs on selected disagreement cases. Between similar-sized models from different families, the losses appear in both directions in both environments (0.07-0.17). The scoring executor also changes repair-location labels and method rankings. Repairs should be verified with the executor that will run them, and repair labels should name their executor.

data.title: V-CAPE: Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing
data.abstract: Recent advances in generative image editing enable complex transformations such as background replacement, object manipulation, and pose adjustment from natural language instructions. However, verifying that these transformations preserve visual consistency, defined as the preservation of an object's intrinsic visual attributes, including geometry, texture, color, and fine-grained details, remains a largely unsolved problem. This challenge is particularly pronounced at scale, where manual inspection is infeasible and automated quality assessment (AutoQA) could become essential. In this work, we introduce Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing (V-CAPE), a large-scale dataset for evaluating visual consistency in generative image editing. The dataset consists of 40K unique source-target product image pairs, each annotated with binary accept/reject labels and structured failure modes capturing fine-grained inconsistencies such as geometric distortions, pose errors, and identity mismatches. V-CAPE combines real-world edited images with a synthetic subset constructed from 3D assets, enabling both realistic evaluation and controlled analysis. Vision-language models (VLMs) across all evaluated size categories on AutoQA achieve accuracy below 65%, indicating that the dataset poses a substantial challenge regardless of model scale. Our results highlight fundamental limitations of current models in verifying visual consistency under transformation, positioning V-CAPE as a benchmark for advancing fine-grained image editing evaluation.

data.title: Emergence of Zonal Flows in an Imbalanced Point-Vortex System
data.abstract: Motivated by experiments on rotating Bose-Einstein condensates, we investigate the statistical mechanics and the non-equilibrium dynamics of an imbalanced gas of oppositely signed Onsager point vortices confined in a disk. To model external forcing and dissipation, we supplement their Hamiltonian dynamics with an annihilation-reinjection (AR) mechanism that preserves the imbalance: oppositely signed vortices are annihilated when they approach closer than a distance representing the healing length, and are subsequently reintroduced into the domain at random locations. At positive energies, the system self-organizes into a large-scale coherent dipole at low imbalance and into a zonal flow at higher imbalance. While AR breaks energy and angular momentum conservation, we argue that the vortex gas evolves quasi-adiabatically through the equilibrium phase space. We capture the topological transition between dipolar and zonal flows both from a statistical and a hydrodynamical perspective. In particular, the bifurcation reflects a non-trivial equilibrium diagram in terms of energy $e$, angular momentum $μ$, and vortex imbalance $η$. We characterize this phase diagram in the "strong mixing'' regime studied by linearizing the Joyce-Montgomery mean-field theory about the weakly non-uniform state. We show that the linear theory is surprisingly relevant for the numerical simulations with AR and suggest that the selection between the dipolar and the zonal configurations in the $(e,μ,η)$ phase space is driven by a hydrodynamical shear instability.

data.title: TRIM: Temporal Run-Time Monitoring of 3D Object Detection via Activation Statistics
data.abstract: Reliable perception is essential to intelligent transportation systems, yet deep neural networks can silently miss safety-critical objects while continuing to produce apparently plausible outputs. Existing run-time monitors for 3D object detection generally assess each frame independently and therefore cannot exploit the temporal evolution of occlusion, point sparsity, and scene complexity. We present TRIM, a lightweight temporal monitor that detects missed-object failures without modifying or retraining the underlying detector. TRIM summarises intermediate activations using compact channel-wise statistics and processes short sequences of these summaries with a temporal convolutional network. Experiments on NuScenes show that temporal monitoring improves AUROC from 0.686 to 0.704 and reduces the false alarm rate at 95% recall from 0.818 to 0.759 compared with single-frame monitoring. Early and intermediate backbone features provide the strongest monitoring signal, while the temporal inference head requires only 0.159 ms on a CPU.

data.title: Conformal Spectrum of (Super) Chiral Ising and XY Models
data.abstract: We determine the spectrum of scaling dimensions of composite operators in the critical Gross-Neveu-Yukawa and Nambu-Jona-Lasinio-Yukawa models through a next-to-leading order semiclassical computation. Their infrared fixed points belong to the chiral Ising and chiral XY universality classes, respectively. At next-to-leading order, we resolve the Lorentz structure of the operator spectrum. For the parameter values at which supersymmetry is expected to emerge in the infrared, we obtain a closed-form expression encoding the full spectrum within the semiclassical methodology. The resulting organization of operators into superconformal multiplets provides further evidence for emergent superconformal dynamics.

data.title: Diagnosing parameter unidentifiability in stochastic dynamics with an application to flocking models
data.abstract: Although flocking behaviour has been studied extensively in active matter physics and mathematical biology, methods for assessing parameter estimability remain underdeveloped. For models formulated as stochastic differential equations (SDEs), we develop a Hessian-based diagnostic framework that detects unidentifiable directions and indicates whether, and how, estimation precision can be improved. The framework utilizes the submartingale structure of the loss function's Hessian and tracks its minimum eigenvalue over time. Under convergence of the time-averaged Hessian, we prove that this eigenvalue grows linearly for identifiable models, but only sublinearly, as $o(t)$, for unidentifiable ones; for a specific type of parameter redundancy, this $o(t)$ bound is tightened to $o(\sqrt{t}\log t)$. Applying the framework to stochastic flocking models, we demonstrate that, in identifiable settings, the magnitude of the eigenvalue reflects the attainable estimation precision. We further uncover a physical mechanism of unidentifiability: as the system approaches the ordered state, the parameters become algebraically degenerate, even though the model contains no trivial redundancy. Identifiability therefore depends on the dynamical regime, not only on model structure. Our framework offers a practical tool for reliable parameter estimation, not only in flocking models but in SDE models across diverse fields.

data.title: Asymptotic stability of clique-saturating edges near Turán thresholds
data.abstract: Let $f_{p+1}(n,m)$ denote the minimum number of $K_{p+1}$-saturating edges in an $n$-vertex $K_{p+1}$-free graph with $m$ edges. In this paper, we investigate the stability of this parameter near the Turán thresholds, with particular emphasis on the role of the minimum degree. We introduce the refined parameter $f_{p+1,p}(n,m,δ)$. It is defined for $K_{p+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, minimum degree $δ$, and containing at least a copy of $K_p$. For every fixed integer $p\ge3$, we establish a stability result when the number of edges is $\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2)$, showing that \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,δ)=\left(\frac{(p-2)^2}{2(p-1)^3}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2), \ δ\geq \left(\frac{p-2}{p-1}+o(1)\right)n. \] We further obtain a stability theorem in the regime where the number of edges is quadratically smaller than $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})$. More precisely, for $0 \leq c< \frac{1}{2p(3p-1)}$, \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,δ)=\left(\frac{1}{2p}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})-(c+o(1))n^2, \ δ\geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}-2c+o(1)\right)n. \]

data.title: Order Maintenance in Worst-Case Constant Time, Verified
data.abstract: Order maintenance asks for a data structure that keeps a sequence of elements under insertions and deletions and tells which of two elements comes first. We give an algorithm, assembled from published components, that performs each operation in worst-case constant time, and verify it in Lean 4. The algorithm is a program for a random-access machine deeply embedded in Lean, whose interpreter counts every instruction. We prove that the program answers every query as a simple reference specification does, that each operation takes at most a fixed number of steps, independent of the number of elements and of the history, and that after $t$ operations no value it has computed has more than $O(\log t)$ bits, so it runs unchanged on a machine with words of that size. A verified translation that preserves step counts exactly connects the high-level proofs to the machine program, so the interpreter is the only cost model to trust. An unverified native implementation shows the algorithm's practical cost.

data.title: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0
data.abstract: We ask what AI coding agents and AI security harnesses find that deterministic static application security testing (SAST) does not, and what they miss that SAST catches. VulnBench 2.0 is a benchmark of 108 hand-curated, attacker-reachable vulnerabilities in 20 open-source web applications in Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python and Java; 62 flow across more than one file. A finding is credited only if it locates the vulnerability's attacker-controlled source and its dangerous sink, each within two lines. We evaluate nine productized configurations under one blind protocol: the Snyk Code static analyzer, Claude Code's /security-review with three model and effort settings (one with the Snyk MCP server), Codex Security with GPT-5.6 Luna, Terra and Sol, and the DeepSec scanner with two model backends. Snyk Code reached 82.4% macro recall (89 of 108) and Claude Code with Opus 5 at xhigh effort 79.3% (85 of 108); they disagree on 28 vulnerabilities, split 16 to 12, too few to tell them apart. Neither engine was sufficient alone: together they reached 101 of 108, the ceiling of all seven comparable configurations combined, and the AI configurations also reported at least seven real vulnerabilities that the reference set did not contain and Snyk Code did not report. What an AI engine misses depends on its harness as much as on its model: without Claude Code's built-in review policy, the same model matched 16 instead of 9 of the 20 vulnerabilities in the classes that policy excludes or restricts (supplementary run on 19 of 20 applications); Codex Security with GPT-5.6 Sol located 80 vulnerabilities at file level but 34 at line level; DeepSec's model-free file selection kept a file from only 56 of the 108 flows. Coverage and cost were only loosely related. The harness, fixtures, reference sets and all run data are public.

data.title: Two-loop BRST-restoring finite counter-terms for chiral non-abelian gauge theories
data.abstract: We study the renormalization of anomaly-free chiral $SU(N)$ gauge theories without scalar fields through two-loop order. We adopt the Breitenlohner--Maison--'t Hooft--Veltman (BMHV) scheme for the treatment of $γ_5$ in dimensional regularization. This prescription induces spurious breaking of BRST symmetry, requiring finite symmetry-restoring counter-terms in addition to the subtraction of ultraviolet divergences. We derive these counter-terms for a general, possibly reducible fermion representation, thus restoring the BRST symmetry, through two loops.

data.title: MiDiff: MIDI-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Drum Audio Enhancement
data.abstract: Bridging the semantic gap between perfect symbolic musical structure and severely degraded acoustic signals offers a powerful paradigm for high-fidelity audio restoration. We introduce MiDiff, a diffusion-based generative model for drum audio enhancement that conditions the reverse process on temporally aligned Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) piano rolls. We extend the Score-Based Generative Models for Speech Enhancement (SGMSE) framework in the complex Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) domain by integrating a pretrained MIDI encoder, multi-scale temporal alignment, and three complementary conditioning strategies: early injection, Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), and cross-attention. We further show that providing the same piano roll only through classifier guidance, driven by an Automatic Drum Transcription (ADT) model on the audio-only score, yields no measurable gain: the symbolic prior is effective when it conditions the score network. To relax the requirement for ground-truth MIDI at inference, we further propose a hybrid reverse schedule that transcribes the diffusion state online with the same noise-aware ADT network and hands over from the audio-only score to MiDiff at a tunable switch time, cutting test FAD by 47% relative to the audio-only baseline without any symbolic input (switch time selected on the test set). We train our model on the StemGMD dataset using a non-additive degradation pipeline that simulates room reverberation with echo, electret capsule frequency response, and soft-clipping saturation with noise. MiDiff substantially outperforms the SGMSE baseline in terms of Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) on both the validation and held-out test sets. Ablation studies demonstrate that combining all three conditioning strategies yields superior performance and that authentic MIDI velocity dynamics are critical for effective symbolic conditioning.

data.title: Think Before You Act: Decision Gate for LLM Agents
data.abstract: LLM agents increasingly perform consequential actions through external tools, yet their proposed actions are often executed without independent verification of policy compliance or task completion. We introduce JevAct, a runtime verification framework that intercepts selected agent actions before execution and enables feedback-driven correction. JevAct compiles domain policies into executable state checks and structured questions evaluated by a prefill-only decision model, which produces probability-based judgments without relying on LLM generation. By combining deterministic verification of tool-state facts with probabilistic assessment of conversational context, the framework identifies potentially invalid actions and premature task termination, providing targeted feedback for bounded revision. JevAct operates independently of the underlying agent model and requires no modifications to its parameters or tools. We evaluate JevAct across eleven LLM agents on $τ^2$-bench Airline and Telecom tasks and BFCL. Results show improvements in agent reliability across multiple models and benchmarks, with particularly consistent gains on Telecom and BFCL, while performance on Airline is more mixed. Overall, these findings suggest that combining structured decision models with executable verification can improve the reliability of tool-using LLM agents.

data.title: When LLM Architectures Meet Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection: a Replication Study
data.abstract: Smart contracts are immutable programs deployed on blockchain platforms, where vulnerabilities can translate directly into financial loss. Among the techniques proposed for their detection, recent work has relied increasingly on Large Language Models (LLMs) guided by carefully crafted prompts. However, the evidence accumulated so far rests almost entirely on the dense Transformer architecture behind the GPT line and on model snapshots already scheduled for deprecation, leaving open the question of whether the reported behaviors reflect a general property of LLMs or an artifact of that specific design. This paper presents an extended replication of the empirical study by Chen et al. on LLM-based smart contract vulnerability detection. We replicate the original protocol on GPT-4 as a baseline, followed by a differentiated replication, executing the protocol on representative models based on Mixture-of-Experts and RNN-like designs, together with an attempted preliminary evaluation of State Space Models. The exact replication confirms the findings of Chen et al., including the high-recall, low-precision detection pattern they report on GPT-4. Nevertheless, the differentiated replication shows that this pattern does not transfer uniformly across the evaluated models. Those from the same architectural family may also exhibit different behaviors, indicating that architectural family alone is insufficient to predict the resulting detection profile. We observe the same qualitative dense-Transformer profile in both GPT-4 and Gemma-3, despite a gap of roughly two orders of magnitude in parameter counts, whereas two Mixture-of-Experts models from different lineages exhibit qualitatively divergent behaviors, indicating that architectural family alone is insufficient to predict the detection profile.

data.title: High-Performance Nuclear Demagnetization Refrigerator Reaching 50 $μ$K
data.abstract: Research in the deep sub-mK regime around 0.1 mK may open new opportunities in condensed matter physics in light of recent rapid progress in quantum technologies and quantum materials. Here, we report the design and performance of a nuclear demagnetization system that provides efficient access to the deep sub-mK regime for a wide range of experiments, using a standard wet dilution refrigerator with a medium-sized copper nuclear stage. We show that the temperature measured by a Pt NMR thermometer reaches 50 $μ$K and that the refrigerator can maintain 100 $μ$K for more than ten days. Remarkably, even with only 12 hours of precooling, the refrigerator cools into the deep sub-mK regime and can maintain 100 $μ$K for more than three days, providing sufficient time for sample measurements. Numerical analyses indicate that the copper nuclear-spin system is cooled to about 18 $μ$K, whereas a local heat leak to the thermometer limits the thermometer temperature to about 50 $μ$K. These features establish the system as a practical platform for efficient experiments in the deep sub-mK regime.

data.title: Cross-Primitive Consistency in Jev
data.abstract: Jev enables efficient decision-making with large language models (LLMs) through typed querying primitives, allowing the same semantic state to be expressed in different formats, such as binary and multiple-choice queries. However, the consistency of decisions across primitives has not been systematically evaluated. This work introduces PrimaCons, a four-axis benchmark for assessing cross-primitive consistency while preserving the semantics of the query. Evaluations across three Jev sizes reveal consistency violations across all four axes. Our analysis shows that these violations follow systematic patterns and that cross-primitive discrepancies predict decision failure with a ROC-AUC of 0.91. To mitigate these inconsistencies, we propose the Cross-Primitive Residual Calibrator (CPRC), which attaches a lightweight residual network to a frozen backbone and jointly optimizes predictive accuracy and cross-primitive consistency. Under a leave-one-domain-out protocol, CPRC reduces cross-primitive inconsistency by 58.57% and improves accuracy by +2.97%., demonstrating its effectiveness in both in-domain and out-of-domain settings. Our findings establish cross-primitive consistency as a key dimension for evaluating Jev and provide a practical approach to improving the reliability of its decisions. Code and benchmark is available at https://github.com/67L1/PrimaCons-CRPR.

data.title: SelectSep: Target-Selective Video Queries for Audio Source Separation
data.abstract: Video-queried sound separation (VQSS) aims to isolate a target sound from an audio mixture using its corresponding video as a query. However, scene-level video queries can become ambiguous when multiple sounding objects are visible, particularly when the target and interferer are semantically similar. We propose SelectSep, a target-selective VQSS framework that jointly uses text and a single click coordinate to specify the target source and instance without requiring segmentation at inference time. We adapt the visual encoder through target-feature distillation with text and click conditioning, and then fine-tune the separator using the adapted visual features. We also introduce an on-screen interference setting, where both the target and interferer are visible, to evaluate target selectivity. Experiments on standard benchmarks and the on-screen interference setting demonstrate consistent improvements in separation quality and target selectivity, particularly for mixtures containing semantically similar sources.

data.title: Approximating the poles of a Painlevé V transcendent for the Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel
data.abstract: The Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel has an expression as an integral containing a Painlevé transcendent $r$ satisfying Painlevé V, in the same way that the Fredholm determinant of the Airy kernel has an expression involving the Hastings-McLeod solution of Painlevé II. In this paper we use Padé approximation to approximate the poles of this Painlevé transcendent $r$ in the complex plane. We use Padé approximation near $0$, Hermite-Padé approximation near $0$ and two-point Padé approximation near $0$ and infinity.

data.title: Topology of Wannierizable Insulators
data.abstract: We study the freedom in choosing Wannier centers and the associated symmetry representations in noninteracting Wannierizable insulators. We compare Wyckoff deformations of atomic configurations with symmetry-preserving adiabatic deformations of occupied states, both with and without adding common occupied atomic orbitals. Explicit examples show that stable Wyckoff equivalence and adiabatic equivalence at fixed filling do not imply each other. In spinless $Fm'm'm'$, an Euler class distinguishes stably Wyckoff-equivalent configurations. In spinless $P\overline1'$, adiabatically equivalent configurations remain distinct under stable Wyckoff deformations. We also classify when stable Wyckoff and stable adiabatic equivalence coincide. They agree in two or fewer dimensions and in three-dimensional spinful systems. For three-dimensional spinless systems, Chern insulator pumps give additional equivalences in 134 magnetic space groups. These groups preserve spacetime orientation and have a point whose site-symmetry group contains $222$, $\overline1'$, or $\overline4'$.

data.title: Uniaxial strain tuning of functional properties in antiferroelectric PbZrO3 membrane capacitors
data.abstract: Lead zirconate (PbZrO3, PZO) is a prototypical antiferroelectric (AFE) system promising for applications such as energy storage and neuromorphic computing. However, in conventional thin-film architectures, its functional potential is often limited by substrate clamping. Although emerging freestanding membrane techniques offer an approach to release this clamping and enable dynamic strain engineering, a systematic understanding of how external strain modulates the switching between AFE and ferroelectric (FE) states is missing. In this study, we investigate the uniaxial strain effects on PZO membrane capacitors transferred onto flexible substrates via a gold-bonding method. We demonstrate that in-plane dynamic strain modulates the AFE-FE switching and functional properties. Corroborated by atomistic simulations, we reveal that the strain-dependent evolution arises from the superposition of the intrinsic strain dependence of specific domain orientation variants and extrinsic strain-induced redistribution of the relative population of different domain variants. These findings provide a predictive understanding of uniaxial strain tuning of AFE-FE switching in PZO, and pave the way for exploiting the functional potential of freestanding antiferroelectric membranes.

data.title: The Reality Gap in Automated Driving Systems Testing: Landscape, Challenges, and Research Directions
data.abstract: Simulation is essential for testing automated driving systems (ADS), but discrepancies between simulation and reality can undermine testing conclusions. It remains unclear which discrepancies the literature addresses and what evidence supports correspondence claims. We present a systematic mapping of 235 primary studies that measure or mitigate the reality gap in ADS testing, selected from 4,195 publications. We characterise objectives, targets, approaches, experimental setups, and evaluation evidence. Our classification distinguishes simulated and real-world execution across six ADS test components, separately for each approach and its evaluation reference. This distinguishes real-world information used to construct an approach from evidence used to evaluate its claims. Of the included studies, 76% address mitigation, primarily targeting scenario and actor realism and perception, while 94% report validation or measurement procedures. Only 61 studies report metrics from multiple families covering sensor/perception correspondence, ADS behaviour, vehicle dynamics, or safety outcomes; this coverage does not establish causal links between discrepancies and test verdicts. The synthesis highlights that real-world content and physical execution must be interpreted against the claim evaluated. The findings motivate claim-specific evaluation and component-level reporting to establish which discrepancies affect testing conclusions and when simulation evidence supports conclusions about real-world ADS behaviour.

data.title: ItemCompass: Real-Time Edge-AI Wearable Vision for Tag-Free Domestic Object Retrieval
data.abstract: Misplacing household objects disrupts daily routines, especially for elderly users. ItemCompass addresses this with a real-time, tag-free wearable AR system that builds a persistent digital twin of the home for natural language object retrieval. A custom eyewear node streams visual and inertial data to an edge server, where YOLOv11n detection, Siamese re-identification, and a Pedestrian Dead Reckoning engine log object locations as Spatial Anchors in InfluxDB. Voice queries are resolved by a local Faster-Whisper and Qwen2 LLM pipeline, delivering concise spoken and AR guidance on a heads-up display. Evaluation shows 0.40 m localization drift, 97.5% step precision, and mAP@0.5 of 0.874, with users rating Accuracy and Trust at 4.6/5.0. The system highlights always-on sensing, conversational spatial memory, and privacy-by-design for wearable computing.

data.title: Competition and cancellation in a tilted Rice--Mele chain: exact Wannier--Stark offset and spectral readout
data.abstract: In a tilted Rice--Mele chain, the Wannier--Stark (WS) ladder becomes staggered, \(E_n=n\Fo+(-1)^{n+1}A\). The offset \(A\) reflects the competition between the staggered onsite energy \(Δ\) and the dimerized hopping \(\dt\), and its cancellation restores spectral equidistance. We determine \(A\) through a systematic strong-field series in the WS basis and a nonperturbative two-band Floquet expression. An exact matrix element reduces the strong-field expansion to Bessel algebra; at the representative working point, truncation at seventh order locates the cancellation point with a theory-internal truncation error of \(0.010\)~Hz, against \(27.3\)~Hz at first order. The Floquet propagator gives the closed form \(A=(\Fo/π)\arcsin(-i\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U/2)\), exact within the two-band model, implying the kinematic bound \(|A|\le\Fo/2\) and identifying cancellation with maximum spectral uniformity. The same analytic structure yields a family of real zeros and complex exceptional points that set the convergence radius of the strong-field series without touching the real axis. On odd-length chains, the hidden-symmetry defect produces a pairing plateau of height \(2|A|\) that persists numerically beyond first order in the modulations, allowing the offset to be read from the static spectrum without Floquet propagation or time evolution. In the bulk, cancellation appears as the merging of two sidebands into a single line at \(\Fo\), a null measurement that requires no calibrated sideband amplitudes, although the tilt and line frequency still need calibration. These signatures provide complementary spectral tests of the staggered WS ladder and a calibration-aware route to precision force sensing.

data.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Questions: Evaluating LLMs on Underspecified Financial Queries
data.abstract: Financial assistants answer questions that sound factual but depend on what the user leaves unsaid: what a data figure measures, which product variant is meant, and the investor's situation and the rules that apply. An assistant that ignores these can still answer with a real number from its data, one that answers a different question. We call this frame collapse. We study it in Indian mutual funds, where product variants and tax rules are formally defined, so the correct answer can be computed for every reading. One study tests each challenge. Given an ambiguously labelled figure, models used it, often under the user's label. Given every alternative labelled, they listed them all, but the layout decided which came first. Missing a fact about the investor, weaker agents assumed a default or an outdated tax rule; requiring the fact did not guarantee its use. Because such answers match their data, checks against the data pass them. An AI judge caught mislabelled figures only when told what each field means, and still passed answers that silently chose another reading. We show how these failures arise, not how often, and propose controls for financial assistants.

data.title: The use of post-quantum cryptography in the automotive context
data.abstract: This study comparatively evaluates post-quantum cryptography (PQC) in automotive communication scenarios, considering the threat posed by quantum algorithms such as Shor's and Grover's algorithms. The simulations use OMNeT++, Veins, INET, and SUMO on two hardware platforms and examine ML-KEM/CRYSTALS-Kyber, ML-DSA/CRYSTALS-Dilithium, and FALCON. ML-KEM and ML-DSA are finalized NIST standards, whereas FALCON is a NIST-selected candidate pending final standardization. The evaluation considers a rural V2V scenario and an urban V2X scenario supported by a roadside unit. Kyber exhibits low {key encapsulation mechanism (KEM)}\color{black} operation latency, Dilithium provides balanced signature performance, and FALCON has high key-generation and signing costs but efficient verification. The results are interpreted as a comparative assessment among the evaluated PQC schemes under the reported simulation conditions; {a conventional ECDSA/ECDH baseline measured in the same simulation setup is also reported for reference.}\color{black} The resulting dataset can support future studies of cryptographic selection in automotive systems.

data.title: Kinematic methods of spiral nature identification: limitations and applicability
data.abstract: The nature of spiral arms in galaxies remains debated, with several competing formation scenarios, including density waves, kinematic spirals, dynamic spirals, and recurrent modes, that are difficult to distinguish observationally. We tested two kinematic methods - the phase reversal method and the velocity harmonic dominance method - using toy models and mock data from TNG50 simulations. For bar resonances, the phase reversal method is strongly orientation-dependent and yields reliable corotation estimates only when the bar is aligned with the disc minor axis. For spiral arms, the phase reversal method does not always yield reliable results and should be used in tondem with another kinematic method. The velocity harmonic dominance method is more robust: it distinguishes between density wave, kinematic, and dynamic spiral patterns, although it still shows some sensitivity to orientation. Uncertainties in the rotation curve do not strongly affect its results. We also apply both methods to the observed grand-design spiral galaxy NGC3938 as an illustrative example; the results suggest the presence of multiple spiral modes, consistent with the recurrent modes scenario and this interpretation relies on different indirect evidence. Based on our findings, we propose a strategy for classifying spiral structure in observed galaxies that combines multiple independent tests. Applying this analysis to an extended sample will allow us to validate its predictive power and to investigate the diversity of spiral formation scenarios.

data.title: "Close enough?" An investigation into multiplication errors in LLMs
data.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently fail at multi-digit arithmetic, but the underlying mechanisms governing these failures remain poorly understood. While recent work demonstrates that addition errors follow a "noisy quantisation" model localised around carry boundaries, whether this framework generalises to multiplication remains an open question. In this work, we evaluate multiplication capabilities across several small base LLMs on a dataset of 16,991 problems spanning varied operand lengths. We show that multiplication errors do not conform to the addition-style noisy quantisation model. Instead, we uncover a novel error regime in small Qwen models: errors in lower-order columns predominantly preserve parity. Conversely, higher-order digit errors shift toward off-by-one carry failures. Our findings suggest that arithmetic computation in LLMs relies on distinct, multi-periodic internal representations where parity is tracked more robustly than exact digit identity, providing new mechanistic insights into numerical reasoning in transformers.

data.title: Quantum Gate Engineering in Superconducting NISQ Platforms: Experimental Methods and Emerging Directions
data.abstract: This review aims to provide researchers, experimentalists, and quantum engineers with an updated and technically grounded perspective on the implementation of quantum gates in superconducting NISQ devices. The goal is to establish a comprehensive bridge between theoretical quantum circuit synthesis and its practical, experimental implementation, focusing on superconducting quantum technologies. We systematically examine the diverse landscape of superconducting qubits and processor architectures, ranging from conventional transmons to alternative and unconventional designs, evaluating their unique design trade-offs, connectivity constraints, device physics, and materials impact. Moving from theory to actual implementation, we detail how single- and two-qubit operations are synthesized via microwave-driven and flux-activated pulses. We here present our pulse engineering, wave shaping, calibration workflows, demonstrating how to bridge the gap between abstract gate models and real-world hardware limitations in the direction of a hardware-software co-design framework. To validate these operations, we choose benchmarking methodologies with the purpose to get the more efficient metric for the specific evaluation aspect, including truth tables and quantum process tomography.
