The process starts from positive soft channels admitting an auxiliary representation $$ U(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{tx}ρ(\mathrm{d}t),\qquad ρ\ge0, $$ with an auxiliary measure having a finite exponential quadratic moment. This rewrites the perceptron as a dense, bipartite Gaussian model with an Ising layer and a continuous auxiliary layer. The CCM blanket geometry then gives two constructive variance profiles, $Q_\ell$ on the Ising side and $Γ_\ell$ on the auxiliary side. The bipartite shell scale is $$ Q_{\ell+1}Γ_{\ell+1}-Q_\ellΓ_\ell, $$ and Gaussian core comparison removes the core contribution $ΔQ_\ellΔΓ_\ell$ under blanket refinement. The scalar cavity functional has three terms, $$ \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{perc}}(ν)=\mathbb{E}\left[\log\langle2\cosh x\rangle_ν+α\log\langle U(s)\rangle_ν-\log\langle e^y\rangle_ν\right], $$ where $x$ is the new-spin field, $s$ is the new-constraint field, and $y$ is the cavity correction. CCM identifies the constructive cavity variables with the Aizenman--Sims--Starr random overlap structure (ROSt) variables. Parisi's recursive averaging then gives $$ \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{perc}}^{\mathrm{CCM}}(ζ,Q,Γ)=X_0(0)+αY_0(0)-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\ell=0}^{R}ζ_\ell\left(Q_{\ell+1}Γ_{\ell+1}-Q_\ellΓ_\ell\right). $$ The replica-symmetric specialization gives Gardner's formula for the generalized Ising perceptron. Specializing the constraint terminal to the hard channel gives the Krauth--Mézard functional for the binary perceptron.

data.title: A Paley-Wiener-Type Theorem with Applications to Inverse Medium Scattering for the Schrödinger Equation
data.abstract: This paper develops a new uniqueness framework for inverse scattering problems for the time-harmonic Schrödinger equation using multi-frequency data. Our approach is based on a Paley-Wiener-type theorem that characterizes the support of the potential through the asymptotic growth of a generalized Fourier integral along imaginary frequencies, allowing for nontrivial amplitude functions. Within this framework, we obtain two major results on identifying the shape of the support of the potential in three dimensions, for both the plane-wave incidence and point source incidence, respectively. For plane-wave incidence, we prove that the location and shape of the convex compact support of an essentially bounded potential are uniquely determined by fixed-angle far-field data from two opposite incident directions or by backscattering far field data, provided that the potential is real-valued and sign-definite near the boundary of its support. For point-source incidence, we show that near-field backscattering data, namely the scattered field evaluated at the source point as the source ranges over a sufficiently large sphere, uniquely determine the location and shape of the convex support under the same assumptions on the potential. The proofs rely on meromorphic extension and the Paley-Wiener-type theorem.

data.title: A doubly charmed strange molecule from coupled-channel dynamics
data.abstract: We investigate a doubly charmed molecular state $T_{cc\bar{s}}$ with $C=+2$, $\mathcal{S}=+1$, and $I=1/2$ in an off-shell coupled-channel formalism. Constructing the interaction kernel from a meson-exchange model based on an effective Lagrangian and solving the coupled-channel scattering equation in the Blankenbecler-Sugar reduction, we find a pole only for $J^P=1^+$ among $J^P=0^\pm$, $1^\pm$, and $2^\pm$. With the reduced cutoff mass of $600$~MeV, we obtain a mass of $3972.90$~MeV, which corresponds to a binding energy of $4.01$~MeV relative to the $D^*D_s$ threshold. Examining the relative signs and magnitudes of the $S$-wave channel couplings extracted from the pole residues, we demonstrate that the pole belongs predominantly to the triplet ($\mathbf{3}_A$) representation. We also discuss the relevance of heavy-quark spin symmetry to the bound state.

data.title: Convergence rates of mixed primal-dual dynamical systems with implicit Hessian damping and Tikhonov regularization
data.abstract: We propose a mixed-order primal--dual dynamical system with implicit Hessian damping and Tikhonov regularization for linearly constrained convex optimization, and derive a corresponding fast primal--dual algorithm. The proposed dynamical system couples a second-order primal equation with a first-order dual equation without requiring twice differentiability of the objective function. An energy analysis establishes $\mathcal{O}(t^{-2})$ convergence rates for the augmented Lagrangian gap, feasibility violation, and objective residual along an extrapolated primal trajectory. For the proposed algorithm, we construct discrete energy estimates and establish the corresponding $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2})$ rates at the extrapolated primal iterates. In particular, in the critical regularization regimes $ε(t)=a/t^2$ and $ε_k=a/k^2$, these accelerated rates hold simultaneously with strong convergence of the primal trajectory and primal iterates to the minimum-norm solution, respectively, under suitable parameter and trajectory conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence behavior of the proposed dynamical system and the corresponding algorithm.

data.title: Phase Retrieval of Bandlimited Signals Using a Morlet Wavelet and an Admissible Companion
data.abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate that complex bandlimited signals can be uniquely recovered (up to a global phase factor) from two families of wavelet transform magnitudes, sampled at twice the Nyquist rate in two frequency bins. These families come from translations of the fixed dilated Morlet wavelet and a fixed companion wavelet. The companion wavelet admits an augmented Morlet--Gaussian representation. We rewrite the two families as two modulated Gaussian convolution measurements of an auxiliary bandlimited signal. Using a Gaussian convolution uniqueness result, we prove that samples on \((4B)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\) determine every signal in \(PW_B^2\) (up to a global phase factor). Compared with earlier wavelet phase retrieval results, our approach requires significantly fewer sampling points.

data.title: Power-Type Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with the Logarithmic Laplacian
data.abstract: We prove global existence of the Cauchy problem of a Schrodinger equation with the logarithmic laplacian and a pure power linearity. We address the focusing and the defocusing cases, and we obtained a sharp blow-up in time result.

data.title: Kinematic Causal Attribution: Black-Box Explanations of Motion versus Geometry for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models
data.abstract: 4D perception models, which classify 3D point-cloud videos, are being built into robots, assistive monitoring and AR, yet before deploying one a practitioner cannot check which cue it relies on: how a body part moves, or what shape it has. 3D attribution is single-frame, video attribution is confined to RGB pixels, gradient maps need white-box access, attention is absent from state-space backbones, and point-level perturbations assume a point correspondence across frames that real depth and LiDAR data lack. We present Kinematic Causal Attribution (KCA), a black-box, interventional attribution method that queries only the model's outputs. Its freeze operator removes a region's motion while keeping its shape, and a shape-free proxy removes the shape while keeping the motion. Together they span a motion$\times$geometry cube for every tracked region, whose order-symmetric Shapley decomposition is complete and whose interaction is measured rather than assumed away. The operators rewrite per-frame point sets, so they need no correspondences, and a context-averaged estimator handles structures that span several regions. We validate KCA on the official PSTNet, P4Transformer and Mamba4D trained on MSR-Action3D. The decisive test is an audit: two binary tasks are built from real clips whose classes differ only in the motion or only in the shape of the same arm, and the motion share of the arm's importance follows the defining cue on all three backbones (0.83 vs. 0.60 on P4Transformer, 0.86 vs. 0.30 on PSTNet, 0.92 vs. 0.61 on Mamba4D), a distinction no single attribution map can make. The split costs no faithfulness: the necessity maps have the lowest deletion AUC on P4Transformer and PSTNet, tie with the best baseline on Mamba4D, and lose their correlation with the trained model's once the weights are randomised. Skeleton ground truth, re-sampling stability and cost complete the validation.

data.title: Sharp approximation thresholds for power means of common-subspace volumes
data.abstract: We study how well a single $k$-dimensional subspace can preserve volume from several positive semidefinite matrices at once. Each matrix is compressed to the subspace and scored by the geometric mean of the eigenvalues of that compression; the scores are aggregated by a weighted power mean of order $p \le 1$. For every fixed $k$ and every fixed rational $p$ we determine the optimal approximation factor: it is achieved by a randomized polynomial-time algorithm, and every larger constant is NP-hard. Above a critical power ($p=-k/2$ over the reals and $p=-k$ over the complex numbers) the factor is an explicit product of Gamma functions. At and below the critical power, every positive constant-factor approximation is NP-hard. The factor comes from a concave relaxation over the positive semidefinite matrices of trace one, which agrees with the volume score at every subspace, followed by ordinary Gaussian rounding. For two rank-$k$ matrices the relaxation is exact, giving a closed-form optimum for Martin means of two subspaces.

data.title: Capillary-gravity water waves with compactly supported vorticity I: Local constructions and regular drift
data.abstract: This five-part series establishes the first systematic theory of capillary--gravity water waves carrying compactly supported vorticity with fixed positive circulation. Treating the free surface and the vortex as coupled unknowns, we study the well-posedness of traveling-wave equilibria, including the existence and continuation of solution branches with respect to bifurcation parameters, as well as their variational structure, geometric rigidity, canonical classification, and conditional dynamics. In this first paper, we construct small-speed solitary waves carrying a point vortex of fixed circulation by solving the free-surface Bernoulli equation and the regular-drift condition simultaneously. We derive the free-surface expansion through fourth order, including the first capillary correction, and second-order corrections to the conformal and physical vortex depths. We also characterize vortex equilibria in prescribed domains through the Kirchhoff--Routh function, proving existence and uniform localization. A joint Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction then regularizes the point vortex into a smooth, compactly supported vorticity core while preserving its circulation and the prescribed vorticity law. Finally, in the periodic setting, we construct a local branch under a nonresonance condition and show that the vortex depth diverges logarithmically as the wave speed approaches a positive limit, in contrast to its inverse-speed growth in the solitary-wave setting.

data.title: Atomic Charge Chirality from Electric Multipoles
data.abstract: We establish an electric-multipole ($Q_{lm}$) criterion for chirality of local atomic charge distributions. For the 11 crystallographic chiral point groups, we identify representative lowest-rank multipole contents required to distinguish the opposite handednesses. For the axial groups $C_n$ and $D_n$ with $n=2,3,4,6$, chirality arises from the relative orientation of two azimuthal anisotropies with $m=n$, belonging to consecutive ranks $l=n$ and $n+1$. Their coexistence produces a latitude-dependent twist of the $n$-fold charge distribution. The polar component, although allowed in $C_n$, is distinct from this chiral mechanism and is not required for handedness. The cubic groups $T$ and $O$ exhibit distinct realizations, with octahedral chirality first appearing at rank nine. We further show that, within a spinless $s$-$p$-$d$-$f$ atomic basis, the scalar charge density contains multipoles only up to rank six and therefore cannot encode the handedness of $C_6$, $D_6$, or $O$. These results connect electric-multipole content and atomic orbital degrees of freedom to the microscopic encoding of crystallographic handedness.

data.title: STRATA: Reinforcement-driven Active Sampling with Tri-paradigm Adaptation for Efficient 3D Spatial Transcriptomics
data.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables joint characterization of tissue morphology and gene expression. However, 3D volumetric ST acquisition remains expensive. AI-driven methods offer a low-cost alternative but remain limited in accuracy, while recent 2D section-wise ST acquisition still rely on dense grid sampling, resulting in redundant measurements and undersampling of biologically informative regions. To bridge the gap, we propose STRATA, a reinforcement-driven active sampling framework with tri-paradigm adaptation for reconstructing dense 3D transcriptomic maps from sparse voxel-wise ST acquisition. STRATA constructs a 3D graph integrating H&E morphology with single-cell priors and employs a reinforcement learning agent to estimate morphological sparsity and transcriptomic informativeness, enabling budget-aware selection of informative spots. Given these sparse measurements, an adaptive tri-paradigm predictor combines retrieval, regression, and cross-layer imputation through lightweight fusion, dynamically weighting their contributions. Experiments across datasets demonstrate improved sampling efficiency and accuracy, particularly under low-budget settings. Code is available at https://github.com/Junchao-Zhu/STRATA.

data.title: Unlocking with the Heart: Investigating User Perceptions of ECG-Based Biometric Authentication
data.abstract: Password-based authentication remains challenging for many users, especially for those who face usability and accessibility issues. The burden of maintaining security can cause user fatigue, frustration and non-engagement. To address these issues, we conducted a pilot study to assess ECG-based biometric authentication as a passwordless alternative and to gather adult participants' perspectives on this approach. The research consisted of a survey study, an authentication prototype and a follow-up usability experience questionnaire. Our approach combined an online survey of 337 adults examining authentication practices and perceptions, with a separate usability evaluation in which 49 participants interacted with a simulated ECG-authentication and password interface in a health-care application prototype, then completed a post-test usability test questionnaire. The survey examined how adults across age groups use and perceive various authentication techniques, their experiences with biometrics, their views on security and convenience, and their willingness to adopt ECG authentication. In parallel, the usability prototype and questionnaire captured participants' responses after hands-on interaction with an ECG authentication prototype.

data.title: Well-posedness of Rough Differential Equations at the Krylov-Röckner Integrability Threshold
data.abstract: We study rough differential equations (RDEs) driven by Brownian (Itô) rough paths with uniformly locally integrable drifts. The diffusion coefficient is assumed to be uniformly elliptic, of class $C^{2+}$ in space and of bounded variation in time, while the drift is $q$-integrable in time and $p$-integrable in space, uniformly on balls of a fixed radius, for some $p,q$ satisfying the Krylov--Röckner condition $\frac dp+\frac2q<1$. We show that, for almost every realization of the Itô rough path lift of the Brownian motion, such an RDE has a unique solution for every initial value. In other words, for almost every realization of the Itô lift, the corresponding rough differential equation has exactly one solution in the class of Davie-type solutions, for every initial value; this is the appropriate notion of path-by-path uniqueness for the corresponding stochastic differential equation (SDE) with multiplicative noise. The proof follows the strategy of Shaposhnikov (2016). The principal new ingredients are the stability of RDEs with bounded variation perturbation and Davie-type estimates for the flow of the driftless equation with non-constant diffusion coefficients, which we derive from known maximal regularity estimates for the corresponding parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs).

data.title: Numerical analysis of geometrical effect on drop deformation and breakup between rotating cylinders
data.abstract: This study numerically investigates the effects of geometrical curvature on drop deformation and breakup in shear flow between counter-rotating concentric cylinders. Simulations were performed using a geometric Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) method incorporating plicRDF interface reconstruction and isoAdvector interface advection, combined with adaptive mesh refinement. Three circular geometries with different values of the non-dimensional geometrical curvature, $κ_{\mathrm F}$, were considered and compared with a planar shear flow system. At fixed Reynolds and Capillary numbers ($Re$ and $Ca$), the breakup morphology differed substantially between the planar and circular systems. In the planar system, the drop underwent relatively symmetric neck thinning, whereas in the circular systems, the drop exhibited asymmetric deformation and pronounced azimuthal elongation. At higher curvature, the drop formed a thin filament that subsequently fragmented, producing multiple satellite drops. Analysis of the internal velocity field and the magnitude of the rate-of-deformation tensor revealed distinct flow and deformation structures associated with these breakup behaviors. Furthermore, the critical $Re$ for breakup, $Re_{\mathrm{cr}}$, decreased with increasing $κ_{\mathrm F}$ at nvestigated $Ca$ values. In contrast, the maximum dimensionless elongation length immediately before breakup at $Re=Re_{\mathrm{cr}}$ increased with $κ_{\mathrm F}$. These findings suggest that geometrical curvature affects not only the breakup threshold but also the deformation process leading to breakup, providing insights into drop breakup in curved shear flows.

data.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents
data.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents often receive access to more files, accounts, and services than a task requires. Prompt injection turns this excess access into an opportunity to redirect execution toward unrelated resources. Applying least privilege therefore requires identifying the assets needed by a task, including assets whose identities emerge only during execution. We present REALM (Required Execution Assets Linked to a Mission), an approach to identifying and maintaining a task's required assets and their permitted uses. The approach represents required assets as Dependency Graph nodes, resolves prerequisite relationships, and admits newly discovered assets through source-scoped selection. It separates discovering an asset from authorizing its use, while preserving the agent's freedom to choose its computation. The REALM Builder maintains the selected grants and projects Asset Files; the Partial API Manager exposes resource-bound Partial APIs to the Agent inside a Task Container. Across 60 clean tasks and 560 injected cases in AgentDyn, it completes 40.0% and 36.4% of tasks and decreases ASR from 16.6% to 0.2% with qwen3.5-flash as the base model.

data.title: Learning Erasing Equal-Length Relational Pattern Languages in the Limit from Positive Data over Binary Alphabets
data.abstract: Relational pattern languages generalize Angluin's pattern languages by requiring the strings substituted for repeated occurrences of a variable to stand in a given relation, rather than to be identical. We study erasing pattern languages under the equal-length relation, where all occurrences of a variable must be replaced by strings of the same length. Over alphabets with at least three letters, this class is known to be learnable in the limit from positive data. We show that over a binary alphabet it is not, which resolves an open question from earlier work. Our proof reveals that non-learnability already holds for the restricted subclass of languages generated by patterns that have exactly three maximal substrings of variables. We then show that patterns with at most two maximal substrings of variables are learnable in the limit from positive data for every alphabet of size at least two. If the target pattern is known to have at most one maximal substring of variables, this can even be achieved by an iterative learner, which updates its hypothesis using only the current example and its previous hypothesis.

data.title: Nonreciprocal coupling enables tunable exceptional-point response in non-Hermitian circuits
data.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) exhibit characteristic square-root spectral responses to weak perturbations, with response magnitudes governed by configuration-dependent prefactors that are often relatively small. Modulating these prefactor while preserving the exceptional characteristics offers an additional degrees of freedom for engineering non-Hermitian sensing responses. Here, we report a nonreciprocal non-Hermitian circuit system with gyrator-meditated coupling that supports a continuous family of EP configurations. Unlike reciprocal coupling, which typically yields a unique EP configuration for balanced gain and loss, nonreciprocal coupling allows the directional forward and backward coupling strengths to be varied while maintaining their product and thus preserving the EP condition and yielding a library of EPs. This additional freedom enables continuous control of the frequency-splitting magnitude without modifying the square-root characteristic dependence on absolute perturbation strength. We show that the spectral splitting induced by a given absolute resistance perturbation can be enhanced by appropriately adjusting the coupling asymmetry. Theoretical predictions, circuit simulations, and experimental reflection-spectrum measurements consistently confirms this tunable response. Our results establish nonreciprocal coupling as an alternative approach for engineering and enhancing EP-induced perturbative responses without changing their characteristic branch-point scaling.

data.title: VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation
data.abstract: The central bottleneck in visual generation and editing has migrated from achieving pixel-level fidelity to satisfying densely constrained user specifications through increasingly agentic workflows. Prevailing agentic generation pipelines remain shallow generate-verify-rewrite loops treating VLM judgments as coarse visual feedback, either discarding repair experience or admitting ungated updates that poison skill library. With memorize and govern periods left open, they degrade into ungoverned iterators of repeated trial-and-error rather than continual self-evolving harness. Towards this issue, we present \textbf{VEvo-Harness}, the first causally-guarded continual self-evolving harness system for agentic visual generation. VEvo-Harness introduces four coupled innovations: (1) \textit{a visual traceback} that densifies sparse judgments into root-cause attributions with a hierarchical verification tree; (2) \textit{a visual continual governance} that admits only causally valid skill patches through counterfactual dual-arm image generation replay; (3) \textit{a lifecycle-managed harness state} that hierarchically distills root-cause-anchored episodes across working, experience, and pattern tiers into a persistent skill library of routable and causally verified capabilities; (4) \textit{a heterogeneous sandbox policy} that orchestrates a diverse action space of repair primitives, dynamically routing cost-aware interventions based on root causes to select the most effective strategy. VEvo-Harness surpasses state-of-the-art agentic methods and rivals proprietary generators (\textit{e.g.}, GPT-Image, Nano-Pro) while maintaining the continual harness evolution and generalization.

data.title: A Geometry-Induced Finite Warburg element for Reversible Diffusion Impedance at Microdisk Electrodes
data.abstract: A compact analytical representation is developed for the diffusion impedance of a disk electrode under reversible conditions, obtained by transforming the chronoamperometric relaxation function into the frequency domain. A Padé approximant is constructed for the uniform-concentration boundary condition, preserving the finite low-frequency diffusion resistance of the steady-state disk current and the high-frequency Cottrell regime. It is extended to reactions in which both oxidized and reduced species contribute, with unequal diffusion coefficients and surface concentrations. Its accuracy is quantified against converged numerical solutions, including an exact solution of the coupled problem with finite-rate kinetics. The approximant reproduces the Saito resistance and the $45^{\circ}$ Warburg phase exactly; its modulus is within 0.6\% of the converged solution for $ωa^2/D\le12$ and 7\% below the Cottrell amplitude at high frequency. The uniform-concentration and uniform-flux boundary conditions both give a diffusion impedance of geometric origin, but differ by up to 11\% in modulus because each couples differently to the spreading diffusion field; a criterion based on the rate constant and the disk radius delineates where each applies. The exact solution shows that this crossover is broad and that the decomposition into a charge-transfer resistance and a diffusion impedance is accurate to about 5\% for $1\le2k^0a/D\le100$. Fitted to a published spectrum of a platinum microdisk, it reproduces the reported diffusion coefficient within 1\%, while the two limiting elements lie 4.8\% below and 4.1\% above it. The element is a practical tool for microdisk impedance analysis.

data.title: CLaW: Codec-Guided Adaptive Latent Watermarking for Traceable Diffusion Image Generation
data.abstract: With the rapid advancement of text-to-image diffusion models, increasingly realistic AI-generated content has raised serious concerns about misuse and copyright infringement. Digital watermarking offers a promising solution by enabling user-level traceability, yet existing methods remain difficult to deploy at scale, hindered by costly model retraining or detection, poor effectiveness-fidelity trade-offs, and limited robustness to image transformations. To address these challenges, we propose CLaW (Codec-guided Latent Watermarking), a robust and efficient watermarking framework for traceable diffusion image generation with frozen diffusion backbones and inversion-free detection. Specifically, CLaW first uses a pretrained watermark codec to map each watermark message to a latent residual, enabling low-cost sampling-time injection. Then, the residual is injected within a late denoising window, where image semantics are better preserved and the watermark signal is less perturbed by subsequent denoising updates, yielding a better balance between watermark effectiveness and image fidelity. Furthermore, we introduce a decoder-guided adaptive injection mechanism that uses decoding confidence as feedback to dynamically calibrate watermark strength, reinforcing weak watermark signals and improving robustness under image transformations. Extensive experiments show that CLaW preserves high visual fidelity and achieves state-of-the-art robustness under image transformations, enabling reliable user-level traceability.

data.title: Joint Rigid Alignment and Morphable Reconstruction from Partial 3D Face Scans
data.abstract: Aligning a partial, real-world 3D face scan to a canonical representation requires solving two coupled problems at once: estimating the rigid pose that brings the scan into a common frame, and completing the facial shape in regions the scan never observed. Existing pipelines typically decouple these steps, running a generic point-cloud registration front end followed by a separate non-rigid fitting or deformation stage. Building on the GeoTransformer superpoint-matching architecture, we propose a single network that predicts both a rigid pose and a shape-complete point cloud in one forward pass: a cross-attention regressor, conditioned on transformer point features and predicted coarse correspondences, maps a partial scan to per-patch coefficients of a 3D morphable face model learned offline from a corpus of 8,000 identities. The resulting morphed template is then used, in the same forward pass, as the target for fine-grained Sinkhorn matching and rigid pose estimation, supervised purely by geometric alignment to ground-truth morphed geometry, so no hand-labeled coefficients are required. Against six classical and learned non-rigid registration baselines on held-out identities, our method leads the strongest ones by 3-4 times on per-vertex error and baselines that collapse the head onto the visible region by more than an order of magnitude, and is simultaneously the most accurate and fastest method on ground-truth-free scans from two independent real-scan datasets, NoW and NPHM. Code will be made publicly available.

data.title: A Novel Approach to Evaluating Evaluation Metrics for Multi-Output Structured Prediction
data.abstract: In multi-output structured prediction tasks, while only one ground truth label may be provided in the training data, multiple equally valid outputs may be possible, making reliable evaluation a persistent challenge. We postulate that human evaluators implicitly use task-specific invariants, e.g., object boundaries in colorized images or named entities in translations, to judge if an output is acceptable. Under this assumption, we introduce a notion of approximate task-specific invariants and use them as diagnostic tools to evaluate a variety of existing metrics for vision and language tasks. We use these task invariants as part of a framework to systematically test metric reliability by encouraging domain-relevant invariants in model outputs via an augmented loss function. In our experiments, we observe that enforcing invariants with an augmented loss yields substantial improvements in popular distributional metrics while more traditional metrics change only marginally. Through this invariants-driven evaluation, we expose where standard metrics fail to detect meaningful differences, and we highlight the conditions under which distributional metrics succeed or still fall short.

data.title: Capillary-gravity water waves with compactly supported vorticity II. Continuation and folds of the solution curve
data.abstract: This five-part series establishes the first systematic theory of capillary--gravity water waves carrying compactly supported vorticity with fixed positive circulation. Treating the free surface and the vortex as coupled unknowns, we study the well-posedness of traveling-wave equilibria, including the existence and continuation of solution branches with respect to bifurcation parameters, as well as their variational structure, geometric rigidity, canonical classification, and conditional dynamics. In this second paper of the series, we apply the Haziot-Wheeler analytic continuation theorem to extend the small-speed point-vortex branch constructed in Part I to a global curve of coupled equilibria. We establish two alternatives: either the geometric control quantity diverges, or it remains bounded along a sequence of solutions with no strongly convergent subsequence. If the second alternative occurs, we use concentration--compactness to obtain a finite profile decomposition without assuming monotonicity of the free surface: a nontrivial centered vortex wave and finitely many reflected pairs of irrotational waves, with a remainder converging strongly to zero. At any simple speed fold, a Schur-complement reduction in the physical vortex coordinate shows that the static energy-momentum Hessians of the two nearby equal-speed waves differ by one in negative index within the symmetric class. Finally, we use a joint two-parameter Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction to extend the regularization of Part I to compact arcs of the global solution curve, carrying the canonical smooth-core branches through their specified simple speed folds. These results provide a global point-vortex reference for the variational construction in Part III and canonical smooth-core comparison arcs for the rigidity and uniqueness theory in Part IV.

data.title: PrivacyFlow: Privacy in AI Agents through Information Flow Analysis and Consequence-Aware Risk Management
data.abstract: Autonomous LLM agents executing multi-step workflows over personal data often misalign with user privacy expectations and leak sensitive, out-of-context information. Although Contextual Integrity (CI) formalizes this problem, existing benchmarks and defenses rarely operationalize CI for realistic multi-step task sequences in evolving environments. In this work, we first introduce agentic PrivacyBench, a benchmark of 5873 tasks in 986 task sequences with dynamic environment updates and CI-grounded allow-sets for sensitive information. We also introduce PrivacyFlow, a defense that separates deliberative privacy planning (System 2) from task execution (System 1), treating each sharing decision as a structured risk-management problem. Before execution, PrivacyFlow traces the provenance and purpose of each planned data flow, models recipient background knowledge, and simulates what external actors could infer. This allows us to model the downstream consequences of disclosure, including inference attacks and context-dependent harms. It then weighs the remaining disclosure risk against task utility and executes a minimized plan, blocks it, or consults the user. Across six models, PrivacyFlow significantly reduces step-level privacy failures and raises the share of completed task sequences without a detected privacy violation by 22--55 percentage points. We further highlight a new privacy--utility--autonomy tradeoff: allowing PrivacyFlow to proactively prompt the user in case of uncertainty can increase authorized task completion at the cost of shifting decision effort back to the user. Our results suggest that proactive CI reasoning can substantially improve agentic privacy and motivate further study of this tradeoff.

data.title: Locally unital $C^*$-algebras and limitations of seminorm criteria for compact operators
data.abstract: We study the problem of geometric characterization of Banach-compact and $\mathcal A$-compact operators on Hilbert $C^*$-modules in terms of uniform structures generated by seminorms. Previously, such a criterion for $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators was obtained by Troitsky for countably generated range modules with a suitable system of seminorms. Using locally unital $C^*$-algebras as modules over themselves, we establish fundamental limitations of such characterizations. Namely, we show that for nonunital locally unital $C^*$-algebras not only does Troitsky's criterion fail to extend, but, more generally, no system of seminorms can characterize $\mathcal A$-precompactness by total boundedness, nor Banach-compactness of bounded operators or $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators by total boundedness of the images of the unit ball. Moreover, the same statement holds for Hilbert $C^*$-modules $\mathcal N$ whenever the algebra $\mathbf K(\mathcal N)$ of $\mathcal A$-compact operators is locally unital and nonunital. We also study Troitsky-type systems of seminorms and their relation to $\mathcal A$-precompactness. We prove that every $\mathcal A$-precompact subset is totally bounded with respect to the strongest of such structures. Consequently, for Hilbert $C^*$-modules admitting a standard frame, all the corresponding notions of total boundedness coincide.

data.title: Classification of Anti-symmetric Solutions to Fractional Lane-Emden System in Borderline Case
data.abstract: We investigate the existence and non-existence of anti-symmetric solutions to the fractional Lane--Emden system in the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$: \begin{equation*}\begin{cases} (-Δ)^s u = v^p & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n_+, (-Δ)^s v = u^q & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n_+, \end{cases}\end{equation*} where $0<s<\frac{1}{2},p,q>0,2s+p=1$, with $u,v$ nonnegative in $\mathbb{R}^n_+$ and anti-symmetric with respect to $\partial\mathbb{R}^n_+$. Li and Zhuo [2023, Sci. China Math.] previously proved non-existence in $L_{2s}$, as well as non-existence in the extended space $L_{2s+1}$ when $1-2s<p,q<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$ and existence in $L_{2s+1}$ when $p+2s<1,q+2s<1$. In this paper, we fill the remaining borderline case $p=1-2s$ in $L_{2s+1}$ space. We establish a non-existence result for $1-2s=p\leq q\leq\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$ and an existence result for $0<q<p=1-2s$. For the non-existence result, we combine a maximum principle for anti-symmetric functions with the method of moving planes to derive a Liouville--type theorem when $1-2s<q\leq\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$. We then iterate the lower-bound estimates to obtain a contradiction through blow-up. To prove the existence of nontrivial solutions when $0<q<1-2s$, we construct a nonhomogeneous solution by a monotone iteration scheme in $L_{2s+1}$ as well as analyze a homogeneous profile. Surprisingly, the homogeneous profile serves as a universal lower bound for all solutions.

data.title: On the well-posedness of a certain model with mixed diffusion appearing in the mathematical biology
data.abstract: The work deals with establishing the global well-posedness in the space $W^{(1,2),2}(R^{2}\times R^{+})$ of the integro-differential equation in the space of two dimensions in the situation when the diffusion term involves the standard Laplace operator in one direction and the fractional Laplacian in another direction in the presence of the drift term. Such model is relevant to the cell population dynamics in the Mathematical Biology. The proof is based on a fixed point technique.

data.title: EgoContact: Evaluating Physical Intelligence with Egocentric Video
data.abstract: Egocentric video has emerged as one of the most scalable sources of data for learning generalizable manipulation priors. Yet, despite its growing use in pretraining robotic policies, it has been underutilized as a validation tool for physical intelligence, a key component of which is understanding where to make contact with an object to achieve an intended interaction. We present EgoContact, a large-scale egocentric dataset for evaluating the generalizability and precision of learned manipulation priors through future contact-point prediction. EgoContact contains 22.5K manually verified interaction events, each with a pre-contact observation, semantic intent, and pixel-precise contact locations. We find that current methods often struggle to predict precise interaction contacts and sometimes fail to localize the target object in diverse, in-the-wild scenes, even when allowed multiple predictions. Furthermore, we demonstrate the usefulness of EgoContact's annotated interactions for robotic manipulation: simply using EgoContact as the memory bank of an existing affordance-transfer policy improves grasp success from 14.2% to 31.2% in simulation and from 16% to 58% on a real robot.

data.title: Reading-Level Verification of Kanji Words in Japanese Financial Speech Synthesis
data.abstract: Few-shot voice cloning makes it cheap to produce daily Japanese financial commentary with several synthetic speakers, but kanji words with more than one reading, such as the word for "market" (shijo vs. ichiba) or "overall trend" (taisei vs. oze), are still misread. A common quality gate transcribes each synthesized sentence with automatic speech recognition (ASR), converts both the input and the transcript to kana, and regenerates on mismatch. We show that this gate is unreliable in both directions: when the audio contains a misreading, the ASR language model frequently writes the expected kanji back, hiding the error, and when the audio is correct, ordinary recognition errors trigger needless regeneration. We propose a reading-level check that scores the expected reading and its confusable alternatives with a connectionist temporal classification (CTC) hiragana recognizer and flags a word when an alternative explains the audio better. On 540 utterances from three voice-cloned production voices covering 30 financial terms, with misreadings injected under controlled conditions, the transcript-based gate detected 78.9% of misreadings at a 44.4% false-alarm rate, whereas the proposed check detected 91.7% at 5.0% (AUC 0.990). On natural kanji input, it caught a front-end error that the transcript-based gate missed for one voice, and reduced regeneration requests from 38.9% to 6.1% of sentences.

data.title: Resonance and Transition-Channel Competition in Cavity-Assisted Floquet-State Stabilization
data.abstract: Static coupling to a dissipative cavity has been proposed as a route to autonomously stabilize Floquet eigenstates. The cavity provides an energy-selective relaxation channel: when its photon energy matches a quasienergy difference modulo drive quanta, it mediates transitions between Floquet states, followed by irreversible photon loss. Here, we show that at intermediate driving frequencies, this resonance condition alone is not sufficient for stabilization. Instead, the steady state is controlled by the interplay between resonance selection and the cavity-induced transition strengths between Floquet states, which can either cooperate or compete. This interplay leads to successful stabilization, mixed steady states despite resonance, and complete breakdown near Floquet-zone hybridization. We further show that the same mechanism extends to multilevel spin-S systems, providing a general framework for understanding when static dissipation can reliably stabilize driven quantum states.

data.title: LesionStudio: A Patient-Informed Platform for Task-Specific Optimization of Emission Tomography Reconstruction and Analysis
data.abstract: Purpose: For task-specific PET and SPECT reconstruction optimization, we developed LesionStudio, an open-source platform incorporating patient background heterogeneity, realistic lesion morphology and texture, and lesion-background interactions beyond conventional phantoms. Methods: LesionStudio, a Python framework built on PyTomography, inserts lesions into PET/SPECT data using modality-specific forward projection and stochastic background ablation. Clinical realism was evaluated by physician review of 30 inserted lesions in eight DLBCL patients from a 1,579-lesion FDG lymphoma library. Quantification and detectability were assessed in FDG PET using spherical and patient-derived lesions varying in size, LBR, and site, reconstructed with OSEM and BSREM. Results: Inserted lesions were visually indistinguishable from true disease (AUC = 0.49). OSEM improved the patient-derived quantification limit from ~3.7 mL at iteration 4 to ~2.0 mL at iteration 10, but with increased noise and edge artifacts. Weakly regularized BSREM (beta = 5) achieved a similar ~2.0 mL limit with stability, whereas stronger regularization increased under-recovery. Detectability was contrast-dependent: no lesions were detected at LBR 2:1, whereas detectable volume ranged from 0.70 to 3.63 mL at LBR 4:1 and decreased to 0.70 mL at LBR 6:1-8:1 for both OSEM and weakly regularized BSREM. Conclusion: Reconstruction settings can shift SUV metrics and detectability enough to affect interpretation, so no single protocol suits every task. OSEM required early stopping for detection and feature stability but more iterations for mean-SUV quantification, whereas weakly regularized BSREM matched both at one setting. LesionStudio (https://github.com/qurit/LesionStudio), with our public library of realistic lesions, provides a reproducible framework for task-specific optimization across radiopharmaceuticals and scanners.

data.title: ACAM-J-MARS: Multi-Atlas Riemannian Spectral Representations for Decoding Advanced Meditation States from fMRI
data.abstract: Inferring jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) states from fMRI data is challenging due to the spatially distributed nature of meditation-related effects, substantial inter-individual variability that can exceed within-subject state differences, and limited sample sizes. Conventional machine-learning approaches often formulate this problem as unimodal, Euclidean, atlas-based classification, thereby neglecting the non-Euclidean geometry of functional connectivity matrices and underrepresenting temporal information in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI); these limitations can lead to suboptimal classification performance. We propose ACAM-J-MARS (\textbf{M}ulti-\textbf{A}tlas \textbf{R}iemannian \textbf{S}pectral representation), which computes functional connectivity using multiple atlases, represents symmetric positive definite (SPD) connectivity matrices on a Riemannian manifold, projects them into a log-Euclidean tangent space, and augments connectivity-derived features with low-frequency BOLD spectral energy to better resolve subtle state differences under heterogeneous variability. Evaluated on 204 segments from 22 practitioners, ACAM-J-MARS improves performance across multiple backbone models, achieving a balanced accuracy of 0.757 for early versus late ACAM-J classification and 0.545 for three-class classification, corresponding to a 10.8-point absolute improvement over the strongest baseline. These findings suggest that the proposed representation improves the decoding of advanced meditative brain states and may enable downstream applications such as closed-loop neurofeedback and real-time psychophysiological brain-computer interfaces.

data.title: Cardinality of the K-cones below a non infinitely often $K$-trivial
data.abstract: Given a real $x\in 2^ω$, how many reals are there that are simpler (or equally simple) to describe than $x$. With ``simpler to describe" characterized by $K$-complexity of initial segments (hence we call such $y$ with $y\leq_K x$ a solution to $x$), if $x$ is infinitely often $K$-trivial (hence i.o. $K$-trivial), then a simple counting argument shows that the number of solutions to $x$ is countable. If $x$ is non i.o. $K$-trivial, then must it admit uncountably many solutions? Motivated by this question, we show that: (1) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ such that most of its solution is i.o. $K$-trivial. i.e., Only countably many solution to $x$ are non i.o. $K$-trivial. In particular, the cardinality of $K$-degree of $x$ is countable. (2) There is a minimal pair of K-degree (meaning their common solutions are all $K$-trivial) so that each of the pair is non i.o. $K$-trivial, generalizing a result of Csima and Montalbán (where the pair is not required to be non i.o. $K$-trivial but non $K$-trivial). (3) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ whose $Δ_K$ complexity grows arbitrarily slow (in a weak sense: $\inf_{m\geq n}Δ_K(x\upharpoonright m)\leq h(n)$ with $h$ a given unbounded and nondecreasing function) such that $x$ admits uncountably many solutions. (4) An ample excess lemma holds for non i.o. $K$-trivial. Namely: $$ \sum_n 2^{-(K(x\upharpoonright n)- \log_2 n)}<\infty. $$ for all non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$. Actually, this even holds for non i.o. $b$-$K$-trivial with $b$ only depends on the universal prefix free machine. The same argument also gives a constant complexity return phenomenon for $K$-trivial where this constant only depends on the universal prefix free machine.

data.title: Stable Electroweak Strings and Nambu Monopoles Nested at Inert-Higgs Interfaces
data.abstract: Electroweak $Z$ strings are generally unstable, and their Nambu-monopole endpoints lack topological protection in the bulk. Using degenerate inert and inert-like Higgs vacua as a solvable reference, we show that their interface supports both defects. The analytic interface carries a normalizable $SU(2)$ relative-orientation field. Its effective theory supports locally stable unit-flux $Z$ strings in a one-vacuum phase and fractional $Z$ strings in a two-vacuum phase. The fractional string carries an $S^2$ orientation field; a Nambu monopole is a second kink between symmetry-related, equal-tension $Z$ strings. We identify phases in which Nambu monopoles are confined or deconfined within the interface: in the confined phase, their $Z$ flux is concentrated into fractional strings, whereas in the deconfined phase, the monopole becomes a vortex within the interface and its $Z$ flux spreads radially through the interface. The electromagnetic magnetic field extends outside the interface in both phases. We determine analytic string profiles, effective-theory stability regions, and the unchanged electromagnetic magnetic charge across this confinement transition.

data.title: Martin-Löf randomness and rK-reducibility
data.abstract: Can random real carry arbitrary information. In terms of (Turing) computability, Kučera and Gács addressed this question in affirmative. i.e., Every real $x\in 2^ω$ is computable from some Martin-Löf random real. This result motivated quantitative versions of coding into random reals. i.e., How many bits of the random oracle are needed to compute the first $n$ bits of $x$. Barmpalias and Lewis-Pye obtained a coding that uses $n+O(\log n)$ many bits. Is it possible for the coding to use $n$ bits exactly? This is equivalent to say, if every real is $rK$-reducible to a Martin-Löf random real. In this paper, we prove that such a coding does not exist. i.e., There exists some real that is not $rK$-reducible to any Martin-Löf random real.

data.title: PRISM: Personalized Item Representations in User History
data.abstract: Sequential recommenders typically construct history inputs from item identifiers or content features using an embedding map shared across users. The same item therefore yields the same initial embedding representation, even when users have different relationships to the item. We propose personalized item representations in user history, where each item's embedding expresses its relationship to the user. Personalization becomes a property of the history inputs themselves, supplying richer evidence for later sequence modeling. We instantiate this idea with PRISM, which reuses upstream ranking computation to generate personalized item embeddings. An autoencoder jointly compresses all layer states from a user tower, a user--item tower, and same-request candidate mixing into one embedding per scored pair for downstream replay. Offline evaluation on Surface 1, a major recommendation surface at billion scale, reports an average downstream normalized entropy (NE) change of $-0.15\%$, compared with $-0.07\%$ for VISTA at similar history lengths. We further identify an empirical sequence-length scaling law: over history lengths of 26--240 events, NE gain follows a fitted power law with exponent 0.468, increasing from 0.06\% to 0.17\%. Therefore, personalized item representations in user history provide a new scaling dimension for improving recommendation quality.

data.title: Simplified dense model theorem for random discrete structures
data.abstract: Dense model theorems of Conlon and Gowers associate to each subset of a sparse random structure a dense set with approximately the same size and configuration counts after rescaling. This allows dense extremal results to be transferred to the random setting. Allen, Böttcher, Lada, and Mergoni Cecchelli recently generalised this approach and established a dense model theorem in an abstract hypergraph framework, with hypotheses that are readily verified in many applications. Both proofs use the separating hyperplane theorem to reduce the existence of dense models to an anti-correlation estimate. We give a simplified proof of a version of this theorem, inspired by the method of hypergraph containers. Our proof constructs dense models from small fingerprints, combining sampling with the Rödl-Ruciński deletion method.

data.title: Adaptive Bayesian Estimation of Conditional Densities Based on Orthogonal Polynomials
data.abstract: We study Bayesian estimation of conditional densities represented by normalized squares of orthogonal polynomial series. We specify the conditional density without modeling the marginal distribution of covariates. A prior on smoothness, the number of terms, and the coefficients gives adaptive posterior contraction at the minimax rate without a logarithmic factor when the normalized square-root representation of the true density is bounded away from zero and sufficiently smooth. For one outcome and $d_x$ covariates, the rate over classes with degree smoothness $s$ is $n^{-s/(2s+d_x+1)}$. The posterior predictive density attains the corresponding minimax squared Hellinger risk. For bounded nonnegative representations in Legendre and Chebyshev classes, we establish the minimax rate at every $s>0$. A prior that also permits a small mixture with the reference density adapts over these classes up to a logarithmic factor and retains the exact rate on the positive, sufficiently smooth subclass. Additional results concern identification, conditional distribution functions and quantiles, coefficient recovery and uniform convergence, independent Gaussian coefficient priors, and selection of polynomial terms.

data.title: Strong-deflection scaling in nearly symmetric thin-shell wormholes
data.abstract: The angular winding of a returning light ray can grow while the family of admissible impacts disappears. We characterize this competition near reflection symmetry in a static thin-shell wormhole joining Schwarzschild exteriors of slightly different masses. Exact shell-frame matching fixes the reflected interval, and a normal coordinate at each nondegenerate photon-sphere maximum gives a composite angular expansion with controlled error on compact interior channel intervals. The result remains valid when the throat distance divided by the mass contrast tends to zero, stays finite or diverges. For a throat distance proportional to a positive power of the fractional mass difference, the width exponent increases from one toward two and then saturates, while the logarithmic winding coefficient decreases from three toward two. Fixed-throat configurations retain their finite-distance amplitude and coefficient three. Reference-subtracted profiles connect the intermediate sector to finite and vanishing scaled throat positions. Independent quadratures test the scaling laws and resolve the slower convergence associated with changing scale ratios. The shrinking solid-angle aperture follows directly from the critical-impact gap. For an axial observer and a transparent test disk confined to the same exterior, the return-phase condition selects the admitted intersections; sampled near-symmetric configurations shift the first available global crossing to a later label. The closing aperture and increasing winding are therefore linked by the accessible radial extent, with disk access determined by the phase accumulated on the emitting segment.

data.title: Sharp derivative inequalities for maximal functions
data.abstract: We determine the optimal constant in the $L^p$-derivative inequality for the uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on the real line for every $1<p<\infty$. It is the unique number $γ_p\in [0,1]$ satisfying $(2p-1)γ_p+(p-1)γ_p^{(2p-1)/(p-1)}=p$. As $p$ goes from $1$ to $+\infty$, $γ_p$ decreases from $1$ to $\sqrt2-1$, and at the endpoints the limiting arguments recover the classical total-variation and Lipschitz inequalities, with the qualitative regularity ingredient at the $BV$ endpoint supplied by Aldaz and Pérez Lázaro.

data.title: Edited Endpoints as Partial Goals for Image-to-Video Generation
data.abstract: Edited endpoint images make the target of an image-to-video transition explicit and can improve transition completion, but also preserve context in the source image's layout. Full-frame endpoint conditioning turns this preserved context into requirements on the video's final state, potentially inducing temporal artifacts. We measure discontinuity with Hard-Cut (HC), late background reversal with Background Motion Reversal (BMR), and motion suppression with Dynamic Degree (DD). These artifacts appear across five video models spanning training-free and learned endpoint conditioning, in model-specific forms. We study Partial, a selective conditioning scheme that constrains only an edit-relevant region estimated from image-editor attention and leaves the remaining terminal content to the video model. Across three backbones on TC-Bench-I2V, Partial reduces temporal artifacts relative to full-frame conditioning, with no significant difference in Transition Completion Ratio (TCR); on Wan2.2-Turbo, uniformly weakening conditioning does not reproduce these reductions. A donor-context intervention keeps full-frame conditioning and replaces only the context outside the edit-relevant region with the final frame of a Partial video. It lowers HC and BMR on HunyuanVideo-1.5 and lowers BMR while restoring DD on Wan2.2-Turbo, with no significant difference in TCR, so constraint extent alone does not account for these artifacts. Together, these findings suggest that edited endpoints should serve as partial future goals, although edit relevance does not guarantee future validity. Code and data will be released at https://github.com/wannagetacat/Edited-Endpoints-I2V.

data.title: EmbodiExp: Compositional Experience Transfer for Embodied Agents
data.abstract: Experience can help embodied agents turn high-level plans into grounded actions, but transferring it across tasks remains challenging: previously effective strategies may be inapplicable to the current state or fail to produce their intended outcomes. We present EmbodiExp, a framework for constructing transferable experiences and composing them online during embodied task execution. Our key observation is that tasks often share subgoals whose completion can be assessed independently of overall task success. We therefore introduce an outcome-grounded subgoal experience that specifies a subgoal, applicability conditions, an adaptable policy, and a verifiable outcome. During execution, applicable experiences guide action generation, while verified outcomes can establish the conditions required by subsequent experiences, enabling online composition. Subgoal-level outcome attribution further enables failure utilization: failed trajectories can still contribute verified local successes and condition-specific guidance on actions to avoid. Experiments on multiple embodied benchmarks under a fold-based protocol with frozen experience banks demonstrate the effectiveness of EmbodiExp.

data.title: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves by a Kerr black hole
data.abstract: We simulate the gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) by a Kerr black hole using a $(1+1)$-dimensional time-domain mode-sum approach. To enable efficient explicit time evolution, we implement a localized hyperboloidal foliation combined with a static field redefinition, ensuring bounded characteristic speeds across an extended, uniform tortoise-coordinate grid. Incident GW initial data are constructed by projecting a plane-wave Weyl tensor onto the Kinnersley tetrad. Through local spin-dyad rotations and Wigner $D$-matrix transformations, our framework accommodates both idealized wave packets and realistic binary coalescence signals at arbitrary incidence and polarization angles. To accurately resolve the lensed waveforms, we evolve over $68,000$ coupled $(j,m)$ modes. Our results reveal that a Kerr black hole acts as a diffraction-limited thick lens, focusing GWs into a forward beam. For idealized wave packets, the primary prompt pulse exhibits a spin-independent transverse Gaussian profile, whereas the subsequent lensing coda is sensitive to the black hole's spin. For binary coalescence signals, strong-field lensing substantially modifies the post-merger ringdown. However, the lensed inspiral and merger phases in Kerr and Schwarzschild backgrounds are virtually identical, yielding waveform mismatches below $2.2\times10^{-5}$ across various inclinations and polarizations. These findings demonstrate that non-spinning Schwarzschild models provide an accurate and computationally economical surrogate to search for strong-field lensing signatures with current ground-based detectors.

data.title: Reasoning or Pattern Exploitation? Mechanistic Insights from RL-Trained Language Models
data.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly described as acquiring "reasoning" skills after reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. However, whether these gains reflect genuine reasoning or more superficial adaptations remains underexplored. In this work, we probe LLMs trained in a finite and exhaustively analyzable logical domain, namely Tic-Tac-Toe, and trace how internal representations evolve across reinforcement learning (RL) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Quantitatively, RL yields high accuracy and robustness across prompt variations, suggesting the emergence of game reasoning. Mechanistic interpretability, however, paints a different picture: features extracted with sparse autoencoders (SAEs) reveal that models primarily adapt to rely more heavily on information already explicit in the prompt, such as whose turn it is, game progression and board occupancy. In comparison, high-level concepts like board symmetries and strategic forks remain weakly represented, raising concerns that reasoning benchmarks overestimate model abilities. This suggests that RL-driven "reasoning" may conflate task-specific adaptations to input information with reasoning ability. We provide, for the first time: (i) a systematic interpretability pipeline tracing representation dynamics across RL training in small-scale LLMs; (ii) an extension of SAE-based feature discovery to hypothesis-driven testing in a finite logical domain; and (iii) an interpretability-based demonstration that RL post-training neither adds nor removes concept information but reorganizes which features dominate the representation, with causal interventions locating the decision downstream of it, in the late-layer state.

data.title: Multi-level Constrained Learning for Underwater Image Enhancement
data.abstract: Underwater image enhancement aims to correct color and recover detail degraded by wavelength-dependent attenuation, scattering, and noise. Paired-reference supervision constrains output similarity, but does not by itself specify the color mapping, the strength of local detail corrections, or consistency with the degraded observation. We propose MCL-UIE, a paired-supervised framework that addresses these requirements by constraining restoration operations and the training objective. Monotonic Chromatic Transform (MCT) restricts global color mapping in log-LMS space through positive diagonal entries and bounded cross-channel coefficients. Uncertainty-Gated Wavelet Reconstruction (UGWR) modulates high-frequency residuals with a learned confidence gate calibrated against normalized wavelet reconstruction errors. During training, Reference-Anchored Degradation Replay (RADR) renders the enhanced image and its paired reference using shared latent degradation proxies, encouraging both to reproduce the input. The three components share a restoration network that combines structured color correction, locally controlled detail recovery, and reference-anchored replay. MCL-UIE ranks first in thirteen of sixteen full-reference dataset-metric comparisons and produces competitive visual results on no-reference benchmarks. Objective ablations indicate that confidence calibration is most effective when combined with replay supervision. RADR is used only during training and adds no inference-time computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Wangtao-Bao/MCL-UIE.

data.title: Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics on nilpotent Lie groups and the quasicentroid condition
data.abstract: We study left-invariant Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics (cyclic-parallel Ricci tensor) on nilpotent Lie groups, focusing on the algebraic condition that the Ricci operator belongs to the quasicentroid $\operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}$. We review and develop the abstract structure theory of quasicentroids, and prove a Central Decomposition Theorem: any nilpotent Riemannian Lie algebra with $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ decomposes as a central product of ideals $\mathfrak{i}_j = E_{λ_j} \oplus \mathfrak{z}$, where $\mathfrak{z}$ is the center of $\mathfrak{n}$ and $E_{λ_j}$ are the negative Ricci eigenspaces. Endowed with the restricted metric, each factor $\mathfrak{i}_j$ is itself a Gray $\mathcal{A}$-space. Finally, we investigate when the general $\mathcal{A}$-metric condition reduces to $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$. We prove this equivalence unconditionally for two-step nilpotent algebras and whenever the metric admits a nice basis, and provide a general characterization via the vanishing of two trace identities.

data.title: Array-Agnostic High-Order Ambisonics Encoding via Diffusion Posterior Sampling
data.abstract: Ambisonics provides a device-independent representation of three-dimensional sound fields; however, extracting these coefficients from practical microphone array recordings remains strongly dependent on array geometry, acoustic transfer functions, and spatial sampling resolution. This pipeline is typically divided into two distinct tasks: encoding, which entails reconstructing the physically resolvable spatial components, and upscaling, which requires generating higher-order coefficients. Model-based approaches often fail on irregular arrays due to ill-conditioned transfer matrices, whereas conventional neural encoders remain strictly tied to the specific acquisition setup seen during training. Furthermore, existing upscaling methods usually assume ideal low-order inputs, ignoring device-specific array artifacts. We present ADEUPS, a unified framework that couples an array-independent Ambisonic diffusion prior with an explicit physical acquisition model during inference, enabling zero-shot encoding and upscaling across diverse array configurations. We train our prior using an order-masking strategy and perform inference via score blending, which we demonstrate to be crucial for solving the underlying inverse problem. Through extensive numerical evaluations across various array geometries, we show that ADEUPS consistently outperforms task- and array-specific baselines. Finally, we conduct subjective listening tests to confirm the perceptual effectiveness of our approach.

data.title: Berry curvature dipole circuit quantum electrodynamics
data.abstract: Quantum three-wave mixing is an important resource in superconducting quantum circuits. The traditional implementation uses Josephson junction arrays and is activated by magnetic flux. Here we introduce the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) quantum circuit element, which achieves quantum three-wave mixing without breaking time-reversal symmetry. This quantum three-wave mixing results from the BCD nonlinear Hall effect in noncentrosymmetric quantum materials taken to a dissipationless, quantum coherent few-photon regime. We show how nonlinear Hall materials can be integrated to superconducting microwave circuits to accomplish multiphoton vacuum Rabi splittings and dynamical stabilization of bosonic Schrödinger cat states. Such BCD circuit quantum electrodynamics are a concrete exemplar of a physical resource for quantum information processing enabled by nonlinear response in quantum materials.

data.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
data.abstract: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and Rényi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.

data.title: Read More, Reason Deeper: Latent Workspaces for Long-Sequence Recommendation
data.abstract: Long-sequence recommendation can improve along two axes: \emph{evidence scaling} exposes longer histories, while \emph{reasoning scaling} adds layers that interpret that evidence for a candidate. Existing models couple them: sequence encoders propagate every added event through depth, whereas one-shot selection prevents later layers from revisiting omitted evidence. We introduce the Latent Workspace Ranker (LWR), which keeps typed evidence in persistent banks and propagates a fixed-size candidate-local workspace. Each layer rereads the banks from its evolving workspace and archives compact post-interaction state, allowing history length and reasoning depth to grow independently. We compare four architectures across various history--depth configurations using evidence scaling at fixed depth, reasoning scaling at fixed 10K history, and their joint compute-efficient frontier. LWR leads all families at long histories, continues improving with reasoning compute, and converts additional training compute into quality gains at the fastest fitted rate on the joint frontier. At 10K history, it improves NE by 0.19% over HSTU while using 69.6% fewer forward GFLOP/request. It also outperforms existing baselines on two billion-scale ranking surfaces. These results show that separating addressable evidence from propagated state makes reading more and reasoning deeper independently controllable and jointly useful.

data.title: Provably Secure Diffusion Watermarking Against Removal Adversaries with Batched Detector Access
data.abstract: Recent latent-based watermarking methods can embed undetectable watermarks into AI-generated content. However, these approaches are vulnerable to removal attacks as their watermark detection boundaries are exposed, prompting the use of secret long-term transformations to hide these boundaries. We show that such defenses are insecure under a stronger threat model motivated by publicly reachable detectors: an adversary with batched detector access can reconstruct the transformations, permanently re-exposing the decision boundary. To address this, we propose a watermarking scheme based on a hybrid of long-term and one-time secret transformations, which prevents the reuse of structure across samples and keeps the long-term secret hidden. Besides undetectability, we show that this scheme is provably secure against removal adversaries with batched detector access, in the sense that no probabilistic polynomial-time adversary can achieve a non-negligible advantage over an adversary restricted to adding isotropic white-noise with a $\sqrt{2}\times$ larger perturbation budget, and we show this $\sqrt{2}$ factor to be tight. Evaluations on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL demonstrate the attack against the existing defense, and show that our scheme preserves generation quality and withstands common perturbations and targeted removal attacks.

data.title: NS-Leibniz bialgebras, the Yang--Baxter equation and relative Rota--Baxter operators
data.abstract: We introduce NS-Leibniz bialgebras and establish their equivalence with matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-Leibniz algebras. In the coboundary case, skew-symmetric solutions of the NS-Leibniz Yang--Baxter equation yield NS-Leibniz bialgebras and correspond to $\mathcal{O}$-operators for the dual regular representation. We study quasi-triangular and factorizable structures, and relate factorizable tensors to quadratic Rota--Baxter NS-Leibniz algebras of any fixed nonzero weight. We also construct compatible bialgebra structures from skew-adjoint Nijenhuis operators commuting with the Rota--Baxter operator.

data.title: Wearable Biosensors for Early Detection and Continuous Monitoring of Postpartum Depression: A Human-Centered Approach
data.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is the leading cause of maternal mortality in the United States. However, there are significant gaps in PPD screening, detection, and treatment. A main challenge stems from limitations in existing methods for early PPD diagnosis and subsequent monitoring and intervention. Mobile technology that incorporates interactive interfaces and continuous wearable biosensors holds major potential to augment clinical decision-making and enhance PPD care. A number of compelling research directions exist in effectively developing such systems, including user experience design, sensing accuracy during perinatal stages, clinical integration and interoperability, acceptance and adoption, and privacy and ethics. By focusing on wearable devices that center women and their experiences, this paper discusses such challenges and opportunities at the intersections of HCI, inclusive physiological computing, and women's health.

data.title: Local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor
data.abstract: We study the local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a self-consistent two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor. For a local $s$-wave tip that couples equally to the two orbitals, anomalous spectral contributions of opposite sign nearly cancel in the clean sample. Nonmagnetic impurities redistribute these contributions and can reverse the local coupling without a corresponding $π$ phase shift of the bond pair fields. Negative coupling appears at off-center sites at weaker impurity potentials than at the impurity site. The impurity-induced change is concentrated at lower quasiparticle energies, while states over a broader energy range contribute to the total clean and impurity couplings. In zero field, the coupling also changes sign as the tip gap is varied, and increasing the tunneling strength can reverse the $m=1$ sine component of the current without changing the sample state. At the chosen coherence-peak energy, increasing impurity strength mainly changes the relative intensities of existing quasiparticle-interference features. In a self-consistent two-vortex state, the Josephson response develops a spatially varying phase relative to the condensate. The response and condensate share the winding close to each core, while larger loops enclose additional winding of the Josephson response. The local Josephson sign and phase reflect the anomalous spectrum and the tip--sample coupling.

data.title: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks
data.abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verification, when needed. To understand how single agents manage these duties during long-horizon execution, we conduct a preliminary study. Our analysis shows that verification has the strongest association with task success, but often occurs late, leaving limited opportunities for correction. We also find that the proportion of duty-relevant information decreases as records from different duties accumulate in a shared context. These findings lead us to examine whether multi-agent systems (MAS) can address these problems by assigning duties to agents with separate contexts. Our analysis shows that this separation alone is insufficient. Agents can lose track of the overall goal and repeat prior investigations. They may also lack necessary background while receiving irrelevant information from others. To maintain goal awareness and coordinate collaboration as task needs change, we propose Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration (GAD). It uses a growing execution graph to organize subtasks and their dependencies. To keep agents focused on their goals, each context retains the original instruction and the assigned task's goal and acceptance conditions. To adapt collaboration and information sharing during execution, agents can divide tasks into subtasks and specify dependencies based on execution evidence. These dependencies guide when agents work and which results they receive. Verification and recovery check subtask results and full task completion against their goals, providing feedback for repair when checks fail.

data.title: Zero-Complement Extrapolation: Parameter Recovery and Classification in Severely Imbalanced Logistic Regression under Rank-Deficient Regimes
data.abstract: Parameter estimation and classification in binary logistic regression deteriorate severely when the number of minority class observations ($n_1$) is smaller than the feature dimension ($p$). Under such rank-deficient rarity ($n_1 < p$), maximum likelihood estimators suffer from quasi-complete separation, penalized likelihood methods exhibit severe intercept bias, and convex minority oversampling techniques such as SMOTE collapse into an $(n_1 - 1)$-dimensional affine subspace. In this paper, we propose a novel \textit{Self-Calibrated Zero-Complement} estimator that shifts the paradigm from minority interpolation to majority fringe extrapolation. Grounded in Stein's Lemma, we prove that the conditional expectation shift of the abundant majority class ($Y=0$) induced by logistic truncation uniquely identifies the true hyperplane normal $\boldsymbolβ$ after Mahalanobis whitening. We further establish that extrapolating synthetic minority instances outward from the high-quantile density fringe of the majority distribution along the conjugate direction preserves full-rank covariance regularity ($\mathrm{rank} = p$). To accommodate both semi-supervised environments (with an unlabeled background mean) and strictly supervised subsamples, we introduce a hybrid estimator incorporating the intrinsic third-moment skewness of the majority class alongside a location-shift-invariant zero-boundary intercept calibration. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and real-world benchmark applications (Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer and Banknote Authentication) under extreme rarity ($n_1 \in \{3, 5\}$) demonstrate that our approach prevents parameter divergence, recovers the oracle hyperplane with high fidelity, and substantially outperforms Firth's regression and SMOTE in F1-score and estimation stability.

data.title: Analyzing Condensation on Patterned Surfaces via Deep Learning
data.abstract: Dropwise condensation is key to power and water systems. State-of-the-art condensation surfaces are often inhomogeneous, either patterned by design or random defects. Inhomogeneous surface features dictate the rates of each stage of dropwise condensation-nucleation, growth, coalescence, and shedding. Characterizing these rates requires the precise detection of thousands of droplets. Yet, existing segmentation methods are unable to detect droplets on inhomogeneous surfaces. We developed TileSAM3, a universal droplet segmentation tool built on the Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3). Hierarchical tiling with per-tile inference followed by post-processing extended SAM3's detection cap and raised the effective resolution of small droplets.
