data.title: Curvature scaling and linear area response in charged black-hole interiors
data.abstract: We identify the mechanisms and range of validity of two scaling laws reported in charged black-hole interiors. In spherical evolutions with a neutral massless scalar, mass inflation produces a large internal mass $m$, followed by a plateau. Small scalar and electric corrections give $K\simeq48m^2/r^6$, where $r$ is the areal radius and $K$ the Kretschmann scalar. The local exponent is near six when the mass and relative curvature correction also vary slowly with radius. The exact bound $K\geq28q^4/(5r^8)$, with $q$ the charge, excludes a finite-coefficient $r^{-6}$ asymptote, while a large plateau mass delays electric corrections to $r\sim q^2/m$. For sufficiently large plateau mass, this classical regime can reach Planckian curvature before electric corrections become significant. At fixed coordinates and initial gauge, a linear response of $ρ=r^2$ to the initial scalar amplitude $A$ gives the half-power radius law near a simple zero. Where both mechanisms apply, $K/m^2\propto(A_*-A)^{-3}$, with $A_*$ the area zero. Full evolutions confirm the electric correction, support the half-power law at several observation times, and test the joint inverse-cube law.

data.title: $γ$-Valued Stein--Tomas Restriction for Schatten Classes
data.abstract: Let $Σ\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact $C^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent Schatten-valued Stein--Tomas range \[ R_Σ:L^p(\mathbb R^3;S^a)\longrightarrowγ(L^2(Σ),S^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] The core endpoint is $E_Σ:γ(L^2(Σ),S^4)\to L^4(\mathbb R^3;S^4)$. After squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the Hilbert--Schmidt class. A local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. We also show that Gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary Banach spaces. Applications include matrix Herglotz waves, a two-dimensional Schrödinger $L^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.

data.title: SDSS-V LVM: Mapping of plasma temperatures in the Lagoon Nebula reveals the origin of long-standing chemical abundance discrepancies
data.abstract: Knowing the chemical composition of interstellar gas is essential for understanding the chemical evolution of galaxies. Ionized nebulae provide key laboratories for this purpose, where chemical abundances are commonly derived from emission lines of heavy ions such as doubly ionized oxygen, $O^{++}$. Abundances can be inferred either from collisionally excited lines (CELs) or from recombination lines (RLs). However, for more than 80 years, the former have yielded systematically lower abundances than the latter. We map this ''abundance discrepancy'' using the first spatially resolved integral field unit (IFU) observations of $O^{++}$ RLs and CELs across a Milky Way H II region: the Lagoon Nebula (a.k.a. M8). Modeling the data using a plasma temperature perturbation model, we present unequivocal evidence that electron temperature ($T_e$) fluctuations drive the abundance discrepancy in M8. We find a tight correlation between the abundance discrepancy and the difference between $T_e$ derived from the classical CEL method and a hybrid RL/CEL approach. We identify this Te discrepancy as an observational proxy for the amplitude of the thermal fluctuations, providing a new, direct way to quantify their effect on nebular abundances. The correlation constrains the mean electron temperature of the gas. Adopting this mean temperature reconciles CEL and RL abundances, effectively eliminating the abundance discrepancy.

data.title: EPC-RawDC: Equivariant Physics Constrained 3D Diffusion with Raw Data Consistency for CBCT to CT Image Synthesis
data.abstract: Cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used for image guided and adaptive radiotherapy, but scatter, noise, reconstruction artifacts, and inaccurate Hounsfield units limit its quantitative use. Recent diffusion approaches for CBCT to CT synthesis remain largely image driven, with limited use of the underlying acquisition physics. We propose EPC-RawDC, a conditional 3D latent diffusion framework that combines volumetric generative modeling with two complementary constraints derived from the same scanner specific CBCT forward model. First, geometry equivariant projection constraint exploits the rotational equivariance of the CBCT forward operator by supervising the synthesized CT through correspondingly transformed reference projections. Second, raw data consistency uses noisy projection measurements of the individual acquisition as scan specific supervision during training. The framework was evaluated on two independent clinical cohorts with distinct scanner geometries and projection sources. For JUST, the physics constraints used measured clinical raw CBCT projections acquired with an Elekta system, whereas for SynthRAD2025 the projection data were simulated from the reference CT using a Varian geometry with Poisson photon statistics. EPC-RawDC achieved an SSIM of 0.97 in both cohorts and improved PSNR over DDPM by 2.66 dB on SynthRAD2025 and 2.10 dB on JUST, while reducing mean MAE by 20.3% and 19.0%, respectively. On SynthRAD2025, projection consistency and equivariant errors were reduced by 55.0% and 41.4% relative to DDPM. These results demonstrate that combining a volumetric diffusion prior with scanner geometry and scan specific projection measurements improves quantitative CBCT to CT synthesis across both simulated and measured projection domains. Code available after publication at https://github.com/ALZAHRAALTALIB/EPC-RawDC.

data.title: Smooth Threshold GARCH: Quasi Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Empirical Evidence
data.abstract: It is well established that the volatility of daily stock returns responds asymmetrically to news, as described by the news impact curve (NIC), which relates volatility to the previous return. Empirical studies suggest that (i) volatility reacts more strongly to negative returns than to positive returns of the same magnitude, (ii) the point of asymmetry, where the NIC attains its minimum, is positive, and (iii) returns above this point often do not increase volatility at all. The popular GJR and A-GARCH models each rule out one of these features. We study the Smooth Threshold GARCH (STGARCH) model, which nests both and allows for (i)-(iii) by combining an estimated threshold, the point of asymmetry, with separate slopes on either side of it. Although the likelihood is not twice continuously differentiable in the threshold, we show that the quasi maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and converges at the usual $\sqrt{n}$-rate, whether or not (iii) holds. If (iii) does not hold, the estimator is asymptotically normal, while if it holds, the slope above the threshold is zero, a value on the boundary of the parameter space, and the limit is non-Gaussian. In that case, the $t$-statistic for (iii) converges to the positive part of a standard normal variable, and the $t$-test of the GJR model remains valid. These results allow us to test the GJR and A-GARCH models, as well as (i)-(iii), within the STGARCH using standard normal critical values. For daily returns on five major stock indices, we reject the GJR model for all five and the A-GARCH model for three, suggesting that the STGARCH improves upon both. Volatility is lowest after returns 0.3-0.6 percentage points above their conditional mean, in line with (i) and (ii). Finally, the hypothesis in (iii) is rejected for two of the five indices.

data.title: Data-driven Regularization for Inverse Problems
data.abstract: In many applications, we are interested in studying an object of interest $x$. However, its properties are often not directly measurable. Instead, we only observe $y = F(x)$, where the (known) function $F$ is referred to as the forward mapping. To infer about $x$ from the observation $y$, we seek an (approximate) inverse mapping $x \approx F^{-1}(y)$. This process is known as solving the inverse problem. In practice, the inverse mapping $F^{-1}$ may be ill-defined or discontinuous, which forces us to choose a certain solution from many possible ones based on prior assumptions on $x$. Such assumptions about $x$ are typically incorporated into the inversion process through regularization. Therefore, the first part of this course focuses on the classical regularization theory of inverse problems. In the second part, we transition to algorithmic approaches for solving inverse problems. The foundation for this lies in the variational formulation of inverse problems, where reconstructions are obtained by minimizing specific functionals. Here, we will explore key optimization principles, discuss their practical implementation, and examine how they contribute to robust reconstructions. Today, classical methods are often modified to incorporate data-driven machine learning techniques, which improve the empirical performance. However, this often comes at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees. Such properties are critical, for example, in medical applications, where one wants to be confident that reconstructed abnormalities are of physical nature and not phantoms resulting from the method. For these reasons, we discuss a number of machine learning methods for inverse problems, such as unrolling techniques, learned regularizers and plug-and-play methods, and explore their performance guarantees.

data.title: Can the $\sim 5$ kpc starburst ring in MW create eROSITA bubbles?
data.abstract: eROSITA bubbles (eRBs) in our Galaxy are thought to be due to the energy injection by the central star-forming region or the central Super Massive Black Hole. Identifying the origin of these bubbles is crucial in constraining the origin of the Fermi Bubbles and the nature of the Galactic feedback. However, some recent opinions suggest that the eRBs may not even have been produced by any central source, but rather a result of a star-formation ring at $R\sim 5$ kpc. In this letter, we perform detailed hydrodynamic simulations to refute that claim and show that such a ring of star formation alone is not able to produce the symmetric eROSITA bubbles - one needs a compact energy injection from the Galactic Center to produce these bubbles. Our study, therefore, suggests that the eROSITA bubbles truly represent the nuclear outflow from our Galaxy.

data.title: Don't Risk It!: Trajectory-Conditioned Distributional Risk for LiDAR-Only Crowd Navigation
data.abstract: Efficient crowd navigation requires anticipating dynamic collision-free space without relying on fragile object tracking. We propose the Don't Risk It Planner (DRIP), an end-to-end LiDAR-only planning framework that couples occupancy forecasting with trajectory-conditioned clearance and uncertainty estimation. Operating directly on LiDAR-derived occupancy grid histories, DRIP predicts a distribution over minimum robot-obstacle clearance for candidate control sequences to evaluate collision risk. The model is trained using a risk cost that grounds predictive uncertainty directly in empirical collision outcomes rather than geometric regression alone. In closed-loop experiments with up to 45 pedestrians, DRIP achieves higher success rates with fewer collisions and reduced freezing behavior compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

data.title: Identifying Logical Operations from Syndrome Histories for qLDPC Codes
data.abstract: Syndrome histories are normally used to detect and correct errors in fault-tolerant quantum computation, but they can also reveal information about the logical operations executed during computation. We study logical-operation identification using syndrome histories alone or together with other classical measurement outcomes. We develop an exact inference method and a scalable approximation that account for unknown circuit faults and ideal measurement randomness. We evaluate automorphisms, logical Pauli measurements, T injections, and logical circuits combining these instructions on \([[18,4,2]]\) and \([[72,12,6]]\) bivariate bicycle (BB) codes under multiple noise models and error rates. A single logical instruction can be identified with over 94\% accuracy under circuit-level noise with error rates between \(10^ {-5} \) and \(10^{-3}\). We also achieve over 99\% accuracy for automorphism-based logical circuits and 78.32\% for logical circuits combining all three instructions. We further analyze identification ambiguities arising from insufficient or indistinguishable measurement information, fault timing, and approximation inference. Together, these results extend the role of syndromes beyond error decoding to identifying executed logical operations and circuits during fault-tolerant quantum computation. They also suggest that access to syndrome histories and related classical measurement outcomes may unintentionally reveal information about the executed computation.

data.title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
data.abstract: We report that allocating compute to synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) never outperforms pure natural-language training in our compute-matched experiments. This holds across four PPT curricula (k-Dyck, neural cellular automata (NCA), declarative reference corpora, and code) and three training regimes: data-constrained, data-unconstrained, and a high token-to-parameter-ratio regime (881M parameters trained on 50B tokens). When natural language is scarce, repeated epochs over a 100M-token corpus beat every synthetic curriculum on natural-language validation loss, with no consistent downstream accuracy advantage from PPT. We find that PPT gains reported in prior work are sensitive to the weight initialization scheme. In an NCA reproduction, we recover a 5.4% perplexity improvement from PPT under the original initialization scheme. An alternative scheme improves both methods, but the no-PPT baseline more, closing the gap between them. However, when PPT receives additional compute rather than a share of the natural-language budget, gains persist at small natural-language budgets even with improved initialization, but disappear by 1B tokens. Finally, models forget what they learn during PPT in subsequent natural-language training; interleaving the same data throughout training prevents forgetting, but does not significantly improve natural-language performance. Our results suggest limited benefits of synthetic pre-pretraining as a distinct training stage and motivate rethinking how such data are used in language model training.

data.title: KM3-230213A: The Highest-Energy Cosmic Neutrino
data.abstract: High-energy neutrinos provide a unique probe of the most extreme non-thermal processes in the Universe. The detection of the ultra-high-energy neutrino event KM3-230213A by the KM3NeT neutrino telescope, with an inferred parent-neutrino energy of O(10^17 eV), represents a major step forward in neutrino astronomy. In this review, we summarize the main properties of the event and discuss its interpretation within different astrophysical and cosmological scenarios, including active galactic nuclei, transient sources, and cosmogenic neutrinos, highlighting the role of multi-messenger constraints. Despite extensive follow-up observations, no unambiguous electromagnetic counterpart has been identified, and the event remains in tension with the absence of comparable detections in other experiments. This situation leaves open the possibility of more complex source scenarios or contributions from physics beyond the Standard Model. We also discuss the implications for the ultra-high-energy neutrino landscape and the prospects for future observations with next-generation detectors. KM3-230213A provides a unique opportunity to probe particle acceleration and neutrino production at energies far beyond the reach of terrestrial experiments.

data.title: Model Theory of Johnson Graphs
data.abstract: A \emph{Johnson graph} $J(n,k)$ is a graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of an underlying set of size $n$ where two vertices are adjacent if they intersect in a subset of size $k-1$. We extend the definition to allow infinite parameters and we study a natural limit theory $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ of Johnson graphs. We show that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is complete and we give an axiomatisation of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, from which we obtain a complete description of the models of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$. We use this to show tameness properties of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, namely that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is $ω$-stable of Morley rank $ω$, but not monadically dependent. In particular it follows that the class of all finite Johnson graphs is stable, and therefore dependent but not monadically dependent.

data.title: One Vector or Many? Clustered Optimal-Transport Steering under Quantization
data.abstract: Activation steering changes what a language model generates by editing its hidden states at inference time. Its most common form adds one vector, the difference of class means (DiM), to every hidden state. CHaRS (concept heterogeneity-aware representation steering) uses optimal transport instead: an entropic plan pairs the clusters of the two classes, and each hidden state moves along a mixture of the cluster displacements, weighted toward its nearest clusters. We study this family of clustered optimal-transport maps for toxicity mitigation in Gemma-2-2B and Granite-3.1-2B, and ask what the plan adds to DiM and whether that survives INT8 and NF4 quantization. We prove an identity: whatever the plan, the displacements averaged with the cluster sizes as weights equal DiM, so a clustered map can differ from DiM only for tokens whose routing weights depart from the cluster sizes. In the CHaRS protocol they stay close, and CHaRS is statistically equivalent to Mean-AcT, which adds DiM at every layer, in all eight pre-specified equivalence tests. A variant fitted on individual tokens, which routes each token mainly to its nearest clusters, leaves 37-39% less toxicity than DiM on Gemma and 51-61% less on Granite at steering strength 3 (toxic-bert), where DiM already removes 76-85% of it. Two other toxicity classifiers confirm the gain on Granite, but on Gemma only one does. At equal strength the variant has somewhat higher perplexity, but at matched toxicity it is slightly more fluent than DiM. Yet a nearly constant map from the same clusters also leaves about 30% less toxicity, so the role of treating tokens differently remains open. Under INT8 and NF4 the variant still leaves less toxicity than DiM, and transferring it from full precision to the NF4 model instead of refitting it adds no significant toxicity after correction for multiple tests.

data.title: Reinforcement Learning Under Runtime Confounding: Policy Learning and Off-Policy Evaluation
data.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to train robust, adaptable systems across healthcare, e-commerce, and robotics. In these settings, legal, ethical, or logistical concerns may preclude certain key variables that drive decisions from being collected during deployment time. This gives rise to a setting known as runtime confounding: the logged data hold full observability, but deployment time lacks knowledge of certain variables, known as runtime confounders. Unlike single timepoint and non-adaptive settings, runtime confounding under reinforcement learning has the potential to propagate over time, as earlier decisions affect future states, observations, and action assignments, leading to biased learning. We address these problems with three contributions: we (1) develop policy learning algorithms under runtime-confounding, (2) develop semi-parametric efficient off-policy estimation procedures, and (3) provide diagnostics for understanding the price of runtime confounding.

data.title: Invariant probability measures on holomorphic functions on the unit disk
data.abstract: We study probability measures on the space of holomorphic functions on the unit disk that are invariant under pre-composition by conformal automorphisms and give no mass to constant functions. We determine the slowest possible growth of functions supported by such measures. Let $M_f(R)$ denote the maximum modulus of $f$ on the hyperbolic ball of radius $R$ centered at the origin. We show that given a non-decreasing function $G:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$, there exists an $\textrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$-invariant probability measure $μ$ on $\textrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{C}) \setminus \{\textrm{constant functions} \}$ such that $\log^+ M_f(R)=O_f(G(R))$ for $μ$ almost every $f$ if and only if $\int_1^\infty (R/G(R)) \, dR <\infty$. For the lower bound, we use a mass transport argument to show that almost every trajectory of the gradient flow of $\log |f|$ has finite energy. To establish sharpness, we construct holomorphic functions of slow growth on infinite Riemann surfaces.

data.title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
data.abstract: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

data.title: Influence of pairing and correlations on transport properties in three-terminal superconducting nanostructure
data.abstract: We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlation effects, inspecting their influence on the conductance and thermopower. Our calculations predict negative values of the nonlocal conductance and reversal of the Seebeck coefficient when the quantum dot ground state is represented by the BCS-type singlet configuration. These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.

data.title: Dynamical mean-field theory for associative memory with block-correlated patterns
data.abstract: In associative memories storing correlated patterns, retrieval of individual memories can compete with symmetric mixed states. A dynamical description is needed to determine how the initial state selects between these outcomes. We extend the generating-functional dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for independent patterns to independent blocks of correlated binary patterns of fixed finite size. The resulting effective single-neuron process has a self-consistent cross-talk noise covariance and self-feedback coefficients that depend on the block-covariance eigenvalues. For hierarchically correlated patterns with nonmonotonic transfer, increasing the loading can permit retrieval from an imperfect initial state before further loading prevents it. DMFT reproduces the retrieval trajectories and basin geometry found in direct simulations. Near the lower boundary of this re-entrant region, direct networks reveal stationary saddles separating coexisting mixed and target-retrieval states. Parameter sensitivities of DMFT trajectories predict nearby shifts of this boundary. At the tested upper boundary, retrieval remains accessible from initial states with larger target overlap, indicating a change in basin access. Under fixed-point convergence assumptions, the theory recovers the equations of generalized self-consistent signal-to-noise analysis.

data.title: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models
data.abstract: Understanding the internal routing of visual concepts is crucial for the safe and controllable adaptation of generative models. While concept localization has been widely studied in diffusion models, the emerging paradigm of next-scale visual autoregressive models remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce LoCo, the first model-agnostic framework to localize where and when specific concepts emerge within autoregressive models. Driven by the native coarse-to-fine nature of next-scale generation, our method precisely maps conceptual knowledge across three distinct dimensions: Layer, Scale, and Position. To systematically localize and evaluate concept routing without context bias, we propose LoCoBench, a comprehensive dataset spanning 10 diverse categories. Extensive probing on image and video autoregressive models like Infinity, HunyuanImage-3.0, and InfinityStar shows that the localized positions are both interpretable and causally related to concept emergence. Building on these insights, we apply our localization method to three key applications: concept erasure, model personalization, and adversarial concept injection. Experiments demonstrate that our targeted intervention achieves state-of-the-art performance, substantially reducing computational overhead while preserving benign utility. Overall, our findings offer insights into how conceptual knowledge is routed during autoregressive generation, introducing a practical pathway for more interpretable, efficient, and secure adaptation.

data.title: Higher-order jet and its application to the Novikov conjecture
data.abstract: In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the deffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher order $μ$-discreteness for subgroup $Γ< {\rm Diff}(M)$. As applications, we show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher order $μ$-discreteness.

data.title: Extracting non-Gaussian information of line-intensity maps with weighted skew spectra
data.abstract: The bispectrum of line-intensity maps carries cosmological and astrophysical information beyond the power spectrum, but its large data vector hampers the analysis of survey data. Skew spectra address this by compressing the bispectrum into a handful of power-spectrum-like observables, cross-spectra of the observed field with filtered squares of it. We present the first application of optimally weighted skew spectra to line-intensity mapping of galaxy-hosted emission, where all clustering and shot-noise terms are luminosity weighted and the mean intensity is unknown. We perform idealized real-space Fisher forecasts for a SPHEREx-like survey of H$α$ emission at $0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 4.6$, in its deep fields and in a noisier all-sky configuration. First, the compression carries over to intensity maps: on perturbative scales and for a fixed redshift evolution of the emitters, four skew spectra, one of them matched to the shot noise, recover the bispectrum constraints on biases, shot noise and cosmological parameters to within a few percent. Second, the joint analysis of the power spectrum and the skew spectra measures the ratios of the second-order biases to the linear bias in each redshift bin. Within a bin the biases are degenerate with the unknown mean intensity, but their ratios are not, so their redshift evolution is measured without a model for the emitters. For emission that depends on halo mass alone, these ratios are determined by luminosity-weighted averages of the halo biases, so their evolution can test the halo-emission connection, including dependence on assembly history or environment. The bias ratios are not accessible to the tree-level real-space power spectrum alone. At $z \lesssim 3$ an all-sky SPHEREx-like configuration can detect departures of order $0.1$ in the bias ratios at $3σ$, while deeper fields perform better in the highest-redshift bins.

data.title: At the EDGES of MADness: phenomenology of relic millicharged atomic dark matter
data.abstract: Millicharged dark matter lives in a corner of parameter space that has been considerably shrinking over the past decades, due to constraints from cosmology, astrophysical systems, and ground-based experiments. A particularly interesting probe is the 21-cm absorption signal at Cosmic Dawn, which attracted interest in light of the EDGES claim: the reported excess absorption can be explained by millicharged dark matter with a fractional electric charge of~$10^{-6} \lesssim ε\lesssim 10^{-4}$, but it must be a subpercent of the total dark matter abundance to remain consistent with the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We show that very low fractions of millicharged dark matter naturally arise from atomic dark matter: a dark sector model that replicates the physics of standard atomic hydrogen. Dark ions undergo the process of dark recombination, leaving a relic ionized component that, in the presence of kinetic mixing, is naturally millicharged. We modify the cosmological Boltzmann solver CLASS to incorporate this scenario, and we investigate the parameter space of millicharged atomic dark matter (MAD) that is allowed by CMB, large-scale structure, and supernovae data. We find there are cosmologically viable regions of MAD parameter space that are consistent with laboratory and astrophysical bounds and also overlap with the EDGES-defined window. Although the EDGES result is likely not a Cosmic Dawn signal, MAD leaves distinctive cosmological signatures, accessible to upcoming 21-cm observations.

data.title: The $K T_{cc}(3875)$ Interaction: Bound State, Scattering Observables and Correlation Function
data.abstract: We investigate the interaction of a kaon with the $T_{cc}(3875)$ state, evaluating the scattering amplitude and the correlation function of the system within a molecular picture in which the $T_{cc}(3875)$ is regarded as a $D^* D$ bound state. Since the $KD^*$ and $KD$ interactions dynamically generate the $D_{s1}(2460)$ and $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ resonances, respectively, both of which are significantly bound with respect to their corresponding particle thresholds, the $KT_{cc}(3875)$ interaction is found to be strongly attractive, leading to the formation of two bound states with binding energies of about 63 MeV and 51 MeV, respectively, with respect to the $KT_{cc}(3875)$ threshold. We also determine the scattering observables at threshold, including the scattering length and effective range, and calculate the correlation function. The latter exhibits features similar to those found in previous studies of the scattering of an external particle off a dynamically generated resonance of molecular nature.

data.title: Quantum Metric Scaling and Its Exceptions in Classical Flat Bands
data.abstract: The quantum metric length has been proposed as the localization length scale in one-dimensional flat bands. Here, we study this quantum metric scaling and the exceptions to it in a classical flat band formed by a locally resonant mass--spring system. We find that the localization length follows the quantum metric length near the flat band but departs from this proportionality at the exact flat-band frequency. Selective mass disorder also produces divergent localization lengths or arbitrarily short tails near the flat-band frequency without changing the clean metric. These exceptions show that disorder can select localization scales beyond those predicted by the quantum metric alone.

data.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
data.abstract: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

data.title: BRACHIO: Broad Representations Across Centres for Head-and-neck Imaging Oncology (HECKTOR 2026)
data.abstract: The HECKTOR 2026 challenge benchmarks machine learning for head and neck cancer, where teams delineate primary and nodal tumour volumes, perform TN staging, and predict recurrence-free survival (RFS). This report describes the submissions for the HECKTOR challenge of team nucli. As the three tasks span both dense and global information from multicentric PET/CT scans, we utilise self-supervised pre-trained encoders, training a 2D DINOv2 encoder (PET-DINOv2-MIPs) on HECKTOR 2026's PET scans. Our final test submission ensembles a DynUNet trained from scratch with a SwinUNETR whose Swin trunk was initialised from a SimMIM-pre-trained checkpoint for segmentation, reaching a mean Dice of 0.5409. For TN staging, GTVp/GTVn geometric features from the segmentation masks are fit to stage probabilities by logistic regression (LR) and fused with PET-DINOv2-MIPs deep features (PCA + LR) via a second-level LR, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.3962 (T-stage) and 0.6432 (N-stage). For the RFS prognosis task, we fine-tune the last two blocks of the PET-DINOv2-MIPs ViT-S encoder jointly with an MLP head under a CoxPH loss, concatenating clinical covariates with the imaging features, reaching a test Harrell's C-index of 0.6577 and a weighted challenge score of 0.5802. The prognosis result is comparable to the best entry of the previous edition and consistent with our internal cross-validation, while our segmentation result is well below it and limits the staging results that depend on it.

data.title: Photon Rings and Mass-Independent Observables of a Five-Dimensional Charged AdS Black Hole
data.abstract: We investigate the optical properties of a five-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black hole. Using the null geodesic equations, we determine the event horizon and photon sphere radii and the critical impact parameter, showing that all decrease with increasing charge, while the photon sphere radius remains independent of the AdS radius. To avoid dependence on the mass scale and the observer-dependent apparent size of the shadow in an AdS spacetime, we introduce two mass-independent geometric observables: the subring exponent $γ$ and the ratio of the critical impact parameter to that of the direct image of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We derive $γ$ in closed form and show that it is independent of the AdS radius and satisfies $2π/\sqrt{3}<γ\leqπ\sqrt{2}$, above the values for four-dimensional Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström black holes. Using a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) forecast based on noiseless mock data with illustrative fractional uncertainties of $5\%$, we find that the dimensionless AdS radius can be constrained with a relative uncertainty of $16$--$19\%$, whereas the charge can be distinguished from zero only for the near-extremal fiducial model considered. Under these assumptions, the subring exponent provides a Gaussian separation of $3.4$--$5.9σ$ from the four-dimensional Schwarzschild black hole.

data.title: Graphical Modeling from Marginal Information via Optimal Transport
data.abstract: A graphical model represents multivariate interactions through conditional independence, but requires jointly observed samples to be fitted to data. When individuals cannot be tracked and only marginal observations are available, as with destructive measurements leading to cross-sectional data, the problem of graphical modeling is confounded with that of assembling a joint law. We show how simultaneous graphical modeling and joint law assembly can be realized via a multi-marginal optimal transport problem with graphical cost. Focusing on Gaussian marginals, we generate a joint law satisfying the Markov properties prescribed by a given graph. Within the class of joint distributions respecting the graph and marginals constraints, our construction selects a member by making the interactions set by the graph as strong as possible under a dependence budget measured by relative entropy. In the empirical setting, where only estimates of the marginals are available, we examine the stability of the problem under perturbations of both the marginals and of the graph weights. The resulting error splits into an estimation term, vanishing with the sample size, and a specification term, which quantifies the cost of a misspecified graph. Finally, we illustrate these findings by numerical experiments.

data.title: Agentic process evidence
data.abstract: The way software gets built is changing dramatically. AI agents now create pull requests, select dependencies, refactor codebases, interpret test failures, and execute infrastructure changes across the entire Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). AI agents are autonomous team members, but unlike human engineers, they are ephemeral - their reasoning, decisions, and tool calls vanish the moment the session ends. Modern Security incidents involving intent mismatch or injection are becoming increasingly common - forcing us to address AI Agents as an insider threat. No widely adopted standard yet enables agentic provenance and governance and its obvious that you can't hold an ephemeral process accountable. The git log was designed for human commits. It shows what changed. It does not show what an AI agent did, which model it used, which tools it called, or whether anyone was accountable for the outcome. Every governance framework, every audit trail, every compliance control in the SDLC was built around one assumption: a human made the decision. That assumption no longer holds. This shift introduces 3 main procedural problems (not addressing scale) - Supply-chain vector - The agentic coder is software, so it is a supply-chain security risk. Policy guardrails - How to ensure the agentic coder is compliant with the policies of the organization. Task-alignment - How to align the agentic coder on its tasks and goals. We introduce Agentic Process Evidence (APE), a signed, tamper-evident, machine-readable attestation of agentic processes, linking the sessions to their outcome (process-aware logging). APE enables Policy-as-Code control over the agentic processes, allowing for human in the loop only when it's needed. We support the in-toto style attestation framework, and the protocol is aligned with the relevant regulations

data.title: Dissipative controller as a hidden source of errors in quantum gates
data.abstract: Quantum systems are typically controlled by classical devices that necessarily dissipate energy to the surrounding environment. By the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, this implies noise in the control field produced. We investigate the relationship between the resulting errors and the entropy produced by the macroscopic controller, working in the context of a concrete minimal model. In the most experimentally relevant regime of fast control and high fidelity, we find a tradeoff between dissipation and control errors. These findings are exemplified by perturbative calculations of the gate fidelity for simple gate implementations and of the fidelity of state transfer via shortcuts to adiabaticity in the Landau-Zener model. Our results quantitatively demonstrate that suppressing errors in quantum control typically comes at the cost of macroscopic dissipation, which is needed to tame fluctuations in the classical controller.

data.title: Uncertainty-aware Coarse-to-Fine Main Pancreatic Duct Segmentation for Width Measurement in 3D MRCP
data.abstract: Assessment of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) from volumetric magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) scans is an essential task for ductal dilatation diagnosis and pancreatic cancer analysis. However, manual assessment is affected by reader variability in which automated analysis may assist. Nevertheless, fully automated and uncertainty-aware MPD analysis from volumetric MRCP remains underexplored area of research. In this study, we propose an automatic and uncertainty-aware deep learning-based pipeline for MPD segmentation and maximum-width analysis from MRCP scans. A coarse localisation model first identifies the ductal region-of-interest, followed by a fine model that segments the MPD within the region. The dataset consists of 256 MPD-segmented MRCP scans from 69 patients. A randomly selected holdout test subset of 14 patients with 55 MRCP volumes was used for evaluation. We employed a five-model cross-validation ensemble for improved performance and uncertainty estimation. The best MPD segmentation performance was 0.634 DSC, 0.744 precision, and 0.593 recall. The mean absolute error for maximum MPD width prediction was 0.355~mm and dilated MPD ($\geq 5$~mm) was detected with 75.0\% sensitivity and 74.4\% specificity. These novel results suggest that automated MPD segmentation can be used to aid MRCP-based duct measurements.

data.title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
data.abstract: We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.

data.title: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
data.abstract: Robot foundation models increasingly rely on flow-based action generation for general-purpose manipulation, yet the generated actions are not guaranteed to satisfy physical constraints such as joint limits and collision avoidance. This problem is especially challenging when the feasible set cannot be described analytically and is accessible only through black-box feasibility oracles. We study this practical oracle-only setting and propose an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard for safe flow-matching robot policies. The safeguard uses binary feasibility queries to correct unsafe updates in the forward pass, while extracting local boundary information to provide constraint-aware learning signals in the backward pass. Combined with discrete-time flow matching, the same safeguard is used during training and inference, enabling forward--backward aligned policy learning without explicit or differentiable constraint models. Experiments on obstacle-aware robotic manipulation demonstrate 100% constraint satisfaction while preserving task performance.

data.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
data.abstract: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

data.title: Disentangling Spin-induced Precession vs. Eccentricity in GW190521 and GW231123
data.abstract: We use the more than 2000 full numerical-relativity simulations included in the fifth release of the RIT binary-black-hole waveform catalog to perform Bayesian parameter estimation, via the rapid iterative fitting algorithm (RIFT), for the gravitational-wave events GW190521 and GW231123. We revisit GW190521, which has previously been identified as potentially possessing large eccentricity upon entering the detector band at $20~\mathrm{Hz}$, and confirm this finding: the highest likelihood is obtained from waveforms that are simultaneously eccentric and spin-precessing, yielding $e_{20} =0.207_{-0.147}^{+0.192}$ and $χ_{1,\perp}=0.717_{-0.406}^{+0.194}$. Applying the same simulation pool to GW231123, we likewise find a preference for spin precession where at 20 Hz $χ_{1,\perp}=0.678_{-0.462}^{+0.218}$, but in this case with negligible eccentricity at both $10~\mathrm{Hz}$ and $20~\mathrm{Hz}$, with $e_{10}=0.097_{-0.073}^{+0.124}$ and $e_{20}=0.056_{-0.045}^{+0.059}$. For comparison, both events are also analyzed using exclusively non-precessing (eccentric and quasi-circular) simulations, which yield lower likelihoods in each case. These results indicate that our approach is capable of discriminating between the effects of eccentricity and spin precession in current gravitational-wave signals. The singled out top peak likelihood NR simulations give estimates of the recoil velocities of the merged final holes of 3965km/s for GW190521, and of 2059km/s for GW231123.

data.title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
data.abstract: Military installation energy readiness depends on having sufficient resources to sustain mission-critical loads throughout a prolonged utility outage. This paper develops a method to help operators manage energy resources during normal grid-connected operation while preserving islanded readiness. A robust viability kernel identifies combinations of battery energy, fuel, and load-shifting capability sufficient to sustain critical load under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation. A probability bound translates stochastic generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count selected to meet a specified availability requirement at islanding. Case studies for a fourteen-day islanding requirement at 0.999 islanding-entry availability show that advance warning of an outage can be used to prepare resources to meet a higher readiness requirement before islanding begins. The case studies further demonstrate that economic-only operation and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy can fail to sustain critical load for the required duration, whereas enforcing the resource-dependent requirement preserves readiness at a modest increase in modeled grid-connected operating cost. These results demonstrate how active resource management can preserve long-duration energy readiness. The framework also helps commanders understand how readiness changes with operating conditions, even when the available resources remain the same.

data.title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
data.abstract: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.

data.title: An HDG-type discretization of 1D embedded blood flow in complex networks with Riemann-coupled junctions
data.abstract: We present a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for one-dimensional blood flow in arterial networks with Windkessel boundary conditions. The scheme uses a Harten--Lax--van Leer (HLL) numerical flux and implicit time integration. After spatial discretization, the complete network---including cell states, hybrid traces, junction conditions, and dynamic $\mathrm{RCR}$ terminal pressures---is written as a residual index-one differential--algebraic equation (DAE) and integrated with variable-step, variable-order backward differentiation formulas. The implicit formulation removes the CFL stability restriction of explicit schemes and allows variable-order, variable-step solvers. The resulting single global residual and Jacobian for the network and its terminal dynamics also provide a natural interface for monolithic coupling with external nonlinear models. We establish local solvability and a semi-discrete energy balance, and show numerically optimal convergence rates for both solution variables in the $L^2$ norm and the broken $H^1$ seminorm. The solver is validated against established benchmarks, including an aortic bifurcation and a $37$-artery network, and is further applied to a cerebral arterial network. Mass conservation is observed in a synthetically generated anatomical liver network of $8\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels, and strong-scaling studies are performed on synthetic networks of $50\,\mathrm{k}$ and $100\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels.

data.title: The coupled spread of information and potential-driven motion in evacuating agent populations
data.abstract: Whether a population evacuates safely depends on two coupled processes: how a warning spreads through it, and how that information moves people. We model this coupling with an agent-based framework, in which each agent's information state--susceptible, exposed, informed or reverted--gates its motion. Only informed agents respond to a global background potential encoding hazards and safe zones, while all agents interact locally through a Lennard-Jones potential. The total potential experienced by an agent drives an Ito stochastic differential equation. Tests show that landscapes with potential minima leave far fewer agents never exposed than in a flat, uniform potential control landscape, as informed agents driven toward the minima sweep past susceptible neighbors. In our tests, conduit routes raise the fraction of agents in the safe-zone minima, but leave greater numbers of agents never exposed, when compared to an unguided evacuation. This is attributed to conduits shortening trips at the cost of informed agents having fewer encounters with susceptible neighbors who could receive their information. Independently, the effective information transmission rate estimated from these encounters falls roughly sixty-fold below its well-mixed value within the first time unit, because state transitions create spatial mechanisms of net transmission suppression that mean-field closure does not capture.

data.title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
data.abstract: Let $π_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\simλn/\log n$, it converges to $2Φ(\sqrt{λ/π})-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.

data.title: Model-Agnostic Search for New Physics in the Presence of Imperfect Background by Smearing the Data
data.abstract: In the search for new particles in high-energy physics, it is necessary to first define the signal region (SR) enriched in signal events, and then compare events in this region with the expected background distribution. While most existing search methods rely on prior domain knowledge of either the signal or the background, there has been less effort to relax both assumptions simultaneously, as methods that weaken one assumption typically rely on strong knowledge of the other. We propose Model-Agnostic Search with Smearing and Imperfect Background (MASSIB), a method that addresses this challenge by learning the density ratio of events relative to a misspecified background distribution using modern tools from machine learning, and defining the SR as the region with high density ratio. Recognizing that a naive application of this idea introduces significant bias in background estimation when interpolating from the control region to the SR, MASSIB mitigates this issue by introducing a "smeared" density ratio, which can be learned efficiently through data-level manipulation and used to define an SR that allows for accurate background estimation. By applying it to various types of simulated Large Hadron Collider (LHC) events with realistic background mismodeling, we demonstrate that MASSIB identifies a data-driven SR that achieves high signal concentration consistently across different types of signals while avoiding bias in background estimation. The method does this without making strong assumptions about either the signal or background distribution. We then show that this robustness extends to the validity and strong statistical power of the resulting hypothesis tests for signal detection, demonstrating the potential of this approach for future model-agnostic searches at the LHC.

data.title: Magnetotransport experiments on side-contacted topological insulator three-terminal Josephson junctions
data.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions have recently attracted substantial attention. The ability to study Andreev bound states in a multi-phase parameter space opens up exciting avenues for generating topologically non-trivial phases in superconducting devices. A particularly interesting case is the trijunction based on a topological insulator (TI), which is predicted to host Majorana zero modes for suitable phase configurations (Fu and Kane, PRL 2008). Here we turn to the platform of the side-contacted TI trijunction and present experimental evidence for a multiterminal Josephson effect. We study the transport properties and find typical features of a two-dimensional critical current contour (CCC) as well as bias regimes in which only a single junction remains dissipationless. We pay particular attention to these features and study the effects of magnetic fields on single junctions within the trijunction, where, depending on the field direction, the supercurrents show Fraunhofer patterns, SQUID oscillations, or a monotonic decay. We find good agreement with semiclassical simulations for a single TI junction that take into account the top and bottom surface states. We observe pronounced non-convex shape deformations of the CCC under perpendicular magnetic fields that reflect the flux buildup in the loop formed by our trijunctions and provide a simple model sufficient to explain the observed effect. Our results provide the foundations for future studies of Majorana zero modes on this platform.

data.title: Multi-excited random walks on general trees
data.abstract: We study multi-excited random walks on infinite locally finite trees. The model is described by placing a stack of ``cookies'' at each vertex, with one cookie consumed on each successive visit. As long as cookies remain, the walk is in an excited regime and makes nearest-neighbour steps according to a prescribed sequence of biases. Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.

data.title: Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network for Medical Image Segmentation
data.abstract: Accurate multi-organ segmentation in computed tomography (CT) is essential for computer-aided diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. However, substantial variations in organ shape and size, together with low tissue contrast and ambiguous boundaries, complicate the modeling of heterogeneous anatomical structures. To address these challenges, we propose a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network (MCDNet), which integrates adaptive local structural enhancement with channel-decoupled long-range modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled State-Space (MCSS) block that divides feature channels into separate processing groups, allowing differentiated structural representations to be learned within an efficient state-space framework. Within each group, a Morphology-Aware Enhancement Module (MAEM) combines deformable convolutions with channel attention to adapt local feature extraction to anatomical shape variations. Group-wise state-space modeling then captures long-range spatial dependencies, and channel gating adaptively integrates the resulting features. Experiments on the Synapse abdominal CT dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of MCDNet, achieving an average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 81.61% for multi-organ segmentation.

data.title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
data.abstract: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.

data.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
data.abstract: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

data.title: Neural Blind Deconvolution for Image Scanning Microscopy
data.abstract: Image scanning microscopy (ISM) acquires one scanned image per detector element, which are then fused into a single image by multi-image deconvolution to obtain a super-resolved image. Its accuracy, however, depends on point spread function (PSF) models that sample- and system-induced aberrations often invalidate. Since differences between the scanned images encode aberration information, we propose a training-free blind Deep Image Prior (DIP) framework that jointly estimates the specimen and the detector-dependent PSFs. The PSFs are parametrised through the detector geometry and shared excitation and emission PSFs, reducing the unknowns while preserving the physical ISM model, and a Gaussian pre-initialisation stabilises the blind optimisation. On experimental tubulin data, blind DIP recovers finer filamentous structures than multi-image deconvolution and DIP with fixed theoretical PSFs, while adapting the PSFs to the measurements.

data.title: Rota universality of shifts on trees
data.abstract: We consider shift operators on infinite directed trees. We prove that under very mild assumptions on the structure of the tree, the resulting operator is universal (in the sense of Rota). We show connections between the spectrum of the operator and the frequency of branching in the tree.

data.title: Simulation of non-stationary anisotropic capillary wave turbulence within the framework of the kinetic equation
data.abstract: In the present work, numerical simulation of the evolution of capillary turbulence was performed on the basis of the wave kinetic equation taking into account energy dissipation at small scales. For an isotropic initial condition, the simulation results reproduce the Zakharov--Filonenko power-law turbulence spectrum for the wave action, \(n_k \sim k^{-17/4}\). The main result of the work is the calculation of the evolution for a substantially anisotropic initial condition. The numerical data indicate that, during the evolution of an anisotropic wave-action distribution, a factorized spectrum \(n(k,φ) \sim k^{-17/4}F(φ)\) is formed in polar coordinates \((k,φ)\), where \(F(φ)\) is a function of the angle in Fourier space. In the regime of a steady power-law distribution in \(k\), the calculated collision integral vanishes with high accuracy in the inertial interval of wavenumbers (the region of the power-law spectrum). Thus, the work provides evidence for the realization of a new strongly anisotropic turbulence spectrum, similar to Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectra.

data.title: Upcycling Language Models for Multiple Specialized Domains
data.abstract: Effective multi-domain adaptation of large language models requires prioritizing relevant domain knowledge while minimizing interference from irrelevant domains. Existing approaches commonly use Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to train a separate adapter for each domain and combine these adapters within one model. However, they either weight adapters equally regardless of the input domain or dynamically weight adapters while still activating all of them including irrelevant ones. Additionally, while efficient, their low-rank structure limits performance. In contrast, upcycling is a model expansion method that adds experts and a router to a dense Transformer layer offering larger capacity than LoRA approaches. In this paper, we propose Domain-Specialized Upcycling (DS-Upcycling) for multi-domain adaptation. We introduce a new domain-aware supervision that allows the router to effectively learn to distinguish domains by selecting the appropriate experts. During fine-tuning on each new domain, we update only the corresponding expert and router while freezing all other parameters. Experiments show that our method achieves the highest average performance across the adapted domains compared to baselines while retaining general performance. With just 256 examples per domain for router supervision, DS-Upcycling achieves 90-98% routing accuracy after adaptation compared with 43-70% for routers trained without our approach.

data.title: Evolutionary tracks and isochrones of the inverse Hall cascade
data.abstract: Decaying MHD turbulence can exhibit an inverse cascade, which means that the height of the spectrum of magnetic energy in the subinertial range increases with time. However, there is evidence for a resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed. It is unclear whether this is caused by reconnection, which is known to depend on resistivity. Here, we show that in the Hall cascade, where no momentum equation is solved, and the induction term is replaced by what corresponds to the negative Lorentz force in MHD, there is still a resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed, but no such dependence is found for an analogous numerical reconnection experiment. This suggests that the resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed is not necessarily related to reconnection.

data.title: Static Response of the Strongly Coupled Electron Gas from Diffusion Monte Carlo
data.abstract: The local field factor $G(q)$ of the HEG describes how exchange and correlation modify the response to a static perturbation, and enters dielectric screening, effective electron--electron interactions, and the xc kernel of TDDFT. Accurate zero-temperature data for $G(q)$, however, remain limited to metallic densities, $r_s\leq10$. In this work, we present diffusion Monte Carlo calculations of the static density response function $χ(q)$ and of $G(q)$ for $2\leq r_s\leq100$, and describe and discuss the methodological steps that enabled these calculations. We show how optimization of the perturbing potential in the trial wave function has an important effect, as a poor choice can reverse the sign of the response. A closed-form expression is provided for its optimal value, together with the density dependence of the linear-response window. We further show that backflow correlations leave $χ(q)$ unchanged and that $G(q)$ depends only weakly on system size even at very low density, so that Slater--Jastrow wave functions and modest system sizes suffice. Together, these results provide a practical guide for future QMC calculations of response properties of the electron gas and real materials. Our results agree with previous DMC data at metallic densities for $q>k_F$, and extend them below $k_F$. They also agree with diagrammatic QMC at $r_s=2$. At lower densities, our results show that $G(q)$ develops a nonmonotonic structure at intermediate-$q$, where the response approaches that of the noninteracting gas. Quantitative agreement is seen with finite-temperature path integral Monte Carlo, suggesting that the previously reported finite-temperature structure is inherited from the ground state. Using a parametrization of $G(q)$ that reproduces our data throughout the liquid phase, we relate this structure to short-range order in the pair correlation function and the static structure factor.

data.title: RepConTUR: A Report-Conditioned Volumetric Multimodal Model for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation
data.abstract: Tumor delineation is required for radiotherapy planning, yet automatic segmentation is limited by errors, predominantly false positives, that distort dose and increase editing time. The radiology report accompanies the scan and localizes disease at the suborgan level, but existing text-promptable models condition on short referring phrases, and most operate in 2D. We present RepConTUR, a single native-3D early-fusion multimodal model that conditions volumetric abdominal tumor segmentation on the narrative report. We extend AbdomenAtlas 3.0 to a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset and generate report-based VQA pairs, yielding four report-derived tasks on the same annotations: referring segmentation (RES), report-grounded segmentation (GSEG), report generation (RRG), and visual question answering (VQA). We train RepConTUR, comprising a 3D CT encoder, an early-fusion language model, and a native-3D segmentation module, jointly on the four tasks. Across liver, kidney and pancreas, RepConTUR attains the highest Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), instance-wise precision, and detection F1 among the text-promptable baselines, and adding the report raises mean precision while leaving recall comparable. Against two vision-only specialists, nnU-Net and the report-supervised R-Super, RepConTUR attains the highest value on every in-domain metric for liver and pancreas and the highest mean DSC, recall, precision, and detection F1 over the four out-of-distribution public cohorts. Ablations indicate that conditioning on the narrative report raises detection F1 from 0.499 to 0.528 within the same model, that joint GSEG training raises RES F1 from 0.450 to 0.482, and that the native-3D segmentation module raises GSEG F1 from 0.139 to 0.528 over its 2D counterpart. Code is available at https://github.com/Oncosoft-Research/RepConTUR.

data.title: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv Problem for $\mathbb{Z}_n^r$
data.abstract: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem is a classical extremal problem in discrete geometry. We prove that, for all positive integers $n$ and $r$, every sequence of $4^r n$ lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^r$ contains $n$ points whose centroid is again a lattice point.

data.title: Reward-Adaptive Co-Evolution of Policy and Rubric
data.abstract: Rubric-based rewards provide fine-grained, interpretable supervision for open-ended reinforcement learning, where holistic scalar rewards struggle to capture multidimensional response quality. Static rubrics can lose discriminative power as the policy distribution evolves, while existing policy--rubric co-evolution methods rely on globally prescribed update schedules that ignore heterogeneous reward informativeness. We introduce RACE, a Reward-Adaptive Co-Evolution framework. At the group level, per-rollout-group training-signal routing classifies groups as informative, diversity-collapsed, or rubric-failed, updating the policy only with informative groups while caching rubric failures. At the phase level, event-triggered phase switching enters rubric optimization upon persistent reward saturation and returns when rubric-reward improvement plateaus. Rubric phases train the generator on cached pairs using a frozen judge and a scale-normalized pairwise-margin reward. Across both levels, online threshold adaptation adjusts routing and switching thresholds through proportional control. Under a unified evaluation protocol, RACE achieves the highest average performance and outperforms the strongest fixed-alternation baseline on all eight tasks, while improving rubric discrimination.

data.title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on Kähler manifolds
data.abstract: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected Kähler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

data.title: Single-atom billiards in an ultracold bath with energy-tunable collisions and threshold-sensitive detection
data.abstract: Transport processes at the microscopic scale can differ strongly from their macroscopic counterparts, particularly when the environment is not a well-defined surface but an unordered thermal medium. Ultracold quantum gases offer a high degree of controllability and directly observable dynamics, thereby providing a versatile platform to study such transport processes under precisely controllable conditions. Here, we realize an energy-tunable single-atom collider by transporting individual cesium atoms at controlled velocity through an ultracold rubidium bath. The constant lattice velocity sets the directed contribution to the collision-energy distribution, while the lattice depth provides a tunable energy threshold for collision-induced transport disruption. By independently varying these parameters together with bath density and temperature, we separate the number of collision events from their probability to disrupt transport. Across a regime with only a few expected collisions per passage, the inferred single-collision ejection probability rises from small values to near unity as the collision energy exceeds the lattice confinement scale. The experiment thus converts microscopic collisional energy transfer into a binary single-atom observable and provides a controlled link between individual scattering events and emergent dissipative transport.

data.title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
data.abstract: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $χ$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$. To the character $χ$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_χ=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $χ$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_χ$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.

data.title: RiskyPy: Toward Model-Calibrated Prompt Generation for Joint Security and Functionality Evaluation of LLM-Generated Code
data.abstract: Evaluating approaches that improve the security of LLM code generation requires datasets that jointly assess security and functionality and remain adapted to the capabilities of the models being studied. However, existing benchmarks are costly to produce and are generally not calibrated to a chosen range of model capabilities. We introduce RiskyPy, an automated pipeline that generates security-oriented code-generation datasets calibrated to model proficiency using functionality and vulnerability canaries. We instantiate RiskyPy for Python using domains covering 18 CWEs from the 2025 CWE Top 25, producing 101 prompts. Experiments on Qwen3-4B and Seed-Coder-8B show that the generated tasks remain functionally accessible, with 57-72% of prompts yielding functional code, while only 5-10% of generations are free of Bandit findings, leaving room for joint evaluation of security and functionality of security improvement approaches.

data.title: Failure of the $H^1\times H^1\longrightarrow L^{1/2,\infty}$ estimate for the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal function and applications
data.abstract: In contrast to Christ's theorem that the lacunary spherical maximal operator is bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ ($d\geq2$), we show that the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal operator $$ \mathcal B_{\mathrm{lac}}(f,g)(x) =\sup_{\ell\in\mathbb Z} \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-2^\ell y)\,g(x-2^\ell z)\,dσ(y,z)\Bigr| $$ is not bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ for any $d\geq1$. In particular, it is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, we construct two finite linear combinations of smooth, compactly supported, mean-zero $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$-atoms for which the ratio of the weak $L^{1/2}$ quasinorm to the product of the two Hardy norms is at least $c_d\log(N+1)$. This lower bound holds already for the supremum over a suitable set of $N$ dyadic radii. For $d=1$ this answers the case $p=q=1$ of a question in Borges's survey. For every $k\ge3$ and $d\ge1$, a modification of the construction proves that the lacunary $k$-linear spherical maximal operator does not map $(H^1(\mathbb R^d))^k$ into $L^{1/k,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. We also indicate extensions to certain hypersurfaces and to horizontal spherical averages on the Heisenberg group.

data.title: The Effective Kerr-Compton Tree Amplitude from Black Hole Perturbation Theory
data.abstract: We develop a new method to construct the tree-level Compton amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a Kerr black hole in post-Minkowskian effective field theory. Building on previous computations that required physical consistency of the amplitude, the method uses wave scattering functions from black hole perturbation theory to uniquely determine additional contact terms. We illustrate the iterative procedure by deriving explicit expressions up to sixth order in spin, including previously unknown sectors at the fifth and sixth orders in spin. The amplitude features complex transcendental structures and a leading dissipative contact term at sixth order in spin. We verify our result against known results in the literature and reproduce the one-loop tail result from black hole perturbation theory.

data.title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
data.abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

data.title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
data.abstract: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.

data.title: Continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior in hybrid Josephson junction arrays
data.abstract: We report finite-temperature scaling of voltage-driven quantum phase transitions in hybrid Josephson junction arrays. A dual-gate geometry separately tunes interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity, providing access to superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes. The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously with electrostatic tuning. Where the three regimes converge, the critical resistivity approaches $h/4e^2$, consistent with the self-dual limit, while the scaling exponent approaches the quantum-percolation estimate. Tuning toward stronger insulating behavior raises the critical resistivity and shifts the scaling exponent toward the classical-percolation value, while both parameters decrease toward the metallic regime. These results connect scaling regimes previously reported in different two-dimensional superconducting systems through continuous electrostatic control.

data.title: Diagonalization and Undecidability in Semi-Thue Systems
