We define a Kripke-induced fuzzy Alexandroff topology and establish a precise correspondence between Łukasiewicz fuzzy Kripke semantics and its topological counterpart. The proposed topological semantics validates the S4 modal axioms that include reflexivity, transitivity, monotonicity, normality, and the necessitation of truth.

data.title: Beyond the Kubo formula: unification of adiabatic and isothermal response in quantum systems
data.abstract: The static limit of the Kubo susceptibility describes the adiabatic response of an isolated quantum system, in which energy-level occupations remain unchanged, and generally differs from the isothermal susceptibility, where these occupations readjust to thermal equilibrium. In this work, we introduce a single dynamical framework in which the adiabatic and isothermal responses arise naturally as two distinct limiting regimes. This can be done by considering explicitly an open system version of the Kubo approach in which the dissipation is governed by a typical thermalization rate of the system. By exchanging the order of the static limit and of the vanishing thermalization rate limit, the protocol yields either the adiabatic or isothermal response. This protocol has a solid physical motivation in terms of the thermalization dynamics and is valid for generic systems. We apply it to the case of the magnetic response of the electron gas and reproduce the expected results.

data.title: Integral Hodge structures and atoms of fourfolds
data.abstract: Following the recent work by OpenAI on the irrationality of very general cubic fourfolds in Hassett divisors, we prove some compatibility of Iritani's blow-up formula with the classical blow-up decomposition of integral Hodge structures. As a consequence, we express OpenAI's birational invariant in terms of the theory of atoms developped by Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu. We also show that, for every smooth complex rational cubic fourfold, the primitive cohomology is isometric as an integral Hodge structure to the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface and we prove irrationality of the very general Verra fourfold.

data.title: Merging and Evolution of Data Bases: A Many-Logic Approach
data.abstract: A new approach to information-based logics using many-logic modal structures (MLMSs) was recently proposed by Martins et al. In such a setting, it is possible to have worlds with different underlying logics within the same frame, all anchored to a base lattice that contains the semantics of each logic as a down-complete sublattice. In this paper, we take the lattice L6, defined by the six-valued semantics of the logic of evidence and truth LET + K , as our base lattice. We also consider four-, three-, and two-valued formal systems associated with down-complete sublattices of L6. These logics are capable of representing paracomplete, paraconsistent, and classical contexts with six, four, three, and two informational scenarios, respectively. As applications of MLMSs, we will discuss the merging and temporal evolution of databases whose underlying logics are two-, three-, four-, and six-valued. We will also investigate inconsistency measures in this context.

data.title: Restricted Peirce's Law and Natural Deduction
data.abstract: The constructive logic JP' is known to be the weakest logic between intuitionistic and minimal logic that satisfies Glivenko's theorem. In spite of this natural and desirable formal property, the motivation for its notion of negation remains rather elusive: it can be characterised by a restriction of Peirce's law or by the double negation of ex falso quodlibet, neither of which is very intuitive. In order to have an alternative perspective on this negation, we study in this paper a couple of natural deduction systems for JP'. We first present a system that is normalisable and satisfies a restricted form of the subformula property. Then a modification of this system is introduced, whose rules satisfy the separation of connectives and the full subformula property. Afterwards we turn our attention to a typed lambda-calculus, with respect to which our natural deduction enjoys the Curry-Howard correspondence, followed by a concluding discussion.

data.title: Paraclassical Logics with Two Negations
data.abstract: We study three paraclassical propositional logics with two negations, CLoaN, CLouN, and CLauN, obtained by pairwise combining the one-negation systems CLuN, CLaN, and CLoN. CLuN's negation is glut-tolerant and paraconsistent, CLaN's negationis gap-tolerant and paracomplete, and CLoN's negation is both paraconsistent and paracomplete. We provide sound and complete two-valued non-deterministic semantics for each of the two-negations systems. We then focus on CLauN, the system containing the primitive dual pair of CLaN and CLuN negations. In this setting, we show deductive relationships between different negations expressible in CLauN; we show two diferent ways to recapture classical logic by means of translations, locally and globally; and we show a duality results for the multiple conclusion consequence relation of the logic.

data.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
data.abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

data.title: Normalisation for a Neutral Free Logic with Definite Descriptions
data.abstract: In this paper, we present a natural deduction system for a strong Kleene-based neutral free logic with definite descriptions. The system combines a three-valued propositional basis with free quantification, identity, existence, and rules for definite descriptions. The main result is a normalisation theorem for a proof-theoretically equivalent restricted formulation of the system; we also establish a corresponding modified subformula property for its fragment.

data.title: Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic With Additive Constants as Extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus
data.abstract: Cyclic Linear Logic (CyMALL, CyBL) is a compromise between Commutative Linear Logic (MALL) and Noncommutative Linear Logic (Bilinear Logic, BL). We do not admit commutativity of the tensor, but we still admit only one De Morgan negation. MALL and its variants are natural extensions of Full Lambek Calculus (FL). Abrusci proved that CyBL is not a conservative extension of FL, if we admit additive constants in these logics. In this paper we show that Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic (CyNBL) with both additive constants is a strongly conservative extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus with only one additive constant - the upper bound - and that this holds even in the presence of an arbitrary set of nonlogical axioms.

data.title: All Symmetries and Boundaries of the Two-Dimensional Free Scalar from Continuous Flat-Gauging
data.abstract: We propose a remote detectability criterion for two-dimensional conformal field theories, which asserts that any local operator outside of the product of the left- and right-moving Virasoro algebras can be detected by some topological line defect. We discuss its relationship to existing results in the conformal net literature. We then use this criterion to argue that the known $SU(2)$ moduli space of unitary conformal boundary conditions and the $SO(4)$ moduli space of unitary topological line defects of the $SU(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model completely capture all unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological lines of the theory. Invoking the fact that the non-compact boson conformal field theory can be obtained from $SU(2)_1$ by "flat-gauging" a $U(1)$ symmetry, we are also able to completely classify the unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological line defects of the two-dimensional free scalar field. In particular, we find a 4-dimensional moduli space of topological line defects, most of which were not known previously. We support our proposed classifications by writing down concrete Lagrangian descriptions of all of the boundaries and lines of the non-compact boson. For every boundary condition, we calculate the corresponding boundary state, and for each pair of boundary conditions, we calculate the corresponding interval Hilbert space. We verify that the annulus partition functions of the theory respect open/closed duality. We also calculate the fusion rules of the topological line defects, their action on local operators, their action on the boundary conditions by parallel fusion, and their corresponding twisted-sector Hilbert spaces.

data.title: A Local Fourier-Transform Proof of Offen's Spherical Transfer Theorem
data.abstract: Let $E/F$ be an unramified quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero and odd residual characteristic. Offen proved that, on the full spherical space of nondegenerate Hermitian matrices, equality of the Hironaka and Satake transforms implies Jacquet--Ye matching. We give a purely local proof of this theorem. The argument combines Jacquet's compatibility of matching with Fourier transform, the Godement--Jacquet functional equation, and Hironaka's scalar functional equation for Hermitian zeta integrals. The local proof recovers Jacquet's spherical-Hecke fundamental lemma from the unit case.

data.title: Sharp convex body sparse bounds and quantitative matrix weighted estimates for Hilbert transforms along curves
data.abstract: We prove convex body sparse bounds for coordinatewise Hilbert transforms along monomial curves and local $C^d$ curves with uniformly nonvanishing torsion on the closed integration interval. Adapting the scalar estimates of Cladek--Ou \cite{CladekOu2018} and the lifting method of Laukkarinen--Lorist \cite{LaukkarinenLorist2026} to the anisotropic geometry, we obtain one sparse family of genuine curve-adapted boxes and quantitative $L^p(W)$ bounds for matrix weights. The convex body sparse exponent range is sharp up to its boundary: estimates hold in the interior of $Ω_d$, while any fixed finite number of sparse families fails outside $\overline{Ω_d}$ when $1/r+1/s>1$. We also establish an explicit endpoint-contact obstruction. For every interior planar exponent pair, a polynomial curve with positive torsion on the open integration interval violates the full-interval sparse estimate.

data.title: The Yottascale at Tera-$Z$: Petascale SUSY?
data.abstract: As experimental and theoretical advances are made, the paradigm of grand unification faces growing challenges. In light of what has been learned at the LHC, from Higgs mass measurement and direct searches for supersymmetry, we contrast the current theoretical predictions in a simplified supersymmetric grand unified theory against present and future experimental precision, focussing on threshold corrections and renormalisation group effects above the electroweak scale. More precisely, the theoretical precision is juxtaposed to the experimental one. Especially, the impact of a future Tera-$Z$ factory such as FCC-ee is examined, while also considering the expected future improvement of proton decay constraints. We find that the improvement on the measurement of the gauge couplings expected at Tera-$Z$ will yield sensitivity to higher loop orders in the evolution of the couplings up to the Yottascale, calling for further theoretical efforts. In a minimal $\rm{SU}(5)$ scenario with nearly degenerate SUSY spectrum, we study the impact of the proton decay constraint on the SUSY scale, comparing 2- and 3-loop analyses. While the 2-loop results point to a SUSY scale around 1 PeV, the 3-loop analysis seems to exclude the model entirely. This follows from the fact that at 1-loop in the GUT threshold corrections, the mass of the colour-triplet Higgs is completely determined by the IR parameters. This \textit{IR determination} is not accidental, but rooted in the group structure and breaking of the GUT theory.

data.title: Quantifying Linepack Storage Potential of Hydrogen Networks
data.abstract: Future hydrogen systems depend on large-scale storage to balance supply and demand. Hydrogen networks can store energy in the pipelines themselves, but the potential of this linepack storage has not been quantified comparably to dedicated storage facilities. We transfer metrics established for conventional storage, such as volume capacity and full-cycle equivalents, to hydrogen networks. To evaluate them, we formulate an optimization problem maximizing linepack storage utilization, subject to non-convex PDE-based constraints describing transient gas flow. We solve the optimization problem over a full-year horizon to capture seasonal variations and to assess the interaction with cavern storage. For computational tractability, we propose a simulation-informed sequential convex programming approach with adaptive time stepping that reduces problem size by up to 98% at accuracy comparable to fixed-resolution methods. For the GasLib-40 topology with German scenario data, the network provides a volume capacity of 24 million normal cubic meters at 28 full-cycle equivalents per year.

data.title: The signature-changing soft-gluon term as a possible source of non-planar $ζ_2$ terms at small $x$ in the non-singlet quark-plus-antiquark splitting function
data.abstract: A relation underlying resummations at small momentum fraction $x$ predicts the highest logarithms of quark-plus-antiquark flavor-difference splitting functions from lower orders. Complete three- and four-loop results violate it at third-highest logarithms by pi-squared terms suppressed for many colors, of unexplained origin and color structure. At four loops Moch and Vogt suggested a squared imaginary phase. We retain the signature-changing soft-gluon term also in positive signature in Kirschner and Lipatov's double-logarithmic equations for forward quark-antiquark scattering, without derivation, with their printed negative-signature sign and adjoint Born term. We show that the proposed equations reproduce both violations in full color for quark-plus-antiquark flavor differences at zero power of $x$, fixed coupling and first order in pi squared, for defining-representation quarks of special unitary groups with at least three colors. The proposed equations at third-highest logarithms use one wave per exchanged color and signature, the retained term at lowest-order strength as the positive-signature color-neutral channel's only new source of these violations, no such terms from gluons across the softest exchanged quark-antiquark pair at comparable or larger transverse momentum, and unchanged quark-pair normalization in the splitting function. This agreement gives three independent tests of one system with no continuous coefficient adjusted to the violations, although corresponding non-quartic quark-minus-antiquark terms are missed. In the proposed equations, the retained term weighted by this phase is a possible origin of both violations. The equations predict these full-color five-loop quark-plus-antiquark terms if the relation otherwise holds and no new source first acts at five loops. Confirmation would support the retained term as the origin of the violations through five loops.

data.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Distributional Paging
data.abstract: Distributional paging seeks a polynomial-time eviction rule that competes with the optimal \emph{online} policy $\mathrm{OPT}$ when requests come from a known stochastic source. Two algorithms by Lund, Phillips, and Reingold [FOCS, 1994] are canonical. Their randomized \emph{dominating distribution} algorithm, for Markov sources, evicts a page drawn from a distribution over the cache satisfying pairwise linear inequalities; their deterministic \emph{median} algorithm, for sources with independent inter-arrival times across pages, evicts the cached page with the largest lower median of its conditional next-request time. Their original guarantees of $4$ and $5$ were recently improved to $2$ and $4$ by Pabbaraju and Vakilian [ICALP 2025]. We show that neither improved constant can be reduced in its respective source model. For Markov paging, we give two complementary factor-$2$ lower-bound constructions, each with an explicit polynomial-time dominating selector. A directed-cycle family has ratio $2k/(k+1)$, while a recurrent four-page family with cache size three has ratio $2-4\varepsilon/3$. For the independent inter-arrival model, we show that the median algorithm is not $c$-competitive for any $c<4$. These are separate results for distinct stochastic models. Matching the known upper bounds, they establish tight competitive ratios of $2$ and $4$, respectively, improving on previous lower bounds of $1.5907$ and $1.511$.

data.title: On the NP-Hardness of Rank-Metric Minimum Distance and Syndrome Decoding, at Every Rate
data.abstract: In this work, we investigate the hardness of computing minimum distance, as well as the hardness of syndrome decoding, for rank-metric codes. It is known (Gaborit and Zémor, IEEE TIT 2016) that for $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-linear rank-metric codes of length $N$, minimum distance when $m=O(N)$ and syndrome decoding when $m=O(N^2)$ are NP-hard under randomized reductions. We obtain a derandomization of these results and a bit more. We show that for any fixed small $\varepsilon>0$, for $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-linear rank-metric codes of length $N$ with $m=O(N^{1+\varepsilon})$, the problems of minimum distance, nearest codeword, and syndrome decoding are NP-hard under deterministic reductions. Further, we can prescribe the rate; that is, if we restrict to codes having any fixed rational rate $R\in(0,1)$, then the NP-hardness for all three problems persists. Our main technical contribution is simple, and possibly of independent interest. The reduction of Gaborit and Zémor (IEEE TIT 2016) relies on a distance-preserving embedding of a Hamming-metric code into a rank-metric code, obtained by multiplying its coordinates by a uniformly random vector. We show that we can choose an explicit vector from a slightly larger extension field.

data.title: Joint Estimation and Network Configuration in Multi-Agent Systems
data.abstract: Distributed consensus-based sensing enables a multi-agent system to collaboratively estimate an unknown state by combining local measurements with information received from neighboring agents. In practice, however, the communication network, transmission delays, and finite-rate communication directly affect the disagreement among agents. On the other hand, agreement among agents does not ensure accuracy, particularly when sensors have different measurement uncertainties. We develop a sampled consensus-plus-innovations framework under realistic wireless network constraints that jointly accounts for inter-agent disagreement and estimation inaccuracy. We derive a computable upper bound on the worst-case steady-state estimation error that captures consensus disagreement due to the communication graph, quantization error, and transmission delay, together with estimation inaccuracy, which accounts for measurement uncertainty against the true state. We then use this bound as a network design objective and propose a semi-distributed auction-based algorithm that jointly modifies the communication graph and link-rate allocation. The proposed method preserves connectivity, converges in finite time to a locally auction-stable network configuration, and reduces the bound on the estimation error at every accepted change. The proposed method has been evaluated on various test cases, and the results show that it reduces the estimation error while maintaining fewer links and allocating moderate link rates in a short time.

data.title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
data.abstract: Imitation learning policies are intended to make robotic manipulation robust to variations in object pose, appearance, and environment that challenge pre-programmed motion. However, real-world performance remains difficult to predict, as conventional optimization signals such as validation loss show no consistent relationship with robot success. To identify the design choices that govern real-world performance, 281 imitation-learning policies spanning seven policy families were evaluated in approximately 1,700 real-robot trials of RJ45 connector grasping and insertion using a five-fingered robotic hand. Controlled ablations showed that observation and action representations dominated conventional optimizer and sampling choices. For point-cloud policies, region-of-interest cropping, representation in the robot-base frame, and normalization within the point encoder each improved success by 70-100 percentage points. For the vision-language-action policy, absolute rather than relative action prediction improved insertion success by up to 70 percentage points. Skill decomposition, multi-view perception, and recovery demonstrations were associated with the strongest-performing systems, although their effects were not independently isolated. Of 67 offline metrics evaluated, only five measures of predicted-motion smoothness and directness reliably correlated with insertion success (r = -0.70 to -0.80), and only within a single policy family. These results identify representation choices as key determinants of real-world imitation-learning performance and show that offline metrics can shortlist policies, but cannot replace real-robot evaluation.

data.title: Witnessing and quantifying stellar rank with the Wigner function
data.abstract: Quantifying non-Gaussianity is essential for assessing the computational power of bosonic quantum systems. We introduce a framework to witness and quantify non-Gaussianity from displaced parity measurements, and we directly apply it to experimental data obtained with superconducting cavities. Our method estimates fidelities with target pure states from the displaced parity measurements, enabling certification of non-Gaussianity via the stellar rank. We further introduce refined witnesses computed by measuring the value of the Wigner function at a few points, providing efficient certification tools outperforming existing ones. Applying these techniques to Fock, binomial, cat, and GKP experimental data, we rigorously certify non-Gaussian resources and establish a stellar rank of $8$ for a GKP state, setting a new benchmark across all quantum platforms. Our methods enable a rigorous quantification of non-Gaussian quantum resources directly applicable to superconducting devices.

data.title: Arithmetical Characterizations of Two Intuitionistic Logical Principles
data.abstract: This paper investigates the role of negation in arithmetic by analyzing subsystems based on subminimal logic. We introduce NA^PR, a system of subminimal arithmetic equipped with all primitive recursive functions, and answer the following four questions: (1) Can we develop reasonable arithmetic within NA^PR? (2) Can we characterize logical rules Absorption of Negation (An) and Ex Falso Quodlibet (ECQ) by arithmetical principles? (3) Are there strict differences in deductive power among NA^PR, MA^PR, and HA? (4) Do MA^PR and MA, and NA^PR and NA have a similar mutual interpretability relationship as HA? We show the following: First, Heyting Arithmetic (HA) is shown to be a conservative extension of NA^PR for positive formulas. Based on NA^PR, we prove that (ECQ) is equivalent to the definability of disjunction, and that (An) is equivalent to a variant of the least number principle. Furthermore, using the constant domain neighbourhood semantics, we show that the systems NA^PR, MA^PR (written as NA^PR+(An)) and HA (written as NA^PR+(An)+(ECQ)) form a strictly increasing hierarchy of strength. Finally, we demonstrate the essential role of primitive recursive functions in weak arithmetic using classical countermodels.

data.title: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes
data.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are effective in solving problems that can be modeled as Markov decision processes (MDPs). These algorithms primarily target forward MDPs whose dynamics evolve over time from an initial state. However, several important problems in different scenarios including stochastic control and network systems exhibit both a forward and a backward dynamics. As a consequence, they cannot be expressed as a standard MDP, thereby calling for a novel theory for RL in this context. Accordingly, this work introduces the concept of Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes (FB-MDPs) for multi-objective problems, develops a novel theoretical framework to characterize their optimal solutions, and proposes a general forward-backward step-wise template that allows to adapt RL algorithms for FB-MDP problems. A Forward Backward Multi Objective Actor Critic (FB-MOAC) algorithm is introduced accordingly to obtain optimal policies with guaranteed convergence and a competitive rate with respect to standard approaches in RL. FB-MOAC is evaluated on diverse use cases in the context of mathematical finance and mobile resource management. The obtained results show that FB-MOAC outperforms the state of the art across different metrics, highlighting its ability to learn and maximize rewards.

data.title: Tableaux Rules for Theories of Definite Descriptions in Positive Free Logic with Some Philosophical Remarks
data.abstract: While Russell's theory of definite descriptions, expressions of the form 'the F', is almost incontrovertible in classical logic, in free logic matters stand differently. Several alternatives have been proposed. In Lambert's hierarchy, the weakest theory is his minimal free theory of definite descriptions (MFD), which only says that anything is the F iff it is the unique existing F, the strongest one is a chosen object theory in which all improper definite descriptions refer to the same object (FD2). Intermediate is Lambert's FD1, which adds ix(x = t) = t as an axiom to MFD. MFD is very weak. FD2 is very strong. One might hope to find intermediate systems in which ix(x = t) = t is provable from more fundamental principles. The present paper considers one avenue where one might hope to find them and closes it. Two theories, FDA and FDH, will be considered that are motivated by considerations from proof-theoretic semantics. The former turns out to be equivalent to FD2, the latter to have unreasonable consequences. A third theory, similarly motivated, is also not viable. The philosophical upshot of this is briefly discussed.

data.title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
data.abstract: AI model marketplaces host providers with heterogeneous costs and capabilities. These differences create an opportunity for computational arbitrage (Olmedo et al., 2026), in which an intermediary purchases inference from a portfolio of models and resells it to users at a profit. Beyond creating profit opportunities for the arbitrageur, computational arbitrage offers financial value to both consumers and providers and could therefore significantly influence AI model markets. While prior work empirically demonstrates the feasibility of computational arbitrage for small model pools, scaling it to large marketplaces requires arbitrage strategies that are both computationally tractable and inexpensive to identify and deploy. In this work, we formalize computational arbitrage as an allocation problem and prove that it is generally NP-hard. However, we show that the optimal allocation can be computed efficiently under a natural diminishing-returns condition on how model performance scales with inference spending. We further develop a sample-efficient method for estimating model performance from limited data, reducing the upfront cost of identifying arbitrage strategies. Our analysis also yields several economic insights: at the optimum, every funded model delivers the same marginal utility per dollar; arbitrage directs revenue away from providers offering little utility relative to their prices; and it rewards complementary specialization.

data.title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
data.abstract: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. Building a complete reconstruction from such specialized predictions therefore typically requires per-sequence optimization. We propose EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric monocular video. To jointly recover these components, it maintains a recurrent scene representation that accumulates geometric evidence over time and provides a shared world space and scale. We introduce hand-centric prompts that fuse pretrained hand priors and local scene context, while MANO vertex queries attend to scene features to predict dense per-vertex contact. These designs enable a single network to jointly estimate camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO hands, and per-vertex hand contact. Despite operating causally, EgoHSI3R achieves the lowest world-space hand joint error on ARCTIC among the evaluated methods, while offering faster inference than existing world-space hand reconstruction pipelines and competitive camera and scene reconstruction accuracy.

data.title: How Global Is Anycast?: Evaluating Performance Gaps
data.abstract: Anycast networks aim to reduce latency by directing users to nearby service sites. However, users can still experience high latency even when accessing services via anycast. Some anycast deployments are localized and intended to serve a specific geographic region, while others are globally distributed to support users worldwide, with the expectation of consistently low latency across locations. In practice, latency can remain poor for certain users due to factors such as routing inefficiencies and peering relationships. These inefficiencies are often more pronounced in regions such as Africa, Asia or South America, where Internet connectivity is generally less mature than in North America or Europe. Despite this, there has been no in-depth analysis of anycast performance in these continents. In this paper, we examine the latency experienced by users in these regions when accessing anycast networks. We analyze more than 10,000 anycast prefixes, quantify the severity of latency problems, and show that clients in Africa, Asia, and South America experience substantially higher latency than those in North America. We also investigate the underlying causes of this performance gap.

data.title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation
data.abstract: Existing whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate metastasis segmentation methods generally rely on images alone, without explicitly incorporating where metastases tend to occur. We investigate whether a population metastasis atlas can improve lesion detection when integrated into model training. We constructed voxel-wise mean and standard deviation maps from 375 expert-annotated training scans and used them to weight the cross-entropy loss of an nnU-Net. The additional penalties for missed lesions and false positives depend on spatial atlas statistics and diminish as predictions become confidently correct. Seven configurations were compared on validation data; three were combined by majority voting into SAILS (Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss enSemble). We compared SAILS with a baseline nnU-Net and inference-time atlas fusion on AutoPET~III (110 disease-positive cases) and Deep-PSMA (100 external cases). No atlas or registration is needed at inference. Results: On AutoPET~III, SAILS improved whole-body Dice (0.531 vs. 0.520; p=0.006), reduced missed-lesion volume (9.5 vs. 12.1 cc/case; p<0.01), and increased pooled lesion sensitivity (0.857 vs. 0.843; p=0.004). On Deep-PSMA, SAILS detected 126 additional reference lesions (sensitivity 0.769 vs. 0.751; p<0.001), without a significant whole-body Dice change (-0.009; p=0.36). High-risk bone Dice improved in both cohorts (0.576 vs. 0.552 and 0.667 vs. 0.653; both p<0.01). False-positive volume increased by 2.3 and 18.2 cc/case, respectively (p<0.001). Atlas-weighted training improves lesion detection, especially in high-risk bone, without test-time atlas registration, but increases false positives.

data.title: How a group that cannot communicate knows itself by its enemy
data.abstract: Teams that cannot communicate seem stuck with what each member sees. We show that their opponent can tell them the rest. Silent hunters, jammed robots and traders who never meet all face an adversary that reacts to the group as a whole; every member can read that reaction, a tell, and learn what no member knows alone. One tell can do the work of a message from every member. The adversary would rather hide, but hiding interferes with its own task, and a team that commits in advance to how it will respond decides how much hiding is worth. A committed team never loses when its opponent cares more about its own goals, and does as well as a fully informed team exactly when the opponent's stake outweighs any gain from lying. Below that point the team learns more by trusting less: in a solved Gaussian model it obtains the truth by promising not to use all of it and keeps the cost the opponent would have paid to conceal; an exact test decides when this holds in finite games. How a team spreads its trust matters too. A lone uninformed member with a full-support prior needs a private coin, but with additive squared-error losses two interchangeable members who respond differently replace it, and a small discount on trust insures against misjudging the enemy. Information, on this view, is not only gathered or aggregated; it is produced by how a team commits to respond.

data.title: An infinite family of conservation laws for perfect compressible fluids
data.abstract: We prove the existence of an infinite family of conservation laws and, more generally, balance laws, satisfied by plane-symmetric flows of perfect compressible fluids, allowing all components of the velocity vector to be possibly non-vanishing. We cover general pressure laws satisfying solely hyperbolicity and asymptotic conditions. We exhibit an almost quadratic formulation of the Euler equations, which we refer to as the J-formulation, and introduce a reduced Euler system based on an effective mass-energy density and an effective pressure law which account for transverse velocities. We establish the existence of a fundamental kernel which we use to generate all spacetime (quasi-)currents, also called mathematical entropy pairs. We derive explicit formulas for their density and flux components, together with the source-terms of the corresponding balance laws. Furthermore, we establish regularity and asymptotic estimates covering the whole range of physical variables, including vacuum. We prove that the kernel is positive on the interior of its support provided the pressure law satisfies a genuine nonlinearity condition, and we also investigate the future-convexity of the spacetime currents. Throughout, the fluid momentum parallel to the orbits of plane-symmetry is kept arbitrary. In turn, this family of spacetime quasi-currents provides a key ingredient in our companion study of torus-symmetric Einstein-Euler flows with weak regularity.

data.title: Kupershmidt--Nijenhuis structures on pre-Leibniz algebras
data.abstract: In this paper, we first construct the dual of a representation of a pre-Leibniz algebra and study infinitesimal deformations of a pre-Leibniz algebra with a representation, which lead to Nijenhuis pairs, characterizing trivial deformations, and to dual-Nijenhuis pairs. Building on these notions, we introduce Kupershmidt-(dual-)Nijenhuis structures and show that they give rise to hierarchies of pairwise compatible Kupershmidt operators, the converse holding under an invertibility condition. Finally, we show that Rota--Baxter--Nijenhuis structures, $r$-$n$ structures and BN-structures all arise as particular cases, and that the first two correspond to each other on quadratic pre-Leibniz algebras.

data.title: $α$-decay widths from two-potential approaches and WKB prefactors
data.abstract: The accurate calculation of $α$-decay widths can be obtained with several equivalent descriptions of the Gurvitz-Kalbermann two-potential approach (TPA) or a semiclassical WKB description having both correct barrier penetrability and consistent inner-state normalization prefactor. This prefactor, which is related to the assault frequency, is implemented in several ways in the literature, producing systematically different results that can be mistaken for $α$ preformation effects. We benchmark single-particle $α$-decay widths across 161 even-even nuclei ($A_p=144$--$252$) using several TPA descriptions and WKB calculations with four common prefactors, employing a Woods-Saxon potential fixed by the quantization-constrained parameter method. The TPA formulas agree to within a few parts in $10^{-8}$, highlighting their robustness. Among semiclassical prefactors, only the widely used round-trip (RT) approximation closely reproduces the TPA widths to within a few percent. An Airy-function analysis reveals this $\cos^2\to 1/2$ averaged WKB prefactor is the correct leading-order semiclassical normalization of the exact quasibound state, clarifying the counterintuitive empirical observations associated with the WKB prefactors. Our benchmark identifies the WKB prefactor appropriate for $α$-decay tunneling analysis and provides a clean reference for isolating preformation and structure effects in future studies.

data.title: Structural Exposure and Subsequent Neighborhood Stability in Temporal Networks: Evidence and Limits of Generalizability
data.abstract: Can temporal path based structural exposure serve as a reliable indicator of subsequent local neighborhood stability across different temporal networks? We investigate this question using the completed observational results from 12 networks spanning face to face nteraction, communication, online activity, and urban mobility. Exposure aggregates source node structural mass along time respecting paths; the outcome is Jaccard neighborhood turnover between later, nonoverlapping windows, with greater turnover indicating lower stability. Six complementary analyses examine the direction and consistency of exposure-turnover associations, proximity to high mass nodes, functional response shapes, distance decay kernels, alternative mass definitions, and temporally ordered changes in source mass. The evidence is heterogeneous rather than uniformly negative or positive. In the primary association analysis, two networks retained positive coefficients after within question false discovery rate adjustment, indicating lower subsequent stability at higher exposure, whereas no negative association survived that adjustment. The pooled proximity coefficient was not distinguishable from zero, and significant mass change associations appeared in opposite directions across networks. More flexible functional, kernel, and mass choices yielded only modest cross validated improvements over simpler comparators; available temporal randomizations also gave model dependent contrasts. The study therefore does not establish structural exposure as a directionally consistent, network independent stability indicator. It also cannot establish a lack of predictive value relative to a no exposure baseline, because that specific comparison and independent cross network validation were unavailable. Incomplete null simulations, unrecorded covariance estimation fallbacks constrain inference.

data.title: Galaxy cluster thermodynamics at z=1.7: Resolved tSZ and X-ray analysis of CL J0459.6-4946
data.abstract: Measurements of the entropy and temperature distribution of the intracluster medium (ICM) of local clusters have proven pivotal for the study of cluster astrophysics. Here, we extend these measurements to $z=1.7$ with a resolved analysis of the ICM in ACT/SPT-CL J0459.6-4946. By combining high-resolution thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich measurements using new, deep ALMA Band 1 and 3 observations, with archival X-ray data, we conclude that the cluster has (i) an ICM with a flat and relatively high ($\approx 200$ keV cm$^2$) entropy distribution out to $\approx 0.3\,r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, (ii) a hot core ($T_{\mathrm{e}} \simeq 14$ keV) with a declining temperature profile, (iii) a short effective path length along the line of sight of $l_{\mathrm{eff}} \simeq (0.75 \pm 0.05) \times r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, and (iv) a clumpiness factor $C = \langle n_{\mathrm{e}}^2 \rangle / \langle n_{\mathrm{e}} \rangle^2 \simeq 1.17 \pm 0.05$ within $r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$. Its dynamic nature and high redshift suggest that the cluster is still thermalising its ICM, consistent with a relatively large hydrostatic mass bias of $b = 1 - M_{500,\mathrm{c,HE}}/M_{500,\mathrm{c,WL}} = 0.27^{+0.32}_{-0.67}$ that we measure with respect to the weak lensing mass. Furthermore, a region with low entropy and high density to the south of the cluster centre is observed in the X-rays yet absent in the Compton-$y$ map, indicating pressure equilibrium; we interpret this as a sloshing cold front -- the first such detection at high redshifts. This case study demonstrates that $\approx 3$h-long ALMA observations, combined with comparatively "short" X-ray exposures ($\approx 122$ ks), can fully characterise the ICM at high redshift, opening a path towards the thermodynamics of young and distant galaxy clusters for larger samples.

data.title: Expression of White and Gray Matter Autism Functional Network Connectivity Signatures in Infancy
data.abstract: Functional connectivity studies have provided valuable insights into altered brain organization in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, most functional connectivity studies focus exclusively on either gray matter (GM) regions or white matter (WM) tracts and examine specific age groups, rather than investigating their functional interactions across brain development. This limits our understanding of how GM-WM functional interactions evolve developmentally and may obscure important aspects of brain network organization in ASD. We combined integrated WM+GM functional network connectivity (FNC) with brain-wide risk scores (BRSs) to quantify ASD-associated pattern expression in ABIDE I/II and an independent infant cohort. We employed a NeuroMark framework with predefined WM and GM intrinsic connectivity networks templates, to estimate subject-level FNC. First, we identified two distinct patterns of altered WM+GM FNC in ASD: GM-related hypoconnectivity centered on the paralimbic network and WM-GM hyperconnectivity centered on the frontal network. These findings highlight the involvement of higher-order cognitive networks and the importance of WM-GM functional interactions in characterizing ASD-related connectivity alterations. Second, infants with a higher familial likelihood of autism exhibited greater mean expression of ASD-associated FNC patterns than those with a lower familial likelihood, as quantified by BRS. These group-level findings do not establish developmental persistence or predict diagnostic outcomes at the individual level.

data.title: Electronic-Structure-Informed Many-Body Encoding for Quantum Machine Learning
data.abstract: Data encoding is a central challenge in quantum machine learning (QML), as it determines how classical information is mapped onto quantum states and influences the expressive power and efficiency of parameterized quantum circuits. Here, we introduce a physics-informed quantum encoding strategy that exploits the intrinsic many-body structure of electronic systems to establish a direct correspondence between the body order of input descriptors and the locality of quantum gates. Specifically, $n$-body electronic descriptors obtained from a single mean-field electronic-structure calculation are encoded through $n$-qubit gates, yielding a systematic hierarchy of quantum circuits with increasing many-body expressivity. Using reduced-density-matrix descriptors, we construct quantum machine-learning models incorporating one- through four-body encodings and benchmark their performance in predicting electron-correlation energies along bond-stretching potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate that increasing the body order of the encoding systematically improves prediction accuracy toward the full configuration interaction limit. Remarkably, disconnected many-particle densities constructed from lower-order electronic information achieve accuracy comparable to explicitly correlated two-particle densities in key cases, providing a computationally inexpensive route to higher-body quantum encodings. These findings establish a connection between the many-body structure of classical data and the design of quantum feature maps, offering a systematic, physically interpretable framework for enhancing the expressivity and predictive performance of quantum machine-learning circuits.

data.title: Unitarity and Positivity Constraints on C- or P-odd Anomalous Quartic Couplings
data.abstract: In this work, we provide a comprehensive study of partial-wave unitarity and positivity constraints in the dimension-eight genuine anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) sector of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We extend previous partial-wave unitarity analyses to include all C- or P-odd operators, thereby completing the coverage of the full basis of 34 operators. We also derive an analytical set of necessary forward-limit positivity bounds that include all CP-odd Wilson coefficients. We demonstrate that non-vanishing CP-odd Wilson coefficients require non-vanishing contributions from the CP-even sector to satisfy the derived positivity conditions. Combining the positivity conditions with partial-wave unitarity, we obtain stronger bounds on twenty-three of the thirty-four Wilson coefficients in this sector of the SMEFT.

data.title: The nodally bound-preserving finite element method for the transport equation
data.abstract: Numerical approximations of transport problems, even when stabilised, often violate the bounds respected by the exact solution. Depending on the problem being solved, this can produce non-physical results, such as negative densities or higher-than-unity concentrations. Various bound-preserving numerical methods exist, yet they are usually either conditionally stable or only first-order accurate. In this context, the present work extends the nodally bound-preserving finite element method to the linear transport equation. As a baseline discretisation we use the least-squares finite element method, which is instrumental in achieving unconditional stability for second-order time stepping. It also leads to symmetric algebraic systems, thereby enabling simple, efficient solvers, which we further enhance through Anderson acceleration. Unconditional stability is proved for the backward Euler and Crank--Nicolson discretisations. We also derive error estimates for the fully discrete second-order scheme and provide various numerical examples, including two-phase incompressible flows.

data.title: The full shadow of a polynomial II. Vanishing root masses and holes
data.abstract: For a complex polynomial $P$, its full shadow is the closure of the set of zeros of all derivatives of all powers $P^n$, and its limiting core is the Hausdorff limit, as $n\to\infty$, of the set of zeros of all derivatives of $P^n$. These sets retain geometric information that weak limits of root-counting measures discard. We determine complete zero-set limits for arrays of polynomials whose roots approach finitely many locations. A cluster containing $o(D)$ roots of a degree-$D$ polynomial can survive outside the limiting support of the derivative zeros, which depends only on the positive limiting masses: under repeated differentiation, the zeros it produces follow a straight path, selected by an explicit min--max condition, and preserve the cluster's exact multiplicity. When such a location instead carries a small positive mass $\varepsilon$, the support of the limiting zero distribution at a fixed ratio of derivative order to degree develops an arc on the $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ scale with a universal local semicircle profile. We use these mechanisms to prove that polynomial shadows can have robust and arbitrarily complicated topology. For every $k\ge2$, there are polynomials with $k+2$ distinct root locations whose limiting cores and full shadows have at least $\binom{k}{2}$ holes; this persists under coefficient perturbations and among square-free polynomials without a reflection axis. In a four-location family, the core and full-shadow areas tend to zero while one hole has area tending to $8/1221$.

data.title: Bounds on the minimum orbital period of general static spherical black holes: a sharp upper bound and a conditional lower bound
data.abstract: We investigate bounds on the minimum orbital period around four-dimensional general static spherical black holes. For all static spherically symmetric black holes with an event horizon, asymptotic flatness and non-negative energy density outside the horizon, we prove $T_{\min}\leq 6\sqrt{3}\,πM$. The bound is sharp and is saturated by the Schwarzschild solution. The lower bound requires an additional condition on the exterior matter: under the tangential pressure condition $p_τ\geq(κ/2)ρ$ with $κ>1$, imposed for all $r\geq r_{g}$, where $r_{g}$ is the largest radius at which $T(r)$ attains its global minimum, we prove $T_{\min}\geq c(κ)M$ with $c(κ)=6\sqrt{3}π(κ-1)\sqrt{κ+2}/κ^{3/2}$. In summary, both bounds apply to the same geometric class and differ only in what they demand of the matter: non-negative energy density suffices for the upper bound, while the lower bound is established under the additional tangential pressure condition.

data.title: Stochastic Minimum Spanning Tree Identification with Binary Weights
data.abstract: We introduce the Stochastic MST Identification Problem, with binary weights. In this problem, we need to identify a minimum spanning tree (MST) of a graph, each of whose edge weights is either 0 or 1. The weight of each edge $e$ is a random variable which is 1 with probability $p_e$ and 0 with probability $1-p_e$. The probability $p_e$ is given for each edge $e$, but the realized weight of an edge can only be determined by querying the edge. The problem is then to determine a strategy for querying the edges of the graph that minimizes the expected number of queries that need to be performed until we can identify a subset of edges that form an MST of the graph. We address both adaptive and non-adaptive versions of this problem. For the non-adaptive version of our Stochastic MST Identification problem, we give an $O(\log E)$-approximation algorithm via a reduction to submodular ranking. For the adaptive version, we show that solving the problem is trivial when all $p_e$ are equal to 1/2, because of a relation to the Tutte polynomial. However, computing the expected cost of an optimal querying strategy is #P-hard, even when all $p_e$ equal $\frac{1}{2}$. For arbitrary $p_e$ values, we present a constant-factor approximation algorithm for simple planar graphs. We investigate the question of whether the submodular goal value approach of Deshpande et al. could be used to achieve a $\log$-factor approximation algorithm that would work for arbitrary $p_e$ values and general graphs. In this context, we address the structural question of determining optimal submodular goal values for MST identification in graphs.

data.title: Hydrodynamic flow in the gut hinders the fixation of beneficial mutants but accelerates their invasion
data.abstract: Gut bacteria experience a spatially structured environment with hydrodynamic flow. Using a branching-process approach, we show that beneficial mutants arising randomly upon division have a reduced fixation probability compared to the well-mixed case. The suppression factor is set by the spatial heterogeneity of mutant fate across the gut. In contrast, the invasion of mutant lineages that avoid early stochastic extinction is accelerated in the gut compared to a matched well-mixed case. Stronger advective flow decreases fixation probabilities while accelerating mutant invasion.

data.title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
data.abstract: Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $ε$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $γ$ with confidence $1-δ$ needs $γ^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-ε)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1δ)$ samples up to constants depending on $ε$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/π(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $ε<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.

data.title: From Quantum Field Fluctuations to High-Redshift AGN: Semiclassical Origins of Halo Mass Function Constraints in the JWST Era
data.abstract: We develop a continuous framework connecting quantum field fluctuations in the early Universe to the abundance and observable properties of galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGN) at cosmic dawn. Beginning with quantum fields in curved Friedmann Lemaitre Robertson Walker spacetime, we follow inflationary vacuum fluctuations into the primordial curvature spectrum, linear matter power spectrum, mass variance $σ(M,z)$, mass peak height $ν(M,z)$, and the statistics of nonlinear halo formation. The Press-Schechter and Sheth-Tormen formalisms provide an analytic description of halo abundance and its dependence on peak rarity. A complementary high redshift halo mass function calibrated with the GUREFT simulations of Yung et al. (2024) provides a numerical description specifically constructed for the cosmic dawn regime probed by JWST. The comparison between these analytic and simulation calibrated prescriptions provides a direct measure of the sensitivity of predicted halo populations to the observations. We separate this cosmological supply of halos from the astrophysical and observational mappings that produce stars, ultraviolet luminosities, and active galactic nuclei. Controlled numerical experiments show that a percent level perturbation in the primordial fluctuation amplitude produces only a modest change in $σ$ and $ν$, but can strongly amplify the exponentially suppressed high $ν$ tail of the Halo Mass Function. This sensitivity increases toward high halo mass and high redshift, identifying rare cosmic dawn populations as potentially powerful probes of primordial statistics while simultaneously exposing the importance of uncertainties in halo abundance. High redshift AGN population statistics and the Ultraviolet Luminosity Function provide additional constraints on the primordial power spectrum and dynamics of primordial inflation theory.

data.title: The Generative Gap Between Speculative Drafter and Continuous Diffusion Language Model
data.abstract: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) and speculative drafters offer efficient language generation but are typically evaluated differently: CDLMs generate independently through iterative refinement, whereas drafters propose text for target-model verification and correction. We compare their architectures without verification, using LangFlow for CDLMs and adapting DSpark's Markov and recurrent-head architectures for standalone generation. All models are trained from scratch for unconditional, single-block OpenWebText generation at lengths 16, 128, and 1024, without target features or verification, using common preprocessing, backbone dimensions, and training-update budgets. We evaluate generation perplexity (GenPPL) with an external language model and distributional similarity to reference text with MAUVE. With default denoising steps equal to sequence length, LangFlow outperforms both DSpark variants on both metrics at lengths 128 and 1024, while DSpark-RNN leads at 16. A conditional KL analysis characterizes dependencies excluded by the Markov head's previous-token conditioning. Recurrent memory removes this restriction and improves both metrics, but the longer-sequence gap persists. Teacher probability matching further lowers Markov GenPPL without observed MAUVE gains. Increasing LangFlow's denoising steps at fixed weights improves both metrics at lengths 16 and 128, changing the length-128 ordering relative to DSpark-RNN. These results establish LangFlow's longer-sequence advantage under the evaluated budgets and highlight iterative full-sequence refinement as a route to improving standalone generation beyond gains from recurrent head memory.

data.title: Predictive Maintenance at the Edge: An Embedded Anomaly Detection Pipeline Trained with Quantum Optimization
data.abstract: This article presents a predictive-maintenance pipeline that detects anomalies in bearings from vibration signals, adapted for deployment at the edge on low-cost microcontrollers, and that uses quantum optimization in two steps of its training. The pipeline consists of a step of vibration feature extraction and a step of classification with a one-class support vector machine (OCSVM). The features are selected by minimum redundancy and maximum relevance (mRMR) with the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), under a limit on computing time. The OCSVM is adapted for inference at the edge without floating-point operations and is trained by a variational quantum algorithm with Pauli-correlation encoding (PCE). In small-scale tests on a simulator, with the Paderborn bearing dataset, the VQE found the optimal selection in 36% of the runs with Adam, and PCE chose better support vectors than chance, until a classical local search made the two equal. A classical baseline, the usual OCSVM trained by SMO with its weights rounded, matched them without any search.

data.title: Simple proofs of a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality and their extensions
data.abstract: We revisit the one-dimensional Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation inequality $$\|u'\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R})}\leq C\|u\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R})}^{1-a}\|u''\|_{L^r(\mathbb{R})}^{a},\qquad u\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}),\quad \tfrac12\leq a\leq 1,$$ and recall how its general form follows from the case $a=\frac12$ by interpolation with an endpoint estimate. For $a=\frac12$ and $p=q=r$, we give four alternative proofs, based on integration by parts (two proofs), on an ODE, and on the $L^p$ theory of singular integrals. The two proofs by integration by parts also cover most of the other admissible exponents. In $\mathbb{R}^N$, the integration by parts arguments give the inequality with explicit constants and, for $p\leq 2$, with the Laplacian in place of the Hessian and a constant independent of the dimension. For weighted measures $w(x)\,dx$, a pointwise version of the ODE argument gives the pointwise inequality $|\nabla u|^2\leq C_N\,Mu\,M(Δu)$, where $M$ is the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, and hence the inequality for Muckenhoupt weights, with the Laplacian and an explicit constant. The integration by parts arguments give it for homogeneous weights of large degree and for superharmonic weights. These results apply, in particular, to power weights and to monomial weights.

data.title: Anisotropic spin splitting in $α$-MnTe epilayers on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates
data.abstract: $α$-MnTe has emerged as a prototypical altermagnetic material, combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting. Here, we investigate the structural and electronic properties of epitaxial $α$-MnTe layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates. The crystalline and surface quality of the epilayers was characterised by reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), confirming the formation of high-quality, single-phase films. The transport measurements were performed, confirming an antiferromagnetic transition and weak ferromagnetism. The electronic structure was studied using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). At 90 K, both samples exhibit relativistic anisotropic valence band splitting, which is substantially larger along the $Γ$-K direction, reaching approximately 300 meV, than along $Γ$-M, where values of about 150~meV are observed. The magnitude and momentum dependence of the splitting are very similar for $α$-MnTe grown on the two different substrates, indicating the robustness of the altermagnetic electronic structure with respect to the epitaxial environment.

data.title: Search for $\mathrm{GeV}$-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
data.abstract: A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $0.228~\mathrm{nb}^{-1}$ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV. This is the first search for axion-like particles produced exclusively by two photons ($γγ\to a\toγγ$) in the forward direction. It extends sensitivity to previously unexplored regions of the parameter space, probing axion-like particle masses and couplings down to 3.0 GeV and $3.2\times10^{-4}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, respectively. This result provides the most stringent limits to date on the production of axion-like particles from exclusive photon-photon fusion processes with masses between 3 and 5 GeV.

data.title: Benchmarking One-Dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Methods on Quantum Hardware
data.abstract: Classical computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods encounter significant computational bottlenecks in large systems and at high Reynolds number flows due to the rapid increase in degrees of freedom, even on flagship supercomputers. As quantum computers emerge, the Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Method (QLBM) has been proposed as a quantum-native alternative for solving fluid dynamics problems. However, until recently, nearly all studies have relied on classical quantum simulators rather than real quantum hardware. This study presents a benchmark of a one-dimensional QLBM implementation executed on three different IBM Quantum hardware. We design and test a quantum circuit for the advection-diffusion equation using amplitude encoding, a Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK)-type collision operator, and a streaming step with periodic boundary conditions. Our numerical experiments evaluate transpiled two-qubit gate count, total circuit depth, runtime, and accuracy metrics including maximum absolute error ($L_\infty$ norm) and root-mean-square error (RMSE). We find that the present collision and streaming operators dominate the overall cost and become the primary scalability bottleneck on current hardware. To mitigate the prohibitive cost of full quantum state tomography on hardware-based benchmarking exercises, we introduce a sampler-based measurement strategy that reconstructs macroscopic density fields directly from computational-basis measurements. This approach substantially reduces measurement overhead while preserving the expected advection-diffusion dynamics on hardware. These results provide a quantitative assessment of QLBM performance in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) regime and identify the principal algorithmic and experimental limitations that must be addressed for QLBM to become viable for fluid dynamics.

data.title: Colloquium: Quantum information processing with ensembles of identical particles
data.abstract: Identical particles underpin most quantum technologies, but the role of indistinguishability in these processes extends far beyond the symmetrization of many-particle states. This Colloquium presents a unified operational perspective on how particle identity, indistinguishability, exchange statistics, and many-particle interference can instead be harnessed as resources for quantum information processing. We first clarify the notions of entanglement and indistinguishability for identical particles, emphasizing their dependence on the accessible measurements and information. We then review how spatial overlap, multiparticle interference, and path identity enable the generation, extraction, protection, and distillation of coherence and entanglement. Their applications to quantum metrology and imaging, state discrimination, teleportation, entanglement swapping, and quantum cloning are examined. Finally, we discuss the thermodynamic role of indistinguishability, from the Gibbs paradox to quantum thermal machines and statistics-driven engines. Across these settings, indistinguishability emerges as a controllable, task-dependent resource whose benefits are determined by state preparation, exchange statistics, interference, and measurement constraints.

data.title: Global and asymptotic properties of self-gravitating nonlinear sigma models
data.abstract: We present an analytical study of the global and asymptotic properties of static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat solutions in general relativity and its \(D\)-dimensional generalization with multiple minimally coupled scalar fields described by a general nonlinear sigma model. Assuming a complete Riemannian target space and a non-negative scalar potential satisfying suitable growth conditions, we prove that solutions remain regular at every finite nonzero radius and can be extended inward to a naked singularity at the center. In particular, this excludes singularities on spherical shells at finite radius. We further show that all solutions exhibit universal asymptotic behavior near the central singularity. Finally, we demonstrate that these spacetimes can possess at most one photon sphere, which, if present, is necessarily unstable.

data.title: Modules with unbalanced support
data.abstract: A finitely generated module has unbalanced support if its support has positive dimension but meets a top-dimensional component of the spectrum only at the closed point. We ask what homological signals are left behind by this geometry. Separating the spectrum into two wings, we prove first Tor nonvanishing for positive-depth modules and give criteria for second Tor nonvanishing. In depth zero, we obtain a structural sequence describing the finite-length torsion under a first Tor vanishing. A recent counterexample to the Peskine--Szpiro dimension inequality conjecture establishes the existence of modules of finite projective dimension and unbalanced support \cite{Ma}. We apply our framework to these modules and establish a numerical torsion--spine balance for linked Cohen--Macaulay wings. We also construct such modules over a reduced Gorenstein ring with exactly two irreducible components.

data.title: Remark About Action for Rastall Gravity
data.abstract: In this short note we study Rastall gravity action as was proposed by Golovnev in [7]. We construct its reparametrization invariant form and determine corresponding equations of motion.

data.title: ProdCrawl: A Replayable Test Collection for Focused Crawling
data.abstract: A focused crawler searches for web pages on a specific topic under a constrained download budget. Since it can only fetch a limited number of pages, its success depends on choosing which links to follow. Focused crawlers are usually evaluated on live websites by harvest rate, the fraction of downloaded pages that are relevant. This has two problems: on the one hand, websites change over time, so a crawl cannot be repeated under the same conditions; on the other hand, there is no ground truth for which pages are relevant. As a result, comparisons between crawlers are unreliable. We present ProdCrawl, a replayable test collection for focused crawling. It comprises static mirrors of 621 company and organization websites, about 1.1 million pages, with each page labeled as a product page or non-product page based on a majority vote among three large language models. Any crawler can be run on exactly the same sites and scored against the same labels. We use ProdCrawl to compare simple baselines (breadth-first, depth-first and text classifiers) with an approach that scores each link by searching for similar link texts whose target pages have already been labeled. Our results show that text classifiers and keyword matching do not significantly outperform breadth-first crawling, whereas neural embeddings, which compare link texts by semantic meaning, outperform all simple strategies. Because every run evaluates over identical pages and labels, these results are exactly reproducible. The collection, codebase, and models are publicly released to support experimental replication and fair crawler comparison.

data.title: Maxwell-Consistent 3-D Magnetic Field Camera using Scalar-Potential-Based Reconstruction
data.abstract: Various applications require accurate 3-D characterization of magnetic fields with high spatial and temporal resolution. Building on our previously introduced spherical magnetic field camera employing 86 three-axis Hall sensors arranged on a spherical surface, we present a novel magnetic-field reconstruction approach based on the magnetic scalar potential and its spherical harmonic expansion. Unlike the previous reconstruction method that expands each vector component separately, our scalar-potential-based formulation is inherently consistent with Maxwell's equations for source-free fields by design, yielding curl-free and divergence-free field models. Using a simulated magnetic gradient field generated by two permanent magnets, we demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher reconstruction accuracy, improved robustness to sensor noise and failure, and substantially reduced non-physical divergence and curl compared to the component-wise baseline. Furthermore, the scalar-potential approach attains superior performance with fewer coefficients, indicating a more efficient use of measurement data allowing higher-degree polynomial representations.

data.title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
data.abstract: Scientific foundation models (SciFMs) have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of PDEs, including the ability to efficiently adapt to unseen data distributions with additional finetuning. As with all neural architectures, finetuning such models comes with the risk of catastrophic forgetting, whereby adapting to new tasks degrades prior knowledge of the model. We study catastrophic forgetting in Walrus-1.3B, a SciFM for continuum dynamics, over the course of a two-stage sim-to-real adaptation: first finetuning on simulated flow around a cylinder and then adapting to experimental data of the same system. We find that finetuning on the simulations rapidly degrades rollout performance on the original pretraining datasets, with one-step errors increasing up to 35x after just 20 epochs. Subsequent adaptation to real data further erodes performance on the simulated task. We characterize the potential drivers of forgetting, such as dataset dependence and task representation similarity. We then show that replaying as little as 1% simulated data during real-data finetuning recovers most of the lost simulation performance while retaining effective adaptation to the experimental dynamics. Our results identify catastrophic forgetting as a practical obstacle to sim-to-real adaptation of SciFMs and show that lightweight replay strategies significantly improve retention.

data.title: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation
data.abstract: Training a large language model is compute-bound, and current recipes divide the work between optimizers by hand: orthogonalized momentum for attention and MLP matrices, Adam-style updates for the rest. This division rests on human priors about which layer type deserves which geometry, and it fixes a single global update budget that every parameter block shares. We introduce FARO, a function-space adaptive optimizer that makes the partition of parameters into blocks the unit of decision. FARO gives each block a geometry by its realized counterfactual return, then freezes the routes and reallocates the frozen per-block budget by cross-block equal risk contribution (ERC), the risk-parity principle from portfolio theory. On a GPT-style model trained on FineWeb, the framework gives two results. First, its FARO-Adaptive arm reaches 3.2780 nats at the full schedule, matching NorMuonAndAdam (3.2794), the best hand-designed recipe: it recovers the human prior without hand-setting per-layer geometry. Second, FARO-ERC improves on that arm: it lowers the clean-data loss at every one of 6 seeds, by 0.0136 nats on average, a modest but robust gain. Its sign test, paired test, and confidence interval all agree, and it exceeds the measured run-to-run noise at no added time or memory. It works by trimming the riskiest blocks rather than expanding the safest, and it holds up under a corrupted stream, still lowering the mean loss and winning the seed majority. The source code is available at https://github.com/wxj630/FARO.

data.title: Generic properties of the Laplace spectrum and eigenfunctions
data.abstract: We prove that the spectrum of the Laplace--Beltrami operator on compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary is generically linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we prove that pointwise products of eigenfunctions generically are linearly independent. The proof is based on conformal perturbations of the metric. The result implies in particular that generically the truncation of the continuous functions on $M$ by spectral projections of the Laplace operator is given by symmetric matrices.

data.title: On the factorization graph of finite groups
data.abstract: Given a finite group $G$, the factorization graph $Γ(G)$ has as vertices the nontrivial proper subgroups of $G$, with two distinct vertices $H$ and $K$ adjacent if and only if $HK = G$. In this paper, we study structural and combinatorial properties of $Γ(G)$ for three families of groups: cyclic groups of square-free order, generalized quaternion groups, and dicyclic groups. For cyclic groups $C_{p_1\cdots p_r}$, we describe the global structure of $Γ(G)$ and determine its order, degree sequence, center, girth, and diameter. We also characterize completely when $Γ(G)$ is claw-free, show that it is non-planar for $r \geq 4$, and prove that after removing all pendant vertices, the resulting induced subgraph is 2-connected; we further compute its exact circumference for small $r$, showing it is Hamiltonian precisely when $r=4, 5$. For generalized quaternion groups, we classify all isolated vertices and prove that the reduced factorization graph has diameter two and a unique central vertex. Moreover, we show that it is planar, has chromatic number~$3$, is Eulerian, and non-Hamiltonian, and that it contains maximal induced stars and triangular book subgraphs. Finally, we analyze the dicyclic case and show that the reduced factorization graph is a complete bipartite graph, from which all main invariants follow directly. An explicit SageMath algorithm for constructing $Γ(G)$ is included.

data.title: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs
data.abstract: We study first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. For strongly observable graphs, [ACBDK15] establishes a minimax regret of $\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{αT})$, where $α$ denotes the independence number of the graph and $T$ denotes the horizon. On the other hand, the best existing first-order bound scales as $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{(κ+1) L^\star})$ [LLZ20], where $κ$ denotes the clique partition number, satisfying $κ+1\geqα$, and $L^\star$ denotes the cumulative loss of the best arm, leaving a gap between the graph dependence in worst-case and first-order guarantees. In this paper, we bridge this gap by obtaining an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$. Our first result is an algorithm for the special case of self-aware graphs, in which every vertex has a self-loop. The algorithm combines the update of EXP3 [ACBFS02] with a sampling rule inspired by exploration by optimization [LS20]. More specifically, we construct a map whose fixed points yield sampling distributions that control the one-round regret remainder in terms of the learner's loss and the graph's independence number, which is crucial in deriving optimal first-order guarantees. We further show that a sufficiently accurate fixed point can be computed in polynomial time by a geometrically convergent iteration. Finally, we extend the algorithm to general strongly observable graphs and achieve the same $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ guarantee by adapting the two-level aggregation approach of [LLZ20].

data.title: Theory of Convective Diffusion
data.abstract: We obtain a hydrodynamic theory of diffusive-scale dynamics in one-dimensional systems with interacting sound modes in the absence of self-interactions. Chaotic systems generically feature three distinct Gaussian relaxation processes: besides normal diffusion, driven by microscopic noise stemming from fast-decaying non-hydrodynamic modes, collisions between sound modes lead to two additional channels: convective diffusion manifesting as an effective multiplicative temporal noise, and an effective additive noise generated by the surrounding hydrodynamic modes. Our theory also includes, as a subclass, integrable systems described by generalized hydrodynamics, representing a pure realization of convective diffusion. Focusing on convective diffusion, we obtain an exact closed-form expression for the higher-point dynamical correlation functions and contrast their structure with those of normal diffusion. Additionally, we show that in convective diffusion each sound mode features a universal non-Gaussian distribution of charge transfer in its comoving frame, thereby establishing anomalous fluctuations as a characteristic feature of diffusive-scale dynamics in integrable systems.

data.title: The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture is true
data.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group. A nowhere-zero $A$-flow of a graph gives every edge a direction and a non-zero value in $A$, so that at every vertex the sum of the values on the entering edges equals the sum on the leaving edges.
