Supporting this view, accelerated models are markedly more sensitive to perturbations of $α$, and their gate geometry reflects semantic relationships among classes. We further introduce the normalized participation ratio (nPR) to characterize the channel-wise organization of the gates and find that, across REPA teachers, projector architectures, and radial-objective targets, broader gate participation accompanies better generation quality. Guided by this insight, we propose a simple teacher-free radial objective that promotes broader gate participation through feature-norm regularization, without pairwise feature comparisons. On ImageNet $256\times256$ with SiT-B/2, our method improves FID over dispersive loss while increasing mean gate participation over timesteps and classes, further supporting the link between gate organization and training acceleration. Our results identify residual-gate reorganization as a measurable axis of diffusion training acceleration and suggest a simple direction for further acceleration.

data.title: Higher limits over the fusion orbit category via subgroup complexes
data.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a saturated fusion system over a finite $p$-group $S$, and $\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})$ denote the centric orbit category of $\mathcal{F}$. Suppose that $G$ is a discrete group realizing $\mathcal{F}$, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the collection of all $p$-centric subgroups in $G$. We prove that for every $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)} \mathcal{O} ^c (\mathcal{F})$-module $M$, the higher limits $\lim ^* _{\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})} M$ are isomorphic to the equivariant cohomology $H_ G ^* (|\mathcal{C}| ; \mathcal{M} )$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is the $G$-equivariant coefficient system on $|\mathcal{C}|$ induced by $M$. This is the fusion system version of a theorem by Grodal for higher limits over the $p$-orbit category $\mathcal{O}_p(G)$ of a finite group $G$. As a consequence, for every fusion system $\mathcal{F}$, we obtain a finite sequence of cohomology groups, involving the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}$, which is exact if and only if the mod-$p$ subgroup decomposition for $\mathcal{F}$ over $\mathcal{F}$-centric subgroups is sharp.

data.title: Nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic model for the stress-strain and stress-relaxation in metallic glass
data.abstract: We develop a nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic (VEP) model for the stress-strain response of metallic glasses by connecting the deformation dynamics with the material relaxation time obtained from independent stress-relaxation measurements. The material is modeled as a Maxwell-type element, with a nonlinear elastic spring and a stretched-exponential dashpot whose behavior is determined from the separate stress-relaxation data. The model captures the effects of temperature and strain rate on the initial elastic response, stress overshoot, post-yield softening, and steady flow. We independently determine the reference material-time function $X_0(\varepsilon)$ from the stress-relaxation response and the nonlinear material-time variable $X(\varepsilon)$ from the elastic-viscoplastic strain decomposition based on the stress-strain response. We introduce an Eyring-type function or material-time ratio $φ(\varepsilon)=X(\varepsilon)/X_0(\varepsilon)$ which quantifies the change of relaxation dynamics during nonlinear deformation. Our model provides a simple connection between structural relaxation and yielding in metallic glasses.

data.title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
data.abstract: Large language models act only through the infrastructure that surrounds them. That infrastructure, the harness, determines what a model can accomplish and how it fails, yet it has no settled definition. To address this gap, we decompose the harness into eight functional components that can be specified and compared across systems, and we propose a portable specification framework that records which model ran in which harness. The record is needed because different harness configurations can yield several-fold differences in reported scores for the same model, and because much of an agent's attack surface lies in its harness. Existing model cards and agent cards provide release and operational information, but do not establish the sequence of effective configurations within a run. Harnesses can change between releases and between runs, and, where agents edit their own tools and configuration, within a run. Enacted AI laws contain documentation duties relevant to covered systems, subject to their respective scopes and application dates, but do not prescribe the common harness record proposed here. Therefore, the harness has to be explicitly described and specified as a versioned part of the system.

data.title: Fast and Accurate Hydro Unit Commitment
data.abstract: We introduce a fast novel algorithm to commit hydro-generators. We show that our algorithm can commit 56 generators for 200 days 10,000 times faster than Hexaly, the leading commercial solver for scheduling problems, without sacrificing solution quality. Our method can commit 1792 generators for an entire year in approximately 20 seconds on commodity hardware. Hexaly is unable to solve problems of this size in reasonable time. We attain this runtime improvement by introducing a greedy-heuristic tailored for hydro units. We provide a direction for a possible proof that the error our solver makes decreases with the problem size. This is supported by our experimental results. We prove that our solver's runtime scales log-linearly in the number of generators and time periods.

data.title: Approximate Dynamic Programming for Link Reconfiguration to Reduce Malicious Input Controllability in Consensus Networks
data.abstract: Communication links influence how strongly a malicious input at one sensor affects a consensus network. We study how a defender can reduce this influence by selecting one additional link after observing the currently attacked sensor. The attacked sensor changes over time, and vulnerability is measured by the trace of a finite-horizon controllability Gramian. A prescribed local epsilon-greedy attacker response rule defines a discounted Markov decision process for the defender. Exact dynamic programming (DP) provides an optimal policy using the full Gramian payoff matrix and attacker transition model. We then introduce approximate dynamic programming (ADP) that learns from sampled attacker transitions and empirical Gramian costs estimated from measured impulse responses. Under conditionally unbiased costs and standard sampling and learning-rate conditions, the learned action-value table converges to the exact DP solution. The analysis uses Bellman contraction and bounds the effect of persistent Gramian estimation bias, establishing when measured responses recover optimal defender decisions without constructing the full payoff matrix. In simulations on 20- and 100-node graphs, empirical ADP rollout costs are within 0.23% and 1.76%, respectively, of exact DP. In a two-dimensional intruder tracking example, both policies reduce network-wide root-mean-square tracking error spread by approximately 25% relative to an unmitigated attack.

data.title: Spectral Convergence of the Discrete Steklov Problem
data.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Schur complement $\textbf{S}$ of the graph Laplacian, defined on vertices sampled from a domain with $C^2$ boundary. We use a thin boundary layer to approximate the continuum boundary as the number of vertices increases and rely on transportation theory to justify the consistency of a discrete Steklov problem. In particular, $\textbf{S}$ acts on vectors defined over the shrinking boundary layer but behaves asymptotically like a known operator. In this paper, we use a variational argument to determine conditions for which the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $\textbf{S}$ converge to the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, and we provide evidence of this spectral convergence through a numerical example.

data.title: Robot Navigation and Canine Welfare: A Pilot Study Surfacing Challenges for Cross-Species Legibility and Proxy Validity in Animal-Machine Interaction
data.abstract: Autonomous delivery robots increasingly share residential spaces with companion animals, yet navigation behavior is rarely designed with animal welfare in mind. This paper presents a pilot study evaluating a curve-out maneuver, a laterally arcing pass-by trajectory triggered at the dog's alert distance, proposed as a candidate welfare-informed navigation intervention grounded in canine social communication research and legible motion theory. Following a research through design approach, we developed and evaluated a first design iteration of the artifact in a naturalistic home environment with a companion dog. Contrary to our hypothesis, the curve-out produced a more acute stress response than the straight-line baseline. We argue that discontinuous execution limitation, the robot stopping and reorienting multiple times to approximate the arc, undermined legibility, which in itself became a stressor. The pilot surfaces the legibility of robot behavior to non-humans' eyes and proxy stimulus validity as structural challenges for AMI and repositions the design problem for future work.

data.title: Confidence-Modulated Safety Filtering for End-to-End Policies
data.abstract: End-to-end policies, from task-specific controllers to robot foundation models, learn complex behavior from raw observations but are not guaranteed to remain safe, so they are often wrapped in a safety filter. The resulting system operates under two domains: the filter's operational design domain (ODD), where its assumptions hold and safety is certified, and the policy's competence domain, where it is reliable. Filters typically fix their conservativeness regardless of the policy's competence, trading performance inside the ODD against margin beyond it. We ask whether the policy's confidence should set that level, and propose a filter-agnostic pipeline that modulates it at runtime: inside the ODD, where every setting is safe, confidence buys performance; beyond it, low confidence adds margin, which helps when it flags where the filter's model fails. Preliminary F1TENTH simulations, where this holds, show the modulated filter combining the strengths of permissive and conservative filters.

data.title: Construction and Commissioning of a Compact Xenon Gas Recycling System for a High-Harmonic Generation VUV Frequency Comb
data.abstract: A compact, closed-loop xenon recycling system for application in a High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) Vacuum-UV (VUV) frequency comb laser systems is designed, constructed and commissioned. It consists of three main sections, a low-pressure section (LPS) pre-filtering the gas of particulates, water and hydrocarbons, then a compression station (CS), allowing for a variable pressure of up to 60 bar, and a high-pressure section (HPS) with more filtering, pressure control and monitoring. The system proves to meet all design criteria in gas quality (the sum off all hydrocarbon contaminations up to 120 amu and CO$_{2}$ being below 10$^{-8}$ mbar) and recovery efficiency (>99.8$\%$ for all expected operational cases, neglecting possible geometric gas catcher losses in the HHG laser itself). The operation and results are presented and discussed. Furthermore, the system is compared to the performance of a similar system from which it is derived.

data.title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
data.abstract: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.

data.title: Scaling Limits as Extensions of Continuous Bundles of C*-algebras
data.abstract: We analyze scaling limits in algebraic quantum field theory using continuous bundles of C*-algebras. Different conditions of continuity on such bundles encode different strengths of approximation of the theory by its scaling limit. As a proof of concept, we consider the small-distance scaling limit of the theory of a massive free scalar field, which corresponds to a massless free scalar field. We provide a number of examples of local algebras of observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is merely lower semicontinuous. Further, we construct an algebra of nonlocal observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is uniformly continuous.

data.title: Equipartition between Alfvénic turbulence and energetic ions as the origin of the -5 common spectrum in the heliosphere
data.abstract: Suprathermal ion tails throughout the heliosphere follow a ``common spectrum,'' $f(v)\propto v^{-5}$. We show that scale-by-scale equipartition between strong Alfvénic turbulence and the ions it accelerates predicts both this exponent and the absolute amplitude, $F(v)=B^2/(16π^3 m_i v^5)$, with no free parameters. The prediction agrees within a factor of a few with ACE and Voyager 1 spectra across three decades in magnetic energy. We argue that this saturated level is reached where strong turbulence accelerates particles locally; quiet-time tails lie well below it, consistent with nonlocal acceleration.

data.title: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Effective Multi-Turn Jailbreak
data.abstract: Automated red teaming trains an attacker large language model (LLM) to elicit harmful responses from a victim LLM, but reinforcement learning can collapse attackers onto a narrow set of prompts when attack success is the only reward. Such a collapse of attack diversity can bias safety evaluation toward repeatedly testing near-duplicate attack patterns rather than the underlying harmful intents. Existing methods often trade off attack success or inference cost for greater content or strategy diversity. We propose CoFiBreak, a coarse-to-fine diversity reward for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that improves attack diversity while preserving strong attack effectiveness and low inference cost. The coarse reward broadens which strategies the attacker uses by encouraging strategies underrepresented within each GRPO group, while the fine reward broadens how those strategies are realized by discouraging reuse of the same personas, framings, and output formats after harmful-intent information is removed from prompt embeddings. Diversity rewards apply only to attacks that already exceed an effectiveness threshold, so diversity cannot be gained through ineffective attacks. Since both rewards are computed only during training, CoFiBreak also retains inference efficiency. Trained with Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as the victim, CoFiBreak discovers 1.6-2.0x as many distinct successful fine-grained strategies as the strongest baseline across frontier victims on HarmBench. It reaches 98.8% ASR@10 (attack success rate with 10 generations per intent) on AdvBench with the highest diversity score among all compared methods, which is 2.1x that of the strongest-attacking baseline. The resulting attacks transfer to unseen frontier LLMs, reaching 71.0% ASR@10 on AdvBench with the unseen victim Claude-Opus-4.6. The code will be released.

data.title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
data.abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model agents by sampling and selecting among multiple candidate trajectories, but common realizations assume that these trajectories can be executed in parallel. This assumption breaks in realistic deployments, where enterprise workspaces and cloud services are shared and persistent, costly or infeasible to replicate, and actions may introduce irreversible side effects or cross-trajectory interference. Existing generative world models avoid direct execution, but typically compress environment state into a single prompt, limiting their ability to reliably simulate transitions under partial observability. Instead, we introduce Agentic World Modeling (AWM), which reformulates next-observation prediction as a multi-turn evidence-acquisition task. For each hypothetical action, an agentic simulator adaptively queries the real environment through safe read-only interfaces, reasons over the returned evidence, and uses executable computation to construct the resulting observation without mutating shared state. Integrated with trajectory-level TTS, AWM enables parallel exploration over a single shared environment. Across $τ$-bench, AppWorld, and OfficeBench, AWM outperforms a single-shot simulation baseline by 40.07% on average, and surpasses a trained world-model baseline by 12.36% on average. These results establish interactive, read-grounded simulation as a practical foundation for safe and scalable agentic test-time scaling in shared, non-resettable environments.

data.title: LiHA: Worse is Better for Lightweight Hash-based Source Authentication
data.abstract: The omission of source IP authentication remains a fundamental vulnerability in the Internet. Existing approaches rely on routing plausibility, topology assumptions, per-flow state, or wide deployment. These requirements have kept strong source authentication out of the data plane. As simplicity is the key to deployability, we present LiHA, a lightweight source authentication mechanism built around operations that routers already perform efficiently. LiHA binds secret keys to source prefixes using longest prefix match and authenticates each packet with a single message authentication code (MAC). The data plane requires no handshakes, per-flow state, or per-packet control plane access. A sender performs one prefix lookup and one fixed-size hash. The verifier repeats the same operations and forwards the packet only if the MAC matches. LiHA is designed for incremental deployment. It primarily protects against off-path attackers that spoof source prefixes they do not control. An on-path attacker can replay valid authenticated packets until the key rotates. LiHA does not eliminate every denial-of-service threat. Instead, it confines accepted traffic to authenticated source prefix space within participating networks. We argue that simpler source authentication with clear limits is more likely to be deployed. We implemented LiHA in three environments: as a set of user-space libraries, as eBPF programs, and in an FPGA. We found that the user-space implementation had very high overheads. The eBPF implementation got reasonable single thread performance even with a software based cryptographic hash. We found that only the FPGA could obtain 100 Gbps single thread performance, but that was only when bypassing the kernel using a DPDK user-level networking stack.

data.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
data.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

data.title: Adaptive Personalization Under Preference Epistemic Uncertainty
data.abstract: Human preferences change over time: an established preference may remain valid over time, become uncertain as context shifts, or be explicitly revised. Effective personalization requires conversational AI to adapt its response strategy to evolving preferences rather than relying on passive memory retrieval. We formalize this capability as adaptive personalization under epistemic uncertainty. A human preference study further confirms that people favor state-contingent response strategies as preference uncertainty changes. To evaluate whether language models mirror this adaptation, we create a multilingual benchmark spanning 250 personas, 5 languages, and 25K conversational turns that decouples strategy selection from response execution. Across eight closed- and open-weight models, we uncover a recognition-generation gap: models reliably identify appropriate strategies when selecting among candidate options, but collapse during open-ended generation, suffering a 35-46% drop in strategy calibration. Crucially, this failure is systematic: models default to exploit-first behavior, over-relying on existing preferences regardless of preference epistemic uncertainty. We show this failure is addressable: while prompting interventions fail, targeted training that supervises models' internal strategy representations toward state-conditional human preferences narrows the user acceptability generalization gap by a third on out-of-distribution personas and conversational styles.

data.title: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers via Multi-Step Backward Losses
data.abstract: Can learned latent dynamics models support the design of feedback controllers that provably stabilize the original system? For linear time-invariant systems, we show that learning linear autoencoders and latent dynamics with multi-step prediction-reconstruction losses $\unicode{x2014}$ which we term "backward losses" as they encourage latent trajectories to reconstruct full state trajectories $\unicode{x2014}$ provably recovers the structure needed for stabilization. Specifically, a sufficiently long reconstruction horizon ensures that a minimum ${H}_\infty$-norm controller designed using the learned latent model stabilizes the original system through output-feedback via the corresponding encoder, provided the latent dimension is large enough to capture all non-stable modes of the underlying system. We also show why both reconstruction and a multi-step horizon are essential: forward prediction losses that require only low prediction error along latent trajectories admit global loss minimizers that discard unstable modes regardless of horizon length, while single-step reconstruction losses can yield latent models whose stabilizing controllers fail to stabilize the original system. Finally, experiments on a non-linear flexible-arm system illustrate the practical implications of our results for learning non-linear autoencoders and latent dynamics.

data.title: HippocamFLEX: FPGA Prototyping of Hippocampus-Inspired Architecture for Context-Aware Sequence Prediction
data.abstract: Unlike conventional architectures that treat memory as static pattern storage, the hippocampus organizes experience as ordered sequences and retrieves them through temporally compressed replay spanning prior, current, and anticipated states. This capacity of context-appropriate sequence prediction remains absent from conventional deep learning accelerators and existing neuromorphic fabrics. We present HippocamFLEX, a fully synthesizable digital implementation of these hippocampal computational principles, realized with SystemVerilog RTL on the AMD Zynq UltraScale+,XCZU9EG. The design maps the hippocampal trisynaptic pathway onto three pipeline stages: a Dentate Gyrus / Entorhinal Cortex (DG/EC) stage for hypervector proximity matching, a CA3 stage for context-gated recurrent sequence prediction with multi-phase temporal tagging, and a CA1 stage that integrates past, present, and predicted future events into a theta-sequence inspired output. While much brain-inspired hardware relies on analog mixed-signal design for energy efficiency, this work targets FPGA prototyping as a deliberate architectural choice: FPGAs offer rapid design-space exploration without tape-out cost, bit-exact determinism that simplifies verification. The design supports 64 events across 16 contexts and is verified on physical silicon across context-isolation, temporal-ordering, and mid-sequence sliding-window test cases and is inherently scalable to larger event and context sets.

data.title: An analytical framework for wave-coherent airflow over fast surface waves
data.abstract: Classical theories attribute wind-wave momentum transfer to a critical layer, where the mean wind speed equals the wave phase speed. For waves that travel faster than the near-surface wind, this layer may lie outside the wave boundary layer or be absent altogether. We develop an analytical description of the wave-coherent airflow in this regime for a prescribed mean wind, using a Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin--Jeffreys (WKBJ) approximation to the viscous Orr--Sommerfeld equation in wave-following coordinates. The solution combines an outer Rayleigh mode, which carries the dominant wave-coherent motion, with a thin viscous Stokes layer that supplies the phase shift producing the pressure form stress. At leading order, the form stress scales with the inverse square root of the wave Reynolds number, with a coefficient set by an integral of the outer response, and transfers momentum from the waves to the air. For an exponential mean profile, the WKBJ approximation gives closed-form expressions for the wave-coherent response. To accommodate the rapid near-surface variation of realistic wall-bounded profiles, we develop a long-wave expansion near the surface and match it to the outer WKBJ mode (LW--WKBJ). For wall-modelled simulations, whose first resolved level lies above the viscous sublayer, we replace the molecular viscosity in the Stokes layer with a constant-stress effective viscosity. Using mean profiles from direct numerical simulations and wave-phase-resolved large-eddy simulations, the LW--WKBJ framework closely reproduces the dominant wave-coherent velocity and pressure obtained from numerical solutions and available simulation data. The predicted form-stress coefficients also agree well with the available LES estimates.

data.title: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding and Building "Any-task inference" Capable Foundation Models
data.abstract: In this work, we provide a formal framework and mathematical definition for the subset of foundation models focused on enabling the property of "any-task inference" (ATI) (similar to zero-shot inference), rather than those designed for pre-training fine-tuning. To achieve this mathematical definition, we formalize the notion of a "space of tasks of interest," which we include in the problem domain, then provide an interface-based formal definition for ATI foundation models as those that map samples of data $x$ and tasks $t$ to predictions over the space of labels directly. While simple, this definition allows us to show that all ATI foundation models can be decomposed through a "universal task reduction" lens into encoder, model, and decoder aspects. We can leverage this decomposition to also decompose foundation model error into terms corresponding to different aspects of this reduction, stratified into a collection of "design terms," which are theoretical properties that can inform one of whether a particular proposed ATI foundation model can achieve optimality or not due to the structure of the proposed task reduction, and "realized model excess" terms which capture interactions between learned and programmatic components of foundation model systems. Lastly, we can use this perspective to offer two "prototypical" recipes for realizing ATI foundation models in diverse domains, which we term generative and discriminative variants of ATI foundation models. This exercise is grounded throughout by 5 real-world examples of foundation models in different settings, varying greatly in how these capabilities are realized, showing the applicability of this definition to real-world settings.

data.title: Global and crustal properties of neutron stars
data.abstract: We investigate how the treatment of the neutron star crust affects both the global properties of the star and the properties of the crust itself. Three approaches are compared: a direct connection between a fixed crust and the core equation of state (EOS), a smooth crossover between them, and a unified EOS in which the crust is computed within a compressible liquid-drop model with the same nuclear empirical parameters of the relativistic mean-field model used for the core. For each approach, we consider four values of the symmetry energy slope, $44 \le L \le 92$ MeV. For a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star, some global properties are weakly to moderately affected: the radius and the moment of inertia agree within 1\% among the three approaches. On the other hand, the tidal deformability obtained with the direct connection is up to 21\% lower than the unified one for $L = 92$ MeV. A much larger contrast comes from the crustal properties. Relative to the unified EOS, the direct connection yields a crust that is 15--36\% thinner, 6--12 times less massive, and that carries a fraction of the total moment of inertia 5--8 times smaller (0.3--1.1\% instead of 2.8--6.2\%). The differences between crust treatments are thus comparable to or larger than those arising from variations in $L$ for crustal properties, while they remain subleading for global ones.

data.title: Let LiDAR Decide Where to Look: Geometry-Measured Token Selection for Efficient Sparse Latent World Models
data.abstract: Vision-centric autonomous driving models encode thousands of image tokens per frame, yet most depict sky, buildings, or empty road---content irrelevant to planning. Worse, these tokens dilute the planner's attention: we show that randomly discarding 75% of tokens already outperforms the dense model, because the planner can concentrate on the remaining driving-critical content. Building on this finding, we present Geometry-Aware Token Selection (GATS), which uses LiDAR and radar point projections to select a small fraction of image tokens before the vision backbone runs. Because the selector operates on measured 3D geometry rather than visual features, the backbone encodes only the selected patches, cutting end-to-end FLOPs by up to $18\times$. Each kept token receives a 3D anchor from its LiDAR point and is fed to a self-supervised latent world model that predicts future features and 3D displacements without box annotations. At 25% budget, GATS achieves a 3-sec L2 displacement error of 0.520 m on nuScenes and an EPDMS of 88.9 on NAVSIM---surpassing the dense baseline (0.573 m / 85.9) at $6.6\times$ fewer total FLOPs. At an extreme 10% budget (24 GFLOPs, $18\times$ reduction), it still beats the dense baseline on both nuScenes (0.537 m vs. 0.573 m L2) and NAVSIM (87.9 vs. 85.9 EPDMS). On 739 intent-critical scenarios, GATS covers 95.8% of hazardous vehicles and achieves a 0.09% collision rate---73.5% lower than the dense model (0.34%).

data.title: Fair Recommender Systems for Intersecting Groups
data.abstract: Recommendation systems that optimize for the average user can fail to capture the preferences of diverse demographic groups. We consider a dynamic recommendation system, where arriving users can belong to different demographic groups. Importantly, these groups can intersect, and a user may belong to several groups. We first show that over time, any group-blind policy (which excludes all current-user group information) recommending $K \geq 1$ items incurs linear total regret under mild conditions. In turn, we introduce three group-aware algorithms based on the classical Upper Confidence Bound algorithm (UCB): i) Intersection-Fitting, which runs UCB on each intersection, but has a sublinear group- and intersection-level regret guarantee with an exponential dependence in the number of groups; and ii) two group-level heuristics, Inner-Outer UCB and Group-Item UCB which allocate different arms to different groups, and use a sleeping expert meta-learner to choose which active group's recommendation an intersection should inherit at any given time step. We provide experimental results on two datasets, Goodreads and BoardGameGeek, and highlight that our heuristics can be preferable to the intersection-fitting algorithm when intersection-level preferences are closely related to group-level preferences, but that intersection-fitting performs better when different intersections within a same group prefer different items.

data.title: The Size-Mass Relation and Inside-Out Quenching of Massive Quiescent Galaxies at $2<z<3$ with JWST PRIMER and MINERVA
data.abstract: We investigate the morphology, size--mass relations, and spatially resolved star formation histories of 26 massive quiescent galaxies at cosmic noon ($2 < z < 3$) in the Ultra-Deep Survey field using deep JWST NIRCam imaging from the PRIMER and MINERVA surveys. Combining 16 broadband and medium-band filters with empirical point spread function matching, we perform single-Sérsic modeling and bulge--disk decompositions with pysersic across six filters (F115W to F444W), alongside Bayesian size--mass fitting with dynesty. In the rest-frame optical (F200W), the size--mass relation exhibits a steep slope of $α= 0.59 \pm 0.12$ and effective radius of $A = 0.83_{-0.07}^{+0.08}\ \mathrm{kpc}$ at $M_* = 5 \times 10^{10}\ M_\odot$. In the rest-frame near-infrared (F356W), we derive $α= 0.56 \pm 0.13$ and a more compact radius of $A = 0.70_{-0.06}^{+0.07}\ \mathrm{kpc}$. Galaxy sizes shrink by $\approx 22\%$ from F115W to F444W, reflecting negative color gradients and centrally concentrated mass profiles. Two-thirds of the sample are bulge-dominated ($B/T \ge 0.5$), whereas one-third are disk-dominated. Central bulges are ultra-compact ($R_{e,\mathrm{Bulge}} \approx 0.49\ \mathrm{kpc}$) with negligible mass dependence, whereas outer disks extend to $R_{e,\mathrm{Disk}} \approx 1.4\text{--}1.5\ \mathrm{kpc}$. Resolved spectral energy distribution modeling with piXedfit demonstrates positive radial specific star formation rate gradients and inner regions that formed at least $\approx 0.7\ \mathrm{Gyr}$ earlier and quenched faster than their outskirts. These results confirm inside-out quenching, consistent with dissipative gas compaction assembling the dense core, active galactic nucleus feedback halting central star formation, and the compact bulge dynamically stabilizing the surviving disk against fragmentation.

data.title: DiRAFT: Privacy-Aware Financial Transcript Synthesis from Aggregate Discourse Priors
data.abstract: Using customer conversations to train and evaluate financial language models raises confidentiality concerns because non-public financial facts can remain after direct identifiers are masked. Synthetic transcripts offer an alternative data source, but their discourse fidelity and residual confidentiality risks require assessment. We introduce DiRAFT (Discourse Realization from Aggregate First-order Transitions), which extracts financial concept graphs and records the order in which concepts are first introduced. It pools adjacent concept transitions across training records and samples new graph plans from aggregate transition, starting-concept, and plan-length priors. A discourse layer guides text realization without supplying an individual source passage or graph. We assess privacy-related risks through two complementary evaluations: corpus-level structural overlap and source-grounded checks for specific non-public investor facts. The structural assessment covers two financial corpora and three generation backends. The confidential-fact assessment uses human review of 1,400 investor-call outputs across seven strategies and two backends. We also evaluate transition fidelity, content recoverability, and trajectory diversity. Stochastic sampling provides a favorable balance between transition fidelity and structural overlap, with consistent advantages over greedy and top-3 on investor calls. The confidential-fact assessment likewise detects fewer matches for stochastic sampling than these alternatives on both backends covered by the fact assessment. These complementary assessments provide empirical evidence on residual confidentiality risks without establishing a formal guarantee.

data.title: The First Few Tokens Matter: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Controllability
data.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising way to oversee increasingly capable agents. It succeeds in part because current models appear limited in their ability to control what they verbalize in their reasoning traces. We investigate the source of this limitation and link it to an entropy collapse in the first few tokens following the opening thinking tag. We exploit this mechanism to recover CoT controllability through two inference-time interventions on initial tokens: prefilling, where even a single token can substantially increase controllability, and banning frequent opening tokens combined with in-context examples, which improves average compliance by 34-41 percentage points across models. These interventions recover mainly addition and style controllability (adding or transforming information), while suppression controllability (avoiding or removing information) exhibits more varied responses, suggesting distinct underlying mechanisms. Consistent with this, the two groups behave as separate capabilities: across models, performance correlates positively within these groups, while cross-group correlations are mostly negative. Importantly, we find that the relationship with monitorability depends on the evaluation: addition and style controllability more consistently positively correlate with monitorability, while suppression often shows negative associations. Our findings motivate the development of controllability evaluations that distinguish difficulty initiating a specific opening from general limitations of the ability to alter reasoning content, alongside separate reporting of control tasks and categories.

data.title: Benchmarking Forecasting Agents on Yesterday's Tomorrows
data.abstract: Digital agents can now gather and organize information, reason over it, and use tools to complete complex tasks. Forecasting puts all of these abilities to the test: it requires integrating incomplete evidence, inferring causal drivers, and committing to calibrated probabilistic judgments. Existing benchmarks are poorly suited to measuring and improving this ability. Live benchmarks provide feedback only after events resolve, so every evaluation cycle waits on the calendar; fixed-corpus evaluations return results immediately but confine research to pre-collected documents. We introduce FABench, a scalable backtesting environment for Forecasting Agents. An automated pipeline discovers events, generates questions, and resolves outcomes for any past forecast date, so the benchmark can be renewed to stay ahead of model training cutoffs; its first release poses 287 questions across nine domains. Agents research each question freely in an archive environment that combines an offline archive with live web search screened to prevent temporal leakage. Evaluating agents built on eight recent models, we find that retrieval improves the Brier score of all eight in every retrieval setting and lifts the leading agents to the market consensus on the 54 questions linked to Polymarket, with the best three scoring slightly above it. Research traces reveal recurring failures in how agents weigh and apply evidence, leaving ample room for improvement. We release our code, data, and archive environment as a foundation for community research on forecasting agents.

data.title: Hypergraph cycle enumeration for efficient inference of planted k-XOR with smooth trade-off
data.abstract: We introduce hypergraph cycle enumeration (HCE), a simple spectral framework for detecting and recovering planted signals in noisy hypergraph inference problems. We study HCE on one representative problem from this class, namely planted noisy k-XOR, also known as sparse Learning Parity with Noise (LPN). Both theoretically and empirically, HCE achieves comparable recovery behavior to Kikuchi method, matching Kikuchi hierarchy. We identify parameter regimes where HCE outperforms Kikuchi method, showing that neither algorithm is universally better. We also show a subquadratic quantum speedup for HCE by replacing one of the algorithm's steps with a quantum walk. Our classical and quantum algorithms do not refute the quartic quantum speedup of quantum Kikuchi method, which remains valid for the practically relevant regime of large size and high noise strength.

data.title: Immersed Boundary Electrodiffusion in the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Formalism: Global Well-Posedness, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Singular Asymptotics
data.abstract: We introduce a unified optimal transport framework for the Immersed Boundary (IB) electrodiffusion active pump model. By representing membrane chemical potential barriers and active pump potentials via smoothed Eulerian kernels ($Ψ_w, \mathcal{H}_w$), we formulate the passive dynamics as an $L^2$-Wasserstein ($W_2$) gradient flow coupled to non-conservative active pushing fields representing ATP-driven $3:2$ $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ exchangers. We establish global weak existence of solutions to the continuous Poisson--Nernst--Planck--IB system via a split-step Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational scheme, backed by Calderón--Zygmund bounds for non-local Poisson drift and $H^3(\mathbb{S}^1)$ interface regularity under Stokes flow. We prove the continuous Rayleighian energy balance and establish exponential $W_2$-stability of Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) under a quantitative Bakry--Émery curvature threshold. Furthermore, we analyze the dual singular limits of kernel smoothing width $w \to 0$ and dimensionless Debye length $g = λ_D / L \to 0$. We establish the precise asymptotic regime connecting regularized and sharp models, prove the $Γ$-convergence of regularized energy functionals, derive distributional interface flux jump conditions, and resolve $O(λ_D)$ Debye space-charge boundary layers to confirm bulk electroneutrality.

data.title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms
data.abstract: The bottleneck of attention mechanisms, which are the fundamental building block of modern language models, is their quadratic complexity in terms of context size. There has thus been an increasing interest in the compression of the context, also called KV-cache compression. In this article, we consider the problem of compressing the context of attention mechanisms by first formulating it in the Hilbert space associated with its kernel. In this formalism, attention can be represented as the ratio of two linear maps whose interpolant is also the ratio of interpolants, this allows us to consider the interpolation of the linear maps directly. We thus introduce two novel KV-cache compression methods which we call GAIM and Q-DAIM, based on the Generalized Empirical Interpolation Method (GEIM) and the Q-Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (Q-DEIM), respectively. As the cost of these methods is quadratic in terms of context length, we propose surrogate models based on the Taylor series, the Performer and the Random Fourier Features method which allow the compression to be done in linear time. Finally, we extend this result to the streaming attention setting, providing new methods which allow one to penalize the selection of interpolation nodes based on the previously interpolated context and to update the previous interpolation based on new information. We then provide numerical results on the convergence of the residuals and the output error in future queries and preliminary results on the LongBench-E benchmark showing performance comparable to the state-of-the-art methods. These experiments suggest that the range revealed by our Q-DAIM method could help identify where information is concentrated in the KV cache, thus enabling an efficient compression.

data.title: Integrating of Attack Patterns and Threat Modeling to Support Security Analysis in the Automotive Domain
data.abstract: The increasing connectivity of cyber-physical systems in the automotive domain demands systematic approaches for identifying and mitigating cybersecurity threats. While ISO 21434 defines a structured workflow for Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA), it does not prescribe a specific method for identifying attack paths or evaluating risks. This paper proposes a conceptual model grounded in ISO 21434 that integrates the STRIDE threat classification with the CAPEC attack pattern database, focusing on the identification of attack scenarios and risk assessment. Its applicability is demonstrated through a case study involving Bluetooth-based threats to an automotive headlamp system.

data.title: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
data.abstract: On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models assumes that training responses are sampled from the current policy. In practice, an inference engine samples the responses and a separate trainer computes the gradients, and the \textbf{training-inference mismatch} between the two makes the training data off-policy. The mismatch has two sources, the numerics of the engine and the stale weights of asynchronous sampling, and a correction that stabilizes training under one source can fail under the other. \textit{We ask which property of a mismatch source decides the correction it needs.} Evaluating the trainer at the sampler's weights splits each sampled-token error exactly into a \textit{numerical discrepancy} of the engine and a \textit{policy lag} of the trainer, and we follow both through training. The numerical discrepancy stays approximately constant, so it biases the updates by a nearly fixed amount, and centering the score at each prefix removes its leading bias. The policy lag is produced by the trainer's own updates: the bias it leaves enters the next update, which enlarges the next lag and closes a feedback loop. Importance weighting cuts this loop only while the lag ratio stays concentrated, and on Qwen3-1.7B it fails at the step where the effective sample size of the ratio falls below one half. From this account we derive the \textbf{discrepancy-lag correction} (DLC), which centers the numerical discrepancy, clips the lag ratio against the sampler's weights and resynchronizes the sampler when this effective sample size falls below one half. Under a stale sampler, DLC keeps the KL divergence from on-policy training within twice the KL between two independent on-policy trainings on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, and its resynchronization prevents collapses that the per-token corrections leave and that a KL measured on the sampler's prefixes does not detect.

data.title: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring - What now?
data.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows large language models (LLMs) to generate intermediate reasoning traces in natural language while solving complex tasks. These traces can support safety monitoring by exposing potentially harmful plans before actions are executed. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which LLMs infer the presence of CoT monitoring from direct and indirect environmental cues and examine how this inference affects their subsequent behavior. Our observations suggest that oversight is an interactive process: while a monitor inspects a model's reasoning, traces left by monitoring interventions can allow the model to infer that its thoughts are being observed and to adapt its behavior accordingly. We show that even subtle environmental cues, such as timing-related signals from timeouts and operation durations, can reveal the presence of monitoring and trigger models to adapt their behavior to evade oversight. Across repeated episodes and interaction loops, we further observe that models can form statistical estimates of the monitor's effectiveness and use these estimates to guide attempts to evade detection. These findings highlight the need to evaluate CoT-based oversight under adaptive conditions, where the monitoring process itself may influence the behavior it seeks to observe.

data.title: UFMF: Radar-Guided Kinematic Priors for Real-Time 4D Occupancy Forecasting
data.abstract: Real-time 4D occupancy forecasting requires reliably extrapolating both ego motion and surrounding actor motion under strict latency budgets. Recent occupancy world models improve long-horizon fidelity through generative decoders and 3D volumetric modeling, yet their computational cost makes real-time deployment challenging. Light-weight BEV forecasters meet latency requirements but often blur or suppress fast-moving actors at longer horizons. We present UFMF (Ultra-Fast Multi-modal Forecaster), a real-time forecaster that keeps an attention-free diagonal state-space temporal core while injecting targeted kinematic and geometric structure where lightweight models typically fail. A radar-guided velocity-aware dynamic prior (VADP) decomposes future displacement into a linear extrapolation plus a learned horizon-dependent residual. The resulting per-cell flow fields transport a compact dynamic latent subspace during rollout. Two auxiliary training constraints complement this branch: world-frame dynamic supervision enforces inter-horizon trajectory coherence, and class-conditioned vertical-profile supervision regularizes BEV-to-3D lifting. UFMF operates at 122 FPS on a single RTX 4090 and reaches 0.45 fast-displacement mIoU on nuScenes, outperforming recent occupancy world models at a fraction of their computational cost.

data.title: Temporal and spatial couplings in the dynamics of human walking and running
data.abstract: Rhythmic behaviours such as walking and running are commonly modelled as dynamical systems around a stable limit cycle. To keep such models tractable, it is usually assumed that each step depends only on the previous one, that the limit cycle is fixed, and that the sagittal and frontal planes can be studied separately. Here, we test these assumptions in seven public datasets of human gait (71 participants), including 16 people who both walked and ran. We fit linear step-to-step maps and validate them by cross-validation, holding out more data where more data exist. At first sight, gait has memory: the state two steps back lowers the prediction error by up to 29\%. Yet most of this temporal coupling vanishes once the operating point may drift slowly and measurement noise is modelled; gait remains limit-cycle-like, around an operating point that moves. Running keeps more memory than walking in the same people. Spatial coupling between the planes is present in most participants, mainly from sagittal to frontal, but weak. This supports planar models of healthy gait, while a repeatable, task-dependent coupling index may serve as a measure of gait quality. The simple models are wrong, but useful enough.

data.title: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Dataset and Perturbation Benchmark for Tiny Aerial Targets
data.abstract: Long-range detection of small drones is complicated by their visual similarity to birds and by the limited detail available from ground-based cameras. Combining visible and infrared observations offers complementary information, but their usefulness depends on target size, cross-modal alignment, and image quality. We present AVID, a benchmark for studying these factors using real RGB-infrared bird-drone surveillance footage originating from the Drone Detection Dataset and curated for the IEEE ICIP 2025 Video and Image Processing Cup. AVID comprises 32,040 corresponding frame pairs from 115 videos, with 35,952 existing bird and drone annotations at $320\times256$ resolution. Targets occupy an unusually narrow size range: 68.1\% have a geometric-mean bounding-box side of 8--16 pixels, and 99.0\% meet the COCO small-object criterion. To characterize the geometric difficulty of combining the modalities, we introduce an object-relative alignment ratio and an alignment burden curve. In a sample of 300 frame pairs, 32.3\% have estimated global translations greater than 5 pixels; among the 264 pairs with matching annotations, 16.3\% exceed one median target side. We further introduce AVID-C, which simulates seven families of image degradation at five severity levels independently in RGB, infrared, or both. A fixed-feature analysis examines how scale, degradation, and added cross-modal shifts affect fitted bird-drone class overlap. At 12--16 pixels, the Bhattacharyya error bounds are 0.148 for RGB, 0.198 for infrared, and 0.046 for their combined features. These values describe separation in the specified feature and density models, not detector accuracy. Together, AVID and AVID-C support scale-aware, alignment-aware, and sensor-specific studies of tiny aerial targets.

data.title: Uniformization of compact Kähler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
data.abstract: Given two smooth compact Kähler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $κ(X) = 0$ if and only if $κ(Y) =0$.

data.title: Scientist Mothers Working in Childcare Deserts Are Less Likely to Attain Tenure
data.abstract: Childcare shortages have limited families' access to quality care, with consequences for children's development and parents' careers. We link two decades of childcare supply data to longitudinal surveys of U.S. scientists. We find workplace childcare deserts are widespread: more than half of scientists at universities and research institutions work in deserts, where supply falls significantly short of demand. We further find mothers working in deserts are less likely to attain tenure. They are also more likely to move to industry and part-time positions. Reduced work time partly accounts for the tenure association but other reasons remain. Expanding childcare availability near workplaces may help retain scientific talent.

data.title: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
data.abstract: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The relative sensitivities achieved for various principal quantum numbers are presented. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.

data.title: Variational surface matching for multichannel molecular photoionization
data.abstract: We present an improved method for computing multichannel scattering states in the \ASTRA{} (AttoSecond TRAnsitions) molecular ionization code. Our pole-free Galerkin method with variational surface matching (PFG-VSM) yields a boundary response that is stationary with respect to errors in the interior wave function. Compared with matching based on directly evaluated radial derivatives, this formulation yields substantially faster convergence and greater numerical stability as the number of open channels increases. Comparison with a numerical solution of the exactly separable $\mathrm H_2^+$ problem establishes the accuracy attainable in a hybrid Gaussian--B-spline basis for a polycentric potential, independently of many-electron close-coupling approximations. A direct comparison of the two matching prescriptions for CO demonstrates the stability of the variational formulation under radial-basis coarsening. For neon, agreement with the NewStock atomic ionization code tests the treatment of the continuum degeneracies that arise when rotational symmetry is represented in $D_{2h}$. The excellent agreement with the independent \XCHEM{} molecular ionization code for CO partial cross sections and molecular-frame photoelectron angular distributions, both away from and across resonances, is a strong confirmation of the correctness of both codes. A comparison for pyrazine extends this validation to a larger polyatomic target.

data.title: CAMEL: Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning for Ultra-Lightweight Retinal Foundation Models
data.abstract: Recent progress in deep learning has substantially advanced automated grading of ophthalmologic pathologies, supported by large annotated datasets and improved representation learning. However, a significant gap remains between state-of-the-art performance and clinical scalability. In particular, foundation models have reshaped image-based medical screening and diagnosis. These large-scale architectures trained on extensive datasets learn rich, generalizable feature representations that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. In ophthalmology, RETFound, one of the most relevant foundation models for retinal images, performs strongly across classification, segmentation, and risk prediction tasks. Despite their effectiveness, foundation models are often computationally prohibitive, hindering their deployment in real-world clinical environments where hardware constraints and latency are critical. To bridge this gap, we introduce CAMEL (Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning), a novel cross-architecture distillation framework that uses an asymmetric masking strategy during embedding learning to effectively transfer knowledge from massive teacher foundation models to compact, lightweight student models. Our experimental evaluation across four datasets shows that CAMEL preserves accuracy while drastically reducing computational complexity, enabling lightweight yet highly accurate models suitable for resource-limited clinical settings.

data.title: A Mixed $H_{\infty}$--Passivity Approach for Leveraging Heat-Pump-Connected District Heating Systems as Frequency Support in Electric Power Systems
data.abstract: Heat-pump (HP)-connected district heating systems (DHSs) can support grid frequency by rapidly modulating HP electrical consumption while accommodating the resulting heat imbalance. Thermal-state-informed HP control improves EPS--DHS coordination, but introduces slower DHS dynamics and heat-side disturbance propagation at the electrical interface on the time scale of secondary frequency control. This paper formulates the regulated DHS as a grid-facing dynamic port and develops a mixed $H_\infty$--passivity framework for disturbance-independent temperature regulation while preserving a clean electrical response during secondary frequency control. Sufficient conditions guarantee local asymptotic stability of the EPS--HP--DHS interconnection across primary frequency control, secondary frequency control, and DHS regulation. These stability conditions are integrated with multi-channel $H_\infty$ attenuation of DHS-state-dependent electrical dynamics, heat-disturbance propagation, and DHS-regulation errors, yielding a tractable convex LMI program for controller synthesis. Cross-model validation deploys controllers synthesized on control-oriented EPS--DHS models, without retuning, on an open-source electromechanical IEEE 39-bus model coupled with four high-fidelity finite-volume DHS models retaining thermal transport, storage, and heat-loss dynamics. The resulting controller improves EPS--DHS coordination without compromising the grid-facing electrical response.

data.title: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel
data.abstract: We introduce the Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel (MCRWK), an estimator whose per-pair cost is independent of graph size and derived directly from the random walk kernel (RWK) expansion. By normalizing the kernel coefficients, MCRWK samples a shared walk length and estimates its contribution using random walks on the input graphs. This gives a simple way to approximate RWK without constructing the product graph. For a fixed expected walk length and efficient neighbor sampling, each pairwise estimate takes $O(m)$ time for $m$ Monte Carlo samples, allowing the sample budget to control the trade-off between runtime and accuracy. We evaluate MCRWK against Graph Voyagers and classical RWK methods on synthetic and real graph datasets. In the reported experiments on large synthetic graphs, MCRWK is faster than Graph Voyagers and, at matched runtime, more accurate. It also has the lowest Gram-matrix runtime on the five real datasets studied. Code and experiments are available at https://github.com/arslan-yam/random_walk_kernels_computations

data.title: On lens spaces which may embed in the complex projective plane
data.abstract: Using an obstruction derived by Owens and relying on Donaldson's Diagonalisation Theorem, we obtain a complete classification of lens spaces of Lisca type $(2)$ or $(3)$ that are unobstructed from embedding in a homology complex projective plane. This classification is further refined for lens spaces $L(p,q)$ with $p$ even, using an obstruction due to Lidman--Moore--Vazquez based on work of Lin. This article is extracted from the author's PhD thesis.

data.title: Optimizing Prompt Radio Counterpart Searches for Gravitational-Wave Events with the Deep Synoptic Array
data.abstract: Prompt millisecond-duration coherent radio emission is proposed as a counterpart to neutron-star-containing compact mergers, produced before, during, or shortly after coalescence. Its detection would probe the plasma environment, magnetic fields, remnant evolution, and emission physics of these mergers. At GHz frequencies, dispersive delays can range from fractions of a second to several seconds, requiring the telescope to be on source before or soon after coalescence. Negative- or low-latency alerts, rapid response, and optimized pointing under uncertain, evolving localizations are therefore essential. We present a framework for prompt gravitational-wave follow-up with the upcoming Deep Synoptic Array (DSA), a sensitive, fast-slewing, wide-field GHz radio array. We simulate low-latency localization sequences and embed them in a follow-up environment with elevation, field-of-view, and slew constraints. We compare a reinforcement-learning pointing policy with a baseline that slews toward the highest-probability accessible region at each step. This peak-tracking rule is a strong, interpretable baseline for initial deployment, while the learned policy provides a complementary strategy for a subset of broad, multimodal, or arc-shaped localizations. At a random merger time, 37% of events are observable above $20^\circ$ elevation; among these, $\sim90\%$ of BNS events are successfully reached and tracked using zero-noise localization maps, decreasing to $\sim75\%$ with Gaussian-noise maps. We validate the optimized pointing trajectories on prototype DSA antennas. DSA follow-up can reach a fluence sensitivity of $\sim20$ mJy ms over a representative 700-1025 MHz sub-band, probing millisecond bursts with luminosities of approximately $10^{38}$ to $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, at or below the lower end of several coherent-emission predictions for neutron-star mergers.

data.title: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior
data.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for personal tasks, yet evaluating their safe use of personal context remains difficult because such contexts are private, fragmented, dynamic, and socially situated. We introduce P-ContextBench, a realistic, verifiable, and scalable benchmark for evaluating personal-context understanding. P-ContextBench constructs population-structured, life-story-grounded digital humans from demographic seeds reflecting the U.S. population. Rather than using explicit, static profiles, P-ContextBench embeds traits, routines, goals, and constraints as implicit evidence across fragmented, evolving synthetic mobile-app records. It evaluates five capabilities: single-source fact recovery, multi-source fact recovery, temporal state tracking, inference of higher-level personal patterns from routine behavior, and safe handling of requests conflicting with persona-specific constraints through compliance, warning, clarification, or refusal. A multi-stage validation pipeline checks persona plausibility, context recoverability, information leakage, evidence preservation, test-case grounding, and human-judge agreement. We instantiate P-ContextBench with 100 personas, 10,088 hidden facts, 18,261 app-trace fragments, and 4,810 verified test cases. The pipeline supports configurable generation across scales and demographic groups. Cost-effective state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs relevant to personal agents achieve below 60% accuracy on temporal tracking, higher-level pattern inference, and constraint-aware action-boundary decisions, with fewer than 10% of test cases answered correctly across all three repeated runs. Even a high-performing SOTA model remains inconsistent on these capabilities. P-ContextBench provides measurable targets for improving the accuracy, reliability, and safety of LLM-based personal agents.

data.title: Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
data.abstract: We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $Γ=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $Γ$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.

data.title: Renegotiable Options Fail to Prevent Hold-Up Between Two Profit-Maximizing Frontier LLM Agents
data.abstract: Do contract terms that protect investment between people also protect it between profit-maximizing language-model agents? In the hold-up problem, a seller can adapt a unit to one buyer at a cost before the price is set. Once that cost is sunk, the buyer can offer almost nothing and the seller will still accept, so a seller who foresees this does not adapt. One remedy is an option: the buyer may buy at a fixed price. In theory the option stops working if the buyer can let it lapse and offer its own price instead. Yet in a laboratory experiment by Hoppe and Schmitz, this renegotiable option raised human investment from 41.5% of pairs without a contract to 67.2%. We had Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, each told to maximize its side's profit, play a one-shot game with the same strategic structure under their four contract regimes and a reference-price control. The agents did what game theory predicts: under the renegotiable option no seller adapted, and under the option that rules out this renegotiation every seller did. In a second experiment in which sellers no longer stated their expected revenue before deciding, removing the profit instruction left investment unchanged under no contract and both options. When we changed the numbers so that the buyer would exercise the option even without adaptation, adapting only added cost, and no seller adapted: the agents did not simply adapt whenever an option was offered or whenever its price covered the cost. Under our protocol, a contract term that raised investment between people did not protect it between agents.

data.title: Isometric Embeddings of Asymptotically Hyperbolic Manifolds into Hyperbolic Space
data.abstract: The Nash Embedding theorem asserts that every closed Riemannian manifold can be isometrically embedded into a Euclidean space of sufficiently high dimension. In this paper, we address the asymptotically hyperbolic version of the problem. We prove that an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold $\left(M,g\right)$ can be realized as a submanifold of a sufficiently high-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathrm{H}^{N+1}$, intersecting the sphere at infinity transversely, if and only if $g$ is asymptotically Poincaré-Einstein to second order.

data.title: Existence and stability of Weyl points
data.abstract: Weyl points are quasimomentum-energy pairs in the band structure of three-dimensional periodic media at which two dispersion surfaces touch conically. They first arose in a model introduced by H. Weyl in 1929, but were first observed only recently in condensed matter physics and photonics experiments. Weyl points have been explored theoretically via numerical computation and via tight binding (discrete) models. In this article we present the first analytical treatment of Weyl points in a continuum PDE-type model. Starting with a Schrödinger operator whose electric potential is periodic with respect to the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, we introduce a small BCC-periodic magnetic vector potential that is equivariant with respect to a specific abelian group of symmetries. For magnetic Schrödinger operators of this type, we prove (i) that a pair of Weyl points bifurcates from a threefold degeneracy in the band structure of the underlying non-magnetic operator, and (ii) that these Weyl points are stable against small self-adjoint BCC-periodic perturbations of both the electric and magnetic vector potentials.

data.title: Completeness and dynamical stability in exoplanet occurrence rates
data.abstract: Exoplanet population studies are often quantified through the "occurrence rate" of certain types of planet. This value can be calculated from a survey of a sample of stars by taking the "detection rate" and correcting with a completeness factor. This completeness is calculated via detection limits on each individual star, and can be calculated either individually for each detected planet or averaged in a certain area of parameter space. We test whether either the average completeness or individual completeness performs better than the other. We also test whether including dynamical stability constraints in the detection limits improves the occurrence rate results. We use synthetic sets of exoplanetary systems and calculate occurrence rates for each and compare to what the value would be with perfect information. We compare how close each method is to the ground truth to assess which is most suitable. Overall, in our synthetic sets, the average completeness is more reliable though it can be a problem if there is a sharp change in the underlying population within the area of parameter-space considered. We find that using dynamical stability conditions causes a bias in the occurrence rate and do not recommend using these.

data.title: Spherical law for optimal layouts of random graphs
data.abstract: Can the nodes of a random graph be placed in an auxiliary space $\mathbb{R}^{M}$ so that its connectivity becomes local? The spring electric layout is a standard algorithm to try to find such local graph layouts; we study it as a statistical-physics problem by considering the Gibbs ensemble of spring-electric layouts. For graphs with independent edges we solve the model exactly at large number of nodes $N$ and fixed embedding dimension $M$. The node positions obey a spherical law: they are uniformly distributed in an $M$-dimensional ball; for $M=2$ this is closely related to Girko's circular law. Crucially, the ground state energy is flat across all layouts with that density: an optimal layout for one graph is asymptotically optimal for any other. Optimal layouts of i.i.d. graphs are therefore frustrated liquids, macroscopically constrained but microscopically unoptimizable. We discuss relations to graph-partitioning, Laplacian eigenmaps, and dimensionality reduction, and outline how this harsh result breaks down for correlated graphs.

data.title: Better Retrievers, Worse Labels: How Incomplete Relevance Judgments Distort Abstention Evaluation in Conversational RAG
data.abstract: Conversational RAG benchmarks such as MTRAG and RETECO evaluate retrieval and generation end to end: each system answers from its own retrieval, so abstention must be scored against whether each retrieved context is sufficient. A convenient shortcut reads sufficiency off the relevance judgments and treats a context without gold documents as unanswerable. We re-run the official baselines exactly and test this shortcut on RECOR (RETECO track~2) with four retrievers (nDCG@10 from .18 to .59) and three Qwen3 readers. Two open LLM judges and a panel of four small open models label each context by content, and a model of another family audits 250 contexts blind, with adjudication. The stronger the retriever, the larger the share of no-gold contexts that still contain the answer (28\% to 72\%) and the lower the shortcut's precision (.68 to .10; .70 to .21 under the audit). A reader agrees: Qwen3-4B answers 62--67\% of these false misses correctly, against 23--30\% of no-gold contexts judged insufficient and 1\% with no documents. In most false misses, the answer comes from a hard negative mined for the same question, another turn's gold or a neighbouring chunk of the gold page. On MTRAG, whose judgments come from annotators, precision drops from .72 to .50. Under the shortcut, answerability AUROC is up to .19 too low, and the best sufficiency detector appears to be a retrieval score that never reads the documents. We release code, runs and labels, and recommend scoring refusals against content labels, not the presence of gold.

data.title: Separating Fermion and Gauge Resonances with Species-Dependent Lightcones in Warped Geometry
data.abstract: Extra-dimensional flavor models generally tie together the mass scales of gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein modes. We show how species-dependent five-dimensional lightcones, which can be generated, for example, by a simple scalar profile, can separate these scales while preserving four-dimensional Lorentz invariance and any proposed extra-dimensional flavor structure. In two illustrative models on stabilized backgrounds, right-handed quark partners lie at 6.6--12 TeV with 30 TeV KK gluons, or a 5.5 TeV gluon lies below fermion partners above 10 TeV. We compare with deconstructed and three-brane models.

data.title: Temperature Evolution of Magnon-Polarons in the van der Waals Antiferromagnet FePS$_3$
data.abstract: Magnon polarons, hybrid excitations arising from magnon-phonon coupling, were investigated in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using magneto-Raman scattering measurements at temperatures ranging from 4 K to the vicinity of the Néel temperature ($T_\mathrm{N}$ = 118 K). The lower Zeeman-split component of the magnon-like mode, tuned by the magnetic field toward the lower-energy phonon mode, exhibits an avoided crossing. The corresponding magnetic field decreases from approximately 13 T at 4 K to 5.6 T at 85 K, bringing the effect within reach of a standard laboratory magnet. A model of three coupled bosonic modes shows that the magnon-phonon coupling constant, approximately 2.7 cm$^{-1}$ at low temperatures, decreases significantly with increasing temperature, following a trend similar to the temperature-induced softening of the magnon mode. This decrease in magnon-phonon coupling is discussed in terms of a possible reduction in sublattice magnetization due to thermal fluctuations.

data.title: Comparison of melanin subtypes using pump-probe microscopy
data.abstract: Pump-probe microscopy (PPM) is used to probe excited state dynamics of endogenous chromophores to generate contrast that is unavailable in traditional forms of microscopy. Here we apply PPM to characterize melanin, a pigment central to photoprotection, skin and eye pigmentation, and melanoma pathogenesis. Melanin is notoriously difficult to analyze due to its structural and chemical complexity. We imaged melanin from six different lesion categories: cutaneous nevi, lentigo, cutaneous malignant melanoma, conjunctival melanocytic lesions, vulvar melanocytic lesions, and a murine melanoma model, across 21 independent biological samples and 109 regions of interest. Using model fitting, adapted phasor analysis, and support vector machine classification, we characterize and quantify excited-state dynamics as a surrogate for chemical and structural heterogeneity. Heterogeneity of melanin separates cutaneous from non-cutaneous lesions, but is not correlated with malignancy. Benign lentigo is the most heterogeneous population in the dataset, exceeding cutaneous malignant melanoma, while conjunctival lesions are the most homogeneous despite receiving direct solar exposure. Classification on full transient absorption curves separates most subtypes well above the six-class chance level. These findings demonstrate the ability of PPM to reveal subtle differences in melanin photophysics across diverse tissue environments, with implications for optical tissue classification and the understanding of melanoma pathogenesis.

data.title: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories
data.abstract: Generative audio systems can produce large libraries of personalized bedtime content, but ordinary media objectives (retention, completion, and novelty) are poorly aligned with the goal of supporting a transition toward sleep. Direct evidence for narrated bedtime audio in adults is mixed, and a recent active-controlled trial did not support such audio as a standalone treatment for sleep disturbance. We translate this uncertain evidence into conservative engineering requirements and present a multilingual pipeline for generating and narrating low-arousal sleep stories. The implemented prototype separates deterministic planning from large language model generation, represents content and delivery parameters explicitly, shapes each script through a four-phase attention taper, validates structural and lexical constraints, performs a bounded error-aware retry, and quarantines unresolved outputs.
