Further, depending on the parameters, while the solitary waves in some cases have only one hump, in other cases the solitary waves have both single and double hump depending on the value of $ω$. We compute the charge $Q$ and the energy $E$ for each of the solitary wave solutions and show that while $E$ and $Q$ depend on coupling constant $g$, their ratio $E/Q$ is independent of $g$. When $κ= 1$, all the NLD models with SS, VV and PP interactions can be reduced to suitable combinations of SS and VV interactions. As a result all solitary waves in these models are bound states with $E/Q<m$.

data.title: Payroll Fraud Detection in Synthetic HR/ERP Graphs: An Inductive Comparison of Rules, Path Features, and Graph Neural Networks
data.abstract: Payroll-fraud screening requires finding hidden employee--payee links while distinguishing suspicious relationships from legitimate ones. We formulate this problem as inductive link prediction and entity ranking on synthetic human-resources and enterprise resource planning (HR/ERP) graphs, with unseen organizations and a matched benign twin for every planted case. An original study on 24 held-out organizations and a prospectively frozen extension compare analyst rules, explicit path features and graph neural networks (GNNs). A tuned gradient-boosted model on chained-join features achieved the highest overall link average precision (AP; 0.823), above the GraIL-style GNN (0.663); its 4-hop AP was 0.646 versus 0.272. Thus, the observed multi-hop gain is not specific to GNNs. On a new synthetic cohort with 2.0% positive entities, chained-join boosting again led (AP 0.798); the relational entity GNN also exceeded record-aware rules (0.707 versus 0.504). At a 2% review budget, their precision was 0.695 versus 0.602. Under 40% failed identifier joins, the entity GNN ranked above chained-join boosting (AP 0.712 versus 0.683, descriptively). Structure-only auditing exposed a shortcut in the initial generator; matched twins reduced the audited twin-pool AUROC to 0.493--0.514. These results separate multi-hop candidate discovery, record-based discrimination and review prioritization within an explicit synthetic evaluation design. Code and data are available from the authors on request.

data.title: Stochastic and Noisy Oracles in Smooth Continuous Optimization
data.abstract: We review models of inexact computational oracles in smooth continuous optimization and their implications for the convergence, computational complexity, and attainable accuracy of optimization algorithms. We adopt a framework in which zeroth-,first-, and second-order oracles are characterized by quantitative error bounds and may accept additional control parameters that influence both their accuracy and computational cost. We introduce deterministic and stochastic oracle models and illustrate their properties through a variety of examples, including finite-difference approximations, stochastic gradients, and randomized derivative estimators. Particular attention is given to the distinction between absolute and relative errors, bias and variance, and stochastic function evaluations with independent or coupled randomness. A central theme of the review is the use of common analytical tools to recover and compare convergence and complexity guarantees under different oracle models. For deterministic and stochastic first-order methods, we show how a general descent inequality leads to complexity bounds under various assumptions on the objective function and all proposed oracle models. In the stochastic setting, we develop bounds on expected stopping times and the accuracy that can be guaranteed under different oracle conditions. We also examine the total computational complexity of algorithms relying on specific oracle constructions and briefly review models of inexact second- order information and their use in optimization algorithms.

data.title: What Paid Triangles Identify about Reserve Uncertainty: Information Boundaries in Loss Reserving
data.abstract: Paid triangles identify some components of reserve uncertainty while others enter through modelling assumptions. We distinguish population identification, recovery by free accident-year-level and two-stage second-moment fits, and precision at practical triangle sizes. In a compound frequency--severity hierarchy, the population law identifies the row dispersion governing non-diversifying reserve variance. With one free level per accident year, its profile likelihood attains its supremum only at homogeneity: the levels absorb realised row heterogeneity on every triangle, in amounts and in counts. Anchoring reopens this channel, but supplies only one observation per accident year. On a $10 \times 10$ triangle the anchored estimate remains uncertain by a factor of several. Within-row allocation dispersion survives conditioning on row totals and hence survives free levels. In the predictive experiments, the treatment of mean-structure estimation error separated the procedures by several times more than the choice among plausible variance laws. A law of the correct form improved coverage only when its dispersion came from a prior instead of the free-level fit. On an outcome-free Schedule~P panel, no amount-only procedure approaches nominal coverage. Strongly one-sided misses reveal a displacement of realised reserves relative to the fitted predictive centres that changing the amount-only variance law cannot repair.

data.title: Elliptic soliton solutions of lattice eigenfunction equations of the KdV type
data.abstract: It is known that some integrable lattice equations can be formulated by the eigenfunctions of the Lax triplet of the lattice potential Korteweg-de Vries (lpKdV) equation; the eigenfunctions satisfy a discrete Abel formula in which the `integration' constant defines the $δ$ parameter in some equations in the Adler-Bobenko-Suris (ABS) classification. In this paper, we present a full Darboux transformation for the Lax triplet of the lpKdV equation, and eigenfunctions are formulated in terms of Casoratians. When the eigenfunctions take the elementary discrete Lamé functions, we get the elliptic $N$-soliton solution for the lpKdV equation after $N$-fold Darboux transformation. We then determine the constant in the discrete Abel formula in this case. The eigenfunctions are used to formulate elliptic $N$-soliton solutions for various equations in the ABS list, such as H3($δ$), $Q1(Δ)$, Q2 and Q3($Δ$) equations.

data.title: CIRCE Divines LLM Task Complexity from Constraint Structure
data.abstract: Estimating whether a problem is too complex for a large language model (LLM) before the model attempts it can guide model routing, how to allocate test-time compute, and suggest the need for new tools to aid the agent. While existing estimators rely on the problem text, LLM-annotated task difficulty labels, or signals obtained after a model attempts to solve the problem, such as its hidden states, none explicitly leverage the constraint structure inherent in the problem: the variables to assign and how the constraints over them interact. We introduce CIRCE, which extracts a problem's structure by using a cheap LLM to construct a Constraint Intermediate Representation that deterministically compiles into the constraint graph. Across seven reasoning benchmarks (including SAT, logic, and math) and four LLMs, even a randomly initialized GNN encoder improves predictions of LLM response correctness, reducing negative log-likelihood from 0.465 to 0.423 and increasing AUROC from 0.691 to 0.727 relative to the strongest baseline for each metric.

data.title: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics
data.abstract: In text-to-SQL and AI-agent analytics, successful SQL execution does not establish semantic correctness under changing business definitions. We study revalidation of fixed queries after changes to refund attribution, tax treatment, eligible populations and exchange-rate dates. An executable verification profile binds the requested revision and knowledge cutoff to legal counterexample data and exact monetary comparison. A preregistered confirmation on 32 newly authored revision families and two local producer bundles retains 192 query-definition cells: 144 nonconforming, 36 finite-suite agreeing and 12 unresolved. Of the nonconforming cells, 63 agree on the current snapshot. At an eight-ledger budget, obligation-guided checking detects 137 discrepancies versus 127 for generic ordering, a paired difference of 6.9 percentage points (family bootstrap 95% interval [2.1, 13.6]; exact family sign-flip p=0.0156). Every ledger arm rejects zero of the 36 agreeing cells. Current-obligation and equal-weight scoring match the guided result, identifying coverage rather than revision-specific priority as the observed source of benefit. Controlled assays, a natural-query pilot and repeated samples provide separate mechanism and robustness evidence. A legal discrepancy refutes conformance; agreement remains restricted to the recorded suite. The study establishes an auditable business-semantic revalidation profile within its authored schema and local-model scope.

data.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
data.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. The method handles entangled bands and accurately reproduces TDDFPT at a fraction of its cost. We use it to compute the total dynamical electron-electron interaction, including direct Coulomb and phonon-mediated interactions with dynamically screened electron-electron and electron-phonon couplings, all on equal footing. In hole-doped monolayer hBN, the hybridization of the carrier plasmon with the longitudinal optical phonon makes the low-energy retarded interaction nonmonotonic in the carrier density, an effect missed by the adiabatic approximation. In metallic monolayer TaS2, nonadiabatic effects are weak and occur only due to the intraband electron-hole continuum and the nesting of nearly parallel Fermi velocities. We also validate the widely used screened-screened approximation for the phonon spectral function. This work opens the way to first-principles studies of spectral functions, transport, and superconductivity with dynamically screened interactions.

data.title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods
data.abstract: Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode. We further show that adjoint operator splitting methods can be described algebraically through the antipode and the canonical involution of the original method. The resulting framework also yields new combinatorial identities and connects the analysis of geometric numerical integrators with the theory of incidence Hopf algebras.

data.title: Spectral Information Content of Diffraction-Limited Images
data.abstract: High-resolution optical imaging is fundamentally limited by diffraction, which imprints wavelength-dependent structure onto the point spread function (PSF) of the optical system. This intrinsic chromaticity implies that in addition to spatial structure, images encode spectral information. We develop the theory of this spectral information content and provide strategies for its optimal extraction with calculations of Fisher information. We show that polychromatic PSF formation can be expressed as a convolution in logarithmic coordinates and define the corresponding spectral transfer function. We derive this function for the Airy disk and find algebraic decay in spectral log-frequency, implying the existence of arbitrarily fine spectral structure in the ideal, noiseless PSF. We use a differentiable forward model to numerically construct the spectral information eigenbasis and quantify the spectroscopic capability of diffraction-limited imaging across a range of noise and detector systematics. We demonstrate injection and recovery of the constrained spectral modes in a realistic simulated example and compare these results with previously reported methods. Our information-theoretic framework provides a generalisable method for spectral characterisation of PSFs spanning a variety of imaging contexts.

data.title: FastHeapDict: Permanent Slot Indexing for Efficient Decrease-Key Operations in Indexed Priority Queues
data.abstract: Efficient decrease-key support remains an important practical concern in priority queues used by shortest-path and graph-processing algorithms. Although duplicate-entry heaps avoid explicit decrease-key operations and are simple to implement, they may accumulate many stale entries when tentative priorities are repeatedly improved. This paper presents FastHeapDict, an indexed binary min-heap based on permanent slot indexing. Instead of repeatedly locating keys through hash-table lookups during heap repair, FastHeapDict assigns each key a stable integer slot and stores that slot directly in heap entries. As a result, position updates during sift-up and sift-down operations are performed through integer indexing while preserving the usual indexed-heap interface. We evaluate FastHeapDict in both Python and C++20 using Dijkstra's algorithm as the primary experimental workload. The benchmarks include constructed dense stress graphs, randomized dense graph variants, and comparisons against duplicate-entry heaps and existing priority-queue alternatives. Across the tested Python workloads, FastHeapDict consistently outperforms the duplicate-entry heapq baseline and the tested heapdict and pqdict implementations. In the C++20 implementation, FastHeapDict also achieves strong constant-factor improvements over std::priority_queue duplicates, std::set-based decrease-key, and std::multiset duplicates. These results indicate that permanent slot indexing can provide a compact and effective implementation strategy for indexed priority queues in workloads where priority updates are frequent.

data.title: A General-Purpose Adaptable Foundation Model for Total-Body PET Kinetic Modelling
data.abstract: Voxel-level kinetic modeling in total-body dynamic positron emission tomography (TB-PET) enables precise physiological quantification but complicates parameter uncertainty estimation. While generative consistency models (CMs) can rapidly estimate Bayesian posterior distributions, they are constrained by type of tracers, kinetic models, and protocols. Training them from scratch whenever a new tracer, model or protocol is used can be computationally intensive. To address this, we introduce LoRACM, a parameter-efficient framework utilizing low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to transfer a pretrained foundation CM to novel TB-PET scenarios. We evaluated three adaptation scenarios using simulated and human data: scanner and protocol transfer for FDG two-tissue compartment modeling; FP-CIT simplified reference tissue modeling; and high-temporal-resolution FDG blood flow imaging via the adiabatic approximation to tissue homogeneity model. Each adaptation was trained in less than 3 hours on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU using 50,000 simulated pairs. In simulations, LoRACM showed strong agreement with results from Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC, which we use as reference posterior distributions), yielding median Kullback-Leibler divergences of 0.05-0.11 and median absolute percentage errors below 1.2% for each kinetic parameter of interest. In human data, LoRACM generated total-body K_i maps comparable to the ones made by non-negative nonlinear least squares (NNLS) fitting and a consistency model trained from scratch. Striatal dopamine binding potential estimates predicted by LoRACM correlated with NNLS estimates (r = 0.968-0.988). LoRACM produced total-body blood flow imaging with FDG matching the one made by NNLS. These underscore the potential of adapting a pretrained CM with LoRA for fast and reliable posterior parameter inference for kinetic models across distinct TB-PET applications.

data.title: AIFaultBench: A Reproducible Benchmark of Real-World Faults in AI Software Systems
data.abstract: AI-based software systems remain difficult to debug because their failures can involve interactions among code, models, data, dependencies, hardware, and execution environments. Existing benchmarks cover specific classes of AI systems, while concerns about fault realism and reproducibility highlight the need for documented execution conditions and evidence. We present AIFaultBench, a benchmark of 770 real-world bugs from 105 AI-based software repositories across 76 organizations. It covers six classes of AI systems: machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, systems based on large language models, agentic AI, and AI tooling and infrastructure. Each bug record connects the original report and affected codebase to structured metadata, environment setup scripts, a reproduction trigger, and investigation evidence. We reproduced 652 bugs (84.7%) under the recorded execution conditions and documented the outcomes of the remaining 118 attempts. Through its broad coverage, documented reproduction evidence, and common structure, AIFaultBench supports empirical studies of AI faults, debugging tool evaluation, practical failure investigation, and teaching with real-world examples.

data.title: Robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz preconditioner for high-frequency Helmholtz problems
data.abstract: We develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed the robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz method (REMs-HS), for the efficient solution of high-frequency Helmholtz problems. The method combines a one-level restricted additive Schwarz preconditioner with impedance transmission conditions (RAS-imp) and an edge multiscale (EMs) coarse solver in a multiplicative way. A key ingredient of our construction is a modified impedance boundary condition (mIBC), which is imposed both on the subdomain problems and on the local problems that generate the EMs coarse space. Compared with the original impedance boundary condition, the mIBC makes the proposed method both stable and inexpensive theoretically. We prove that the resulting REMs-HS preconditioner gives rise to a uniform convergent fixed-point iteration for large wavenumbers. Moreover, the required resolution conditions are substantially relaxed. Only a mild condition on the level parameter $\ell$ of the hierarchical coarse basis $\ell>\frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$ is needed, which is markedly weaker than the conditions in previous analyses. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method for Helmholtz problems with large wavenumbers.

data.title: Unavoidable flats in matroids excluding a uniform minor
data.abstract: We extend a theorem of Geelen, Kroeker, and Nelson on unavoidable flats in $\operatorname{GF}(q)$-representable matroids. For all integers $1\le a\le b$ and $n\ge1$, we prove that every simple matroid of sufficiently large rank with no $U_{a,b}$-minor has a rank-$n$ flat whose restriction is free or isomorphic to a projective or affine geometry over a finite field.

data.title: RepGen: Reproducing Deep Learning Bugs through Context-Aware Code Generation and Verification
data.abstract: Reproducing deep learning (DL) bugs is challenging because failures can involve source code, models, data, dependencies, and execution environments. Incomplete bug reports further complicate reproduction by omitting essential details. We present RepGen, an open-source tool for reproducing DL bugs through context-aware code generation and iterative verification. Given a bug report and repository, RepGen explores the codebase to build a learning-enhanced context, develop a reproduction plan, and generate candidate scripts. It refines candidates using static checks and LLM feedback to improve their correctness and relevance. When enabled, the tool prepares the execution environment, runs the script, and assesses its output against the reported failure. RepGen provides an interactive command-line interface supporting local and hosted LLMs, configurable execution budgets, and inspectable artifacts, along with a GitHub Action for automated issue processing. The underlying approach reproduced 85 of 106 real-world DL bugs (80.19%). A controlled study with 27 developers showed a 23.35% improvement in reproduction success and a 56.8% reduction in reproduction time.

data.title: Flash Word : ESL Listening Support with Subtitle Skimming
data.abstract: Listening to English audio with English subtitles is thought to be effective for ESL students to improve listening comprehension skills. However, for those who learn English as a second language it can be hard to finish English subtitles. Also they are unlikely to focus on listening while being busy reading subtitles. We propose Flash Word, a subtitling system which generates and presents shortened intralingual subtitles for English audio by detecting keywords from the script. Flash Word extracts keywords from scripts using an existing algorithm, and shows them one at a time like a flashcard. The system calculates when the keywords are being pronounced and aligns them correctly. Flash Word aims to enable ESL students to focus better on listening by minimising the cost of reading subtitles.

data.title: Local Budget Benefits, Population Commitment, and Solver Performance: A DGO Case Study with Controlled DE Transfer
data.abstract: An evaluated candidate can improve a local search step, alter the population used by later steps, and affect a solver's final result. We distinguish these three questions using Da Gou Gun Optimization (DGO), a population optimizer designed for this study. Its JQ100 configuration evaluates an interpolation candidate during a two-sided probe. We define local budget value, population commitment effects and complete-policy performance, and give an exact example in which a locally better commitment leads to a worse continuation. Short-horizon matched comparisons favor interpolation on eligible quadratic states. Paired continuations yield mixed effect estimates, with primary group intervals spanning zero. Complete-policy comparisons favor JQ100 over the tested classical references in aggregate; a matched-start comparison has favorable means but intervals spanning parity. On 24 boxed BBOB functions, target-truncated geometric-mean error ratios favor JQ100 over the tested classical policies and favor L-SHADE and CMA-ES over JQ100 under the stated initialization and stopping rules. Local evaluation gains, commitment effects and solver competitiveness therefore require separate comparisons.

data.title: QUAL: Quantile Alignment Improves Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models
data.abstract: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide zero-shot forecasts for unseen series, but their accuracy varies across datasets. Combining several models can reduce this variability, yet zero-shot deployment provides no target labels for selecting or weighting them. We find that a model pool is useful not only as a final ensemble, but also as a probability reference for transforming each member forecast. Aligning quantiles through this pool-relative reference improves every member forecast in aggregate. Motivated by this finding, we propose QUAL (Quantile alignment), a simple label-free framework for improving and combining diverse TSFMs. QUAL first produces aligned member forecasts, then applies Huber aggregation and rearrangement to obtain a robust combined forecast without training or model modification. On GIFT-Eval, quantile alignment reduces average member MASE and CRPS by 7.4% and 9.8%. The full framework remains robust when weak forecasters enter a candidate pool whose quality cannot be verified in advance. Code is available at https://github.com/junhyeokkang/QUAL.

data.title: Anisotropic Boltzmann transport in a tight-binding superlattice: Exact results for power-law energy-dependent scattering
data.abstract: We develop a complete Boltzmann transport theory for the in-plane ($σ_{xx}$) and out-of-plane ($σ_{zz}$) conductivities of an electronic superlattice consisting of a periodic stack of two-dimensional (2D) parabolic-band layers coupled along the superlattice axis by nearest-neighbor tunneling $t$, in the physically relevant regime $t\ll E_F$ where the Fermi surface is an open, corrugated cylinder. Within the relaxation-time approximation with a power-law energy-dependent scattering time $τ(E)\propto E^{p}$, we study the seven models $p=0,\pm1,\pm3/2,\pm2$ as functions of the 2D electron density $n$ per layer and temperature $T$. For $p=-2$ (in plane) and $p\le -1$ (out of plane), long-lived carriers at the miniband bottom can dominate transport at finite temperature. For $p=-2$, these carriers produce a pronounced peak in $σ_{zz}(T)$ at $T\sim E_F$. We find that the temperature dependence of the anisotropic metallic dc conductivity can be highly counterintuitive depending on $t$, $T$, and $p$, with no generic increase or decrease with temperature. The Lorenz ratio is determined by the energy variance of the current-carrying electrons; the Wiedemann-Franz (WF) law is exact as $T\to0$ for all models at fixed $t$, with anisotropic corrections at finite temperature. Band-edge carriers first enhance the interlayer Lorenz ratio up to several times its low-temperature value through thermal occupation of separated energy ranges within the same electron band and then suppress it at high temperature by energy filtering. Strong violations of the Wiedemann-Franz law can therefore arise from miniband structure and energy-dependent elastic scattering alone.

data.title: Variance Bounds and Strict Log-Concavity for Forest Coronas
data.abstract: We prove that the size of a random independent set in every nonempty forest has variance strictly smaller than its mean at common activity $0<t\le1$. A rooted quadratic reserve gives quantitative forms of this inequality. Mean matching transfers the bounds to fixed-weight canonical completion laws, and exact binomial moments prove strict log-concavity for every forest corona and every well-covered forest. The stronger factorial normalization $((m-j)!i_j)_{j=0}^m$ is strictly log-concave; we give explicit coefficient margins, terminal sharpness, one-less smoothing, and the exact universal three-index binomial ULC prefix. An exact attachment argument doubles the rooted reserve for every nontrivial unweighted tree. For a single marked root, a square reserve holds through $Θ=\tfrac12e^{3-2W(1/e)}$ and for every positive mark at roots of degree at most four. A stronger reserve holds through mark $15/14$. These estimates yield marked clique, adjacent-pair, and repulsive two-piece variance bounds with fixed-weight canonical transfer. Finally, arbitrary positive site activities in $[3t/4,t]$ satisfy a uniform rooted reserve on every forest. This proves strict log-concavity for weighted forest coronas with compatible base marks. An explicit weighted-star obstruction shows why an unrestricted heterogeneous extension is impossible. Complete proofs are included, together with the required classical graph characterization and variance comparison.

data.title: Optimal climate policy in incomplete electricity markets
data.abstract: Incomplete long-term contracting in electricity markets can expose investors and consumers to inefficient levels of risk. This paper investigates how incompleteness impacts the optimal choice of climate policy. We develop a game-theoretic model of optimal policy-making in anticipation of how electricity market agents react to a given policy when gas prices and demand are uncertain and contracting is incomplete. In illustrative experiments, we observe that renewable subsidies and carbon prices induce an insurance co-benefit when markets are incomplete. This is because, relative to a complete market benchmark, incompleteness shifts investment from renewables toward gas and exposes consumers to uninsured risk from inter-annual volatility in electricity prices. By incentivizing investment in renewables, subsidies and carbon prices indirectly counteract these distortions. Consequently, incompleteness increases the optimal subsidy and carbon price levels in our experiments. Renewable subsidies exhibit a stronger insurance effect than carbon pricing, as the latter leads to more investment in gas with carbon capture and storage and more volatile electricity prices. While carbon pricing is more economically efficient than subsidies in complete markets, incompleteness shrinks its efficiency advantage and even leads to cases where subsidies are more economically efficient.

data.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
data.abstract: Self-distillation methods for large language models with an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher already retain a history of student updates. Muon nevertheless stores a separate momentum buffer, increasing persistent training memory. We propose Muon with Reused Teacher (Muon-RT), which reuses the teacher-student displacement to eliminate momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices. We show that this displacement encodes an exponentially weighted history of applied updates and smooths temporally uncorrelated noise under a local model. Muon-RT removes its radial component, normalizes it spectrally, and mixes it with the current gradient after Newton-Schulz (NS) orthogonalization. Under explicit regularity and alignment assumptions, we establish linear contraction of an expected objective-gap bound toward a residual error level. With Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Muon-RT improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.6 points with 42% less persistent memory, and over momentum Muon by 5.4 points with 27% less persistent memory. With Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, it improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.0 points.

data.title: Defect TQFTs, the Generalized Cobordism Hypothesis, and Algebraic $K$-Theory
data.abstract: By constructing a fully dualizable category $\mathrm{Bord}^{\mathcal{C}}_n$ as the left adjoint of the forgetful functor, we state a generalized cobordism hypothesis. As a corollary, we establish a generalized Pontryagin-Thom isomorphism that gives a geometric interpretation of higher algebraic $K$-theory using cobordism classes of framed manifolds and stratified spaces decorated by categorical string diagrams, which we call lasagnas. For finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, these decorations are branched local systems. We also examine low-dimensional representatives, including $K_1$, Steinberg-group presentations of $K_2$, and fillings related to the Steinberg relation, providing a more explicit construction of Ghys' manifold.

data.title: Long-Time Behavior towards Generic Riemann Solutions for Radiative Euler Equations
data.abstract: We study the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional radiative Euler equations, where the Riemann pattern consists of a $1$-rarefaction wave, a $2$-contact discontinuity, and a $3$-shock wave. We prove that, for sufficiently small wave strengths and initial perturbations, the Cauchy problem admits a unique global solution, which converges uniformly as $t\to \infty$ to a composite wave of the $1$-rarefaction wave, $2$-viscous contact wave, and $3$-radiative shock profile with a time-dependent shift. As a key ingredient, we establish a comprehensive set of quantitative estimates for weak radiative shock profiles. Our proof is based on the method of $a$-contraction with shifts. In all previous applications of the $a$-contraction method to the study of long-time behavior, the proof has relied essentially on the parabolic structure provided by either viscosity or heat conduction. In this work, we extend the method to a hyperbolic-elliptic system without parabolic structure.

data.title: Differential rank preservation manifold learning
data.abstract: Manifold learning methods like t-SNE and UMAP preserve local neighborhoods, but they do not preserve the ranking of the neighbors inside them. Two embeddings can return the same neighbor set while disagreeing on which point is closest. This loss of order degrades downstream applications that value the order in the embedding. We propose Smooth Rank t-SNE (SR-tSNE), which adds a differentiable rank term to the standard t-SNE loss. To enable efficient training, this term uses a sigmoid rank approximation to explicitly force a point's true high-dimensional neighbors to outrank unrelated intruders and retain their original order. We also introduce Ordinal DLP (O-DLP), an extension of the Degree of Locality Preservation (DLP) metric that credits a neighbor only when it returns at its original rank. Across eight benchmarks spanning image, text, speech, remote-sensing and single-cell data, SR-tSNE outperforms 12 baselines in rank preservation and neighborhood overlap. Ablation studies demonstrate our rank term alone boosts O-DLP by 5% to 28%, a gain not achievable using standard pairwise loss. This advantage transfers to downstream applications. SR-tSNE achieves the best label-transfer performance across seven vision datasets. For cell-type discovery across six single-cell datasets, it ranks first in 17 of 18 dataset-metric combinations, whether clustering resolution is selected with or without cell-type labels. In intraday trading, SR-tSNE achieves higher returns, lower risk, and lower turnover than the baselines. To our knowledge, SR-tSNE is the first t-SNE-family method with explicit order preservation.

data.title: Memory and Recall of Color Images Using Neural Networks-1 - The Cue-Ball Model based on the Associative Memory Mechanism -
data.abstract: This paper presents a neural network model for storing and recalling color images of different sizes using the Cue BallRecall Net systems [1,2,3,4,5]. The Cue Ball system consists of a Recall Net composed of multiple memory neurons each responsible for memorizing a single, distinct memory and a large number of neurons that represent image patterns. The images used in this study [6] consist of ten images(see Appendix). The pixel values of these images were converted into digital values and used for subsequent processing. Accordingly, the Cue Ball contains ten Cue neurons, corresponding to the ten images stored in memory. The number of pixels varies among the images, and therefore, the number of Recall neurons comprising the Recall Net also varies accordingly. In this study, the number of Recall neurons was prepared between 106,134 and 360,000, depending on the number of pixels in each image. In this simulation, after the connection weights (wjip, vijp) had been learned, we have used the learning and recall algorithms to investigate whether the Cue neuron which had memorized a specific image could be identified by the Recall Net when that a memorized image has been presented. Therefore, the most important simulation result is which Cue neuron responds when a memorized image is presented to the Recall Net. If the Cue neuron that memorizes the presented image responds, its output can be used to obtain the corresponding image data. By adding a BMP header to the resulting image data, the original memorized image can be accurately recalled.

data.title: Transmission and filtering of stochastic rhythms in bursty gene expression
data.abstract: How stochastic rhythms in upstream regulatory signals are transmitted to downstream gene expression is a fundamental question in systems biology. Although experiments have shown that molecular degradation strongly influences downstream rhythmic responses, a general quantitative theory explaining how degradation, stochastic bursting, and upstream timing variability jointly govern rhythm transmission remains lacking. Here we develop a general analytical framework based on a martingale-based orthogonal decomposition, applicable to arbitrarily complex upstream dynamics, including memory effects. We derive exact autocorrelation and power-spectrum transmission laws, establish an oscillation-efficiency contraction principle, and identify a critical degradation rate that provides a necessary and sufficient condition for stochastic rhythm transmission. An explicit rhythm-transmission relation reveals that increasing burst frequency and modulation depth promotes rhythm transmission, whereas greater variability in upstream cycle duration suppresses it. In particular, increasing burst size leaves oscillation efficiency unchanged. The predicted degradation threshold correctly separates all ten pulsing and nonpulsing p53 target proteins reported in previous experiments. These results provide a theoretical foundation for understanding how cells selectively preserve or integrate rhythmic regulatory signals.

data.title: Deck Reconstruction for Restricted Word Classes
data.abstract: For a binary word $x\in \{0,1\}^+$, the $k$-deck of $x$ is the multiset of all length-$k$ subsequences counted with multiplicity. The deck reconstruction problem asks for the minimum $k$ such that every word of a fixed length is uniquely determined by its $k$-deck. In this paper, we study deck reconstruction for several restricted classes of binary words, including words with exactly $s$ ones, words with at most $\ell$ runs of ones, and words where the indices of ones are given by a monotone polynomial of degree $d$. We prove that for these classes of words, their reconstruction thresholds are bounded by a function of the structural complexity of the class. We also study weak deck reconstruction, in which subwords may contain "wildcard" symbols that map to either 0 or 1. By generalizing a "template lemma" of Dudík and Schulman, we improve the upper bound in an open question about weak reconstruction from Dudík and Schulman. Finally, for the class of periodic words with period $d$, we prove that its in-class reconstruction threshold is equal to the general reconstruction threshold for words of length $d$, and give a general template construction producing further classes with the same threshold-preservation phenomenon.

data.title: An Empirical Study on Learning Rooftop Solar Potential from Satellite Imagery Directly Without Explicit Geometry
data.abstract: Rooftop solar potential estimation often relies on LiDAR, digital surface models (DSMs), or pipelines that explicitly reconstruct roof geometry before estimating solar potential. We propose Direct Rooftop Solar Prediction (DRSP), an end-to-end formulation that maps satellite imagery and coarse regional sunlight information directly to application-level solar outputs. DRSP neither requires explicit geometric representations as input nor predicts roof orientation, slope, height, DSMs, or other geometric quantities as intermediate outputs, and therefore requires no geometric intermediate supervision. To enable large-scale study of this formulation, we develop a programmatic data-curation pipeline that converts per-panel information from the Google Solar API into usable-rooftop masks and spatial solar-energy targets, yielding two geographically distinct datasets containing approximately 60K rooftops from the U.S. Midwest and 87K from Texas. We demonstrate the feasibility of DRSP and systematically characterize the effects of geographic training distribution, model depth, image resolution, regional sunlight conditioning, and heatmap regression objectives. Overall, our results suggest that useful rooftop-scale solar information can be learned directly from 2D imagery without explicit geometric intermediate representations, offering a simpler path toward large-scale solar assessment. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/joshualee124/direct_rooftop_solar_prediction.

data.title: Calibration of Large Model Quantization based on HiFloat4 Format
data.abstract: Quantization of Large Language Models (LLMs) has become increasingly important for reducing the computational costs and resource requirements for practical deployment. Growing interest in this area has motivated the community to move beyond 8-bit quantization towards 4-bit precision, leading to the development of customized 4-bit formats such as MXFP4 and NVFP4. Recently, HiFloat4 (HiF4) has emerged as a competitive alternative which adopts a Block Floating-Point (BFP) format with a three-level scaling hierarchy, thereby achieving a significantly larger dynamic range. While quantization can substantially reduce memory usage and accelerate inference, it frequently introduces accuracy degradation. Calibration is therefore essential for narrowing the performance gap between low-precision quantized models and their full-precision counterparts. Nevertheless, existing calibration methods are mainly designed and validated using integer-precision formats, such as INT4, lacking support for HiF4 due to its hierarchical BFP structure. In this paper, we investigate three calibration approaches, namely HiGPTQ, HiAutoRound, and HiFlatQuant, to further enhance model quantization based on the HiF4 format. Extensive experiment s demonstrate that all three proposed approaches improve inference accuracy compared with direct HiF4 conversion, reducing the gap between HiF4 and BF16 to less than 1% and outperforming the state-of-the-art NVFP4 format across various models and downstream tasks.

data.title: Clusters of primes revisited
data.abstract: We revisit the generalized Rayleigh quotient optimization problem related to the Maynard-Tao sieve with the goal of finding a more efficient function basis. We demonstrate that a family based on products of reciprocals, previously used in asymptotic estimates for $H_m = \liminf_{n \to \infty}(p_{n+m}-p_n)$, provides results that are close to the theoretical limits of the sieve across many regimes. In particular, we establish $H_2 \leq 31 \, 140$, $H_3 \leq 2 \, 560 \, 022$, $H_4 \leq 193 \, 672 \, 056$, and $H_5 \leq 13 \, 659 \, 045 \, 840$. We also show that, as $k \to \infty$, the related variational quantity $M_k$, introduced by Maynard, satisfies the lower bound $M_k \geq \log k - 0.273572 + o(1)$.

data.title: Predicting Human-Gain Curves under Local Proxy Optimization from Repeated Ratings
data.abstract: Optimizing a proxy objective can improve human-perceived quality, but the resulting gain can vary with optimization strength. Average proxy-human correlation alone does not reveal how human-perceived quality changes as optimization strength increases. We propose PACE (Proxy Alignment and Curvature Expansion), a pre-optimization diagnostic that uses repeated human ratings to predict the human-gain curve induced by a fixed proxy. The method models proxy optimization as a KL-regularized exponential tilt. At KL radius $d$, the local gain is approximated by $A\sqrt{d}+Bd$, where $A$ measures first-order proxy-human alignment and $B$ captures the leading second-order correction along the proxy-optimization path. We estimate $A$ and $B$ from repeated human ratings on calibration items and test the resulting gain-curve prediction on held-out evaluation items. Across SummEval, analysis-eligible WMT MQM clusters, an OpenMEVA-MAGS ROC/WP repeated-rating slice, and a GPT-4o judge proxy experiment, PACE consistently reduces held-out gain-prediction error relative to $A$-only, zero-gain, and reliability-only baselines. With the same pre-pool information, it is competitive with flexible proxy-conditional calibration, and a LoRA-DPO experiment provides a modest bridge to actual optimization. Transfer experiments across datasets and evaluation slices show that source coefficients are useful priors, but target calibration further improves prediction. The resulting diagnostic is local and one-sided: it characterizes gentle optimization along the positive tilt branch of a fixed item pool.

data.title: A spectral theory of zeta functions of function fields
data.abstract: We study Hilbert spaces constructed from the Weil quadratic form associated with the zeta function of a curve over a finite field, together with self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator on these spaces. For a distinguished family of these extensions, we prove that the eigenvalues converge to the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function and that the corresponding entire spectral functions, after normalization, converge locally uniformly to an infinite product determined by these zeros. These limits occur as the interval parameter approaches a finite endpoint, rather than infinity as in the setting of the Riemann zeta function. We also realize the global Hilbert space through the Rosati trace pairing and show that translation by $\log q$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by normalized Frobenius. This provides a geometric model for the analogous analytic constructions associated with the Riemann zeta function.

data.title: Language Models Show a "Women-Are-Wonderful" Effect in Blame Attribution That is Not Just Leniency
data.abstract: This paper investigates the Women-Are-Wonderful (WaW) effect in language-model blame attribution: a favorable bias in which women receive more positive evaluations than men. Using 11,270 interpersonal conflicts from r/AmItheAsshole, we construct matched counterfactuals that vary the gender of the person being judged (the original poster) and the person affected (the counter-party). Across four language models, gender changes a minority of verdicts, but those changes consistently favor women. The effect is strongly role-dependent. Making the original poster a woman reduces the odds of blame by 9--52%, while making the counter-party a woman multiplies them by 2.7--9.2X. Counter-party WaW also varies across conflict types, strengthening in communication and relationship conflicts and weakening in family conflicts. Exploratory probes suggest that counter-party gender can shift judgments of sympathy, reasonableness, harm and protection. WaW is therefore not just leniency toward women being judged: models also judge conduct more harshly when it affects a woman.

data.title: Derived products and top-degree inverse limits
data.abstract: We compute top derived products and inverse limits on products of affine lines with doubled origin over $B[s]$, for any nonzero commutative ring $B$. For every $B$-module $M$, the two top obstruction modules fit into an explicit exact sequence and contain $M^{\mathbb N}/M^{(\mathbb N)}$as a natural $B$-module direct summand.This gives exact product dimensions, sharp vanishing bounds for inverse sequences, and faithfulness in the coefficient module. For a Grothendieck category of finite product dimension, we also obtain degree shifts under adjoining commuting locally nilpotent endomorphisms and prove that this construction preserves top-degree vanishing for epimorphic inverse sequences. A fixed Gabriel--Popescu presentation then describes the general top obstruction through actual Ext sequences and separates two module-theoretic terms.

data.title: CompoSET: A Controlled Single-Edit Benchmark for Vision-Language Compositionality
data.abstract: Vision-language compositionality is the ability to identify which properties, relations, quantities, and states bind to which entities in both an image and a caption, and to match those bindings across modalities. Existing benchmarks evaluate this ability through image-text matching: a model ranks candidate image-caption match similarities and succeeds when the correct match comes on top. In such datasets, paired images differ by more than a single binding: scene, layout, and content all differ, with 97% of pixels changing on average. Such pairs do not isolate compositionality: results are confounded by global image differences. We introduce Compositional Single-EdiT (CompoSET), a benchmark dataset in which each base image-caption pair has an edited counterpart, or foil, that preserves the scene but differs by a single controlled edit, such as color, count, spatial relation, or object state. Base and foil images preserve naturalistic scene complexity yet are visually near-identical: only 8% of pixels change on average. Our dataset has many foils per base scene (~22) in order to separate scene difficulty from edit difficulty, a distinction one-foil-per-base benchmarks cannot make. CompoSET contains 1,776 instances across 80 naturalistic scenes, spanning 16 edit types in 4 semantic categories, with captions at 3 verbosity levels. We test 22 dual-encoder VLMs and find that all models perform at or below chance level on CompoSET, despite scoring well on prior benchmarks. This suggests that apparent progress under prior image-text matching protocols may be an artifact arising from confounds in benchmark design, and that compositional understanding in dual-encoder VLMs is far from solved. CompoSET addresses the confounds and offers a better controlled benchmark to measure future progress.

data.title: MAGIKS: Multimodal Alignment and Gravitational-Wave-Conditioned Interaction for Kilonova Search
data.abstract: We present MAGIKS, a multimodal framework for gravitational-wave (GW)-triggered kilonova identification that formulates counterpart search as query-conditioned gallery retrieval. Following an align-before-fuse design, MAGIKS combines GW source parameters and sky-localization maps with irregularly sampled multiband optical light curves and sky coordinates. A time-aware supervised contrastive objective provides coarse cross-modal alignment, while dual cross-attention evaluates consistency between optical coordinates and GW localization, and between GW parameters and optical evolution. We train and evaluate MAGIKS on simulated binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole mergers, Rubin Observatory kilonova light curves from regular survey observations and target-of-opportunity follow-up, GW-detected mergers without Rubin-detectable kilonova counterparts, and realistic non-kilonova contaminants. In independent galleries with one true counterpart and time- and sky-compatible distractors, MAGIKS outperforms optical-only and sky-localization-only ranking, with increasing gains as galleries grow. At 5000 candidates, it ranks the counterpart first for 39.8% of queries, versus 4.8% and 0.2% for these baselines. In a GW170817 study, we generate counterfactual Rubin observations using released GW parameters and three-dimensional localization, the measured counterpart position, and host distance. At the same gallery size, MAGIKS achieves top-1 and top-10 retrieval rates of 87.3% and 95.7%. It correctly classifies 94.2% of associated and non-associated GW-optical pairs. In a separate crossed-pair experiment, its matching score responds significantly to controlled changes in all five tested GW parameters. These results support GW-conditioned kilonova candidate prioritisation for future multi-messenger follow-up.

data.title: Quantum Vehicle Routing Problem: a smart initialization strategy for ill-conditioned optimization landscapes
data.abstract: With the expansion of complex transport infrastructure, new paths for linking different destinations have emerged, allowing the definition of multiple routes. The introduction of new roads may also lead to disruptions in traffic flow. This problem can be generalized into a special case of VRP, which aims to find the optimal route for a fleet of vehicles within a network of destinations. Finding solutions to this problem requires an exponential number of operations, hindering the ability of exact solvers to deal with large instances, which must therefore be tackled using heuristics, often leading to suboptimal results. Quantum-based algorithms may allow us to find exact solutions in polynomial time with high probability, offering a potential future alternative to classical solvers and in this work, we focus on the QAOA. Our novel contributions are a parameter-initialization strategy that improves the convergence probability and the integration of the subtour constraints directly into the optimization without using additional qubits by employing an approximation of exponential equality constraints. We believe that our results pave the way for effectively solving instances of VRP using quantum-based solutions, leveraging the space-efficient problem encoding and our initialization strategy, which limits the effect of barren-plateau under random parameter initialization.

data.title: Entangled Measurement Outcomes for Optimal Postselection in Quantum Batteries
data.abstract: Postselection can enhance the performance of a selected quantum battery branch, raising the question of whether the optimum can always be achieved by product measurements on the auxiliary subsystems. For battery auxiliary states obtained by mixing a pure state with global white noise of strength p, the conditional ergotropy reduces to a generalized Rayleigh quotient. For 0<p<1, product postselection attains the joint optimum if and only if the eigenspace associated with the largest generalized eigenvalue contains a product vector. For two auxiliary qubits, a strict product-joint gap therefore occurs precisely when this eigenspace is one dimensional and spanned by an entangled vector. Noisy W and GHZ states display qualitatively different behavior: the three qubit W state exhibits a strict gap throughout 0<p<1, whereas the three qubit GHZ state admits a product optimum. For interacting two qubit batteries, the optimal postselection can switch from a Bell outcome to a product outcome as the coupling strength is varied. By contrast, the outcome averaged capacity and ergotropy are independent of the measurement basis, showing that the joint measurement advantage is genuinely postselective.

data.title: Marginal effects for the stochastic actor-oriented model
data.abstract: Parameter estimates of stochastic actor-oriented models for network evolution are notoriously hard to interpret. Especially a comparison of parameter estimates is problematic, both between different models for the same data set and between the same model for different data sets. Effect size measures based on the calculation of marginal effects are proposed as an alternative to standardize the scale of interpretation but can and should not universally erase the effects of differences in scale and heterogeneity. Simulation experiments show how an omitted effect displaces coefficients and marginal effects differently, and an analysis of empirical friendship network data finds that reciprocity and triadic closure reinforce one another when ties are created but partially substitute for one another when ties are maintained, a contrast the coefficients do not reveal.

data.title: Circular regular dessins with underlying graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$: the metacyclic case
data.abstract: A dessin is a 2-cell embedding of a connected bipartite graph into an orientable closed surface. It is regular if the colour- and orientation-preserving automorphism group acts regularly on edges, and circular if every face boundary is a simple cycle. We classify and enumerate circular regular dessins of the complete bipartite multigraph ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$ ($e\ge f\ge 2$, $d\ge 1$) whose automorphism group is {\it metacyclic}. This extends the work of Fan (circular, metacyclic) and Cai--Hu (regular, metacyclic) from simple graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}$ to multigraphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$. Such dessins correspond to non-exact bicyclic factorisations $G=ła\rłb\r\cong\ZZ_{2^{e+d}}\ZZ_{2^{f+d}}$, where $ła\r\capłb\r\cong\ZZ_{2^d}$ and $łba\r\cap ła\r=łba\r\cap łb\r=1$. In general, a group admitting such a factorisation need not be metacyclic; in this paper we impose the additional condition that $G$ is a metacyclic 2-group. Under this assumption, we obtain explicit enumeration formulas for the number of such dessins up to isomorphism. Together with the known classifications for simple graphs (the case $d=0$), this completes the enumeration of the metacyclic case for 2-power complete bipartite multigraphs.

data.title: Confident Fools or Careful Searchers? A Behavioural Study of When LLMs Search Beyond Their Static Internal Memory
data.abstract: Agentic LLM assistants must repeatedly decide whether to answer from memory or to call a tool such as web search. Unnecessary searches cost latency and money; missing ones yield confident but unsupported answers. Prior work mostly measures verbalised confidence or trains new adaptive-retrieval methods, and rarely audits the search decisions that deployed products actually make. We introduce a benchmark of 400 multiple-choice questions that combines widely known inside-knowledge (IK) questions, which should be answered directly, with outside-knowledge (OK) questions about facts from news published after the models' training cut-offs (to our knowledge), which should trigger search or, without tools, abstention. Each item offers an abstain option, and two action-level scores, NAS and KIS, reward searching on OK questions and restraint on IK questions. Across five commercial LLMs with and without their vendors' web search, GPT-5 mini and Grok 4 Fast search on over 90% of OK but only 1% of IK questions, whereas Mistral Small searches on just 20% of OK questions, often abstaining instead of using its tool; one product's search indicator proved unusable. Searching is partly triggered by explicit temporal cues: on uncued OK questions, the NAS of the two selective models falls from about 0.72 to 0.57--0.58. The scores thus measure the search triggering of specific products, not metacognition in a strict sense.

data.title: Bounds for lattice points in terms of volume and successive minima
data.abstract: We prove, in every dimension, the upper bound conjectured by Betke, Henk and Wills for the lattice-point enumerator in terms of volume and successive minima. For every convex body $K\subset R^n$ and full-rank lattice $Λ$, we establish $$ \#(K\capΛ)\le\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\detΛ}\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1+\frac{iλ_i}{2}\right), $$ where $λ_i$ are the successive minima of $(K-K)/2$ with respect to $Λ$. Equality holds precisely for lattice translates of positive integral dilates of unimodular simplices. We also prove $$ \#(\mathrm{int}K\capΛ)\ge\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\detΛ} \left(1-\frac{n}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}λ_i-\frac{n}{2}λ_n\right), $$ which implies the lower estimate with factor $1-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n iλ_i$. In dimension two we prove the lower bound with factor $(1-λ_1/2)(1-λ_2)$ when $λ_2\le1$. We also observe that a conjectured product lower bound for origin-symmetric bodies fails in dimension three. The proofs combine geometric compression, lattice-cell counts in coordinate sections, and an elementary coefficient comparison.

data.title: Statistical inference for quantile correlation regression with bivariate outcomes
data.abstract: It is increasing scientifically important to recognize, quantify and visualize the dependence structure between the bivariate outcomes. In this paper, we investigate conditional dependence using a new dependence measure, the quantile correlation coefficient, which is defined by the Pearson correlation of two quantile-hits of bivariate outcomes. Furthermore, we propose a new regression model for covariate effects directly on the quantile correlation coefficient via a generalized linear regression model. The proposed model has intuitive interpretation and provides a comprehensive view of covariate effects across quantiles of bivariate outcomes. The proposed estimator enjoys desirable asymptotic properties including uniform consistency and weak convergence as a process in the quantile index. Additionally, we develop the general hypothesis testing for the regression coefficients, with applications to summarize covariate effects across the quantile ranges. Simulation studies demonstrate the good finite sample performance of the proposed estimation and inference procedures. Two empirical applications of the proposed method reveal interesting insights in premature twins data for measuring association and ChIP-seq data for measuring reproducibility.

data.title: MotorSense: A Video-EMG Dataset of Motoric Representations for Action Understanding
data.abstract: Computer vision models learn hand action only from its visual consequences, without access to the underlying embodied motor signals. We address this absence with MotorSense, the first large-scale paired egocentric video and surface electromyography (EMG) dataset. MotorSense pairs bimanual EMG bands with egocentric video and yields synchronized video, bimanual EMG and IMU, and audio across 100 hours of unscripted manipulation. EMG offers a powerful scalable alternative to manual annotation: it captures finger movement, hand configuration, and the forces exerted between hand and environment as a dense signal free of occlusion and labeler bias, whereas manual annotation is costly, subjective, and unreliable under occlusion. We use MotorSense to learn sensorimotor alignment, producing an organization of action that is shared across the visual and motoric spaces, through cross-modal pre-training between video and EMG. The resultant vision models are then transferred to downstream tasks that benefit from sensorimotor alignment: in this case, action recognition, 3D hand reconstruction, and 3D contact reconstruction. We further demonstrate a generative application in which EMG motor signals are used to condition a video diffusion model, yielding videos of fine-grained hand manipulation. Across four action-centric computer vision tasks and eight popular video datasets, we demonstrate that sensorimotor alignment provides a stronger foundation for visual representation learning than conventional self-supervised learning methods over video, outperforming every baseline across all tasks and datasets evaluated.

data.title: Strong solvability and its failure for critical SDEs
data.abstract: We revisit the construction of strong solutions to singular SDEs by compactness on Wiener space. For spatially varying diffusion coefficients, assuming sufficiently small form bounds on the drift and diffusion gradient, we use basic energy estimates and an extended compactness criterion for Wiener functionals to construct an approximation-independent stochastic flow of homeomorphisms. Both forward and inverse maps have local Sobolev moment bounds, and the resulting strong solutions are pathwise unique in a class of solutions satisfying a Krylov estimate. We also show that the endpoint critical condition $b\in L^\infty_tL^d_x$, together with $\mathrm{div } b=0$ does not guarantee the existence of a strong solution. For every $d\geq2$, we construct a SDE with a divergence-free drift in this class and an additive Brownian noise, started from the origin, has a weak solution unique in law, but no strong solution. The proof uses logarithmic rescaling to characterize strong solvability by whether the sample measures of an associated stationary diffusion are Dirac masses. Positivity of the top Lyapunov exponent, combined with random SRB theory, rules out this concentration and hence strong solvability.

data.title: When Should AI Agents Ask? Clarification Requests Under Limited Human Attention
data.abstract: AI agents increasingly carry out delegated tasks in parallel, with one person overseeing several of them at once. In practice, an agent often lacks information its task requires, such as an unstated preference, constraint, or specification. It can ask the human to clarify, or it can search for the information itself, for example in past records, which takes time and effort and may fail. In this paper, we study how to coordinate these decisions across several agents that share one human with limited attention. We build a stylized model in which each agent can search, ask, or continue the parts of its task that do not depend on the missing information, and we formulate the problem as a dynamic program. We first show that whether an agent should ask depends on more than its own uncertainty: an agent with other work to do can be better off asking earlier, and which question the human should answer first depends on all waiting questions, so no ranking computed agent by agent is optimal. We then propose the Pairwise Coordination Policy (PCP), which uses exact one- and two-task problems to estimate how pairs of tasks delay each other when they share the human. Theoretically, PCP is exactly optimal when at most two requirements remain unresolved and costs at most twice the optimum when every unresolved requirement must be resolved by the human. We evaluate PCP on 864 synthetic cases and in a case study with LLM agents. On the synthetic benchmark, PCP's mean gap to optimal cost is 0.07%, and it reduces cost by an average of 18-31% relative to three standard rules for when to ask. In the LLM case study, agents completed every task correctly, and PCP achieved the lowest mean cost in all tested settings.

data.title: One Verdict Is Not Enough: Regression Testing Learned World Models and Their Test Harnesses
data.abstract: Learned world models ship as software components whose model versions, preprocessing, and test harnesses change between releases. Work on model updates already counts per-sample regressions, or negative flips, that an accuracy check hides. Two problems remain: a test can pass under one configuration and fail under another, and a harness fault can produce erroneous scores and wrong verdicts without a crash. We present TetraState, a regression-testing protocol for paired possible/impossible video tests. Each test runs under four fixed model-native configurations; its number of correct verdicts assigns one of four outcome classes. Inconclusive tests and failed executions are reported separately alongside the verdict rate. Revisions are compared by per-test outcome transitions, and the harness is versioned as part of the system under test. On all 506 IntPhys 2 Main tests and two heterogeneous systems, Cosmos 3 Nano and V-JEPA 2, two V-JEPA 2 harness revisions move modal accuracy by only 0.2 and 2.6 points yet change 11 and 214 test labels; in the second, accuracy rises although fewer tests are judged correctly, and 43 regressions keep the modal verdict, so a modal-verdict flip check misses them. These results outline a research agenda on configuration-level regression oracles for learned components.

data.title: Weil Operators and Remainders of Anderson Generating Functions over a Punctured Projective Line
data.abstract: Let $A_ρ$ be the coordinate ring of the projective line over $\Fq$ with a closed point of degree $N$ removed. We give finite formulas for higher Weil operators in a basis of Riemann--Roch spaces, which recover the formulas of Hu--Ou--Yang when $N=1$. We identifythese operators with representatives of the residue Casimir tensors and obtain a determinant formula for the Weil pairing, relative to a chosen determinant realization. For a normalized rank-one Drinfeld module, we compute the remainder of its Anderson generating function modulo any nonconstant $p\in A_ρ$. The formula includes multiple zeros and a zero at the ordinary point at infinity. Its last coefficient is a nonzero scalar multiple of an exponential division value. When $(p)$ is a finite principal prime, a value of the associated special function at one zero of $p$ generates the torsion field after adjoining that zero. We give an explicit $q$-linear formula recovering a torsion generator from this value. We also specialize the evaluation theorem of Gazda--Maurischat and compute the different as the principal ideal $(\partial_xp)$.

data.title: When Disclosure Is Compulsory: Evaluating Ride-Hailing Rebalancing Policies with Self-Interested LLM Driver Agents
data.abstract: The EU Platform Work Directive, to be transposed by December 2026, requires ride-hailing platforms to state in plain language the main parameters of their automated decisions and how a worker's behaviour affects them. Such rules are exactly what a large language model (LLM) can read, so drivers will be able to let one decide for them. We compare two main families of rebalancing policy once their rules are public: a reactive policy (R) that sends idle drivers to cover requests just lost, and an anticipatory policy (A) that plans moves on a demand forecast. Each driver is an LLM agent maximizing its own net income, given no rules (N) or the rules at the directive's level of detail (L). We test two LLMs, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Jev, which understand the rules equally well, in a three-zone model and in Manhattan. With the rules disclosed, drivers follow the platform more closely: in Manhattan, the share of relocation offers they decline falls from about four in five to one in four under both policies. Yet the effects differ by policy. For the platform, disclosure costs R 3.7% of its profit in Manhattan, as R now pays for moves drivers used to make for free, while A's profit is unchanged; the two policies, which tie on profit under full compliance, end 6.1% apart. For drivers, disclosure raises income in the small model under both policies and LLMs; for users, it raises the service rate there by 10 to 18 percentage points. In Manhattan, self-interested drivers also make A a win-win-win against full compliance, raising driver income, platform profit and service rate by 10 to 12% each. Rebalancing policies that perform equally well under full compliance can thus show opposite results under mandatory disclosure. The study offers a framework to evaluate such policies under the new requirement and is, to our knowledge, the first to do so with LLM agents.

data.title: Atomistic Emergence of Vibrational Polariton Condensation
data.abstract: Nonequilibrium polariton condensation is a macroscopic quantum phenomenon in which overwhelming population accumulation is observed at the band edge of the lower polariton (LP) dispersion curve under incoherent material pumping. As a promising route toward nonequilibrium Bose--Einstein condensates, its description, however, remains predominantly limited to models with phenomenological material parameters. Herein, a fully atomistic description of vibrational polariton condensation is developed by employing mesoscale cavity molecular dynamics simulations, a method which self-consistently propagates classical electromagnetic dynamics coupled to realistic molecules in a multimode Fabry--Pérot cavity. Under continuous-wave pumping, a lower polariton condensate forms when the infrared cavity is coupled to harmonic, homogeneously broadened molecular vibrations, such as the bending modes of liquid CO2 and CS2, whereas anharmonic stretching modes and liquids with fast intramolecular relaxation hardly condense. The role of libration-bending coupling for facilitating the LP condensation is further discussed. GPU-accelerated mesoscale simulations involving approximately 50 million atoms additionally provide direct two-dimensional real-space imaging of fluid-like polariton patterns during the condensation formation. Overall, this study provides key design insights into vibrational polariton condensation as a novel approach for controlling liquid-phase chemistry.

data.title: Teacher-guided multi-task learning for integrated plasma monitoring on EAST
data.abstract: This paper integrates tokamak plasma disruption prediction, Edge-Localized Mode (ELM) monitoring, Multifaceted Asymmetric Radiation From the Edge (MARFE) detection, and H/L-mode identification into a unified Multi-Task Learning (MTL) model. This integration aims to realize MTL's potential for improving task performance while reducing inference time. However, on datasets constructed from selected EAST discharges recorded between 2015 and 2020, this study found that the traditional MTL method underperformed the corresponding Single-Task Learning (STL) method on some tasks. This performance degradation is the well-known issue of negative transfer. To address this issue, this study proposes the teacher-guided MTL method, using task-specific STL ensembles (teachers) to guide the training of an MTL model (student). The ensemble teachers guide training through soft-target distillation losses for each task of the MTL student model, and increased weighting of each shot's peak-disruptivity window in the disruption prediction label-supervised loss. Test-set results showed that the teacher-guided MTL method outperformed the corresponding STL method in ROC-AUC for all four tasks, eliminating the negative transfer observed with the traditional MTL method. In addition, on the same single GPU or single physical CPU core, the MTL student model can substantially reduce the inference time required to generate all four task outputs compared with the four STL baseline models. This paper offers a promising route to plasma monitoring systems that cover a broader range of phenomena, improve per-task performance and reduce inference time with limited real-time computational resources, supporting future high-performance plasma operation.

data.title: Language Non-Invariance in the Ideological Evaluation of Large Language Models
data.abstract: Recent multilingual studies show that political evaluations of large language models (LLMs) can vary across languages. This paper examines how robust this non-invariance is to questionnaire translation, surface wording, stochastic model variation, and instrument choice, and how much it matters for cross-model comparison. Using the Political Compass, the analysis compares the positions of five LLMs, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, GPT-5.2, Qwen-2.5, and Mistral Large, on its economic and social axes in English, Spanish, and French, with repeated stochastic draws. Additional exercises use independent Spanish and French translations, paraphrased versions in all three languages, and an alternative ideological instrument. Measured ideological positions are not language-invariant: relative to English, between four and five of the ten pairwise model rankings reverse in Spanish or French, depending on the language and axis. The broad cross-language pattern persists under independent translations, indicating that it is not solely an artifact of the official questionnaire versions. Yet the magnitude of particular shifts, and in some cases their sign, remains sensitive to wording and instrument choice. The evidence therefore supports a measurement interpretation: ideological audits recover language- and instrument-conditioned outcomes rather than a language-free political attribute. Because a single provider serves distinct linguistic constituencies through a common product, without users observing what other constituencies receive, this lack of comparability also bears on political accountability and cross-model comparisons.

data.title: Optical Signature of Bias-Induced Carrier Injection in a WSe2/MoS2 Heterostructure Diode
data.abstract: We investigate the bias-dependent photoluminescence (PL) response of a WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructure diode. Under forward bias, trion-related emission in WSe$_2$ is markedly enhanced, whereas reverse bias produces minimal spectral changes. This asymmetric response cannot be explained by electric-field effects alone and instead reflects carrier injection at the functional interface. These results demonstrate that PL provides a direct optical probe of carrier injection in an operating van der Waals heterostructure. More broadly, this approach establishes spatially resolved PL spectroscopy as a versatile tool for pinpointing the interfaces governing device operation in van der Waals heterostructures.

data.title: The Competitive Ratio of Online Budgeted Allocation is Strictly Smaller than $1-1/e$
data.abstract: A well-known conjecture in online algorithms is that the (randomized) competitive ratio of online budgeted allocation is $1-1/e$. We refute this conjecture and show that every randomized online algorithm has competitive ratio at most $1 - 1/e - \varepsilon$ for a (small) absolute constant $\varepsilon > 0$.

data.title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to the Liouville Equation on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
data.abstract: We study stable solutions of the discrete Liouville equation \[ -Δu=e^u \] on infinite, locally finite graphs with polynomial volume growth. We prove that no stable solution exists whenever the order $d$ of polynomial volume growth satisfies $d<10$.

data.title: Induced Lorentzian geometry from the fermionic quantum metric
data.abstract: Quantum geometry is conventionally understood in parameter or momentum space and need not be related to a geometry in configuration space. Here we show for Dirac fermions in a background electromagnetic field that an induced Lorentzian geometry is generated from the fermionic quantum metric. We study a Lorentz covariant phase space worldline path integral construction, whose application of the adiabatic theorem onto spin degrees of freedom leads to the appearance of the Berry phase at $O(\hbar)$, and the quantum metric at $O(\hbar^2)$ in the worldline action. Both the Feynman and retarded/advanced propagators are examined in 3+1 and 2+1 dimensions, whose different on-shell implementations lead to related quantum metrics; QED/QED${}_3$ and condensed matter Dirac theory are considered. An effective theory is found by integrating out the momenta degrees of freedom, which gives rise to an emergent Lorentzian metric in configuration space, whose perturbation to the flat metric is dependent on the quantum metric and the background field strength. Apart from the spin degrees of freedom encoded into the Berry phase, the effective theory describes a scalar particle moving in the induced quantum geometry. Phenomenological applications to the covariant geometry are further studied using spectral holonomy in a gapped 3-dimensional Dirac material.

data.title: Turnpike Properties for Exploratory Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Indefinite Cost Functionals
data.abstract: Continuous-time exploratory stochastic control provides a stochastic control framework for the exploration--exploitation trade-off in reinforcement learning. In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of finite-horizon exploratory stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control problems as the time horizon $T\to\infty$, and establish so-called turnpike properties for such problems. In the finite-horizon setting, we derive a feedback representation of the exploratory stochastic LQ problem and analyze its long-time structure.
