Our theory is justified by the bidirectional population transfer and a holomonic quantum gate implemented by a non-Hermitian three-level system in $Λ$ type. For the population transfer, controlled gain and loss reduce the required coherent pulse area, enabling shorter transfer times than the Hermitian benchmark with the same average Rabi frequency. Our work integrates the universal quantum control (UQC) into the biorthogonal representation, displaying full-rank passage engineering with coherent operations in non-Hermitian systems.

data.title: Market Efficiency and Capacity Investment under Flexible Price-Making Loads: A Computational Study
data.abstract: Large flexible loads such as data centers can shift consumption across locations and hours to lower their bills. We model a price-making consumer leading the system operator in a Stackelberg game and compare its shifts with a cost-minimizing planner's over a simulated RTS-GMLC year. Strategic temporal and spatial shifting capture 75% and 93% of the planner's savings, forgoing the rest mostly by withholding flexibility to protect favorable prices. Scarce capacity and abundant renewables raise this share for temporal shifting; scarce transmission lowers it for spatial shifting. Temporal and spatial flexibility substitute for thermal and transmission capacity, respectively, and complement renewables.

data.title: Only constant mean curvature surfaces in $E(κ,τ)$, $τ\ne0$, have a holomorphic original Abresch-Rosenberg differential
data.abstract:
For immersed surfaces in the homogeneous spaces $E(κ,τ)$ with $τ

data.title: Quantum Advantage in Beam-Displacement Estimation for Inter-Satellite Quantum-Secure Time Transfer
data.abstract: In this work, we investigate the practical feasibility of achieving a quantum advantage, in the context of inter-satellite quantum communication, of satellite position estimation. The investigation focuses on a quantum-enhanced scheme in which squeezing is added to the derivative mode of a Gaussian probe beam as a means of estimating photon-beam displacement. The performance of the scheme is compared against the standard quantum limit achieved by an optimal classical beam-displacement estimation scheme under a fair same-total-energy constraint. We find that although the benefit provided by squeezing rapidly diminishes as the inter-satellite distance increases due to diffraction-induced beam spreading and subsequent truncation by the finite receiver aperture, a quantum advantage can still be expected over inter-satellite distances up to approximately 100 km under practical satellite configurations. This distance scale between satellites is anticipated for Starlink-type satellite constellations.

data.title: Beyond CLIP: Calibrated (Few-Shot) Defect Detection With System One Decision Models
data.abstract: Cameras and vision sensors are widely used for product and process inspection in manufacturing environments. Traditionally, this process required thousands of images of both nominal and defective products to train such models. Recent research shows that vision transformer (ViT) models, such as CLIP, can reduce this requirement to 50-100 images per nominal and defective class. However, collecting even 50 defective images can be difficult in high-yield or low-volume manufacturing processes. In this paper, we examine the utility of two recently proposed structured decision models (Jev and Clef-Flash) in applications using as few as k=2 reference images per class at inference. In the process, we provide three main contributions: (a) a framework for k-shot learning of these models for image classification/inspection applications; (b) an agentic approach for automatically refining the text descriptions that guide image classification in these decision models; and (c) an approach to calibrate the resulting defect probabilities to improve their reliability for inspection decisions. We test these contributions in five manufacturing case studies. Using two reference images per class, both Jev and Clef-Flash outperform CLIP's test accuracies with the same references (0.75-1.00 [Jev] and 0.71-0.99 [Clef-Flash] vs 0.67-0.84 [CLIP]). Furthermore, we show that our agentic refinement of text descriptions significantly improves accuracy across 6 of 8 model-application combinations, and our calibration approach reduces the Brier score in 13 of the 15 model-application configurations. To support the reproducibility of our work, we provide our replication code and have created the R "decisions" package for evaluating additional models. We also provide a publicly available web app that allows practitioners to inspect their own images with no code.

data.title: Filtration theorems, Hilbert functions, and generic freeness
data.abstract: Let $M$ be a finitely generated module over a ring $R$ that is a finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring $A$ by $r$ elements. We prove that there are finitely many primes $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ of $A$ such that $M$ has a countable ascending filtration by finitely generated $A$-modules with the property that every factor $F_n$ has a filtration by cyclic modules of the form $A/P_i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that the number of copies $H_i(n)$ of $A/P_i$ that occur in the filtration of $F_n$ is an eventually polynomial function of $n$. We prove a number of bounds on the degrees of these eventually polynomial functions: $r-1$ is always a bound, and the dimension of $\dim(M_P)-1$ is a bound under mild hypotheses. One application is an immediate proof Grothedieck's classic theorem on generic freeness. Several other applications are given.

data.title: Algebraic Vector Fields of Connected Semi-simple Matrix Groups are 3-generated
data.abstract: We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields for any connected, semi-simple matrix group over $\mathbb{F}$, for $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$, can be generated by three $\mathbb{F}$-complete algebraic vector fields.

data.title: Iris on Indirection Theory: Lightweight Higher-order Ghost State
data.abstract: Today, semantic models of languages with concurrency and higher-order state are constructed using step-indexed predicates over resources and higher-order ghost state. There are two main lines of work for constructing such models. On the one hand, Iris provides these in full generality, at the cost of a large body of mechanised domain theory that is difficult to learn and port to new proof assistants. On the other hand, Indirection Theory is much simpler through the use of ordinary dependent types, but its foundation in separation algebra limits the expressiveness of its resource model compared to Iris-style higher-order ghost state. We resolve this conundrum by showing that Indirection Theory can be as expressive as Iris. To that end, we give a lightweight mechanisation of Indirection Theory in Lean, generalised so knots contain resources from an Iris-style resource algebra functor. We then reconstruct the Iris base logic on top of it. The advantage of this approach is in the elementary metatheory: a user can follow the whole construction without domain theory. We conduct two case studies to show that the base logic is expressive and faithful to Iris: a biorthogonal logical relation for higher-order state, and an Iris-style program logic with invariants and user-definable ghost state, complete enough to verify concurrent and higher-order programs.

data.title: Rainbow Hamiltonian paths in graph collections under edge-size conditions
data.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct graphs of order $n$ on the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $φ\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{φ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. In this paper, we show that if $n\ge3$, $e(G_i)> \binom{n-2}{2}+2$ for each $i\in[n-1]$ and $G_j$ is connected for some $j\in[n-1]$, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian path in $\mathbf{G}$ unless $n=6$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{5}\cong K_2\vee 4K_1$, or $n=8$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{7}\cong K_3\vee 5K_1$. This corrects Theorem 6 in [Graphs Combin., \textbf{41}(6)(2025), 119] and relaxes its hypothesis from requiring all $G_i$ to be connected to only requiring that at least one $G_i$ is connected, where $i\in[n-1]$. Moreover, we show that if $n\ge2$ and $e(G_i)\ge \binom{n-1}{2}$ for each $i\in[n-1]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ contains a rainbow Hamiltonian path unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{n-1}\cong K_{n-1}\cup K_1$, or $n=4$ with $G_1=G_2=G_3\cong K_{1,3}$. As a consequence, Theorem 2 of [Discrete Math., \textbf{347}(2024), 114128] follows immediately.

data.title: Interpretable Multiple-Instance Learning of Glomerular Pathomics and Subtype Ratios for eGFR Classification
data.abstract: Chronic kidney disease is characterized by structural alterations in renal tissue and progressive loss of kidney function. While glomerular subtype ratios provide a compact and clinically meaningful summary of glomerular composition, representing pathomic information using whole-slide image (WSI)-level mean values diminishes glomerulus-level heterogeneity and the contribution of less prevalent patterns. In this proof-of-concept study, we investigated whether modeling individual glomeruli using multiple-instance learning (MIL) could provide complementary information to conventional subtype ratios for estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) classification. We analyzed 162 kidney-biopsy WSIs from 162 patients, categorizing renal function as eGFR < 60 or >= 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Quantitative size, shape, intensity, and texture features were extracted from segmented glomeruli, representing each patient as a bag of glomerular instances. An attention-based MIL model was trained to aggregate these heterogeneous pathomic profiles. We evaluated subtype ratios, pathomics, and their combination using ABMIL, with a mean-pooled multilayer perceptron baseline. In five-fold cross-validation, the subtype-ratio-only model achieved an AUC of 0.7262 +/- 0.0596. MIL using pathomics alone achieved an AUC of 0.7362 +/- 0.0788, whereas integrating pathomics with subtype ratios produced the highest mean AUC of 0.7630 +/- 0.0665. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine individual feature contributions. These results demonstrate that MIL-based pathomics can complement established glomerular subtype ratios by capturing additional glomerulus-level information for quantitative kidney-biopsy analysis.

data.title: Shifting Focus by Reliability: Geometric Fusion Modulation for Robust RGB-T Detection
data.abstract: RGB-thermal (RGB-T) object detectors combine visible and thermal imagery for robust detection, but signal corruption in either stream can substantially degrade accuracy. Restoration-based methods incur significant latency and do not consistently improve downstream accuracy, raising a more direct question: rather than restoring corrupted inputs, can we efficiently adapt the detector to their varying signal quality? Conventional PEFT offers an efficient route, but its input-independent corrections cannot track diverse test-time corruptions. Our controlled corruption sweeps show that corruption types have similar effects near clean conditions but diverge increasingly with severity, motivating corruption-aware, per-input adaptation. We therefore propose PG-FM (Prompt-Guided Feature Modulation), which adapts RGB-T object detectors to the estimated corruption type and severity of each modality. Under controlled RGB-T corruption simulations, PG-FM preserves clean-set performance, improves mAP50 by up to 20.8 points on FLIR and 19.9 points on KAIST, and transfers without retraining to unmodified, naturally acquired external RGB-T datasets.

data.title: On hot spots of the torsion function and the ground state of the Laplacian
data.abstract: We compare the maximum points \(P_Ω\) and \(Q_Ω\) of the torsion function and the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction. We begin with a systematic analytic description of both hot spots over the full range of opening angles of circular sectors: uniqueness, strict monotonicity with respect to the angle, distinct small-angle asymptotics, and explicit limiting equations in the slit-disk limit. We also prove the existence of a coincidence angle and establish arithmetic properties of the limiting coordinates. We then consider bounded convex planar domains with a line of symmetry, and we prove the sharp diameter-normalized identity \[ \sup_Ω \frac{|P_Ω-Q_Ω|}{\operatorname{diam}(Ω)}=\frac12. \] Its upper-bound argument uses standard localization in the heart and an elementary geometric enclosure. Sharpness follows from thin convex domains with a vanishing relative width perturbation peaking near one endpoint: the torsion hot spot approaches that endpoint, whereas the ground-state hot spot approaches the midpoint.

data.title: Terminal-state theorems for a two-stage Maki--Thompson rumor model: final size, stifler composition, and non-identifiability from pooled statistics
data.abstract: Rumor models of the Daley--Kendall and Maki--Thompson family anchor the statistical mechanics of social contagion, yet the stifler composition a rumor leaves behind has resisted closed-form analysis. Inspired by the asymmetric two-step pairing (A2SP) process of step-growth polymerization, we import its common-factor cancellation into a minimal two-stage MT variant in which re-contacted spreaders are re-activated into a senior class at rate $αk_1$ rather than stifled, and obtain exact terminal-state theorems. (i) Saturation: the rumor exhausts the ignorant pool for every stifling-to-recruitment ratio $μ>0$, with a three-way tail classification and a logarithmically critical line at $μ=1$. (ii) Final size: the terminal stifler pool splits as $(x_1,x_2)=(μ/(α+μ),α/(α+μ))$, independent of seed size; the fingerprint inverts linearly ($α=μx_2/x_1$) and matches Gillespie simulations within $0.95\%$. (iii) Pooled versus history-resolved: pooled statistics are exactly $α$-free on any static graph; only the history-resolved composition carries $α$. Restoring the classic teller-retires channel breaks the exact closure beyond quantified gates (contact rates of $1$--$3\%$ of $k_1$ for spreader channels at $μ\leq1.5$, up to $32\%$ at $μ=2$), and on configuration-model networks the composition bias decays as $\langle k\rangle^{-0.71}$. An exploratory inversion of 354,930 Higgs--Twitter retweet episodes, screened by an identity check and four negative controls, yields $\hatα=2.21\%$ (joint cluster-bootstrap CI $[1.6\%,3.0\%]$; $\approx3.7\%$ after calibration at the matched threshold). Terminal compositions identify this effective re-activation rate, an upper bound on contact-coupled re-activation; the mechanism itself requires timing information beyond the terminal state.

data.title: Resource Locks and Fast Unlock for Shared Balances in Certificate-Based Payment Systems
data.abstract: Certificate-based payment systems such as FastPay settle a payment with one round of signatures from a quorum of validators and avoid global ordering. The client collects the signatures, and validators never talk to each other. We observe that this client-driven design is complete only as long as no lock is ever undone. Each account has a single writer, a conflict can only come from that writer's own misbehavior, and the account stays locked as the penalty. Stablecoin payments routinely need balances that several accounts debit: treasuries, merchant pools, allowances and subscriptions. There, honest accounts race, locks must be undone, and a quorum certificate held privately by a client can be silently overridden. We prove that no unlock rule is safe in this setting unless certificate formation is visible to validators. We present a hybrid protocol. Personal accounts keep the client-driven FastPay path unchanged. A shared resource is a balance with its own version number and a set of authorized accounts. Transactions on shared resources are submitted to any validator and certified by a two-phase broadcast, ECHO then READY. The admission check requires both the sender's nonce and the resource's nonce to be free. Without contention, this path needs no consensus. When concurrent debits split the votes in any proportion, validators detect the split themselves, freeze the affected resource version, and resolve it with one agreement instance scoped to that version. Losing transactions return their sender nonce. We prove consistency, no overdraft, validity, finality and liveness. The protocol composes with the PDCC reconfiguration protocol.

data.title: Nonthermal coalescence parameter of light nuclei production in pp collisions at LHC energies
data.abstract: We study the light nucleus production in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=7$ and $13$~TeV reported by the ALICE Collaboration within the color string fragmentation framework. We adopt the Schwinger mechanism with string tension fluctuations as the particle production mechanism describing the $p_T$ spectrum. The approximately thermal behavior observed in the light-nucleus spectra motivates the use of a perturbative series expansion of the $q$-Gaussian string tension fluctuations around $q=1$. The resulting $p_T$ spectrum is expressed as a perturbative series expansion around the thermal distribution with nonthermal corrections given by Gamma distributions, providing closed forms for the effective temperature, moments, and cumulants. In the superstatistical framework, the associated temperature fluctuations show that the medium in which light nuclei are produced is out of equilibrium. Additionally, we derive closed formulas for the coalescence parameter at arbitrary order, which agree well with experimental data. Our results also show that the mass--temperature relation ($T_N/m_N \approx AT_A/m_A$) between the nucleons and nuclei is not preserved in the coalescence process.

data.title: Falcons: Pushing the Speed-Ratio Limits of Lossy Compression for Parallel Scientific Applications
data.abstract: The extreme volume of scientific data has become a critical challenge for modern exa-scale scientific computing applications, and error-bounded lossy compression remains indispensable for scientific data management due to its high data reduction rate and controllable data fidelity. However, to ensure sufficient data reduction, existing compressors incur prohibitive computational overheads in real-world parallel scientific computing applications. To overcome the performance bottlenecks of error-bounded lossy compression, we present \textbf{Falcons}, a broadly deployable error-bounded lossy compressor that simultaneously achieves \textbf{high compression ratios with ultra-fast throughput, minimizing the overhead in parallel scientific applications}. Falcons integrates three key designs: memory-regularized interpolation with SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) vectorization, distribution-adaptive lossless coding, and application-oriented optimizations for multiple parallelization schemes. Across our evaluations on cutting-edge supercomputers, Falcons clearly outperforms state-of-the-art compressors, simultaneously achieving up to 29\% compression ratio improvement and 255\% throughput improvement. In case studies of real-world applications, Falcons accelerates large-scale parallel data I/O and remote transfer by up to 44.6\% and 51.5\%, and provides 1.55$\times$ end-to-end speedup for the full WRF (Weather Research \& Forecasting) application workflow.

data.title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models
data.abstract: Real-world image editing requires coordinating multiple visual transformations with content preservation and reference constraints, yet aggregate scores can readily obscure unmet local requirements. Effective evaluation must therefore identify local failures and translate them into priorities for subsequent model improvement. We introduce WeGenEditBench, comprising 2,740 evaluation instances and 148 task types across single-image, text-intensive, and multi-reference editing. Pre-generated checklists shared across models decompose each request into atomic requirements; item-level deductions and visual evidence are established first and then summarized into scores for edit execution, preservation, visual quality, and task-specific correctness. To support the experience-acquisition component of recursive self-improvement (RSI), we develop WeGenEvoStudio, a unified multi-agent harness for RSI-oriented learning that integrates model-conditioned failure diagnosis, retrieval-grounded data construction, supervised adaptation, and re-evaluation. Among 15 evaluated configurations, GPT-Image-2 leads single-image editing with an Overall score of 4.076, while Seedream-5.0-Pro leads text-intensive editing at 4.291. Evolution experiments across four generation and editing benchmarks demonstrate substantial targeted gains: on their report-selected Top-5 single-image targets, FLUX.2 [dev] improves Overall from 1.083 to 3.517, while Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 gains 13.2%. Together, our benchmark and harness provide a foundation for developing more reliable image models through interpretable evaluation and feedback-driven learning.

data.title: Random-Sign IBLTs: Calibration-Free Self-Sizing After Decoding Failure
data.abstract: We propose the random-sign Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT) for calibration-free self-sizing after decoding failure. In a two-round set reconciliation protocol, the receiver uses the failed first-round table to estimate an upper bound on the unknown difference size $d$ and size the second-round table. In standard IBLTs, failure selection couples the overlap bias with the sign composition of the set difference, making practical sizing depend on offline simulation calibration. A shared pseudorandom sign independent of the position mapping removes this dependence while preserving cell fields, field widths, and ideal peeling recovery. We prove exact unbiasedness on every fixed mapping, a Gaussian limit after failure for $d\gg\sqrt M$, and a discrete limit dominated by duplicate edge pairs at smaller scales, where $M$ is the number of cells. These results yield a Skellam upper-bound rule whose conditional miss rate is asymptotically at most the target risk, uniformly over all $d\ge2$, without offline calibration. More than 500 million paired decoding trials and end-to-end protocol experiments support the design. For small differences, the Gaussian rule's conditional miss rate exceeds the target by more than a factor of 8. The Skellam rule meets the target within sampling error across all 189 tested load configurations. Total two-round communication approaches that of an oracle using the true $d$ in the same protocol. With fixed deployment parameters, precomputed table lookup reduces sizing to less than one microsecond, with total protocol time within 0.5 percent of the Gaussian rule.

data.title: EMT Assessment of SCR and X/R Effects on Current-Priority-Dependent LVRT Response of a Grid-Following BESS
data.abstract: Low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) forces a grid-following inverter to allocate finite converter current between active- and reactive-current objectives. This paper uses a PSCAD electromagnetic-transient (EMT) representation of an aggregated battery energy storage system (BESS) to quantify how short-circuit ratio (SCR) and grid impedance X/R ratio alter that tradeoff. Active-current priority and reactive-current priority are compared for five paired grid conditions under the same 150-ms balanced three-phase fault, with pre-fault active power approximately 0.84 pu, POI reactive-power exchange near 0 pu, and a 1.0-pu dq-current limit. Fundamental positive-sequence voltage and power are reconstructed from 100-$μ$s three-phase EMT outputs. Across the fixed-fault SCR sweep, the Q-priority late-fault voltage advantage increases from 0.046 pu in the strongest tested grid to 0.129 pu in the weakest; the weakest P-priority case also shows active-power reversal and a pronounced controller-frequency excursion. At fixed SCR, changing X/R produces a smaller increase from 0.092 to 0.112 pu, mainly through reduced P-priority voltage support. Because the common physical fault also deepens the passive retained-voltage condition as SCR decreases, the SCR result is interpreted as a fixed-fault grid-strength sensitivity rather than a constant-sag comparison. Grid strength is the larger sensitivity in the tested matrix, while X/R remains an additional modifier under the studied fault conditions.

data.title: Beyond Scarcity: When Encoder Adaptation Is Worthwhile
data.abstract: Long-tailed recognition often learns a shared representation before correcting the classifier for class imbalance. Once the classifier has been rebalanced, however, final accuracy does not reveal whether further encoder adaptation remains worthwhile. Standard imbalance benchmarks obscure this question because they jointly vary the number of distinct examples available to rare classes and the frequency with which those examples shape the representation. We introduce a controlled evaluation framework that separates unique support from representation allocation and estimates the incremental value of encoder updates through matched classifier-only and full-network continuations from a common corrected model. The framework combines stage-specific controls, multiple representation and adaptation objectives, whole-distribution metrics, and hierarchical inference over class assignments, support reconstructions, and optimization runs. Across the controlled study, the same low-support regime moves from one in which classifier-only training is adequate to one in which encoder adaptation yields a practically meaningful benefit solely as representation allocation becomes more imbalanced. The transition persists across classifier corrections, representation objectives, normalization and augmentation controls, and ImageNet-scale evaluation, while preserving frequent-class accuracy. Under the prespecified one-percentage-point operating margin, the two regimes are separated by simultaneous confidence bounds. These results show that benchmark construction can alter a post-correction training decision and that support size alone does not characterize the remaining value of representation adaptation.

data.title: Capability-Conditioned Graph Control Barrier Functions for Zero-Shot Safe Navigation of Heterogeneous Mobile Robot Teams
data.abstract: Multi-robot systems are increasingly deployed as heterogeneous fleets with diverse kinematic and actuation capabilities. While graph control barrier function (GCBF) methods provide a scalable framework for decentralized safe control, existing approaches typically assume homogeneous robot dynamics. Methods that directly encode robot classes can distinguish known types, but do not represent state-dependent motion capabilities or naturally transfer to unseen robot models. To address this challenge, we propose the Capability-Conditioned Heterogeneous Graph Control Barrier Function (CC-HGCBF), defined in a shared second-order reference-point operational space. This formulation provides a common geometric representation of safety across heterogeneous robots while retaining their model-specific dynamics and admissible control constraints. To enable zero-shot transfer, we introduce the Radial Capability Field (RCF), a compact, fixed-dimensional representation of each robot's state-dependent finite-horizon reachable velocity set. Conditioning the shared graph barrier and decentralized policy on the RCF enables them to adapt to changes in robot state, kinematic constraints, and control limits without relying on predefined robot identities. We jointly train the barrier and policy using proactive safety labeling and neural CBF-QP supervision, and evaluate them on mixed teams containing both seen and unseen robot models. Experiments demonstrate scalable safe coordination and zero-shot transfer to robot models and capability variations withheld during training. Physical-robot experiments further demonstrate zero-shot deployment to unseen kinematic models without retraining.

data.title: Beyond Response Scoring: An AI-aware Cognitive Supervision Framework for Automated Mathematical Short Answer Grading
data.abstract: Transformer-based language models have achieved remarkable success in automated short answer grading (ASAG). However, current methods in ASAG struggle to comprehend, reason about and evaluate complex mathematical answers involving symbols and formulas. These score-only methods fail to generalize across diverse responses and skill states associated with identical scores. Moreover, they ignore the potential upward bias introduced by generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage in assessing students' performance and knowledge mastery. To address these limitations, we propose AICG (AI-aware Cognitive-supervised Grading), a two-branch multi-task framework. The first branch combines RoBERTa-based regression, ordinal, and classification heads for individual-answer grading. The second branch uses an expert-designed Q-matrix to associate responses with assessed skills and jointly predicts G-DINA-derived skill mastery and learning gain. Through the shared encoder, these skill-level targets provide cognitive supervision for answer grading beyond score labels. AICG further uses a Gen-AI detector, trained through supervised contrastive pretraining followed by linear classification, to estimate assistance probabilities and convert them into reliability weights, attenuating unreliable cognitive evidence during learning assessment. We conduct experiments on 49,402 instructor-graded responses spanning 19 academic semesters. Relative to RoBERTa regression, AICG reduces mean absolute error (MAE) by 50.3% and improves quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) from 0.798 to 0.927. Ablations identify Q-matrix-guided cognitive supervision as the primary source of improvement, while AI-aware weighting further reduces overall MAE by 4.2% over the unweighted cognitive model and consistently improves MAE and QWK across the four most recent post-Gen-AI semesters.

data.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
data.abstract: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost? We present TinyAstral, a two-stage approach. We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test. We then freeze the final harness, collect teacher trajectories with reasoning and failure recovery, and distill a small student that replaces the teacher in the same harness. On RoboTwin, harness evolution raises the teacher's success from 33.4% to 63.6%; the final 4B student reaches 62.8%. Across four harness versions, distilled 4B students score close to their corresponding teachers, and later versions yield stronger students, showing that harness evolution gains carry into compact models. The harness gains also transfer to other frozen planners without retraining. On identical episodes, the final 4B student outperforms open 4B agents, the open 27B harness-RSI model SenseNova-RoboRSI, and our own teacher model placed in three competitors' harnesses. It stays close to its teacher on all three training benchmarks, and on three benchmarks never used for RSI or training it scores close to a 552B planner running the same harness. On the measured deployment episodes, it uses about one fifth of its teacher's accelerator time.

data.title: Web application for retrospective geomagnetic storm detection, main phase analysis and identification of solar wind influence on storm intensity
data.abstract: This work presents a web application for retrospective detection and analysis of geomagnetic storms using hourly Dst and solar wind data from OMNIWeb. The application detects storm events, identifies their main phases, computes solar wind derived parameters during the main phase, and examines their relationship with storm intensity. Its detection and main phase identification parameters are user-adjustable, allowing different assumptions to be tested interactively rather than imposed through a single fixed parameter set. The analysis covers the period from 1964 through May 2026. Using the default parameter set, 1796 storms with Dst_min <= -50 nT were detected, including 1422 moderate storms (-100 < Dst_min <= -50 nT), 347 intense storms (-250 < Dst_min <= -100 nT), and 27 super-storms (Dst_min <= -250 nT). After filtering for reliable main phase identification, 1643 storms were retained. The average main phase duration per class was 9.25 hours for moderate storms, 11.30 hours for intense storms and 13.75 hours for super-storms. After also requiring OMNIWeb solar wind data availability, 990 storms remained for examining the relationship between storm intensity and solar wind derived parameters over the main phase. The strongest correlations with |Dst_min| were obtained for peak dawn-dusk electric field (Eyp: R = 0.836), peak southward IMF (Bzp: R = -0.811), and integrated electric field (Eyi: R = 0.759). These results are consistent with the importance of the solar wind electric field and southward interplanetary magnetic field in geomagnetic storm development. All outputs are downloadable for further user-defined analysis.

data.title: A Positional Realizability Theory of Length Generalization in Single-Head Attention
data.abstract: Why does length generalization (LG) depend so sharply on the positional encoding (PE)? Relative schemes extrapolate fixed offsets, absolute schemes fix positions, and neither handles growing offsets. We give a realizability theory for a deliberately controlled abstraction, a single positional-only attention head, that derives this well-documented empirical pattern and says precisely where it holds and breaks. The device is a simulation transfer operator $T_L$ that re-evaluates a selected length-$L_0$-realizing positional kernel on the longer grid, with a scalar $α_L \in [0,1]$ read off before any training from $(Φ, t_n)$ alone. Here $α_L$ serves as the computable witness of that taxonomy's derivation, not as a stronger empirical predictor. Our results are a relative-head deep-row characterization for kernels with a strict unique global maximizer (Theorem 2), an absolute/relative duality that derives the pattern (Proposition 4), a learned-absolute underdetermination result, and a static expressivity bound; a sufficiency theorem (Theorem 1) bridges $α_L$ to LG, and the general deterministic case is a precise open conjecture (correcting a tempting but invalid "outside-colspan" argument). Experiments confirm the structure: in the controlled single-head regime $α_L$ exactly separates the taxonomy's generalizing and non-generalizing (PE, task) cells (2625 trained-model measurements; stable at vocab 64/d=128). Together, these results turn the received PE taxonomy into a positional-kernel transfer theorem, and identify the content and depth mechanisms that escape it. The theory concerns the positional channel alone: tasks whose targets depend on token content, including the standard length-generalization suite such as addition and sorting, fall outside Theorem 2.

data.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
data.abstract: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schrödinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

data.title: DistFlow and Its Conic Relaxation: Regularity, Monotonicity, and Hybrid Exactness via Graph Decomposition
data.abstract: Classical exactness conditions for conic relaxations of the DistFlow model rely, among other assumptions, either on all nodal injections being adjustable or on a network-wide path condition. In practice, these conditions may not hold uniformly across a feeder: controllable distributed energy resources (DERs) sit at some buses and fixed loads at others, while reverse flows from DER-rich regions can violate the path condition. This paper certifies exactness region by region and composes the regional certificates, accounting for perturbations that propagate downstream through voltages. We first introduce a subtree voltage stability region, in which the network and all compatible subtrees remain regular. Within it, two endpoint sign conditions, one relaxing the nonnegative-flow assumption and one implied by the classical path condition, yield monotone responses of voltages, currents, and losses to root voltages. Using duality, the implicit function theorem, and sign properties of inverse sensitivity matrices, we recast both classical arguments as individual sign certificates on branch multipliers. This turns exactness into a branchwise property that can be certified region by region. A partition rule then splits the network into dispatchable and passive subtrees, and a hybrid certificate combines their local conditions into exactness of the full-network relaxation, under additional operating-limit and objective conditions. In particular, placing controllable DERs at both ends of a branch with large reverse flow exempts that branch from the passive sign conditions.

data.title: Control-Layer Interpretation of Reactive Power Recovery Limits in EMT-RMS Model Benchmarking of Inverter-Based Resources
data.abstract: EMT--RMS benchmarking is widely used to verify cross-platform consistency of inverter-based resource (IBR) dynamic models. This paper examines a 200 MW anonymized IBR represented in PSCAD and PSS/E. The EMT model separates inverter electrical capability from a plant-level power plant controller (PPC) recovery target, whereas the RMS model represents these functions through REECC and REPCA parameters. Directly assigning the PPC target of $\pm 0.2764$ pu to REPCA hard reactive limits is initialization-inconsistent at the original lagging operating point because the initial reactive command is 0.396273 pu. A second, near-unity-power-factor operating point initializes successfully with the same diagnostic limit, demonstrating that the conflict is operating-point dependent. Using the non-conflicting capability mapping removes the original hard-limit conflict, but the benchmark still shows 18.5--30.2 MVAr post-event POI reactive-power differences from PSCAD. A one-at-a-time REPCA $K_c$ sensitivity under matched benchmark initial conditions further shows that RMS recovery is parameter- and limit-dependent: at $K_c=0.05$ and 0.10 the aggregate machine reactive output reaches the configured capability bounds, while $K_c=0.15$ moves VDOWN, VUP, and HVRT off those bounds and changes their settled POI reactive power by 8.94, 18.00, and 3.17 MVAr, respectively. Machine-to-POI accounting further shows why machine-side saturation need not reproduce the POI-level PPC recovery magnitude. The results distinguish initialization feasibility from recovery equivalence and provide a control-layer diagnostic workflow beyond waveform comparison.

data.title: Corroborative Learning: Mutual Enhancement through Task-Response Reconstruction
data.abstract: In pattern analysis, models trained independently for the same task often develop complementary capabilities through differences in architecture, data, and optimization. Exploiting complementarity while retaining independent deployment is central to collaborative learning. Most methods establish transfer by reducing differences in predictions, relations, or representations between target and collaborator, although these differences also underlie complementarity. This creates a structural trade-off between reducing differences for knowledge exchange and preserving them for complementarity. We therefore propose Corroborative Learning (CL). Each model forms task-driven responses, with cross-group support from its collaborator. Source-excluded reconstruction of response increments from collaborator representations separates fitting and evaluation across disjoint groups and selectively constrains directions by cross-group reconstructability. The process requires no direct output or feature matching or additional inference dependency. Furthermore, with linear reconstruction and fixed collaborator representations, the loss equals a positive semidefinite directional regularizer, constraining less reconstructable directions more strongly. Signal and noise conditions characterize when directional shrinkage reduces response-estimation error. Across six language tasks, 24 models, and 36 pairs, CL improves over capacity-matched independent adaptation on every task, with positive gains across most directed model combinations. Pairwise comparisons show broad advantages over transfer and mutual-learning methods and different gains from complementarity across collaboration rules. Low-label language and vision results support cross-domain applicability. Task-relevant differences can support mutual enhancement without eliminating disagreement.

data.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant Γ_{1,4} = 8
data.abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants Γ_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.

data.title: A Large Eddy Simulation Study of Turbine Pitch Motion Effects on Power Generation in Fully Developed Floating Wind Turbine Arrays
data.abstract: Interactions between floating wind turbines and the marine atmospheric boundary layer affect turbine wakes and power output. This study examines the impact of turbine representations and platform pitching motion on power predictions for aligned floating wind turbine arrays. Large-eddy simulations (LES) are performed for a fully developed wind turbine array boundary layer with periodic streamwise and spanwise boundary conditions and moving surface drag (MOSD) at the bottom surface. A proposed power-curve-aware extension of the conventional actuator disk model (PCADM) is compared with the traditional constant coefficient actuator disk model (CCADM), which is valid in principle only during Region 2 operation. Harmonic pitching motion matched to a representative ocean wave frequency is prescribed for IEA 15MW turbines mounted on the UMaine VolturnUS-S platform. Results demonstrate that the CCADM produces unphysical power overshoot when relative velocities induced by harmonic pitching periodically exceed rated speed, while the PCADM eliminates these unrealistic excursions from the actual turbine operating range. Various wind-wave conditions and relative pitching motions for an aligned farm with PCADM turbines are analyzed, including in-phase, opposite-phase, and incommensurate-phase row-to-row relative turbine motion. Results reveal that, depending on operational regions, turbine pitching motion can either increase or decrease mean turbine power output. Among the relative phases considered, in-phase motions produce larger fluctuations at the farm scale due to stronger turbine-turbine correlations. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for turbine motion and associated changes in operational regions when modeling turbine and wind farm power production in LES of offshore floating wind farms using actuator disk representations.

data.title: RTL-Interact: Training EDA-Interactive Models for Multi-Task RTL Design
data.abstract: Large language models offer a promising route to register-transfer-level (RTL) design, but reliable implementations require checking and revision based on electronic design automation (EDA) tools' feedback. Existing RTL-specialized models often lack learned interaction with such EDA tools or rely on separate generation and repair components. We introduce RTL-Interact, a multi-task post-training framework that trains a single RTL-specialized model to generate RTL, construct task-appropriate EDA checks, and revise implementations using tool feedback. The framework combines automatically constructed multi-task demonstrations with staged supervision from chain-of-thought to tool-integrated reasoning. We further introduce Pattern-Aware Policy Optimization (PAPO) for multi-task reinforcement learning. PAPO augments Group Relative Policy Optimization with correctness-gated rewards that favor concise successful checking while rewarding effective revision, and uses task grouping to preserve coverage across objectives. On CVDP, RTL-Interact-32B achieves 48.7% weighted Pass@1 and 68.9% Pass@5, surpassing its teacher model, DeepSeek-V3.2, while RTL-Interact-8B achieves 44.9% weighted Pass@1. Additionally, we show that PAPO can reduce average tool calls by 63.8% while improving Pass@1. Both models also outperform all RTL-specialized baselines on VerilogEval v2 and RTLLM v2, demonstrating the effectiveness of our method.

data.title: Imputing Missing Data in Longitudinal Life-Logging Athlete Data
data.abstract: Long-term, diverse personal informatics data enables athletes to understand and act on their health and performance goals, whether assessing readiness right now, tracking how soreness relates to training load over time, or predicting how sleep affects next-day performance. However, the inherent missingness in longitudinal data, if handled inappropriately, can bias these analyses. To our knowledge, no prior work has systematically benchmarked classical and deep learning imputation methods on long-term self-tracking data from athlete populations. We evaluate six imputation methods across four missingness mechanisms at missingness rates spanning 10-80%. Using seven diverse long-term self-tracking datasets from 231 individuals, we assess both point accuracy and the preservation of temporal and multivariate structure. Our results show that no single method dominates across all conditions and reveal a critical trade-off: while PAIN is superior on point-wise accuracy, deep learning methods (BRITS, GRU-D, and GRIN) are better at preserving multivariate and temporal structure, particularly under higher missingness. Our findings offer a practical, goal-conditioned framework that guides researchers in selecting imputation strategies aligned with both the underlying missingness mechanism and the specific analytical goal of long-term self-tracking studies.

data.title: Delta-Seeker: Closed-Loop Generative Search for Novel Circuit Design Discovery
data.abstract: Generative models are increasingly used for circuit synthesis and optimization by proposing topologies, sizing devices, and exploring large design spaces. We investigate whether they can instead support design discovery, where generated structures must depart from known designs while producing reproducible electrical behavior. We propose Delta-Seeker, a closed-loop circuit search framework that combines discrete diffusion for topology generation and mutation with structural checking, SPICE-in-the-loop sizing, Pareto selection, and feedback from prior search outcomes. The search controller uses progress and recurring structural failures to allocate evaluation effort and steer subsequent topology generation, while independent re-sizing and operating-corner analysis are performed only after search. In generator-only experiments, cross-generation feedback increases structurally valid children from 143 to 945 and reduces the faulty-candidate fraction from 0.925 to 0.761. In op-amp topology discovery at matched sizing cost, Delta-Seeker yields 54 designs that remain feasible in at least three of four independent re-sizings and 18 that additionally pass device-level checks and supply-temperature corner analysis, compared with 38 and 10 under fixed control. Removing cross-generation memory reduces independently robust discoveries from 54 to 43 and seven-corner robust discoveries from 40 to 27. In DC-DC converter search, nearest-parent analysis identifies a corpus-absent topology whose generated switching current path changes its nearest training-corpus parent from infeasible at all four operating corners to feasible at all four, while increasing median efficiency from 31.2% to 98.96%. These results show that closed-loop generative search can support circuit discovery beyond structural novelty by identifying new topologies with independently verified changes in circuit operation.

data.title: Evolution of Financial AI: From Statistical Models to Agentic AI
data.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in finance has evolved from statistical learning and machine learning for structured prediction, through deep learning and foundation models for representation learning, language understanding, and reasoning, to retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-grounded reasoning and agentic AI for autonomous planning and execution. In this paper, we examine how researchers and practitioners can select and apply AI methods in finance. We first show that the major paradigms of financial AI address fundamentally different classes of problems, rather than forming a strict hierarchy of capability. We then review the current state of research on AI in finance and trace how these paradigms have reshaped financial data, financial tasks, decision support, and human-AI collaboration. Building on this, we propose practical guidelines for matching AI paradigms to task characteristics, and show that more advanced models, such as foundation models or autonomous agents, are not universally superior. We conclude by outlining open challenges for researchers and practitioners working toward reliable financial AI.

data.title: More Eccentric, Not Always Less Detectable: High Mass Holds Its Ground, Low Mass Loses Reach
data.abstract: Gravitational waves from eccentric compact binary coalescences trace dynamical binary formation, but matched-filtering searches responsible for most detections rely on quasicircular templates. Quantifying any sensitivity loss is crucial for assessing population completeness and the need for dedicated eccentric template banks. We present the first systematic GstLAL search study spanning eccentricities up to $e_{\rm 15Hz}=0.99$ and broad ranges of chirp mass, mass ratio, inclination, and aligned spin. Using TEOBResumS-Dalí waveforms, we inject eccentric signals and measure recovered signal-to-noise ratio, signal-consistency statistics, false-alarm rate, and sensitive volume and distance. For high-mass binaries ($\mathcal{M}_c\gtrsim30\,M_\odot$), sensitive distance is nearly independent of eccentricity, demonstrating that greater eccentricity does not necessarily reduce search sensitivity. In contrast, for low-mass binaries, sensitive distance falls by up to $\sim50\%$ near $e_{\rm 15Hz}\approx0.75$. Although the absolute loss in reach is modest given their low quasicircular sensitivity, this relative reduction exceeds the increase in sensitive distance between the second and third observing runs of the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA collaboration and is consistent with previous low-mass studies. We also find that waveform matches at fixed source parameters substantially overpredict search sensitivity loss, meaning that the pipeline's signal-consistency test and maximization over its template bank mitigate much of the predicted sensitivity loss. This highlights the need for end-to-end injection campaigns to establish the detectability of eccentric binaries.

data.title: Source projection for calibrated transfer learning in survival prediction
data.abstract: Transfer learning can improve survival prediction in cohorts with few events. An external model may capture useful covariate associations yet systematically overestimate or underestimate risk in the target population, creating a need for selective borrowing. We propose Source Projection Transfer (SPT) for fixed-horizon prediction with a target generalized additive model. SPT requires only source predictions at target covariates, supporting generalized additive, Cox and neural-network source models without individual-level source data. It projects source log-odds scores onto the target basis and borrows through two separately adapted channels: a projection-centered penalty transfers effect shapes, while intercept-recalibrated soft labels inform probabilities at the target risk level. Under local asymptotics, projection avoids the strictly positive risk cost of estimating an uninformative additional source direction. Each channel asymptotically switches off under its corresponding persistent-mismatch condition. In log-logistic and Weibull simulations with covariate shift, SPT improves mean Brier score and discrimination over target-only modeling in all 24 setting-distribution-horizon combinations. Matched comparisons show improvements over borrowing through source probabilities alone across settings, and over borrowing the complete source score under structural mismatch. In UK Biobank-to-SPRINT mortality prediction among standard-treatment participants with reduced kidney function, SPT improves mean discrimination at 24, 30 and 36 months, with Brier improvements at 24 and 36 months. SPT enables flexible source learners to inform a parsimonious target model while adapting to differences between populations.

data.title: Coarse3D: Controllable and Faithful Sparse Structure Generation for Image-to-3D
data.abstract: Coarse-to-fine 3D-native generation relies heavily on the first-stage sparse structure, which determines the global orientation and overall geometry for subsequent refinement. However, existing coarse generators suffer from two key limitations: their orientation is difficult to control due to ambiguous semantic canonicalization, and their structures are often inconsistent with input images due to weak 2D-3D grounding. We propose Coarse3D, a sparse-structure generation model that produces orientation-controllable and structurally faithful voxel geometry from arbitrary unposed images. Coarse3D introduces three designs: a first-frame anchored canonical space that aligns generation with the first input view while preserving object-centric normalization; a dual-tower DiT that couples generation with auxiliary feed-forward reconstruction to learn spatially grounded features; and spatial-prior guided attention that regularizes cross-attention with pixel-to-voxel correspondence. Coarse3D can directly replace the coarse stage of existing pipelines. Experiments show that it substantially improves sparse structure quality and consistently enhances final 3D generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

data.title: TRIDENT and SHAKTI: A Framework and Benchmark for Hindi AI-Text Detection
data.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly multilingual, distinguishing human-written from AI-generated text is essential for maintaining information integrity. However, research remains English-centric, with limited benchmarks for low-resource languages such as Hindi. To address this gap, we introduce SHAKTI, a large-scale Hindi benchmark covering four genres, eight LLM families, multiple prompting strategies, and adversarial transformations. We evaluate its quality through human annotation and analyze linguistic, grammatical, and sentiment-based differences between human- and AI-generated texts. Building on these findings, we propose TRIDENT, a round-trip translation-based detection framework with three variants: TRIDENT-S (static threshold), TRIDENT-D (dynamic threshold), and TRIDENT-C (logistic regression using multi-distance RTT features). TRIDENT leverages semantic consistency between original and round-trip translated texts to identify AI-generated content. Extensive experiments show that TRIDENT outperforms conventional and supervised baselines, with TRIDENT-S achieving the best overall performance. Further evaluations across seven languages, adversarial settings, and unseen LLMs demonstrate its multilingual applicability and robustness, while highlighting sensitivity to the translation model.

data.title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
data.abstract: Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention. We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.

data.title: Efficient Importance Sampling of Brownian Motion Avoiding Poissonian Obstacles for Long Time
data.abstract: We design and analyze an efficient importance sampling estimator of the probability that, over a long time horizon, a Brownian particle avoids obstacles of a fixed radius placed according to an independent Poisson random field. Donsker and Varadhan identify the exponential decay rate of this probability as the optimal balance between the volume cleared of obstacles and the spectral cost of confinement, and the confinement results of Sznitman and Povel show that the particle survives by localizing its path in a ball of (roughly) deterministic radius but with a random center. This strategy makes direct Monte Carlo exponentially ineffective over long horizons, and makes a practical yet asymptotically optimal sampler non-trivial to design, since the sampler must track the random region swept out by the path. For every fixed dimension \(d\ge2\) and every fixed obstacle radius, we construct a sequential importance sampler that is unbiased and asymptotically optimal. The full algorithm has finite expected total work at every fixed horizon, and both its expected work and the coefficient of variation grow at most subexponentially with the time horizon. The method avoids repeatedly solving eigenvalue problems on the evolving explored regions and suits parallel implementation. Numerical experiments illustrate the efficiency of the method.

data.title: CONSORT: Uncertainty-Constrained Multi-Robot Planning for Cooperative Localization in GPS-Denied Environments
data.abstract: Centralized multi-agent path planning with cooperative localization in GPS-denied environments is generally computationally intractable when formulated in full belief space due to tightly coupled uncertainty dynamics. Prior work typically approximates belief dynamics or restricts inter-agent coupling. This work examines a multi-agent planning problem in which a primary agent must reach a goal in minimum time subject to a chance-constrained collision-avoidance requirement and a terminal bound on localization uncertainty. We obtain a tractable surrogate of the underlying belief-space problem by optimizing over the mean-state trajectories of all agents and propagating covariance for terminal constraint evaluation only. We propose CONSORT (Cooperative Navigation with Support-Optimized Routing and Trajectories), a discrete-to-continuous pipeline combining hexagonal-grid joint search with spline-based trajectory refinement. Across 50 randomized scenarios, the planners separate as the terminal uncertainty bound tightens, with CONSORT solving 80% of scenarios where the strongest baseline solves 54%, at comparable path length. In marine simulations, with the plans executed under feedback control on an independently developed factor-graph estimate, the trajectories remain collision-free and their terminal uncertainty falls within 6% of the planner's prediction.

data.title: Experts Exhibit Structured Redundancy: Structure-Preserving Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models
data.abstract: Sparse MoE mechanism significantly improves the trade-off between model capacity and inference efficiency. However, practical deployment still requires storing all experts, resulting in substantial memory overhead. We show that expert outputs in MoE layers exhibit structured redundancy. Across different models and task categories, the stable rank and entropy effective rank of expert outputs are consistently far below the nominal number of experts, while expert output distributions also exhibit fewer effective modes. Motivated by these observations, we reformulate expert pruning as a structure-preserving expert subset selection problem and efficiently optimize it via a greedy strategy, rather than only independently scoring and ranking individual experts or exhaustively searching over expert combinations. We propose two expert pruning methods under the unified structure-preserving framework: Projection Energy Expert Pruning (PEEP), which preserves the functional subspace by maximizing weighted projection energy, and Distributional Coverage Expert Pruning (DCEP), which preserves the distributional geometry by minimizing weighted coverage error. Both methods incorporate router-derived weights as priors, enabling them to jointly preserve the global structural relationships among experts while accounting for the local importance of individual experts. Experiments on DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate that, at the expert retention ratios of 75% and 50%, our methods outperform the state-of-the-art baselines on the majority of benchmarks and consistently achieve the best average performance across both general tasks and mathematical reasoning tasks.

data.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
data.abstract: Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$. The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $ι_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincaré duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.

data.title: Inference in an interactive multi-type branching network
data.abstract: We study statistical inference for a high-dimensional stochastic interaction model observed only through low-dimensional aggregate data. The model describes pairwise communication between $d$ individuals as a collection of mutually interacting branching processes with immigration, where activity on one directed pair may trigger subsequent activity in the reverse direction. The latent interaction counts are not observed. Instead, for each individual, only the total number of messages sent and received in each time slot is available. This aggregation gives rise to an inverse problem in which the parameters governing the latent pairwise dynamics must be recovered from substantially compressed observations.

data.title: Frequency-Calibrated Decision-Focused Learning for BESS Dispatch Under Renewable Uncertainty
data.abstract: Battery energy storage system (BESS) flexibility depends on state of charge and intertemporal operating constraints. Renewable forecast errors of similar magnitudes can lead to different BESS dispatch results. An error may alter early charging or discharging decisions and reduce the flexibility available for subsequent regulation, while another may have little effect on the resulting schedule. To account for these unequal consequences, this paper proposes Frequency-Calibrated Decision-Focused Learning (FC-DFL), which trains renewable predictors using the realized operating costs of their induced BESS schedules. Gaussian smoothing and solver-based zeroth-order estimation provide training feedback without requiring differentiating through the non-differentiable mixed-integer BESS dispatch problem. The same decision feedback is further combined with prediction sensitivity to develop a decision-oriented XAI method that identifies the input features and forecast periods most consequential to BESS operation. Case studies using German wind and solar data show that FC-DFL reduces the integrated absolute frequency-deviation metric by 6.05% and decision regret by 23.92% relative to accuracy-based predict-then-optimize method. The XAI analysis further demonstrates that the identified high-impact forecast periods produce 2.84 times larger average absolute changes in realized operating cost than low-impact periods. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating downstream decision-making outcomes into renewable forecasting and demonstrate the value of FC-DFL in improving BESS regulation and providing operationally meaningful forecast explanations.

data.title: Understanding LLM-Based Bargaining of Driving Agents in Mixed-Autonomy Traffic
data.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a flexible computational approach for modeling social interactions among heterogeneous agents. This paper develops a novel framework towards characterizing and understanding LLM-based population-level bargaining of shared road space between autonomous vehicle (AV) and human-driven vehicle (HV) agents in mixed-autonomy traffic. Through controlled experiments varying traffic density, agent objectives, and traffic-domain knowledge, we first characterize bargaining outcomes and observe heterogeneous agreement rates across different experimental conditions. To understand how the bargaining process shapes the outcomes, we introduce a behavioral taxonomy that jointly characterizes numerical bidding actions and communicative attitudes. We examine two complementary aspects of social interaction: inter-agent bargaining dynamics and private-to-public behavioral transformation. Results reveal distinct interaction patterns associated with agreement and breakdown, including greater constructive reciprocity in agreement trials and more frequent conflict escalation in breakdown trials. Furthermore, private and public communicative attitudes often differ even when numerical bids remain unchanged. These findings illustrate how LLM-based bargaining simulations can support a structured analysis of social interaction behaviors in mixed-autonomy traffic.

data.title: Longitudinal electric corner modes in continuum quantum gauge theory with matter
data.abstract: Subregions in gauge theories give rise to edge modes and corner charges supported on their boundaries. While this is well-established classically and in quantum lattice gauge theories, the fate of corner modes remains poorly understood in continuum quantum field theories owing to their distributional nature. In this paper, we revisit this challenge and propose a new corner operator for a regional Cauchy slice algebra generated by local gauge-invariant observables of scalar QED in Minkowski spacetime. The corner mode is given by the longitudinal electric field sourced by the matter outside the subregion and thus constitutes a centre for the regional algebra. Our main goal is to show that there exists a perturbative GNS state on this algebra that quantises this mode. Pulling back the Fock vacuum to the slice, we construct this state by renormalising the divergences arising from the lack of temporal smearing. We clarify that the inclusion of the new centre mode necessitates a further renormalisation on the corner of the region, thereby physically distinguishing it and breaking the translation invariance of the state. Our work shows how the requirements of locality, renormalisability, and positivity together put strong constraints on the existence of a continuum quantum field theory which supports corner modes as genuine quantum operators. We finish with comments about the von Neumann completion of the regional algebra, as well as possible physical interpretations of the renormalised vacuum state.

data.title: Plasmoid Instability in Inhomogeneous Current Sheets
data.abstract: Plasmoid instability in inhomogeneous current sheets is investigated using electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations of collisionless magnetic reconnection. Simulations with and without small random perturbations are compared to examine the effects of symmetry breaking and spatial inhomogeneity. The current-sheet width immediately before disruption remains close to the electron skin depth, whereas the disruption aspect ratio varies significantly between primary and later current sheets. Random perturbations also produce asymmetric plasmoid topologies in which neighboring X points no longer share a common separatrix. These results suggest that spatial inhomogeneity is an important factor in the disruption of dynamically evolving current sheets.

data.title: Effect of quark-hadron phase transitions on the neutron star mass distribution
data.abstract: The neutron star (NS) mass distribution serves as a crucial probe of the dense matter equation of state (EOS) and core-collapse supernova explosion mechanisms. Although observations reveal a bimodal NS mass distribution, existing theoretical simulations often struggle to naturally reproduce the high-mass peak, and the impact of the quark-hadron phase transition (PT) in high-density nuclear matter remains largely unexplored. Employing the 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamics code GR1D with hybrid EOSs incorporating a first-order PT (RDF1.1 and RDF1.2), we systematically simulate core-collapse supernovae for progenitors with zero-age main-sequence masses ranging from 13 to 120 $M_\odot$. Our results reveal a threefold impact of the PT onset density on the final supernova fate: in low-compactness progenitors, an early PT truncates accretion and produces less massive NSs; in the critical-compactness regime, it facilitates successful explosions; and in high-compactness progenitors, it accelerates black hole formation. Compared with the $\sim 1.4\,M_\odot$ peak typical of the conventional core-collapse scenario, the inclusion of the PT produces NSs with masses centered around $1.70\,M_\odot$ for RDF1.1 and within $1.55$--$1.70\,M_\odot$ for RDF1.2. Furthermore, we identify a novel formation channel whereby low-compactness progenitors with failed initial shocks can form more massive NSs via a PT-induced second shock. Due to the fixed nature of the PT boundary, the final NS masses exhibit a pronounced clustering effect. This study elucidates the critical role of the quark-hadron PT in shaping the NS mass distribution, providing important astrophysical constraints on the properties of high-density nuclear matter and the formation mechanism of massive NSs.

data.title: Generative SDEs with Trainable Diffusion and Density-Based Losses
data.abstract: We develop a divergence-kernel method for jointly optimizing neural SDE drift and diffusion fields and the initial Gaussian distribution, using losses that depend directly on the terminal density. In two- and eight-dimensional Gaussian-mixture experiments, we learn time-independent fields and obtain far fewer off-mode samples than score-based generators with similar parameter counts. The drift attracts samples toward the modes, while the diffusion helps disperse excess probability between them.

data.title: A Unified Framework for Probability Estimation of Data-Dependent Events
data.abstract: We study the general problem of estimating $D(\dde(S))$, the probability that an unknown distribution $D$ assigns to an event determined by a sample $S$ of $n$ i.i.d.\ draws from $D$ through a known mapping $\dde$. The estimation algorithm knows $\dde$ and $S$ but does not have access to any additional samples from $D$. This formulation captures classical missing mass, the data-dependent targets of adaptive data analysis and post-selection inference, and the test error of a data-trained predictor, whose estimation was recently studied by \new{Gastpar et al.\ (2024a,b)}. Within this framework we examine the two classical approaches to estimation. The error of the empirical plug-in estimator is exactly a generalization gap, so generalization bounds transfer to it directly. The leave-one-out estimator, which recovers the Good--Turing estimator, is accurate for every mapping that is stable under the deletion of one sample point, including new structured examples such as neighborhoods of the sample and pierced sets. The main application of our framework is to error estimation for a predictor that combines a base classifier with memorized exceptions, a structure common in theory and in practice. For it, the test error is exactly the missing mass restricted to the error region of the base classifier, a region selected by the same sample. We formulate the general problem of \emph{adaptive missing mass estimation} to address such dependence and propose a natural hybrid estimator, the Good--Turing estimator restricted to the selected region. We show that the generalization of the base classifier alone does not guarantee the accuracy of this estimator, and derive two bounds on its error: the first one based on the VC dimension of possible error regions and another based on the mutual information of the selected region with the sample.

data.title: MEMIG: Self-evolving Memory Construction for Antibody Optimization
data.abstract: Memory has become central to self-evolving LLM agents, which store and retrieve experience from past rollouts to guide future decisions. Existing systems represent this experience as free-form natural language and maintain it by rewriting, which fits tasks whose experience is narratable. However, in scientific discovery and optimization, experience is often a quantity measured by an oracle under a specific context. Rewriting it as text leaves no index for where a record should be, replaces a measurement with a description, and cannot express how interventions interact. To address this, we argue that agent memory for biomolecule optimization should instead be indexable, quantitative, and structured, and we introduce MEMIG. This memory construction framework realizes these three properties. In detail, MEMIG addresses each insight with a domain-grounded identifier and accumulates the quantitative effect measured by a property oracle, so that updates remain local and retrieval becomes an exact lookup. Next, MEMIG connects insights whose interventions are applied together and measures their epistasis by decomposing each evaluated set. Our results show that MEMIG improves performance in most settings across in silico antibody optimization tasks.

data.title: Equation informed time reparametrization for physics informed neural networks
data.abstract: Physics Informed Neural Networks offer a mesh-free approach to solving differential equations, but their application to time-dependent problems remains challenging, particularly when the governing dynamics involve widely different time scales. With collocation points spread uniformly in time, short intervals of rapid change are under resolved. This work introduces an equation informed time reparameterization framework that modifies the temporal coordinate used during PINN training based on the local dynamics of the governing equation. The proposed method follows a two stage procedure. First, a pilot PINN training provides an approximate solution, which is used to linearize the governing differential operator and estimate its local response to small perturbations. These responses are combined into a time-dependent rate function, large where the dynamics are fast, that defines a strictly increasing transformation from physical time to a new computational time coordinate. A second PINN is then trained on the transformed governing equation, with uniformly sampled collocation points in the new coordinate producing a nonuniform distribution in physical time. Different combination rules and spatial reduction strategies are considered. With the cost of the pilot training included, the method reduces the error by a factor of 4 to 29 relative to the best alternative method on the Kachanov Rabotnov creep-damage model near rupture, and by a factor of 5 to 16 relative to every alternative method on the Frank-Kamenetskii equation near blow up.

data.title: Gravitational Memory from AdS States in the Flat-Space Limit
data.abstract: We study linearized gravitational reconstruction in global AdS$_4$ with dynamical scalar matter, building on vacuum Einstein perturbations with fixed boundary metric and nontrivial normalizable data. External scalar sources prepare an excited state and modify the holographic Ward identities, while subsequent evolution can proceed without boundary driving. Separating the bulk matter-sourced response from vacuum perturbations, we derive an electric quadrupole master equation with the matter-dependent corrections required by the Einstein constraints. We also verify that a cylindrical boundary integral reproduces the Regge--Wheeler master field mode by mode, without identifying it with the full global Fefferman--Graham reconstruction. For weakly interacting scalars that become massless in the flat-space limit, we extract the Bondi shear and news from retarded gravitational evolution.
