data.title: Optimistic Gradient Algorithms with Randomized Coordinate and Variance Reduction Strategies for Composite Inclusions
data.abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of possibly nonmonotone finite-sum composite inclusions in which evaluating all components or updating all coordinates at every iteration can be computationally expensive. We develop two optimistic gradient frameworks that combine variance reduction with randomized block-coordinate updates. The first framework applies under a blockwise average Lipschitz continuity condition and the existence of a weak-Minty solution. It achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/k)$ convergence rate for the expected squared residual, and its iterates converge almost surely under mild additional conditions. The second framework relies on a backward-forward reformulation under average co-coercivity and co-hypomonotonicity. It achieves faster $\mathcal{O}(1/k^2)$ and $o(1/k^2)$ rates for the expected squared residual, as well as $o(1/k^2)$ almost-sure rates. For both frameworks, we provide a generic condition on the stochastic estimator that covers mini-batch, loopless SVRG, and a generalized JacSketch-type estimator, and we derive the corresponding oracle complexities under importance-based block sampling. In particular, in highly heterogeneous regimes, the L-SVRG and JacSketch variants attain $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-2}\big)$ and $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-1}\big)$ oracle complexities for the nonaccelerated and accelerated methods, respectively. Numerical experiments illustrate the effects of variance reduction and block-coordinate sampling, and compare the proposed methods with existing baselines.

data.title: The Valence and Inner Shell Ionization Properties of Sr I - III by Non-Thermal Electrons in Kilonovae
data.abstract: The presence of strontium (Z = 38) was identified from spectra of the first multi-messenger kilonova transient, AT2017gfo, with the evolution of its spectral signature indicating a rapidly changing ionization balance. Interpretation of spectra at later times requires a more detailed understanding of recombination and ionization processes, including ionization by `non-thermal' electrons produced by beta decay. Published measurements of the ionization cross sections of Sr I and Sr II show complex structures likely arising from excitation autoionization. Using the Flexible Atomic Code we report calculations of the valence and inner shell ionization cross sections for Sr I, Sr II, and Sr III, and recover similar structures in the ionization cross sections. Though no measurements exist for Sr III, the calculations suggest negligible contributions from excitation autoionization. These new data are incorporated into Spencer-Fano models of non-thermal electron degradation and coupled to an ionization balance solver. The effects of excitation autoionization, treated as excitation with the additional production of an Auger electron, on the degradation spectra of non-thermal are explored. Calculations at both level- and configuration-average resolution return ion fractions that agree within 5-20%. The calculations probe the impact of including final-charge-state-resolved branching ratios for inner shell ionization which result in multi-ionization events from successive Auger cascades. Omission of these branching ratios is shown to have large impacts on the ionization balance. The calculated cross sections will be provided on Zenodo.

data.title: The L1157 filament as traced in HNCO by the LMT
data.abstract: Context. The L1157 outflow is a prototype of chemically active outflows where to look for molecular species linked to complex chemistry. Aims. With the aim of imaging the large (parsec) scale structure of key prebiotic molecules, we have mapped the whole blue-lobe of the L1157 outflow with the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT), proving the potential of this facility to detect weak and extended molecular emission. Methods. Isocyanic acid, HNCO, an important precursor of complex chemistry, was chosen to be observed in its (4_0,4-3_0-3) transition at 87.925 GHz with the SEQUOIA focal-plane array, covering an area of 3x3 arcmin2 centered at the position of the main shock L1157-B1, which included a large portion of the vicinity of the protostellar region. Results. The HNCO emission was detected not only from the outflow but it also was found tracing a structure of about 0.3 pc in length, corresponding to the filament from which the protostellar system was born. Conclusions. The HNCO molecule was found to be a tracer of the densest part of filaments in molecular clouds, and given its importance in the formation of more complex molecules, its presence in the cold, quiescent filamentary gas indicates that the building blocks of complex chemistry are already well established in stages prior to protostellar warming or shocks. By allowing the detection of structures related with the filament, these observations proved the LMT potentialities to map weak and extended components in molecular clouds.

data.title: Decomposing Irregular Time Series into Interpretable Temporal Patterns with Mixture-of-Experts
data.abstract: Irregularly-spaced sequential data, such as transaction logs, encode multi-scale temporal structure that is critical for prediction but difficult to recover explicitly with standard sequence models, which often trade interpretability for performance. We introduce MoTIF, an interpretable framework using mixture-of-experts (MoE) attention to decompose irregular time series into temporal patterns spanning minute-to-year scales. Each expert is trained via temporal alignment that induces attention specialization to a designated cyclical or within-range pattern, with label-free routing supervision that learns to activate the correct expert from patterns present in the data. On synthetic data with known temporal structure, MoTIF recovers correct routing well above chance (0.389/0.829 for range/cyclical patterns vs. 0.091 random) and outperforms all baselines, including a standard transformer and an unspecialized MoE, on next-value prediction. On a public credit card transaction dataset, MoTIF achieves higher macro-F1 than all baselines for next-amount prediction. Its learned routing reveals structure a black-box model cannot: transactions are governed primarily by intraday and short-interval rhythms, while fraudulent transactions show bursty, calendar-agnostic timing versus the steadier periodicity of legitimate ones. On downstream fraud detection, MoTIF matches standard transformer and MoE baselines and clearly outperforms recent sequential recommendation models used as embedding baselines. These results show that decomposing temporal structure into interpretable, expert-specific patterns need not sacrifice predictive accuracy, offering a practical route to sequence models that are both accurate and auditable in high-stakes settings. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MoTIF-82E4.

data.title: Reading the Count: Prediction Markets and Brazil's 2026 Presidential Election
data.abstract: We rebuild the public count of Brazil's 2026 presidential runoff minute by minute from the electoral court's section-level records and compare it with every trade on Kalshi and Polymarket. A projection published live on the night gave the eventual winner, Lula, a probability of 0.998 from 19:15, with 1.6% of sections counted. The markets reached 0.9 at 20:24, with 46% counted. Read as the projection's central estimate with a wider uncertainty, their prices imply a standard deviation of the final margin about four times the live projection's, and about twice that of a section-level projection calibrated on the 2018 runoff, the earlier night with the largest errors. Valued at these projections, takers' purchases of Lula after the count resumed had an expected profit of 4 to 18 cents per Kalshi contract after fees; valued at a state-level extrapolation of the count, it was zero. During a two-hour suspension of the count the markets gave Lula 0.25 to 0.44, below every reading we compute afterwards from the sections then public, none of which was available live. On the first-round night, when the headline count showed the eventual leader ahead from its first file, the same markets were faster than our projection.

data.title: Efficient NPN Classification for Large Functions using Graph Neural Network
data.abstract: Two Boolean functions are considered NPN equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by negating inputs, permuting inputs, or negating the output. Efficient NPN classification is valuable in fields such as logic synthesis, quantum computing, and information theory. However, exact NPN classification demands exhaustive enumeration of all possible input permutations and negations. Its complexity grows exponentially, making it impractical for larger functions with more inputs. In this paper, we introduce the first learning-based formulation for NPN classification by recasting it as NPN action prediction. Our method represents Boolean functions as AND-Inverter Graphs (AIGs) and applies a bidirectional heterogeneous graph neural network to predict input negations, output negation, and input permutations. To mitigate the non-canonicity of logic networks, we further introduce graph rewriting techniques that reduce structural ambiguity and recover useful symmetries before prediction. Experimental results show that NPN action prediction is learnable, that the resulting canonicalization quality improves over heuristic baselines, and that on practical benchmarks our method approaches exact methods on tractable cases while scaling to functions with up to 16 inputs.

data.title: Autoformalization for Ambiguous Inputs: Precision, Coverage, and Cost across SQL and Logical Forms
data.abstract: Agentic systems translate natural-language requests into executable artifacts while managing ambiguity and inference cost. We evaluate seven autoformalization workflows on SQL and first-order logic benchmarks for ambiguous inputs. Across five SQL workflows, the raw model leads with F1 of 53.35% on AMBROSIA and 60.85% on AmbiQT. On AmP, DRIFT gains 15.98 F1 points over the raw model at 2.03 times its token cost, whereas LoC uses 18.65 times the raw model's tokens with lower F1. Within AutoCedar, structured interpretation lowers F1 by 6.44-6.95 points and raises AMBROSIA token use 2.2-fold. Paired reviewer comparisons show modest Kimi K3 gains of 1.93 points on AMBROSIA and 2.04 on AmbiQT. Clear-ambiguous AMBROSIA analysis shows greater relative stability for AutoCedar, with a smaller F1 drop than the raw model (11.46 vs. 16.68 points), alongside lower aggregate F1 (50.16% vs. 53.35%). Autoformalization alone does not guarantee robustness to ambiguity: the tested additions offer no uniformly effective remedy, making accuracy, ambiguity handling, and inference cost joint design requirements.

data.title: CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS): Power Spectrum Injections and Survey Sensitivity
data.abstract: Artificial signal injection into real data is a key tool in time-domain radio astronomy, with particular import to the study of pulsars and Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs). Many surveys inject into the time series to probe observational biases impacting the detection of radio transients. In the case of the CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stack Search (CHAMPSS), the computational demands of both hardware and software time series injections force an alternative approach. We present methods for injecting artificial pulsar signals into the Fourier power spectrum. The injection process detailed here is computationally negligible compared to the overhead of the CHAMPSS search pipeline. We use injections to probe the in-system biases of the CHAMPSS survey. CHAMPSS is most sensitive to pulsars with frequencies on the order of 0.1 - 100 Hz and fluxes > 1 mJy. Our injections show weak overall sensitivity dependence on other factors such as dispersion measure (DM), duty cycle, and sky coordinates, but complex non-monotonic interactions between all parameters. Our findings suggest that frequency-dependent noise, especially low-frequency or "red" noise, and sampling limitations at higher frequencies are the dominant extrinsic factors decreasing CHAMPSS' sensitivity to pulsars.

data.title: DEPLOY-RL: Active Boundary Discovery and Conservative Certification for Deployable Reinforcement Learning in Safety-Critical Continuous Processes
data.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies often outperform classical controllers in simulation, yet rarely reach production in safety-critical processes. The barrier is that there is no principled way to answer "Is this policy safe to deploy?" with statistical guarantees. We introduce DEPLOY-RL, a post-training certification framework built on one key insight: deployment certification requires discovering where failures occur (boundary discovery), not measuring how much everywhere (uniform reconstruction). Our contributions: (1) a contract-coupled acquisition function that concentrates sampling on certification-critical boundaries, achieving approximately 2x sample efficiency with a semi-empirical ambiguity reduction bound (domain-calibrated convergence guarantee); (2) conformal risk control providing finite-sample false-go guarantees (<= alpha) under explicit deployment contracts; (3) a three-way decision framework (Deploy/No-Deploy/Abstain) with fail-safe PID/MPC fallback. In simulations on papermaking (industrial digital twin) and Tennessee Eastman (public benchmark), DEPLOY-RL achieves 4.4% false-go rate (vs. 8.6% for the best baseline) while retaining 88.6% policy coverage, the only method achieving <5% false-go with >85% coverage among 14 baselines under our evaluation protocol.

data.title: Nuclear Charge Radii from Precision Bound-Electron g-Factor Measurements
data.abstract: An efficient method to determine absolute nuclear charge radii from high-precision bound-electron g-factor measurements in hydrogenlike ions is put forward. Assuming that a nuclear model independent radius determination is possible, we demonstrate that this method can improve the precision of the nuclear radius for several poorly known heavy isotopes by up to two orders of magnitude compared to current literature values, by utilizing recent breakthroughs in the quantum electrodynamics (QED) theory of the bound-electron g-factor [B. Sikora, V. A. Yerokhin, C. H. Keitel, and Z. Harman, Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 123001 (2025)]. This opens a new, independent pathway for testing nuclear structure models and resolving nuclear structure anomalies.

data.title: SPARK: Self-Correcting Embodied Memory via Physical Re-Observation
data.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have seen growing adoption in embodied settings as language-queryable memories of the environment. However, existing approaches often assume a reliable single-episode knowledge base (KB) or accumulate observations across episodes without correcting prior errors. Such errors can persist through incorrect semantic labels, inaccurate object positions, and inconsistent spatial relationships. To address this, we present SPARK, a corrective multi-episode framework for embodied RAG. After the first episode, a semantic critic flags regions of the KB, a targeted planner generates revisits, and a selective merge adds, removes, or replaces KB information based on the new observations. We evaluate SPARK on four outdoor AirSim maps under two degraded viewpoint conditions, using perception-built KBs, a visibility-constrained oracle used only for evaluation, and a fixed set of 158 embodied question answering (EQA) questions scored before and after correction. A single corrective episode improves downstream EQA on every map under both conditions while storing 13-41% fewer objects than append-only updating, with gains up to 2.7x on one map-condition pair. Extending correction through Episode 4 brings every map above the EQA performance of its undegraded reference. Ablations show that the critic's three signals each contribute to performance, that targeted revisits achieve a larger mean gain than untargeted ones under the same budget, and that selective merging achieves gains comparable to append-only updating with a smaller KB. Overall, SPARK demonstrates the value of correcting embodied memory through targeted re-observation, particularly as embodied systems scale and the risk of accumulated errors increases.

data.title: Queering the Audits: Community-Based Auditing of AI Harms to Queer Communities
data.abstract: AI systems embed majority-group defaults into training data, evaluation metrics, and category definitions, producing documented harms for queer communities including erasure, misclassification, and discrimination. Standard technical audits often rely on aggregate measures and cannot detect harms that be come visible only through the lived experience of affected communities. We conducted a participatory auditing workshop at EurIPS 2025 where 16 queer community members audited four case studies using the 4Cs harm taxonomy (Content, Conduct, Contact, Contract) applied across the AI lifecycle. Participants used structured worksheets and plenary synthesis to classify harms and trace them to their origins in the development pipeline. Across all four cases, participants traced harms to problem definition and data collection, and they identified contractual structures that extract value from vulnerable populations while providing minimal recourse. These findings illustrate that community-informed auditing surfaces concrete, identity-specific harms that aggregate evaluation methods risk overlooking.

data.title: Stability of Solitons in the Parametrically Driven and Damped Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation in Arbitrary Dimension
data.abstract: We study the spectral stability of soliton solutions of the parametrically driven and damped nonlinear Schrödinger (PDDNLS) equation with power-law nonlinearity $|Ψ|^{2κ}Ψ$ in $N$ dimensions. We identify two families of stationary solutions, $Ψ_\pm$, whose existence is determined by two conditions: one involving the nonlinearity exponent~$κ$ and the spatial dimension~$N$, and another involving the forcing amplitude~$r$ and the damping coefficient~$ρ$. By linearising around these solutions and introducing a convenient parametrisation through~$\varepsilon$, we reduce the stability problem to a dissipationless eigenvalue problem for two Schrödinger-type operators, $L_0$ and $L_1$. We prove that $Ψ_-$ is always unstable, while for $Ψ_+$, we carry out a complete spectral analysis by decomposing the problem into angular momentum sectors $\mathcal{S}_l$. We show that modes with $l \geq 2$ generate no instabilities and that no complex quadruplets arise on~$\mathcal{S}_1$. We also derive an analytical instability criterion on $\mathcal{S}_l$ by combining a Vakhitov--Kolokolov-type argument with a local analysis that determines the direction of the eigenvalue splitting near the origin. In addition, we uncover new phenomena at both small and large values of $κ$ that were not investigated in earlier one-dimensional studies. Numerical stability diagrams for $N = 1, 2, 3$ are presented.

data.title: Exact Asymptotics for the Harmonic Descent Chain and Extended Convergence Bounds for Recursive Statistics
data.abstract: We give an exact asymptotic expansion of the occupation probabilities $a(n,k)$ of the harmonic descent chain, introduced by D. Aldous, as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $k\in\mathrm{o}(\sqrt{n})$. In addition, we extend the recent results of Brandenberger et al. by giving a bound on the rate of convergence of sequences defined recursively by $x_n = \frac{1}{H_{n-1}}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{x_i}{n-i}$ for more general initial conditions. This result enables the application of an existing central limit theorem, also by Brandenberger et al., to statistics of the critical beta-splitting tree which satisfy our more general initial conditions.

data.title: Robustness of Median-based Splitting Rules for Causal Trees
data.abstract: Causal forests (Athey and Imbens, 2016) are a widely used method for the estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Standard implementations use mean-based splitting criteria, which perform well when the outcome distribution is well-behaved and free of contamination, such as outliers or heavy tails. However, real-world data are rarely clean. Outcome perturbations can affect the tree structure selected by mean-based splitting rules and lead to unreliable treatment effect estimates. In this study, we systematically examine the robustness of causal forests to irregularities in the outcome distribution. Building on the median-based splitting criteria introduced by Maßmann and Gliszczyńska-Schroeder (2026), we empirically investigate three median-based splitting criteria: Median Absolute Deviation (MAD), Least Median of Squares (LMS), and Median Squared Deviation (MSD). We conduct Monte Carlo experiments and apply the methods to empirical benchmark datasets from the causal inference literature to compare the performance of the median-based approaches with standard causal forests. We additionally examine pointwise confidence interval coverage using the Bootstrap of Little Bags and the infinitesimal jackknife. The results indicate that median-based splitting criteria can reduce sensitivity to outcome irregularities in specific scenarios, particularly in the presence of extreme heavy-tailed noise and nonlinear treatment effect heterogeneity. However, these benefits are scenario-dependent and do not consistently lead to more accurate conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimates.

data.title: Top quark couplings at the muon collider
data.abstract: We present an overview of the sensitivity of a muon collider to the flavor-diagonal electroweak couplings of the top quark, using dimension-six operators of the Warsaw basis. Of the nine fermion-boson operators involving the top quark, the bounds on three are not competitive with existing limits, and we focus on the remaining six. We estimate individual $95\%$ CL limits on the corresponding Wilson coefficients at $\sqrt{s} = 3$, $6$, $10$, and $14$~TeV from $2σ$ statistical cross-section uncertainties, and assess the effect of an assumed systematic uncertainty. We consider six top-quark production modes: $t\bar t$, $t \bar t h$, $t \bar t ν\bar ν$, $t \bar t μ^+ μ^-$, single-top $t\bar b μ^- \bar ν_μ$, and single-top-plus-Higgs, the last three for several rapidity coverages of the final-state muons. The $s$-channel $t\bar t$ and $t\bar t h$ processes give the strongest sensitivity to the electroweak dipole couplings, with allowed intervals narrower than the current LHC ones by factors of about $3$ to $6$ at $\sqrt{s} = 3$ and $6$ TeV, and by an order of magnitude or more at $10$ and $14$ TeV. The left- and right-handed $ttZ$ couplings, as well as the Yukawa $tth$ couplings (for $\sqrt{s} \geq 6$ TeV), are best probed in $t \bar t ν\bar ν$ production, while the right-handed $tbW$ coupling is best probed in single-top production. For the $ttZ$ and $tbW$ couplings, the limits improve on the current LHC bounds by factors from about $1.5$ to more than an order of magnitude. Our results agree with previous analyses of the Yukawa and the dipole couplings, and provide a roadmap for more in-depth studies.

data.title: On the Limits of Test-Time Compute for Self-Evaluation
data.abstract: Self-verification and aggregation have emerged as popular approaches for bridging the gap between pass@1 and pass@N. However, increasing the number of candidates does not consistently narrow the gap between final-answer accuracy and pass@N. To understand this limitation, we use ranking error to measure how reliably models distinguish their correct generations from incorrect ones. We show that ranking error admits a bias-variance decomposition, with both components shaped by algorithmic design choices and inference compute. Across our experiments, additional compute reduces variance, while bias initially decreases before approaching a plateau. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Scorpio, a simple and general method that jointly scores randomly grouped candidates. Across math, code, and puzzle benchmarks, Scorpio improves verification, tree search, and aggregation. For verification, Scorpio improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by up to 7 percentage points while matching or exceeding that baseline's peak accuracy with 17-42% lower inference cost. For tree search, using Scorpio to score partial solutions and select the final answer improves accuracy by up to 10 percentage points over prior methods. Finally, Scorpio improves the scaling of aggregation-based methods by 11 percentage points on coding tasks.

data.title: SIEVE: Preserving Cross-Image Evidence via Depth-Aware Token Compression
data.abstract: Multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) incur substantial computation when processing long visual sequences. Compressing these sequences must preserve complementary evidence across images and keep tokens from different images separate. Global selection can underrepresent question-relevant images, and pruning in early decoder layers risks removing relevant content before sufficient multimodal processing, yet existing methods spend most of the budget on these early layers. We propose SIEVE, a training-free, single-pass framework that jointly allocates visual tokens across images and decoder depth. SIEVE first pools each image into a compact spatial grid to reduce early processing cost. It then progressively selects representatives using prompt attention under equal per-image quotas and aggregates unselected tokens into similar representatives from the same image. These operations keep every image represented and its tokens separate from other images, while refining the retained representations. A closed-form schedule sets retention counts to target a prescribed average token budget across decoder layers. Across four VLM backbones, SIEVE achieves the highest average at a 6.25% budget on five multi-image benchmarks and four single-image benchmarks, and the highest mean on two video benchmarks. On LLaVA-OneVision-7B, it outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.96 and 9.03 points at 6.25% and 12.5% budgets, and at 12.5% it exceeds the uncompressed model by 2.01 points with 6.6x fewer prefill FLOPs.

data.title: Cross-Prompt Reuse of Entity-Replacement Responses
data.abstract: With model weights fixed, we measure how much of an entity-replacement response transfers between English factual questions, beyond whether answers change. We add the hidden-state change from two source questions to a target question about the same entity, comparing the predicted log-probability shift between two relations' published answers, given known answer prefixes, with the measured one. Hidden reuse injects the aligned change at 50% depth before the target's remaining layers; direct reuse adds source output-score changes. With other-relation sources, hidden reuse removes 45% and 49% of no-change error on 0.5-1B Qwen and Llama. Gemma-2-2B removes 22% and passes one of three comparisons in plain text without its default beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token. A later protocol restoring it yields 58-68%, passing every comparison on three cohorts. Larger checkpoints, chat format and new entities show replication and format- or cohort-dependent failures. On small plain-format checkpoints, other-relation hidden reuse mainly reproduces the shift both relations' questions share, without reliably lowering relation-selective error. With target-relation sources, hidden reuse's post hoc advantage over direct reuse is 0.2-0.9 nats outside chat format, unconfirmed and not replacement-specific. The same relation-neutral change at both questions' entity tokens lowers relation-selective error more than random or other-replacement changes, indicating receiving-question dependence.

data.title: Stability, discretization, and optimality of continuous-time causal optimal transport
data.abstract: We prove stability of continuous-time causal and bicausal optimal transport problems when both marginals converge in adapted Wasserstein distance along common vanishing time shifts. The marginal laws, filtrations, and costs may all vary, while the limit remains the original causal or bicausal transport problem. This allows for time discretization and the approximation of transport problems between non-degenerate scalar fractional stochastic differential equations by their Wong--Zakai schemes. We further establish sufficient conditions so that the synchronous coupling is optimal for the bicausal transport problem between scalar fractional stochastic differential equations under continuous, nonnegative submodular costs of polynomial growth. This result covers all Hurst parameters \(H\in(0,1)\) up to an additional order-preserving commutator condition on the corresponding coefficients for the rough regime \(H\in(0,1/2)\).

data.title: A Julia implementation of Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation in periodic systems
data.abstract: We present a flexible Julia codebase implementing Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation (HHG) in periodic tight-binding systems. Using the frequency-domain Fourier-Sambe formalism, the package maps the time-dependent Schroedinger equation onto a static eigenvalue problem. This allows direct computation of Floquet states, quasienergy bands, and harmonic currents for 1D, 2D, or 3D lattices under arbitrary light polarizations. The implementation supports both analytical Fourier-Bessel expansions (via Peierls substitution) and numerical Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT). We validate the code against a canonical 1D two-band model and showcase its capabilities on 2D honeycomb systems: gapped graphene mapping HHG cutoff scaling with hopping parameters and the Kane-Mele model, exploring field-induced quasienergy gaps and topological transitions under linear and circular driving fields. In addition to the theoretical presentation, we provide a flexible and efficient open-source Julia implementation of the Floquet formalism: https://github.com/Ashwin-A-Pillai/Floquet-Fourier-Numericals/tree/main.

data.title: The recognition problem for 4-manifolds and the unknotting problem for 2-spheres in 4-manifolds
data.abstract: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a given 4-manifold is PL homeomorphic to the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 . We also show that the TOP and PL unknotting problems for all surfaces in the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 are unsolvable.

data.title: Unpacking the process of watching a 360-degree video: How physiological responses and head rotation relate to affective and cognitive outcomes
data.abstract: A defining feature of 360-degree video is that the perceptual experience is actively constructed. As viewers turn their heads, shift their gaze, and encounter changing visuals, their perceptual experience is not predetermined, but rather emerges through ongoing exploration. Yet, it is unclear how the process of watching immersive videos unfolds, and how it is related to psychological and physiological outcomes. We present a large-scale study (N=200) in which participants experienced one of 10 pieces of 360-degree videos in virtual reality. Results showed that greater head rotation was associated with greater valence, higher attention focus, longer length of subjective review, and lower simulator sickness; greater pupil dilation was associated with lower valence, lower review ratings, and greater use of negative tone in written reviews. A mediation analysis revealed that participants who rotated their heads more experienced greater frame-to-frame pixel-level perceptual changes in their field of view, which in turn resulted in greater valence and lower simulator sickness. Moreover, participants tended to rotate their heads toward field of view regions with greater perceptual movement, while directing their eye gaze toward less perceptually dynamic areas within that view. We outline theoretical and practical contributions for designing 360-degree content and predicting experiential outcomes.

data.title: The role of salinity in Snowball Earth: A simplified coupled atmosphere--ocean--ice model
data.abstract: The Neoproterozoic Snowball Earth events represent among the most extreme climate states in Earth's history, with ice covering all or nearly all of the ocean. Despite its control on the seawater freezing point and on the partitioning of water between the ocean and ice, salinity has not been well-represented in Snowball Earth models---typically prescribed, simplified, or ignored. Sea-glacier dynamics under open-ocean conditions have similarly lacked adequate treatment. We extend the one-dimensional coupled atmosphere-ocean-ice model of Pollard and Kasting (2005, J. Geophys. Res. Oceans 110, C07010) by adding prognostic latitudinal salinity dynamics, global ocean mass conservation and salt conservation, and a revised sea-glacier momentum equation, along with a greenhouse-gas term allowing transitions between full-snowball and partially open-ocean states. The model produces two equilibrium states exhibiting strong hysteresis under varying greenhouse forcing. Higher initial ocean salinity systematically lowers the CO$_2$ thresholds for both the onset and the termination of glaciation, reflecting freezing-point depression and coupled dynamics among salinity, ocean volume, and marine ice thickness. Under full glaciation, the shrinking ocean becomes hypersaline, feeding back on thermal structure and equilibrium ice thickness. Across a 72-case factorial ensemble spanning Neoproterozoic-relevant ranges, a marginal-effect analysis shows that only ice albedo shifts the thresholds more than initial salinity (69.1\% and 80.5\% versus 21.3\% and 9.7\% for initiation and deglaciation), followed by the solar constant (8.9\% and 5.6\%) and geothermal heat flux (0.6\% and 4.2\%). Salinity should therefore be treated as an active variable in studies of Snowball thresholds.

data.title: Kinetics of pollutant adsorption onto polymers: the Langevin dynamics study
data.abstract: We study adsorption kinetics of low-molecular-weight adsorbate particles on a polymer via the Langevin dynamics. The impact of the polymer molecular weight and of the strength of the polymer-particle attraction are examined. We consider mixtures of $n_p$ chains of the length $N$ with adsorbate, where $n_pN=600$ holds. Analysis includes examination of visualizations and evaluation of adsorption capacity, binding energy, average gyration radius, and asphericity of the polymer-adsorbate complexes. Both adsorption capacity and total binding energy show monotonic, logistic-like behavior; the former reaches a plateau sooner than the latter does, indicating further optimization of the maximum-capacity complex. Binding energy per particle and asphericity of complexes both demonstrate non-trivial behaviors, with distinct extrema at the intermediate stages of adsorption. The analysis reveals three stages of adsorption: (i) formation of small polymer-particle complexes, (ii) gradual merge of these into a single complex, (iii) stationary state. The stage (i) completes faster for short chains, as in this case fewer conformational rearrangements are required. The stage (ii) completes faster for long chains because of the necklace-like arrangement of small complexes along a long chain, which promotes their merge vs. diffusion-driven merge of the complexes of short chains. Our results indicate that for the rapid removal of pollutants in the high interaction regime, it is more effective to use the set of short polymer chains. On the other hand, long linear chains are optimal for adsorbing pollutants in a weak interaction regime.

data.title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers
data.abstract: AI "humanizers" rewrite machine-generated text so that detectors classify it as human-written. Public leaderboards score evasion and embedding similarity, but not whether checkable details survive. We check whether numbers, dates, person and organization names, and quoted spans survive each rewrite, using a rule-based checker validated by two AI annotators (precision 0.84-1.00, recall 0.93-0.95; no human annotation). In the October 2026 cycle of a public humanizer leaderboard, all 11 commercial tools changed or dropped at least one of these units in 35-65% of the documents that contained one. Most changes were to quoted spans; counting numbers and names alone, 10 of the 11 tools still altered at least one in 20% or more of the documents. The September 2026 cycle was similar (19-50%). An open 12B humanizer kept at least 97% of numbers and names in fact-dense U.S. federal agency text, but reworded 67-78% of the quoted spans, against its own prompt. Unit retention and detector evasion were not clearly related across tools (Spearman rho = -0.46, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.08), and the open model's four released files (two of them quantization-aware low-bit files) did not show the pre-registered monotone trade-off. On federal texts with matched human, AI-styled and humanized versions, a general-purpose decision model, Jev, asked a single zero-shot question, separated human originals from humanized rewrites with AUROC 0.864 (0.827-0.902), 0.18-0.22 higher than Binoculars, Fast-DetectGPT and the adversarially trained RADAR, while calling 24% of the human originals AI at a 0.5 threshold. On the AI-styled rewrites by 2026 models, both perplexity-based detectors scored below chance (AUROC 0.37 and 0.39), also with line breaks removed. Hypotheses, data rules and analyses were frozen before the main runs; two earlier data contacts are disclosed. We release the checker and the per-item results.

data.title: Recurrence in Sequence Space: How Epistasis Mimics Shared Ancestry
data.abstract: Sequences in a protein family do not explore the sequence space freely: folding, packing, and binding couple residues, so the set of viable sequences is irreducibly correlated, a phenomenon referred to as epistasis. We show that such correlations lower the \emph{intrinsic dimension} $d_{\rm IN}$ of sequence space, counteracting the concentration of measure and broadening the distribution of pairwise distances. Consequentially, they make it likely that independently evolving lineages \emph{recur}, approaching one another by chance long after they last shared an ancestor. Using Kac's lemma we show that the logarithmic mean recurrence time grows linearly with the intrinsic dimension, $\log τ_{\rm rec} \propto {d_{\rm IN}}$ for typical sequences, so strongly constrained (low-dimensional) families recur often and generate sequence similarity that carries no genealogical signal. We establish this first in a solvable Ising-like model with tunable correlation, then in a real protein family using Potts models and Markov chain Monte Carlo, where $d_{\rm IN}$ remains predictive of recurrence even in multi-basins landscapes. Because recurrence is a property of the evolutionary process rather than of any estimator, it bounds the recoverability of deep history for distance-based and likelihood methods alike.

data.title: Statistical Sheaf Modeling Methods for Measuring Qualia Structures
data.abstract: Mathematical sheaves are an abstraction that captures the notion that consistency between local properties can lead to a global picture. There are a number of (mathematical) phenomena that sheaves exhibit, which seem tantalizingly close to what one might hope a theory of qualia would explain. Recently, the theory and abstraction of sheaves has been transformed into robust computational tools for understanding complex systems. These tools are now ripe to help qualia researchers forge robust and testable models. Intuitively, as conscious entities, rather than experiencing ``everything all at once,'' our experience is coherent to varying degrees. Sheaves can model this rather nicely. This chapter presents the practical and theoretical considerations of sheaves in data modeling, with a view towards computational models that can support statistical hypothesis testing.

data.title: Second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle for solenoidal fields: sharp constants, optimizers and sharp stability
data.abstract:
The second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle of Cazacu, Flynn and Lam is the uncertainty principle for the gradient of a function. Motivated by the question of Maz'ya on the uncertainty principle for divergence-free vector fields, solved by Cazacu, Flynn and Lam for $N=2$ and by Hamamoto for $N\ge3$, we study the second order principle for divergence-free fields $\mathbf{U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that $\int|Δ\mathbf{U}|^2dx\int|x|^2|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx\ge C_N^2(\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx)^2$, where $C_N=1+ rac12\sqrt{N^2+8}$ for $N\ge3$ and $C_2=1+\sqrt2$. For the velocity of an incompressible flow, $\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2$ and $\int|Δ\mathbf{U}|^2$ are, up to constant factors, the enstrophy and the palinstrophy, so the inequality bounds the palinstrophy from below in terms of the enstrophy and the spatial spread of the velocity gradient. The constant $C_N$ is sharp and larger than the constant $ rac{N+2}{2}$ for general fields, and all the optimizers are explicit fields with Kummer function profiles. We also obtain the sharp constants on the poloidal and the toroidal fields of each degree. Then we prove the sharp stability of the inequality. In sum form, the deficit controls a chain of squared distances to explicit families of poloidal and toroidal fields, with all the constants sharp. In product form, we find the sharp stability constant in all dimensions. For $N\ge4$ it is $ rac12(\sqrt{N^2+4N-4}-\sqrt{N^2+8})$, and it is attained by swirling flows, the toroidal fields of degree one. On the Fourier side, the sixth order poloidal problem becomes a first order Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality for radial functions, and its stability follows from weighted Poincaré inequalities with Gaussian type measures.

data.title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
data.abstract: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions. In addition, we associate a special G-pcongruence to each pair of strong G-pmorphisms. Then, we study products, co-products, equalizers, co-equalizers, pullbacks, and pushouts in the category G-pActTop. We find that the category of topological partial actions is finitely complete and contains a co-complete subcategory. Finally, we show that the relationship between a topological partial action and its enveloping action is functorial. As a consequence, we obtain that the categorical product in G-ActTop coincides with the categorical product in G-pActTop. Moreover, the envelope of a co-product in G-pActTop is given by the co-product of the respective envelopes.

data.title: Hamiltonian Cycle Construction in Rectangular Grid Graphs with Three-Stacked Triangular Holes
data.abstract: The Hamiltonian cycle problem is NP-complete for general grid graphs, while several structured classes admit efficient construction algorithms. In this paper, we investigate Hamiltonian cycle construction in rectangular grid graphs containing a three-stacked right-triangular hole. We explore two complementary approaches based on the geometric structure of the hole and the parity properties of rectangular subgraphs. The first approach constructs a Hamiltonian path in the complementary reversed staircase region, extends it into an inner Hamiltonian cycle, and merges it with a cycle in the surrounding graph. The second approach partitions the graph into six rectangular subgraphs and constructs a global Hamiltonian cycle by merging local cycles along compatible boundaries. When odd-sized rectangular subgraphs prevent direct cycle construction, we develop parity-based repartitioning techniques that transform selected configurations into even-sized rectangles. We provide constructions for adjacent and nonadjacent odd-sized configurations and investigate reductions for cases involving multiple odd-sized regions. These results establish a constructive framework for Hamiltonian cycles in grid graphs with staircase-shaped holes and identify the remaining cases requiring further analysis.

data.title: Beyond the reduced Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation: Singular potential, global well-posedness, and micromagnetic limits
data.abstract: We study the full nonlinear mean-field Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation in micromagnetics arising from Garanin's spin-polarisation model [D. Garanin. Fokker-Planck and Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch equations for classical ferromagnets. Phys. Rev. B, 55 (1997)] prior to the usual near-equilibrium reduction. The equation combines a singular inverse-Langevin potential with a mobility whose longitudinal component degenerates at saturation, together with exchange, anisotropy, and the nonlocal whole-space stray field. The natural state space is the closed unit ball $|m|\leq 1$. For any $H^1$ initial data satisfying $|m_0|\leq1$, including saturated data of infinite free energy, we construct global weak solutions and derive instantaneous separation from saturation $|m|=1$. This restores uniform parabolicity and yields the thermodynamic formulation and exact energy identity for positive times. We further establish a quantitative low-temperature limit to the Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation and prove convergence of global trajectories to a single equilibrium. A spectral Curie-type threshold characterises the stability of the paramagnetic state and yields exponential relaxation above the threshold. Finally, for uniformly separated data we prove strong well-posedness, including global strong solutions in one- and two-dimensional domains, and exponential stability of non-degenerate equilibria, with a small-data global theory in three dimensions.

data.title: 5d SCFTs and Intersection Theory of Generalized Toric Threefolds
data.abstract: Five-dimensional superconformal field theories are intrinsically strongly coupled fixed points that can be realized as M-theory on local Calabi-Yau threefolds with canonical singularities. The low-energy effective theory on their extended Coulomb branch is governed by a cubic prepotential, determined by the triple intersection numbers of divisors in the resolved geometry. For toric threefolds, dual to 5-brane webs, these numbers are computed combinatorially from the toric polygon. However, no such description has been available for generalized toric polygons (GTPs), dual to 5-brane webs with 7-branes, since the corresponding generalized toric Calabi-Yau threefolds are generally non-toric. We show that the 7-brane data are encoded by additional lines in the GTP, which correspond to non-toric, non-compact divisors that we call exuberant divisors. Building on a local analysis of these divisors and on the associativity of the intersection product, we develop an algorithm that computes the triple intersection numbers, and hence the prepotential, directly from the combinatorial data of the GTP. We illustrate it in examples and provide a Mathematica code implementation of the intersection algorithm.

data.title: When appearance and motion disagree: evaluating class-motion consistency against disguised uncrewed surface vessels
data.abstract: Defense systems for maritime assets must distinguish approaching benign craft from uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) with sufficient warning to act. Shore cameras using computer vision can separate hostile vessels from benign traffic, but these systems may be attacked using an adversarial hull patch or physical disguise. We evaluate adversarial hull patches and find they suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but never cause misclassification as benign. Physical disguise, however, can bypass both a camera check and a radar presence check. To evaluate defenses, we develop a hybrid replay protocol from automatic identification system (AIS) tracks that combines recorded benign motion with direct or off-axis attack run-ins. We find that for recreational-labeled vessels attacking via direct run-in within 4 nautical miles, an asset-relative closing-rate check flags 94-95% at 15-20 knots, compared with 12% for a track-only speed check. The checks are complementary on off-axis approaches, constraining the attacker to remain below both thresholds and extending the time required to reach the asset. Flagging on either check has a 4.9% held-out false-alarm rate overall and 12.3% on recreational traffic. The replay-based evaluation protocol supports comparative test and evaluation of defense methods.

data.title: Modeling CO Line Luminosity with FIRE simulations: II. Comparison With Observations, CO Luminosity Functions and Redshift Evolution
data.abstract: We present predictions for the CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) luminosities of 765, 850, 887 and 915 galaxies at z=0, 1, 2 and 3, respectively, drawn from the Feedback in Realistic Environments (FIRE-2) simulations and post-processed with SKIRT radiative transfer and CLOUDY line emission calculations. We compare our CO line luminosity predictions with existing observations. At z=0, our predictions reproduce the observed scatter and mean relation between star formation rate (SFR) and CO(1-0) luminosity for both massive star-forming galaxies and low-metallicity dwarf galaxies. We also reproduce the observed superlinear power-law slope between CO(1-0) luminosity and metallicity. At z=1, our CO(2-1) predictions scatter to much lower luminosities than observed, which likely reflects the limited sensitivity of current surveys. At fixed SFR, our CO(1-0) luminosities decrease by roughly an order of magnitude per unit increase in redshift. This decline is likely driven by the decrease in metallicity with increasing redshift, since FIRE-2 galaxies with comparable SFR and metallicity produce similar CO(1-0) luminosities regardless of redshift. At fixed stellar mass, the predicted luminosities show no redshift dependence. These results show that our FIRE-2 predictions reproduce the observed scaling relations between CO(1-0) luminosity and galaxy properties wherever the observed galaxies are robustly detected. This gives us confidence in our predictions for the regime where no observational data exist, and suggests that our luminosity predictions can be used to build predictive models for CO line intensity mapping experiments.

data.title: Sealed, Lightweight gRPC-Based Muon Telescopes for Muography Applications
data.abstract: Portable muon detection systems are increasingly in demand for muography applications in environments requiring flexible installation and transportability. We present the ongoing development and implementation of portable muon tracking systems based on glass Resistive Plate Chambers (gRPCs). The work addresses the fabrication and assembly of compact, position-sensitive RPC detectors, along with their performance when operated with a standard gas mixture and coupled to external front-end electronics and a scalable multi-channel data-acquisition system. The system design prioritizes modular construction, mechanical robustness, operational safety, autonomous functionality, and cost-effectiveness. Measurements with atmospheric muons demonstrated stable detector performance and reliable tracking capability, confirming the suitability of this architecture for muographic measurements. We conclude with an outlook on further developments of the detection system.

data.title: Exploring Collaborative Debating Models for the future of science
data.abstract: AI is expanding what researchers can produce. A substantial increase in scientific output would also change how that work is organised and distributed, as earlier shifts in the scale of science have done. This paper develops a thought experiment around Collaborative Debating Models (CDMs), topic-focused environments where researchers work with AI and one another to pursue questions and maintain an evolving account of their field. Individual contributions would remain attributable as ongoing debate and further analysis change the shared account. The paper considers how journals could evolve into these gathering places and how different forms of ownership would shape scientific agendas and the support for continuing work. CDMs could connect participants to remote laboratories and other research services to conduct new studies, with shared repositories making the resulting data available for further inquiry. The proposal links expanded scientific production to collective interpretation through continuing assessment and revision, while leaving room for disciplinary differences in how contributions are reviewed and recognised.

data.title: Toolpath Overhang Optimization for the Large-Format 3D Printing of Bespoke Shapes
data.abstract: This paper presents a closed curve trimming algorithm for overhang optimization in large-format support-free 3D printing of bespoke manifold shapes. Large-format 3D printing enables efficient fabrication of complex, bespoke shapes. Because of the material properties and surface quality requirements, such shapes are typically printed without support structures and have to be designed as support-free. Most current methods of overhang optimization are limited to certain types of geometry and do not apply to bespoke shapes. Our method directly optimizes sliced toolpath curves with minimal geometric modification. Given an overhang limit, it ensures that all resulting toolpath curves are strictly within the overhang limit while preserving their orientation and preventing intersections. The algorithm is based on curve offsetting and trimming, and is applicable to closed toolpath curves that represent the boundaries of a solid volume.

data.title: Comparing the fusion of $^{19}$O and $^{20}$O ions with protons at near barrier energies
data.abstract: Proton capture on $^{19,20}$O nuclei was measured in inverse kinematics with the active-target detector MuSIC@Indiana using CH$_4$ as the target gas. Direct measurement of the (p,n) cross section was enabled by the intrinsically high efficiency and self-normalizing nature of the measurement. The excitation function of both (p,n) reactions exhibits an oscillatory behavior. For the neutron-rich nuclei studied, determining the (p,n) cross section provides access to the proton fusion cross section because the proton's de Broglie wavelength is much larger than that of the heavy ion. A significant suppression of the cross section in $^{19}$O compared to $^{20}$O is observed, suggesting level-density differences. While the coupled channel calculations reproduce the oscillatory behavior observed in the case of $^{20}$O, they fail to predict the oscillatory behavior observed in $^{19}$O or the overall suppression of the fusion cross section.

data.title: Oscillatory instability of subcritical stationary solutions in the parametrically driven, damped nonlinear Dirac equation
data.abstract: The dynamics of the nonlinear Dirac equation (NLDE) under the influence of dissipation and parametric forcing exhibit complex phenomenologies, including soliton destruction and chaotic transitions, which have been extensively observed in numerical simulations. However, a rigorous analytical understanding of the underlying instability mechanisms in the subcritical regime has remained open. In this work, we provide a theoretical answer to these numerical findings by establishing the spectral instability of the fundamental soliton solution. Our methodology relies on a three-step approach linking local asymptotic analyses with global topological arguments. First, we characterize the generalized null space at the critical parameter ($λ_c$), revealing the onset of instability through the splitting of the zero eigenvalue within a parity-dependent subspace. Second, in the non-relativistic limit ($λ\to 0$), we use a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction to reduce the linearized Dirac's operators into a Pöschl--Teller Schrödinger operator, thereby identifying the instability source as a unique real pair of discrete eigenvalues in the restricted problem. Third, we extend these local results to the entire subcritical domain using a topological continuation argument, which tracks the invariance of the spectral parity in a subset of the complex plane. These analytical results rigorously confirm the instability of the soliton, providing the mathematical mechanism for the wave collapse observed in the driven-damped system.

data.title: Unlearning by Extrapolating a Shrink-and-Heal Lookahead
data.abstract: Unlearning aims to make a large language model behave like one retrained without its forget set. Prevailing likelihood-suppression objectives, however, lack an explicit forgetting target: they continually reward lower forget-set likelihood, making forgetting sensitive to the optimization budget. We address this limitation by estimating the direction toward the oracle without training it. Our key idea is to shrink the fine-tuned model toward its pre-fine-tuning weights and briefly re-learn the retain set, thereby removing the forget-specific contribution; in the linearized regime, this shrink-and-heal lookahead moves the model a fixed fraction of the way to the retrained model, its unique fixed point. Our method, SHIFT, extrapolates the lookahead's per-token changes into distillation targets and iteratively refines them. Evaluated against eleven baselines under a unified OpenUnlearning protocol, SHIFT achieves the highest aggregate score across all TOFU settings and the closest oracle alignment, 3.7x closer on average than the next-best method; on MUSE, it preserves the most retain knowledge. Under larger optimization budgets, baselines overshoot the oracle, while SHIFT remains near it, even under relearning attacks.

data.title: MoRE-GS: Motion-Regime Experts for Future Gaussian Splatting
data.abstract: Future dynamic novel-view synthesis requires extrapolating multiple motion regimes within the same scene. A single dynamics model may not simultaneously represent stationary regions, coordinated motion, local interactions, and articulated trajectories. We introduce Motion Regime Expert Routing for Gaussian Splatting (MoRE-GS), a causal, render-aware framework for forecasting dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes. MoRE-GS freezes a Gaussian representation reconstructed exclusively from the observed temporal prefix and forecasts its control-keypoint motion using four complementary experts: persistence, a coefficient-space Transformer, a graph convolutional network, and a structured Transformer with rigid and non-rigid motion constraints. A compact routing table assigns expert mixtures across soft motion groups and forecast-horizon bins, while a persistence gate suppresses unreliable extrapolation. Across D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes, MoRE-GS achieves improved performance against other methods, and these results demonstrate that renderer-calibrated composition of complementary motion predictors improves causal dynamic Gaussian forecasting across heterogeneous motion regimes. Project page: https://advanced-vision-and-learning-lab.github.io/MoRE-GS-website/

data.title: A geometry-aware framework for electromagnetic fields in GATE 10
data.abstract: Objective. An increasing number of medical-physics applications require the modelling of charged-particle transport in electromagnetic (EM) fields. We aim to provide GATE 10 users with a flexible mechanism for defining such fields in Monte Carlo simulations while preserving the native Geant4 particle-transport machinery. Approach. Our framework separates the handling of coordinates from EM field evaluation. Fields are attached to geometry volumes, defined in their local frame, and represented by analytic expressions, field maps, or arbitrary Python functions. They automatically follow the position and orientation of these volumes, including in nested and dynamic geometries. We validated the framework against native Geant4 transport and tested coordinate transformations, nested volumes, and dynamic geometry. We also compared the computational cost of the three field representations. Main results. The framework reproduced the native Geant4 trajectories exactly for all tested field types with direct Geant4 counterparts. Coordinate transformations introduced only floating-point-level differences, while simulations with dynamically changing geometry reproduced the equivalent static configurations exactly. All three representations produced equivalent transport. Mapped fields added at most 18% to the single-threaded runtime of analytic fields, while Python functions required 6.9 times as much. The compiled representations scaled with the number of threads, whereas Python functions became slower as threads were added. Significance. The framework adds flexible, geometry-aware EM field definitions to GATE 10 without modifying the underlying Geant4 transport machinery, and is part of the open-source GATE 10 codebase. It also provides a basis for extending GATE 10 with additional field representations in the future.

data.title: Dysfunctional Functionals and their Therapies in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
data.abstract: The exchange-correlation functional in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) is known to have dependence on past densities and initial states, and yet this memory-dependence is ignored in practical calculations which almost always use an adiabatic approximation. We discuss the dysfunction that arises due to this deficiency and point to therapies that go beyond the adiabatic approximation. Still, adiabatic TDDFT has had success in a wide range of systems for response properties and for fully non-equilibrium dynamics, and why this is so is only partially understood. This, together with the rigorous foundation of the exact theory and its favorable system-size scaling, provides tremendous impetus for continuing to strive towards improved approximations to the exact functionals, and a deeper understanding of the impact of approximations in applications.

data.title: HD 210058 b and BD+37 4838 b: A precessing eccentric hot Jupiter and a misaligned substellar companion around two A-type stars
data.abstract: The number of A- and F-type stars known to host exoplanets is relatively low, as is the number of planets with measured spin-orbit angle, which is the angle between the planet's orbital axis and the star's rotational axis. Expanding the sample of such systems is important for constraining the formation and migration mechanisms of close-in giant planets around early-type stars. We aim to measure the sky-projected spin-orbit angles of HD~210058b (TOI-1355b) and BD+37~4838b (TOI-1414b), two objects still listed as candidate exoplanets, and to assess the planetary nature of these systems. Both of their host stars are fast rotators. We analyzed TESS photometry together with transit time-series of HARPS-N spectra. For both objects, we created cross-correlation functions from the spectra to analyze Doppler tomography and detect and model the Doppler shadow, while we also used the photometric observations to refine a number of previously poorly constrained photometric and spectroscopic parameters of both the host stars and the companions. When possible, we used the derived results to constrain the companion masses. We verified the planetary and substellar nature for both objects respectively. We report HD~210058~b to be a giant hot Jupiter with a mass of 10 M_Jup, residing on a slightly misaligned orbit with the sky-projected spin-orbit angle λ=-32 -6 +4 deg. Archival photometry reveals continuously changing inclination and impact parameter, pointing to a nodal precession with period of 860 yr, and giving availability of only about six upcoming years for any further transit observations. The second target, BD+37~4838~b, orbits a hybrid γ~Dor-δ~Sct pulsator on a misaligned orbit with λ=56.9 +1.4 -2.3 deg. Since we could not reliably recover its mass, we only report an upper limit of approx. 24.3 M_Jup, leaving the possible planetary nature of this object unresolved.

data.title: A sharp plank theorem for cube annuli
data.abstract: We prove a conjecture of András Bezdek on plank coverings of square annuli. A plank in a Euclidean space is the closed region between two distinct parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between them. Let $Q$ be a unit square and let $H$ be a square of side length $1/2$ whose sides are parallel to those of $Q$. Then every finite family of planks covering $Q\setminus H$ has total width at least $1$. More generally, if an axis-parallel box with side lengths $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ is removed from the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\sum_jh_j = d-1$, then every finite plank covering of the remaining set has total width at least one. The bounds are sharp.

data.title: Where Intention Goes, Responsibility Flows: Grounding AI Accountability in the Machine Learning Paradigm
data.abstract: An opening salvo of lawsuits in U.S. courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack. This Perspective points out that these converging paths share a unifying principle, built on the very engineering architecture of machine learning (ML) itself. Every ML system, across all variants, is constituted by a human-specified objective function before learning begins. Training data, deployment context, user interaction, and post-deployment oversight add further layers of deliberate human intention traceable to identifiable actors. AI output is therefore not the expression of a single speaker but a composite of layered human intents. It takes a village to raise an AI, and everyone in that village bears a duty of care. This transforms AI accountability from a philosophical puzzle into a tractable legal inquiry: trace the chain of intentional design decisions across the ML pipeline, grade each actor's responsibility by their intent's specificity and foreseeability, and apportion liability accordingly, following the standard three doctrine-neutral questions (attribution, causation, apportionment). Sufficient for most cases, four gaps remain: who owes what share when many hands build one system, proving fault inside an opaque model, harms that surface only after deployment, and remedies that match the technology's pace. Targeted reforms drawing on environmental, vaccine, and financial regulatory precedents can close these gaps without requiring new legal categories, AI speech rights, AI legal personhood, or defining AI consciousness.

data.title: Absorption Probabilities for Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension
data.abstract: For every dimension $d\ge1$, we determine the probability that a prescribed point in $\mathbb R^d$ belongs to the convex hull over $[0,1]$ of a standard Brownian motion starting at the origin or of a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$. We obtain explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving only standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability $p_3^B(r)$ for a prescribed point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r) =\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,π^{3/2}} \int_0^\infty \left(\fracπ{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right) \mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4} (K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d} v, \] where $K_ν$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For each fixed dimension $d\ge1$ and each prescribed nonzero point in $\mathbb R^d$, we derive precise asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of Brownian motion on $[0,T]$ and a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$ over the same interval, as $T\to\infty$. The corresponding probabilities are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively. We also consider the first time $τ_d$ at which the growing convex hull of a standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb R^d$ absorbs a prescribed point at distance one from the origin. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of $τ_d$ explicitly. Although $\mathbb E[τ_d]=\infty$ in every dimension, we prove \[ \frac{\logτ_d-2d}{2\sqrt d} \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty. \] In particular, $τ_d^{1/d}\to\mathrm{e}^2$ in probability, as $d\to\infty$. Surprisingly, the same limit holds for $S_d^{1/d}$, where $S_d$ is the first time at which the Brownian convex hull contains the entire unit ball.

data.title: Non-Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics of Glass-Forming Liquids under Continuous Cooling: Microscopic Inner Clocks, Fictive Temperatures, and Kauzmann Diagrams
data.abstract: The description of macroscopic properties in out-of-equilibrium amorphous solids such as gels and glasses, typically processed under finite cooling rates, remains a fundamental challenge for modern statistical physics. In this work, we employ the Non-Equilibrium Self-Consistent Generalized Langevin Equation (NESCGLE) theory to construct a microscopic description of the structural and calorimetric glass transition under continuous cooling. Building upon the microscopic Onsager-Machlup interpretation of Narayanaswamy's material time (the inner clock $u(t)$) [J.Chem.Phys. 156, 244506 (2022)], we recover Tool's fictive temperature $T_f$ directly from the evolving spatial pair correlations and show that wavenumber dispersion naturally generalizes the classical scalar $T_f$ into a continuous mode spectrum governed by de Gennes narrowing at the primary cage peak. Across wide variations in cooling rate down to the quasi-static limit, the theory yields first-principles non-equilibrium Kauzmann diagrams for the two-body excess entropy that dynamically avert the Kauzmann crisis above the ideal dynamic arrest temperature $T_c$, while predicting sigmoidal relaxational heat-capacity steps consistent with computer simulations and calorimetry. Finally, we extract the cooling-rate-dependent glass transition temperature $T_g(q)$ from both equal-area integrals and differential heat-capacity landmarks, demonstrating that its asymptotic approach toward $T_c$ obeys a critical power-law scaling governed directly by the equilibrium dynamic arrest exponent.

data.title: LF-VideoQA: Evaluating Long-Video Understanding with Long-Form Theory-of-Mind Questions
data.abstract: The hardest part of understanding a long video is not pinpointing any one moment but synthesizing many, e.g., answering a question that requires tracking what develops across hours of content and articulating how the pieces fit together. To date, most long-video QA datasets require only a short answer or a multiple-choice selection, oversimplifying the long-video understanding task to retrieval. We introduce LF-VideoQA, a dataset for long-form, open-ended question answering over long narrative videos built on theory-of-mind questions: a character's belief depends on everything they have seen or been told, so each question demands assembling and reasoning from evidence distributed across the video. The dataset contains more than 6,300 questions on 94 recent films; each requires reasoning over scenes spanning an average of 23 minutes and comes with a question-specific rubric for recall and precision scoring. The dataset is created entirely automatically by annotating screenplays with scene events and each character's first-order beliefs and meta-beliefs, then generating (question, answer, rubric) triples through LLM-based question generation and verification; human studies validate their quality. We evaluate four families of state-of-the-art open-source VLMs across three settings and find the task highly challenging: (i) even an oracle with access to the screenplay falls well short of complete answers; (ii) the best non-oracle model attains barely half of the recall level of the oracle; (iii) unlike on prior long-video benchmarks, captions and subtitles underperform the video itself, indicating that the questions need visual evidence; and (iv) recall is the predominant bottleneck, with answers omitting many required rubric claims.

data.title: Agent Stack for ML Training Lifecycle: Generation, Validation, and Optimization
data.abstract: Production model development requires repeated architecture design, platform integration, debugging, training, and evaluation. We present an agent stack deployed at LinkedIn with two independently usable agent loops: AutoTorch for model generation and migration, and AutoResearch for model optimization. AutoTorch generates PyTorch models and training pipelines for TensorFlow migration, XGBoost replacement, and new-model development. Executable validation hooks check platform API compliance, trainability, and conversion fidelity on sampled data, guiding iterative repair before engineer review and full-scale distributed training. AutoResearch explores architecture and training-configuration changes through expert-steered or autonomous experimentation. An external orchestrator manages parallel trials, experiment history, candidate selection, and wall-clock budgets across agent sessions. A shared runtime preserves execution state independently of agent reasoning and allocates GPUs separately from agent execution. Across ranking, content understanding, and recommendation workloads, AutoTorch completed generation and full-scale training in 92 of 115 workflow runs (80%). Of these, 77 (83.7%) produced models meeting post-training quality requirements. In a separate cohort, AutoResearch improved the primary task metric on held-out data for 28 of 100 production pipelines. Engineering teams estimate that the stack reduced elapsed end-to-end migration time from approximately eight weeks to two weeks, a 4x speedup.

data.title: Current Results on Light Hypernuclei in the WASA-FRS HypHI Experiment
data.abstract: The current understanding of light hypernuclei, subatomic nuclei exhibiting strangeness, is being actively investigated by several collaborations. Recent studies employing high-energy heavy-ion beams have revealed unexpected results for the three-body bound state $^3_Λ$H, known as the hypertriton. Experimental measurements of its lifetime and binding energy across multiple experiments have produced a puzzling situation referred to as the ``hypertriton puzzle''. This puzzle is the central focus of the data analysis from the WASA-FRS HypHI experiment at GSI-FAIR within the SuperFRS Experiment collaboration. Light hypernuclei are being investigated using 1.96 GeV/u $^6$Li beams impinging on a fixed carbon target, in conjunction with the WASA detector system and the Fragment Separator (FRS) at GSI-FAIR. The WASA-FRS experimental campaign was carried out during the first quarter of 2022. The primary objective of the experiment is to measure the lifetimes of $^3_Λ$H and $^4_Λ$H. The possible observation of the nn$Λ$ state constitutes the second component of the WASA-FRS research program. This contribution provides an overview of our investigation of hypernuclei. Focusing on the WASA-FRS HypHI experiment, details of the current analysis status are presented.

data.title: Dependence-Aware Risk Assessment and Optimal Design of AI-Agent Safeguard Systems
data.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on safeguards to prevent unauthorized actions while preserving legitimate service. However, existing risk assessments often focus on individual safeguard performance while overlooking dependence among safeguard decisions. This paper develops a dependence-aware framework for risk assessment and optimal design of multi-component AI safeguard systems, jointly selecting configurations and operating policies for sequential layered screening and selective verification. We establish stochastic comparisons of layered-screening error probabilities and invocation costs under lower-orthant ordering. For selective verification, we characterize exactly which policies have error probabilities and review costs that respond monotonically to stronger dependence under supermodular ordering. For a fixed first stage and reviewer, we show that the optimal routing map is a two-threshold rule in the first-stage likelihood ratio. An accompanying open-source software package, Dependence-Aware Policy Optimization Algorithms (DAPOA), facilitates the practical implementation of the proposed framework. Numerical experiments show that ignoring dependence can lead to inaccurate risk assessments and infeasible safeguard designs, with independence-based selections violating security requirements in six of eight scenarios. An empirical study using four LLM safeguards on benchmark-derived agent actions further demonstrates the practical implications of dependence modeling. Under the principal operating setting, dependence-aware selection lowers held-out total cost by 39.6% relative to independence-based selection.

data.title: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks
data.abstract: Humans possess a remarkable ability to draw inferences from limited data. While some inferences are made intuitively from past experience, others require online reasoning based on novel information given in context. Here, we formalize these strategies, which we term geometric and algebraic inference, and study their computational tradeoffs in humans and neural networks. The geometric strategy gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect underlying relational structure, making subsequent inference cheap. The algebraic strategy flexibly attends to and reasons over novel relations given in context, but costs additional computation at inference time. We identify opposing signatures of these two strategies in transitive inference, a domain widely studied across species, and characterize the conditions under which each is observed. Our framework predicts that the geometric strategy should be dominant when relations are familiar, whereas the algebraic should emerge to support de novo inferences drawn in context. Multiple experiments demonstrate these opposing signatures in humans, neural networks trained from scratch, and large language models (LLMs). Causal interventions in the neural networks reveal that the geometric and algebraic strategies depend on representational geometry and selective attention mechanisms, respectively, and reproduce the effects of analogous neurobiological disruptions in humans. Our framework unifies these effects with disparate phenomena, including content effects observed in human and LLM reasoning and data-distribution effects observed in machine learning. Our findings reconcile competing views of cognitive flexibility that emphasize either representational geometry or algebraic manipulation by showing that each can have unique strengths, and can characterize different aspects of both human and neural network behavior.

data.title: On the properties of the potential and the spherical harmonic expansions for general planets
data.abstract: The convergence of spherical harmonic expansions (SHEs) of gravitational potentials below the Brillouin sphere has been a long-standing problem in potential theory and geodesy.
